title: Bengals waive WR Ke'Shawn Williams
summary: With the Bengals bringing back one receiver, they’re letting go of another.
full_text: With the Bengals bringing back one receiver, they’re letting go of another. Jeremy Fowler of ESPN reports Cincinnati has waived receiver/returner Ke’Shawn Williams. Williams muffed a punt return in the fourth quarter of Sunday’s loss to the Steelers. That allowed Pittsburgh to tie the game at 27-27 before Pittsburgh eventually got another field goal to win, 30-27. News emerged earlier on Tuesday that the Bengals are signing Mitchell Tinsley off of the Texans’ practice squad. Tinsley played all 17 games for Cincinnati last year.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Travis Hunter got a lot more work on the defensive side of the ball in Week 3
summary: In Week 2, Jaguars cornerback/receiver Travis Hunter had only 31 defensive snaps.
full_text: In Week 2, Jaguars cornerback/receiver Travis Hunter had only 31 defensive snaps. As expected , he got a lot more in Week 3. Hunter was on the field for 45 defensive plays, in a game that featured his first career interception. On offense, he continues to not do much. After getting six snaps in Week 2, he got only five in Week 3. He was targeted in neither game. And so it seems as if the Jaguars are moving him toward being a full-time cornerback, and a very part-time receiver. Whether that means he has accepted his apparent fate remains to be seen. He wants to play both sides of the ball. He wants to have the ball in his hands. And he seems to be concerned that, if he plays only defense and successfully locks down half of the field, he'll rarely touch the ball. Regardless, his long-term best interests could be best served by playing only defense. Especially since the Jaguars have a great collection of receivers.
author: Mike Florio

title: Chop Robinson: Not sure why I got called for roughing Patrick Mahomes, but I had to play on
summary: Dolphins linebacker Chop Robinson is not complaining about the controversial penalty he got for roughing Patrick Mahomes on Sunday, but he is wondering what he could have done differently.
full_text: Dolphins linebacker Chop Robinson is not complaining about the controversial penalty he got for roughing Patrick Mahomes on Sunday, but he is wondering what he could have done differently. Asked what he could have done to avoid the roughing penalty, which the officials said was for landing on Mahomes with his body weight, Robinson said he doesn't know. "I'm honestly not too sure, but either way, that's what they called, so that's what we got to play on. Next play," Robinson said. Robinson put his hands down to break his own fall on top of Mahomes, but he said he'll try to do that earlier in the process of falling to the ground next time. "Just put my hands out earlier, but it's a football play. That's what the refs called, so I had to move on from it," Robinson said. "That's what I could do better on that play, but that's what they called, and that's what it is." Asked about practicing hitting quarterbacks without landing on them, Robinson said that's a hard thing to do because defensive players don't hit quarterbacks in practice. "I don't know, that's a hard question. When you can't really work it, you can't hit a quarterback in practice. But I did what I was taught and told to do, and that's what they called, so that's what it is," Robinson said. The penalty was very costly for the Dolphins, as it came after Mahomes had thrown an incompletion in his own end zone on third down. If not for the penalty, the Chiefs would have punted from deep in their own territory, and the Dolphins would have taken over in good field position while trailing 14-10 in the third quarter. Instead, the 15-yard penalty and automatic first down kept alive a Chiefs drive that ended up lasting 13 plays, covering 80 yards, and ending with a field goal that gave the Chiefs a 17-10 lead in the fourth quarter. "Of course we wanted to keep them in the end zone, but again, that's what they called. There's nothing I could do about it, just play the next play, and just try to stop them, get the ball back to the offense," Robinson said. The penalty was one of the biggest plays of the game, and one that Robinson isn't sure how he could have avoided.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Ben Johnson: Case Keenum's touchdown run was a "Mike Martz special" play call
summary: Bears head coach Ben Johnson has earned a reputation as an offensive innovator, but he didn't come up with the idea that led to one of his team's touchdowns in Monday's 27-7 win over the Eagles.
full_text: Bears head coach Ben Johnson has earned a reputation as an offensive innovator, but he didn't come up with the idea that led to one of his team's touchdowns in Monday's 27-7 win over the Eagles. Quarterback Case Keenum ran for a one-yard score in the fourth quarter on a play that saw the two Chicago guards pull in opposite directions while Keenum followed center Garrett Bradbury up the middle for the score. After the game, Johnson credited former Rams head coach Mike Martz with coming up with the play design. “That’s a Mike Martz special right there, that's the old sucker sneak," Johnson said. "I think they were a little bit tight initially and then they stemmed out at the last second, which gave us the green light to get to that play. It’s an old play, an old but a good play right there.” Martz memorably called the play during Super Bowl XXXVI and it resulted in a Kurt Warner touchdown run. Johnson was a teenager when that game was played, but Martz's ingenuity stuck with him.
author: Josh Alper

title: T.J. Edwards got nothing from eavesdropping on Eagles' huddle
summary: Monday night's game between the Eagles and Bears featured a moment in which former Eagles (now Bears) linebacker T.J.
full_text: Monday night's game between the Eagles and Bears featured a moment in which former Eagles (now Bears) linebacker T.J. Edwards tiptoed toward the huddle to try to hear what Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts was saying. Then the play started, and Edwards intercepted a pass from Hurts. After the game, Edwards was asked whether he picked anything up from his eavesdropping attempt. "No," Edwards said, via Kevin Fishbain of The Athletic . "I was like, 'Maybe I'll hear some familiar stuff,' and like they must have changed language up because I had no idea what they were talking about ." That's no surprise. Edwards last played for the Eagles in 2022. They've had four offensive coordinators since Edwards left. Regardless, Edwards brings to the Bears a knowledge of Hurts and other players with whom he played. It's one of the basic realities of today's high-mobility NFL. Little things can be picked up and possibly used later. Tendencies, tells, habits, etc. Every quarterback needs to be keeping notes on all defenders he faces in practice, and every defender needs to be keeping notes on all quarterbacks they face in practice. Today's coworker can be tomorrow's enemy, and an edge can come from anywhere.
author: Mike Florio

title: Report: Damien Lewis to miss at least Week 4 with UCL injury
summary: The Panthers will not have one of their starting offensive linemen for at least Sunday’s game.
full_text: The Panthers will not have one of their starting offensive linemen for at least Sunday’s game. Per Mike Garafolo of NFL Network, left guard Damien Lewis will be sidelined for a few weeks with a UCL injury in his elbow. But there’s a chance Lewis will miss just one game, as the Panthers have a bye in Week 5. Head coach Dave Canales mentioned in his Monday press conference that the team was doing imaging on Lewis’ injury and the bye would be taken into consideration when it comes to a return-to-play timeline. Lewis has been with the Panthers since 2024, having signed a four-year contract with the club.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Ben Johnson takes another dig at Jared Goff's mobility
summary: When Bears coach Ben Johnson compared the mobility of quarterback Caleb Williams to the lack of mobility of Jared Goff in 2025, Johnson promptly explained he wasn't taking a shot at Goff.
full_text: When Bears coach Ben Johnson compared the mobility of quarterback Caleb Williams to the lack of mobility of Jared Goff in 2025, Johnson promptly explained he wasn't taking a shot at Goff. " It was not a shot at Jared ," Johnson said in early 2025. "I’ve talked to Jared about it. Sometimes your comments get skewed a little bit. That was not my intent. He certainly understands that. It was more directed towards Caleb and what he brings to the table." Fast forward to last night, and Johnson took another apparent shot at Goff. "Well, I've got a little history with that, of calling plays for someone not so mobile," Johnson said regarding the different playing styles of Williams and Case Keenum. Johnson likely will say again that it wasn't a shot at Goff. And it really isn't. Everyone knows Jared Goff isn't Usain Bolt. Still, watch the video . Johnson knew what was coming. And he smirked a couple of times while the question was being asked. He knew exactly what he was going to say. And he seemed to enjoy it. There's a refreshing cheekiness to Johnson that often shines through. Indeed, Johnson added another remark about the fact that, for the first time in his career as a play-caller, he was working with someone who wasn't the first overall pick in the draft. "Now, I don't have a history with someone that's not a number one pick though," Johnson said after his latest non-shot shot at Goff. "So that was apparently a big deal." It wasn't necessarily a "big deal." But it was, you know, a fact. The latest fact is that it doesn't matter, and that Johnson was able to take a guy who hadn't played in a regular-season game in 1,009 days and make him look like a Pro Bowler. It's no surprise, given that Johnson took a guy the Rams couldn't wait to get rid of and turned him into a high-end starter.
author: Mike Florio

title: Jerry Jones: No explanation for end of Ravens loss that you're satisfied with
summary: The Cowboys' chances of winning Sunday's game against the Ravens in Brazil unraveled in the final seconds of the fourth quarter.
full_text: The Cowboys' chances of winning Sunday's game against the Ravens in Brazil unraveled in the final seconds of the fourth quarter. After the team used its final timeout after a short run by quarterback Dak Prescott on second down from the 5-yard-line, they dialed up a pass play that appeared to get wide receiver George Pickens open in the end zone. Prescott threw the ball away as Pickens got free, which both he and head coach Brian Schottenheimer said was by design after the game. During a Tuesday appearance on 105.3 The Fan, Cowboys owner Jerry Jones was asked about the sequence from the timing of the timeout through Prescott's throw. “There’s no explanation that you’re satisfied with ," Jones said. "None. Let’s be sure that we all understand that. They don't have one that they’re satisfied with. We made mistakes during that time, there’s no question about it. There’s no explanation. There’s an evaluation of how to not make the same mistakes again, which is what you should be doing. We can’t get that back. No way to get it back. What you can do is use it — if there’s any aspect of it that you want to just not even think happened. Any aspect of it, use it to get better.” The Cowboys settled for a field goal with seven seconds left, which turned out to be just enough time for the Ravens to set up a 56-yard game-winning field goal of their own. The handling of the kickoff, which went for a touchback that took no time off the clock, was another matter lacking a satisfying rationale that might make the loss sit better with anyone.
author: Josh Alper

title: Andy Reid: I'll let you know when Josh Simmons is coming back
summary: The Chiefs have started the season 3-0 despite not having their starting left tackle available.
full_text: The Chiefs have started the season 3-0 despite not having their starting left tackle available. Josh Simmons has been sidelined by a back injury that’s been considered week-to-week. But it’s currently unclear if Simmons will return to practice in advance of Sunday’s matchup with the 3-0 Raiders. “I'll tell you what, I will let you guys know when Josh is coming back. I'll be the first to tell you,” head coach Andy Reid said in his Monday news conference. “We’ll just see how all that works.” Simmons appeared in eight games as a rookie in 2025. Undrafted rookie Khalil Benson has started in Simmons’ stead at left tackle and has helped keep Patrick Mahomes upright. The quarterback has been sacked just four times through the first three weeks.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Senate passes the Protect College Sports Act
summary: Report says there's a "0.0 percent chance" the House passes it before election day in November.
full_text: Big-time college sports has moved halfway toward the federal bailout they crave. The rest of the journey is unlikely to happen soon. The U.S. Senate passed the so-called "Protect College Sports Act" on Monday night, by a vote of 77-22. The bill now goes to the U.S. House of Representatives. Earlier in the day, Pat Forde of SI.com cited an unnamed source who said that there is a “0.0 percent chance " the House will pass the bill before the midterm elections. With the Democrats widely expected to seize control of the House in November, the question then becomes whether it will do any meaningful business before the next Congress convenes in January. So there's still a long way to go before the NCAA and its members get the antitrust exemption and other benefits designed to stave off a catastrophe. Even as college football is more popular and profitable than ever. There's chaos, they say. From whose perspective? The players, after years of being exploited by a system that denied them the opportunity to participate meaningfully in the value they generate, are sitting pretty. It's not chaotic for them; it's the free market in operation. But the schools apparently can't be trusted to balance their budgets, which is bullshit. Every American business faces an ongoing challenge to adapt or fail. In lieu of expecting the administrators to come up with a better way to carve up the pie and/or to spend within their means, they want artificial restrictions on what the players can make. That's not how it should be. And, despite the Senate vote, maybe it won't be.
author: Mike Florio

title: Dolphins put De'Von Achane on injured reserve
summary: Dolphins running back De'Von Achane's season is over after he suffered a torn ACL in Sunday's loss to the Chiefs and the Dolphins made a roster move related to the injury on Monday.
full_text: Dolphins running back De'Von Achane's season is over after he suffered a torn ACL in Sunday's loss to the Chiefs and the Dolphins made a roster move related to the injury on Monday. Achane was placed on injured reserve as part of a series of roster moves in Miami. The Dolphins also waived defensive lineman Keith Cooper off of the 53-man roster and released defensive linemen Clelin Ferrell and Jordan Miller from the practice squad. Dolphins head coach Jeff Hafley said at a Monday press conference that his "heart breaks" for Achane and said that all of the team's other running backs will have roles in filling in for him. Jaylen Wright and Ollie Gordon are the other backs on the 53-man roster, but the Dolphins could add to that group now that they have two open roster spots at their disposal.
author: Josh Alper

title: J.J. McCarthy joins a small group of first-round quarterbacks who made quick exits
summary: The Vikings have scrapped the J.J.
full_text: The Vikings have scrapped the J.J. McCarthy experience after the 2024 first-round pick made only 10 starts in two-plus seasons. That adds McCarthy to a short list of first-round quarterbacks who, for whatever reason, didn't last very long with the teams that drafted them. Via Kevin Seifert of ESPN, Elias Sports Bureau identifies only four first-round quarterbacks in the past 25 years who started 10 or fewer games for the team that picked them. Paxton Lynch, the 2016 first-round pick of the Broncos, started only four games in Denver. He never played in a regular-season game for any other team. Trey Lance, for whom the 49ers traded up in 2021 to make the third overall selection, started only four games in San Francisco. (He has since made eight appearances with two starts for the Cowboys and Chargers.) Johnny Manziel, a first-round pick of the Browns in 2014, started eight games in Cleveland. He never played for another NFL team. McCarthy had exactly 10 starts with the Vikings. He won six of them. But the Vikings have opted to take a fifth-round pick in order to move on from him. While it's far less than the first-round pick plus more that they gave up to get him, it's more than what they would have gotten if he'd been cut before the start of the 2026 season. Which seemed to be a real possibility in late August, especially after he slipped to third on the depth chart. Either way, the Vikings pulled the plug. And now they'll have to hope that McCarthy doesn't become the latest second-act (or third-act) quarterback who becomes a star for someone else. Sure, the Vikings would never say it out loud. They don't need to. They know that the only thing that will make their McCarthy misadventures worse will be watching him become for someone else what the Vikings hoped he would be.
author: Mike Florio

title: 49ers to open DE Mykel Williams' practice window this week
summary: The 49ers signed defensive end Matt Judon on Monday, because of their injuries at the position.
full_text: The 49ers signed defensive end Matt Judon on Monday, because of their injuries at the position. But they could see the return of one of their big names in the not-too-distant future. The 49ers plan to open the practice window for defensive end Mykel Williams on Wednesday, coach Kyle Shanahan said. Williams started the season on the active/physically unable to perform (PUP) list. That required him to miss at least the first four games of the season. He will now need some ramp-up time before making it back to game action. Williams, a first-round pick in 2025, tore the ACL and lateral meniscus in his right knee during a Nov. 2 game against the Giants.
author: Charean Williams

title: Bears LT Braxton Jones questionable to return with knee injury
summary: Bears left tackle Braxton Jones is in the training room for further evaluation after a third-quarter injury.
full_text: Bears left tackle Braxton Jones is in the training room for further evaluation after a third-quarter injury. Jones was injured on a third-down incompletion with 10:21 remaining in the quarter. His right leg appeared to buckle on a bull rush by Jonathan Greenard, and Jones needed help getting off the field. The Bears list Jones as questionable to return with a knee injury. Theo Benedet replaced Jones, with Ozzy Trapilo inactive. Benedet played nine snaps in the first half, according to Brad Biggs of the Chicago Tribune . The Bears added a field goal in the third quarter, with Cairo Santos' 48-yard kick giving Chicago a 13-7 lead.
author: Charean Williams

title: Klint Kubiak is the early favorite for coach of the year
summary: In the battle of the offensive coordinators of the last two Super Bowl winners, Raiders coach Klint Kubiak got the better of Saints coach Kellen Moore.
full_text: In the battle of the offensive coordinators of the last two Super Bowl winners, Raiders coach Klint Kubiak got the better of Saints coach Kellen Moore. The 35-27 victory moved the Raiders to 3-0. To no surprise, Kubiak is the early favorite for coach of the year. One big reason for that is "coach of the year" typically means "coach whose team most exceeded the generally accepted preseason expectations." Under that test, it could be no one (for now) other than Kubiak. The Raiders were 3-14 in 2025. They're now 3-0. And they've played well enough to show it's not a fluke. Meanwhile, Kubiak has become only the third Raiders coach to launch his career with three straight wins. The others were Bill Callahan in 2002 and John Madden in 1969. Callahan took the Raiders to the Super Bowl. Madden, in his first year, took the Raiders to the AFL Championship. If Kubiak simply takes the Raiders to the 7th seed, he'll likely be getting a trophy that his father, Gary, never won. While pursuing the possibility of having the first father-son picnic that consists of both guys showing up with a Super Bowl trophy.
author: Mike Florio

title: Vikings send J.J. McCarthy to the Giants for a 2027 fifth-round pick
summary: Minnesota send 10th pick in 2024 to New York.
full_text: The J.J. McCarthy experiment in Minnesota has ended. In New York, it's just beginning. Per multiple reports, the Vikings have traded the tenth overall pick in the 2024 draft to the Giants. In return, the Vikings will receive a 2027 fifth-round pick. The Giants have a clear need at the position, given the knee injury that will keep Jaxson Dart out for at least the rest of the regular season. On Sunday, the starter was Jameis Winston, with Jake Haener as the understudy. In Minnesota, McCarthy lost the starting job to Kyler Murray before falling behind Carson Wentz to the third spot on the depth chart. From the moment McCarthy was benched, it seemed that he was on borrowed time in Minnesota — even though everyone involved was saying all the right things. For the Giants, the move brings the former Michigan quarterback (coached by Jim Harbaugh) to the NFL team coached by John Harbaugh. For now, Winston is the starter. Whether McCarthy gets an opportunity to play depends on whether Winston is injured — and whether Winston remains sufficiently effective.
author: Mike Florio

title: Vikings GM Nolan Teasley: J.J. McCarthy trade was the best decision for the Vikings
summary: Nolan Teasley was not the Vikings' General Manager who drafted J.J.
full_text: Nolan Teasley was not the Vikings' General Manager who drafted J.J. McCarthy, but he became the one who ended the quarterback's time in Minnesota on Monday. McCarthy was traded to the Giants in exchange for a 2027 fifth-round pick and Teasley explained the decision to cut ties with the 2024 first-round pick at a press conference on Monday afternoon. Teasley said that McCarthy, who was the third-string quarterback, did not request a trade, but that the Vikings believed that making a move was "the best path forward and the best decision." "We have a responsibility to make decisions that we believe are in the best interest of the organization, of the Vikings holistically," Teasley said. "Sometimes, those decisions aren't easy, but you just have to recognize when a different situation or a new opportunity presents itself it has the opportunity to present better outcomes.” Teasley had spoken about McCarthy continuing to develop throughout the offseason and said that he continues "to believe that his story is not written in this league and that he has potential to continue to grow and develop and make a difference" as an NFL player, but that won't be happening in Minnesota. He also called the fifth-round pick an asset that could potentially help the Vikings this season as they could move it again in a trade before the deadline.
author: Josh Alper

title: Nick Sirianni on Jalen Hurts medical check: "Doctors have to do their job"
summary: Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts was visibly frustrated by a sideline concussion evaluation that kept him off the field for a promising drive that ended in an Andy Dalton interception during Monday night's game against the Bears.
full_text: Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts was visibly frustrated by a sideline concussion evaluation that kept him off the field for a promising drive that ended in an Andy Dalton interception during Monday night's game against the Bears. Eagles coach Nick Sirianni didn't love the moment, either, but he understands the importance of ensuring that the players are kept safe and healthy. "Obviously frustrating," Sirianni told Lisa Salters of ESPN at halftime of Monday night's game, "but the doctors have to do their job. The guys — they got to protect these guys. And, you know, we have a hit on the sideline that they looked at, and that's the way it goes. We gotta be able to run the ball in from the one, regardless of who's in there. Yeah, I'm bummed that Jalen wasn't in for that. We got to take care of the ball with Andy. But, hey, I mean, they're doing their best to keep the players safe." Unlike former Giants coach Brian Daboll last year in a prime-time game against the Eagles, the emotional Sirianni stayed away from the tent. The punishment imposed by the league on the Giants, Daboll, and running back Cam Skattebo may have had something to do with that. Regardless, Sirianni gets it. If a player is getting checked for a concussion, he's not available. The coaching staff and the players have no choice but to adapt to that circumstance.
author: Mike Florio

title: Case Keenum's second TD pass has Bears holding 20-7 lead
summary: The Bears looked like they might be in trouble early in the practice week, with their top two quarterbacks on the injury report.
full_text: The Bears looked like they might be in trouble early in the practice week, with their top two quarterbacks on the injury report. Caleb Williams is inactive tonight with a hamstring injury, and Tyson Bagent is serving as the backup after clearing concussion protocol. But the Bears have Case Keenum, who is making his 67th career start. He has thrown his 80th and 81st career touchdown passes tonight, with the latter giving the Bears a 20-7 lead. Keenum hit Kalif Raymond for a 41-yard touchdown on the Eagles' busted coverage with 5:47 remaining in the third quarter. Keenum is 22-of-29 for 242 yards and two touchdowns, and Raymond has six catches for 90 yards and a touchdown. The Eagles began the second half with three three-and-outs and have 12 yards in the third quarter.
author: Charean Williams

title: Monday Night Football: Case Keenum, Bears beat Eagles 27-7
summary: The Bears third-string quarterback hadn't played since 2023.
full_text: Case Keenum, playing his first game since 2023, ran for a touchdown and threw two touchdowns in leading the Bears to a 27-7 blowout of the Eagles. Both teams are 2-1. Despite playing without starting quarterback Caleb Williams, who is out with a hamstring injury, the Bears dominated the Eagles. Keenum, in his 67th career start, joined Ryan Fitzpatrick as the only quarterbacks to win starts for seven different NFL teams. He threw an 8-yard touchdown to Luther Burden and a 41-yarder to Kalif Raymond. A 6-yard touchdown pass to Colston Loveland was overturned on replay, with the tight end just short of the goal line. Keenum ended the team's scoring in the fourth quarter with a 1-yard touchdown run on third down. Keenum went 24-of-34 for 247 yards. Raymond caught six passes for 90 yards, and Burden added seven for 61. The Bears outgained the Eagles 375 to 248 yards and held the ball for 36:53. Philadelphia never led. The Eagles did close to within 10-7 at halftime, with Jalen Hurts scoring on the tush push on the final play of the half. Philadelphia, though, opened the second half with three consecutive three-and-outs and 12 total yards. The Eagles, who had 62 yards in the second half, shot themselves in the cleat all night. Andy Dalton, who briefly replaced Hurts after the starter was pulled out of the game for a concussion check, threw an interception into the end zone from the 2-yard line. It was rookie Dillon Thieneman's first career pick. Hurts threw an interception at the Chicago 46; Tank Bigsby lost a fumble at his own 15; the Eagles were 2-of-9 on third downs; and they committed 10 penalties, including four on defense. Hurts went 16-of-25 for 153 yards and an interception, with DeVonta Smith catching six for 65. Saquon Barkley had 15 rushes for 82 yards.
author: Charean Williams

title: Ben Johnson praises Case Keenum, doesn't say who Bears' starting QB will be next week
summary: With Caleb Williams recovering from a hamstring injury, the Bears may turn to Tyson Bagent Sunday against the Jets.
full_text: Bears head coach Ben Johnson praised third-string quarterback Case Keenum after Monday night's win over the Eagles, but Johnson wasn't ready to say whether Keenum will start again on Sunday against the Jets. "It's all about Case Keenum," Johnson said. "What he was able to do here tonight, I thought he did an extraordinary job. When the running game's not going, being able to lean into the passing game as a play caller . . . He played really efficient football and I couldn't be more proud of him for that." Keenum started against the Eagles because Caleb Williams is out with a hamstring injury and second-string quarterback Tyson Bagent spent most of the week in the league's concussion protocol. Bagent was active as the Bears' No. 2 quarterback, and Johnson said it's too soon to say whether Bagent will be No. 1 against the Jets. "We'll have a discussion as a coaching staff and we'll see where we need to go from here," Johnson said. "But I said it last week and I'll say it again: There was a reason Tyson ended training camp as our No. 2 quarterback." Johnson said the Bears have three quarterbacks they can win with. "Whether it's Caleb, whether it's Tyson, whether it's Case," Johnson said, "we've got one of the best quarterback rooms in the NFL."
author: Michael David Smith

title: PFT's Week 4 2026 NFL power rankings
summary: There's a new sheriff in town (and they're dressed like 1960s Batman).
full_text: 1. Bills (last week No. 2; 3-0): The Bills are No. 1, but the Adam West Batman uniforms would be No. 32. 2. Chiefs (No. 4; 3-0): The Chiefs are back . . . to playing with their food before winning easily. 3. 49ers (No. 5; 3-0): They're dropping like flies but still winning every week. 4. Broncos (No. 6; 2-1): The Rams let the Broncos hang around just long enough to steal it. 5. author: Mike Florio

title: Report: Bengals to bring back WR Mitchell Tinsley
summary: Wide receiver Mitchell Tinsley played in every game for the Bengals last season and he is reportedly heading back to Cincinnati this week.
full_text: Wide receiver Mitchell Tinsley played in every game for the Bengals last season and he is reportedly heading back to Cincinnati this week. Adam Schefter of ESPN reports that the Bengals will sign Tinsley off of the Texans' practice squad. Tinsley was cut by the Bengals at the end of camp and he signed with the Texans earlier this month. Tinsley started four times for the Bengals last year and finished the season with eight catches for 116 yards and two touchdowns. He also appeared in two games for Washington during the 2023 season. The Bengals put Andrei Iosivas on injured reserve last week, which left Dohnte Myers, Colby Young, and Ke'Shawn Williams as the wideouts behind Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins.
author: Josh Alper

title: Robert Saleh: Cam Ward made a bad decision, but he isn't reckless
summary: After quarterback Cam Ward threw an interception in the end zone late in the fourth quarter of Sunday's 12-7 loss to the Giants, Titans head coach Robert Saleh said that Ward has "to be smarter with the football."
full_text: After quarterback Cam Ward threw an interception in the end zone late in the fourth quarter of Sunday's 12-7 loss to the Giants, Titans head coach Robert Saleh said that Ward has "to be smarter with the football ." Saleh spent more time discussing Ward's decision making during his Monday press conference. Saleh said that he thinks Ward has been "spot on" with his decisions in most respects, which makes it "unfortunate that one of his critical mistakes came on the last play of the game" but does not make Ward a reckless player with the ball. "He gave him a bad ball ," Saleh said, via the team's website. "Bad decision, not a reckless decision, bad decision, which I'm sure he recognizes. But Cam is far from reckless." Recklessness may not be Ward's chief issue, but the simple fact for the Titans is that their offense is not productive enough to overcome even an occasional mistake. They've scored 37 points in three weeks and that number is going to need to climb for Ward to have a compelling case that he's the long-term answer in Tennessee.
author: Josh Alper

title: Jaguars got football from Travis Hunter's first interception after sideline squabble
summary: Jaguars cornerback Travis Hunter's first NFL interception helped Jacksonville beat the Patriots on Sunday, but it also touched off an odd scene on the sideline.
full_text: Jaguars cornerback Travis Hunter's first NFL interception helped Jacksonville beat the Patriots on Sunday, but it also touched off an odd scene on the sideline. Hunter spun the ball on the ground while celebrating the takeaway and teammate Josh Hines-Allen tried to retrieve it as a souvenir from a Patriots ballboy who had picked it up. Video of the interaction showed Hines-Allen trying to take the ball, which was zealously protected by the ballboy who shouted that Hines-Allen should not touch him. A Jaguars staffer eventually stepped in and the game went on. During a videoconference on Monday, Jaguars head coach Liam Coen said the team was working to get the ball for Hunter. "I was just talking about it ," Coen said, via Mark Long of the Associated Press. "I haven't gotten a clean answer. We've been in communication with those guys over there. I think they've gotten it sorted out; I can't say for certain if we got the actual ball or not. I know there was something that went on there. I think it's all squared away. We'll get it taken care of." Cornerback Jourdan Lewis noted that Hunter "could have helped us out by not spinning the ball and forgetting about it," but the Jaguars later confirmed that they were able to secure the ball.
author: Josh Alper

title: Buccaneers WR Jalen McMillan is expected to miss 6-8 weeks with knee injury
summary: Quarterback Baker Mayfield's dislocated thumb was the headline news for the Buccaneers on the injury front in Week 3, but he isn't the only offensive player set to miss time.
full_text: Quarterback Baker Mayfield's dislocated thumb was the headline news for the Buccaneers on the injury front in Week 3, but he isn't the only offensive player set to miss time. Wide receiver Jalen McMillan left Tampa's 23-16 loss to the Vikings with a left knee injury. Per multiple reports, McMillan will miss 6-8 weeks after suffering a PCL injury. McMillan initially hurt his knee over the summer and this is an aggravation of the previous injury. McMillan had eight touchdown catches as a rookie in 2024, but he was limited to four games by a neck injury last year and hopes that he'd return to an impactful role in the offense this year have taken a major hit.
author: Josh Alper

title: Kevin O'Connell: We're going to improve, ascend as an offense
summary: The Vikings are 3-0, but it isn't because they have found an offensive groove so far this season.
full_text: The Vikings are 3-0, but it isn't because they have found an offensive groove so far this season. In three weeks of work, they have managed to pick up a league-worst 715 yards and their passing game has been the least productive in the league. That didn't stop them from trading quarterback J.J. McCarthy to the Giants on Monday and head coach Kevin O'Connell expressed confidence later in the day that starter Kyler Murray will be able to create better results with more time in the offense. "Look, we've seen Kyler play 11 snaps in one game and played against a good defense on the road yesterday. There's a lot of things beyond Kyler that we need to improve, including myself, and we're going to do that, and we're going to ascend as an offense ," O'Connell said, via the team's website. "I believe in our guys. I believe in where we can get to as a team, and I just love the fact that collectively we're able to come together and find a way to win football games." Things got particularly bleak for the Vikings in the second half in Tampa on Sunday as they gained 77 yards and picked up four first downs while turning the ball over once and punting four times. A game against the winless Dolphins this week gives the Vikings a chance to find some better footing and questions about when that will happen will get a bit more pointed if they continue to scuffle the way they did against the Buccaneers.
author: Josh Alper

title: Eagles defense has to "get on the same page" after loss to Bears
summary: When the Eagles faced the Bears in 2025, they gave up 281 rushing yards in a Black Friday loss.
full_text: When the Eagles faced the Bears in 2025, they gave up 281 rushing yards in a Black Friday loss. The Eagles had more success against the Chicago rushing attack on Monday night, but the result wasn't any better. Bears third-string quarterback Case Keenum was never sacked and rarely pressured while going 24-of-34 for 247 yards and two touchdowns in his first start since the 2023 season. Missed tackles were an issue somewhat obscured by wins in the first two weeks of the season and that remained a problem for a defense that has yet to force a turnover this season. Add that to breakdowns in coverage that led to big plays like a Kalif Raymond touchdown catch and there's a lot for the unit to work on. Defensive back Cooper DeJean chalked that Raymond touchdown up to "miscommunication" and said the defense needs to focus on cleaning that up first. “We just got to get on the same page ,” DeJean said, via Jeff Neiburg of the Philadelphia Inquirer . Week 4 brings a date with the Rams on a short week, so that work will have to begin right away for the Eagles to put themselves on better footing in the future.
author: Josh Alper

title: Nick Sirianni regrets his emotional outburst after hit on Jalen Hurts
summary: Sirianni appeared to be screaming at Bears linebacker D'Marco Jackson, who was flagged for unnecessary roughness.
full_text: Eagles coach Nick Sirianni appeared to be screaming obscenities toward Bears linebacker D'Marco Jackson after a hit on quarterback Jalen Hurts that forced Hurts to leave the game for a concussion evaluation on Monday night. Afterward, Sirianni regretted it. Sirianni said after the Eagles' 27-7 loss to the Bears that he doesn't think Jackson, who was flagged for unnecessary roughness, was trying to make a dirty play. "You want to always fight for your players and protect your players," Sirianni said. "I always come away when I have a moment like that with remorse. 'Man, I shouldn't have let my emotions get the best of me.' Those guys are out there trying to make a play. It was close on the sideline. It ended up being a penalty, obviously you never want to see your quarterback get hit like that. But it's in the heat of the moment, I know nobody is trying to hurt anybody out there, and I always have remorse when I act that way. But I always love fighting for our players. I love our guys. So the emotion of the game probably got the better of me today and I have to learn from that. In that particular moment I have to be more steady in that situation. Be able to move on and go to the next play. I didn't like how I handled that." Sirianni was critical of himself in his post-game comments, saying he got out-coached. After the Eagles' first loss, Sirianni has some things he needs to work on.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Bears' Ben Johnson takes playful shot at his former quarterback Jared Goff
summary: Johnson discussed the difference in preparing for a mobile vs. non-mobile quarterback
full_text:
Chicago Bears head coach Ben Johnson has made it clear, once again, that he doesn't think Jared Goff is the most mobile quarterback out there. Without much prompting on Monday, Johnson took a friendly jab at his former quarterback, whom he worked with as the offensive coordinator for the Detroit Lions from 2022 to 2024.
On 'Monday Night Football,' Johnson was given the challenge of defeating the Philadelphia Eagles with Bears quarterback Caleb Williams , who was sidelined with a hamstring strain. Instead, he had Case Keenum , a quarterback who hasn't played in 1,009 days. But with Johnson's help, he finished with 247 yards, two touchdowns, and no interceptions in the 27-7 victory.
After the game, Johnson seemed to take a shot at Goff. When asked how he prepares for a quarterback who stays in the pocket more than one who can run with the ball often, Johnson said , smiling, "Well, I've got a little history with that, of calling plays for someone not so mobile."
No one is arguing that Goff is the greatest rushing quarterback, but it's notable that this is the second time Johnson has called the Lions star out for it.
In 2025, Johnson seemingly took a shot at Goff when complimenting Williams' mobility, but later said his comments got skewed. Johnson said at the time that he spoke to Goff about it and explained it was merely meant to compliment Williams, not diss anyone.
Goff certainly isn't able to take off quite like some other quarterbacks in the league, including Williams. Over his 11-year career, Goff has 611 rushing yards, with a career-high of 108 in a single season. Williams has 984 yards in two seasons, plus the two games played this year, with a career high of 489 yards in a season, coming in his rookie year. Keenum had six rushing yards on four attempts on Monday night and has 457 total yards on the ground in his 12-year career.
Johnson's comment also may be a callout for anyone who says Johnson can't win without a top quarterback or a quarterback with a certain scheme.
"Now, I don't have a history with someone that's not a number one pick though," Johnson continued. "So that was apparently a big deal."
Johnson was named the Lions OC in 2022, one year after Goff joined the team. He became the head coach of the Bears in 2025, one year after Williams was drafted, so he's only known first-overall picks. Goff was the No. 1 pick in 2016, and Williams was the No. 1 pick in 2024. Keenum, however, went undrafted in 2012.
In his first season with Chicago, the Bears went 11-6, winning the NFC North. The Bears are now 2-1 and will face the 1-2 New York Jets next week.
author: Shanna McCarriston

title: Who's to blame for Eagles' embarrassing loss to Bears? Jalen Hurts bears big responsibility but not all
summary: Let's play the Eagles blame game after a disastrous loss in Chicago
full_text:
The Eagles ' 27-7 loss to the Bears wasn't just an upset defeat. It was an embarrassment on the national stage. A team facing a third-string quarterback got outclassed in every single aspect: coaching, execution, preparation, offense, defense, poise, discipline, decision-making and quite literally anything and everything else that goes into a football game.
Among the questions to ask: Why were the Eagles so bad? Why is the offense seemingly stuck in the mud? Why did the defense get carved up by Case Keenum ? Why did it take so long for the team to show signs of life in both halves? Why was Jalen Hurts so bad, and why did Saquon Barkley go invisible? Why did the team commit 10 penalties?
It's important to recognize this is one game of 17. The Eagles entered 2-0, and while it hadn't been pretty in either of the first two weeks, wins are wins. The sky isn't falling in Philadelphia. Well, let me revise that: The sky shouldn't be falling in Philadelphia, but those fans have zero patience even when the team is winning. When they're losing? It turns quickly.
So who deserves the most blame for such a poor showing? Let's share the worst pie in the world: the blame pie.
Give Sirianni at least a little credit after the game: He didn't hide.
"It was a true team loss," he said. "And when it's a true team loss, I have to look at myself first. We weren't ready to coach. We weren't ready to play. And that ultimately starts and  ends with me. Again, it's my responsibility. Every product, everything that's on that field is my responsibility. I didn't do a good enough job."
He's right. He failed the team on many occasions. When Hurts had to go to the medical tent, Sirianni absolutely lost his mind. He directed his anger in many directions, including at a Bears player . He expressed remorse for that after the game.
By the way, Eagles fans might be upset with Hurts having to leave in a crucial moment and Andy Dalton coming in and throwing an interception. But even Sirianni admitted that's just doctors doing their job. No external forces made the Eagles get stuffed near the goal line or made Dalton make a horrible throw.
Perhaps the best thing a coach can be — more than an X's and O's genius, a great motivator, a great decision maker or a great in-game adjuster — is a leader. Someone who is calm in the face of adversity. Sirianni failed there.
He also failed on two fourth-down decisions, punting on a fourth-and-1 near midfield but going for a fourth-and-5 just a few yards further up the field on the next drive. Again, Sirianni regretted it after the game.
Sirianni's team was undisciplined, too, racking up 10 penalties. That's at least somewhat his fault. They sleepwalked to start both halves. And finally, as a non-play-calling, CEO-type head coach, Sirianni bears responsibility for making the right hires at coordinator. Right now, Sean Mannion and Hurts are not meshing at all. Speaking of that duo ...
I went back and watched all 30 of Hurts' dropbacks, and there were several frustrating moments. The biggest issue here, fundamentally, is that Hurts isn't a super anticipatory thrower, especially over the middle of the field. There were multiple opportunities to attack this area, including once when both DeVonta Smith and Makai Lemon beat their cornerbacks off the line. The play gets disrupted somewhat when Barkley gets run over in protection, but Hurts actually avoided the initial pressure. He went into play extension/scramble mode immediately thereafter, though. If he had hung onto this passing concept for just a hair longer, the Eagles might have had a big play.
Early in the game, Hurts was pretty clean — a blitzer broke through, but not until after Hurts had thrown the ball — and he left a dump-off for Barkley about 5 yards short. This also could have been a big gainer, and Barkley knew it.
Hurts was 4-for-10 for 23 yards when pressured. That's not good.
The Mannion-Hurts duo's weaknesses are clear. Mannion came from Green Bay, where Jordan Love is one of the most anticipatory throwers in the NFL . He's not afraid to take these deep, middle-field shots before they're technically open. Hurts isn't there yet.
As I said above, Hurts missed some opportunities. But Mannion didn't do a great job of helping him out, either. On Hurts' second pass, for example, he does one half of the play right: A screen for Barkley is available if Hurts can access it. The problem? He has backup tight end E.J. Jenkins coming all the way across the formation and trying to block Montez Sweat , which is never going to happen.
Hurts gets sped up. One could put a little bit of blame on Hurts here — if he maneuvers to his left and throws to Barkley, a big play is available. But Hurts has always been a quarterback who can get antsy when pressured. He throws the ball nowhere near Barkley and gets called for grounding. It's a bad play by Hurts and an iffy play design by Mannion.
The Eagles' short passing game really was a mess, and it has been all season. Hurts is 12-for-21 for 6 yards — 6 YARDS!!! — on throws behind the line of scrimmage this year.  That's 0.3 yards per attempt, by far the worst in the NFL.
Mannion deserves more blame for Barkley disappearing in the second half after 11 carries for 73 yards (6.6 per pop) in the first half. Yes, the Eagles were down, but not so far down that Barkley manages just four carries for 9 yards in the second half.
Oh yeah, and there were five offensive penalties, including three pre-snap. Gross. Right now, the Eagles are 27th in offensive success rate.
Mannion has lots of hard questions and few easy answers.
And here's where it all comes together. The offensive line is a mess. After Landon Dickerson landed on IR, the Eagles moved Cam Jurgens from center to Dickerson's left guard spot. The results have been bad.
Here are the two plays that can best describe what the Eagles' offense is dealing with right now: a combination of quarterback, play-caller, and offensive line issues. The fact that they're both plays involving the same defender and the same offensive lineman makes it all the more alarming.
T.J. Edwards PBU and pick. Dude was all over the place last night. pic.twitter.com/085F16bew6
In the first, T.J. Edwards (53) blitzes and then drops, and Jurgens isn't quick enough to get back to Booker (94). Edwards nearly ends up with a pick; Hurts gets hit by a free runner. I didn't love the play call here with both receivers on the right side basically not involved.
In the second, Hurts changes the play. Jurgens gets blown back by Booker, and Hurts is locked on Smith the entire time, completely ignoring an open Lemon at the bottom of the screen. Edwards gets his pick.
On both plays, Jurgens gets beat. He allowed five hurries on the night. Lane Johnson allowed two, and Tyler Steen allowed one. Steen also had a brutal, unnecessary holding call that wiped out a 19-yard Barkley run. Johnson had a holding call on the play where Hurts got hit late, offsetting what would have been a personal foul on Chicago.
Johnson finished tied 24th in PFF's tackle ratings in pass protection this week; Jordan Mailata was 27th. That's below their high standard. Jurgens finished 71st out of 76 guards in pass pro rankings this week. Changes should be coming.
This may seem low, but really, the defense wasn't nearly as bad as it's been made out to be. It stopped the run. It allowed zero points when a Tank Bigsby fumble set the Bears up at the Chicago 15-yard line. Yes, the Bears finished with 27 points, but they went just 2-for-5 in the red zone. This defensive effort was good enough to win this game, or at least keep it close. We cannot say the same about the offense.
Still, zero sacks and zero turnovers against Keenum is ghastly. Keenum was 11-for-12 for 128 yards on play action. He was 10-for-11 for 136 yards and a touchdown against the blitz. Vic Fangio seemed intent on stopping the run after Chicago rolled up 281 yards on the ground against Philadelphia last year, and the Eagles did…
author: Zachary Pereles

title: Ravens facing unexpected crisis at key offensive position heading into Week 4 game vs. Titans
summary: The Ravens might need to start making some phone calls to fill this position
full_text:
The Baltimore Ravens went down to Brazil and beat the Dallas Cowboys in a wild game on Sunday, but that 34-31 victory came at a huge cost. The Ravens lost two centers to injury, and now they have exactly zero centers on their roster.
Jovaughn Gwyn went into the game as the starting center, but he went down with an ankle injury in the second half. With Gwyn out, Ethan Pocic stepped in, but he wasn't on the field for long. Pocic suffered a knee injury, which knocked him out of the game as well.
At that point, the Ravens were out of centers, so they had to reshuffle their offensive line to make things work. The team made the decision to have rookie Vega Ioane make the shift from right guard to center, but that move left a gaping hole at right guard that was eventually filled by Andrew Vorhees .
If the Ravens knew they were going to get Gwyn or Pocic back on the field this week, then the center problem would simply fix itself, because they would roll with one of those guys on Sunday against the Titans . However, they can't do that, because both guys are expected to be out for awhile, according to coach Jesse Minter.
"I don't have the full details, but they both look like they'll be a little bit long term," Minter said Monday, via the team's website .
With both players expected to be out "long term," that puts the Ravens in somewhat of a bind.
After watching Ioane play a solid game against the Cowboys, it sounds like the Ravens are going to keep him at center, at least for this week's game against Tennessee.
"As we sort through making our roster better over the next couple of days, he'll prepare to play that position," Minter said. "We'll figure out the best five guys to put out there for this particular week. We may add a piece or two from losing a couple of guys."
Ioane, who was the 14th overall pick in the draft this year, was an All-America offensive lineman at Penn State, but he played less than 20 snaps at center during his four-year college career. Ioane did take a few practice snaps at center over the past few weeks, so he wasn't completely in the dark when he was for forced to play the position against Dallas.
"A big mindset from college too, our O-line coach was always talking about, 'Be ready for when your number's called,'" Ioane said follwing the win, via The Athletic . "It's unfortunate how it happened, but you just got to step up and be ready for the moment."
Putting Ioane at center this week is certainly a short-term solution, but that will still leave the Ravens looking for a longer-term fix to the problem.
The Ravens have a center for Week 4 in Ioane, but it will be interesting to see how they handle things going forward. If Ioane plays well, then they could keep him at center as long as they're comfortable with who they have at right guard. Vorhees would seem to have the upper-hand to play right guard, but the Ravens do also have Emery Jones Jr. , who could potentially serve as the starter.
If the Ravens want to add a free agent, they could call Kevin Zeitler . The former Pro Bowl guard is open to playing this year, but only for a contender, according to Sports Illustrated . Not only do the Ravens meet that criteria, but Zeitler has a history with the team because he spent three seasons in Baltimore (2021-23).
Adding a guard in free agency would probably make a lot more sense than adding a center and that's mostly because there aren't really any quality centers available in free agency, or really, even to trade for.
It was a rough offseason for center depth: The Bears lost their starter ( Drew Dalman ) to retirement, the Chargers lost their starter ( Tyler Biadasz ) to a season-ending injury and the Lions lost their starter ( Cade Mays ) to a broken wrist that will likely sideline him until after Detroit's Week 6 bye . Basically, most teams likely won't be interested in parting ways with any center depth they have, which is why it would make more sense for the Ravens to sign a guard like Zeitler while keeping Ioane at center until either Gwyn or Pocic can return.
For Baltimore, the center position has been plagued by injuries this year. During training camp, they held a competition to see who would replace Tyler Linderbaum , who signed with the Raiders back in March. Danny Pinter appeared on track to win the job, but he tore his patellar tendon during camp, an injury that knocked him out for the season. At that point Gwyn ended up beating out Pocic for the starting job, but now they're both out, which leaves the Ravens with no experienced centers on the roster.
Baltimore did have center Corey Bullock in training camp, but he got released and although the team was hoping to stash him on their practice squad, he got claimed on waivers by the Panthers .
"Once we lost Danny, we were kind of down to two," Minter said. "You always want to have that third guy, particularly when one of the guys we were going to potentially keep on practice squad got claimed. Now, you're trying to create depth at that position. Credit to (Ioane). He went in there at a couple of critical moments of the game and our offense scored a go-ahead touchdown and obviously operating on that last drive."
Lamar Jackson is the star of the Ravens' offense, but right now, Baltimore needs to find someone who can snap him the ball. For this week, that will be Ioane, but it will be interesting to see what Minter decides to do going forward.
author: John Breech

author: Owen OBrien

title: Return of the feature back: Why NFL running backs are making a massive comeback
summary: Several factors are helping fuel a major resurgence for ground attacks across the league
full_text:
From Walter Payton to Emmitt Smith to Adrian Peterson to Derrick Henry , the NFL has always had prominent names at running back, but the depth of the position is cyclical. When the league was experiencing a higher volume of 4,000-yard passers, the number of running backs exceeding 1,000 rushing yards fell. But the tide may be turning and embracing the feature back once again.
Over the last four years, the league has averaged 15 rushers exceeding 1,000 rushing yards each season. The previous five years saw just 9.6 rushers accomplish that feat each year. The numbers are obviously slightly boosted over the last four seasons due to the implementation of a 17-game schedule. But there are 18 on pace for 1,000 rushing yards this season, with a handful of others, including Saquon Barkley, close. The usual suspects are among that group, but so too are the likes of Kyle Monangai , Bhayshul Tuten and Cam Skattebo .
CBS Sports' Pete Prisco wrote a story in September about the passing game diminishing over the last decade. Some of the reasoning applied in that article also translates to the run game. Before diving into the change and why it helps the run game flourish, let's look at the raw data.
All data is from TruMedia and is based on the regular season
Through Week 3 of the 2026 NFL regular season, teams are averaging 61.5 offensive plays per game. The average had been 63.1 over the past decade. When slicing the pie, designed quarterback runs have dropped precipitously each of the past five years. Quarterbacks like Lamar Jackson are still effectively scrambling, but those opportunities and more are being funneled to running backs. Last season's pass attempts per team (545.0) was the lowest over the last decade. With the exception of the 2023 season, the percentage of run plays has risen every year since 2019.
As Prisco discussed, disciples of Eagles defensive coordinator Vic Fangio have pervaded the league and spread the two high safety look, which limits explosive plays in the passing game. The number of explosive plays last season was the lowest since 2017. Defenses are content to give up small gains, expecting offenses to grow impatient and make a mistake pushing the ball downfield.
If the opposition puts fewer or lighter players in the box, then running the football is an effective counter.
Offensive line play and creative defensive formations
For quite some time, there has been a narrative that there are not enough quality offensive tackles in the NFL. The institution of the transfer portal and NIL, which encourages players to change colleges, has had a two-fold impact on the unit in the pros. In some cases, a change of scenery exposes some players  to more resources and better coaching. In other cases, a lack of continuity may impede a lineman's development.
Prisco also wrote how defensive coaches, such as Jesse Minter, Mike Macdonald and Brian Flores, have done a great job giving the opposition exotic pre- and post-snap looks. NFL teams have had a greater willingness to transition a lineman from the position they played in college to a new one in the NFL, which I wrote about in 2025 . As a result, little details like communicating and handling those aforementioned twists and stunts by the defensive line can often get lost in translation.
Running the football is one way to mitigate those communication issues. Leaning on the defense in the run game is often more natural for linemen than asking them to hold up against more athletic pass rushers.
Improved starting field position and the rise of the kicker with a leg cannon
The new kickoff rules instituted in 2024 have led to improved average starting field position, with the average field position being 30.2 yards or greater since the rules took effect. It had never reached the 29-yard line over the prior decade.
Meanwhile, the number of made field goal attempts of 50+ yards has exploded. On average, there have been 172.5 such kicks over the last four years. Before then, there had never been more than 120 in a season dating back to 2016. The league is on pace for 198 made attempts from 50+ yards this season.
Between the improved starting field position and the success of kickers from 50+ yards, an offense may need less than 37 yards to be in field goal range. Offenses are incentivized to take those small incremental gains as opposed to hunting the big plays.
Lighter defensive personnel
For years, defenses had incorporated lighter personnel to combat the spread nature of the NFL pass game. Teams were taking a third linebacker off the field in favor of a nickel defensive back. There has been a higher volume of sub-250-pound edge rushers and sub-250-pound rushers, in general. With less mass in the box, heavier offensive personnel can move bodies around in the run game.
One of the more overly-discussed NFL trends this offseason was the usage of two-plus tight ends. The league utilized two-plus tight ends on 33.2% of offensive snaps last season -- a full 3% higher than the previous 10-year high set in 2024. Through three weeks in 2026, that number is even higher (35.1%).
Fourth down aggressiveness has risen
From the COVID season through the 2025 season, NFL teams went for it on 4th down 20.3% of the time. Over the prior four years, dating to 2016, the average was 14.1%. The evidence is circumstantial for distance, stage of the game, offensive effectiveness, etc., but it usually evens out over the course of the season. Although this year's average is lower through Week 3, it is still significantly higher than the pre-COVID timeframe.
Why is this relevant? Teams have an additional down to achieve 10 yards for a first down. A team must average 2.5 yards per play as opposed to 3.33 yards, which opens the door to more rush opportunities. In the past, a third-and-7 may have been an obvious passing situation, but if a team knows it's going for it on 4th down, then running the football on third down to open the playbook is a consideration.
For quite some time, the running back position had been devalued. Prominent players at the position met to strategize contract objectives when some teams employed the strategy of not extending a running back after the player's rookie contract, franchising the player to maintain control for an additional year or short-changing the player in long-term negotiations. As a result, teams often favored players at more premium positions early in the NFL Draft , because it was more likely that player would sign a second contract with the team. There was greater value in having an elite performer at wide receiver, edge rusher or offensive tackle. For example, the franchise tag rate, which weighs the 10 highest-paid players at each position, for a wide receiver is roughly $27.3 million this season, whereas the running back number is roughly $14.3 million.
What could recent trends do for the value of the running back position? Teams have always shown a willingness to take a running back early in the draft if the talent is there. Arizona selected Jeremiyah Love No. 3 overall in the 2026 NFL Draft. Teams have also been more willing to extend running backs recently, but the average annual salary still lags behind other positions -- a fact that likely will not change until the average career expectancy gives teams more confidence in offering those long-term deals. Players like Saquon Barkley reaching free agency is good for the earnings potential of the position.

title: Eagles coach Nick Sirianni expresses remorse for shouting expletive at Bears player for hit on Jalen Hurts
summary: Sirianni said he let the emotions get the best of him
full_text:
Midway through the second quarter of the Philadelphia Eagles ' embarrassing 27-7 "Monday Night Football" loss to the Chicago Bears , quarterback Jalen Hurts dropped back to pass, saw pressure in his face and scrambled toward the sideline in an effort to pick up the first down. Just as Hurts was reaching both the line to gain and the sideline, Bears linebacker D'Marco Jackson laid him out with a massive hit.
JALEN HURTS TAKES A BRUTAL LATE HIT 😳 Hurts stays down for a while after the contact, and Philadelphia immediately checks on its quarterback. pic.twitter.com/5ayRay5fsO
Jackson was flagged for a personal foul for the late hit, which offset a holding penalty on the Eagles. Hurts was pulled from the game to get checked for a concussion (he was cleared and later returned), and backup quarterback Andy Dalton ended up throwing an interception on the drive.
But before that happened, Eagles coach Nick Sirianni was enraged by what he felt was a brutally late hit on Hurts (replays showed Jackson actually hit Hurts just as his toe stepped on the sideline, but watching the play live it definitely looked like a dirty hit), and he let Jackson know about it. Cameras caught Sirianni screaming at Jackson, "You're a p---y!"
Nick Sirianni: “You’re 🫵🏼 a pu$$y” pic.twitter.com/Y0twfCSM2Y
After the game, Sirianni expressed remorse for his actions in the heat of the moment.
"Obviously, you want to always fight for your players, and protect your players," Sirianni said. "I always come away when I have a moment like that with remorse of, 'Man, I shouldn't have let my emotions get the best of me.'"
Sirianni also acknowledged that the hit was closer than it may have initially looked, and still felt that he acted in a way that wasn't appropriate for the situation.
"Those guys are out there trying to make a play. It was close on the sideline, ended up being a penalty," Sirianni said. "Obviously, you never want to see your quarterback get hit like that, but it's in the heat of the moment. I know nobody is trying to hurt anybody out there, and I always have remorse when I act that way. But I always love fighting for our players. I love our guys.
"The emotion of the game probably got the better of me and I have to learn from that. I have to be more steady in that situation, be able to -- like I say to the guys -- be able to move on and go to the next play. I didn't like how I handled that."

title: NFL Week 4 injury panic meter: Updates on Baker Mayfield, Justin Jefferson and more
summary: A look at some of the biggest injuries from around the NFL
full_text:
Injuries are unfortunately a part of football, and all 32 NFL teams have been affected to some degree. We've seen starting quarterbacks such as Jaxson Dart , Jayden Daniels and Caleb Williams go down with different ailments, Los Angeles Rams star wideout Puka Nacua has already missed two out of three games due to a nagging hip/groin issue, while Indianapolis Colts wideout Alec Pierce was placed on injured reserve with his heel injury.
We saw even more notable players go down with injuries in Week 3 -- some of them unfortunately season-ending. Now that the dust has settled, let's take a look at some of the most recent medical updates from around the league, and examine if fans should be panicking or not.
The Miami Dolphins were expected to be one of the worst teams in the NFL this year, but they now have lost their best player in star running back De'Von Achane . He tore his ACL during the 24-10 loss to the Kansas City Chiefs on Sunday, meaning Malik Willis will have to lean on Ollie Gordon II and Jaylen Wright moving forward.
The Dolphins are statistically one of the worst offenses in the NFL, averaging 290.7 total yards per game. In his three games played, Achane turned 41 touches into 176 yards and zero touchdowns. Miami actually just became the first team since 2021 to not hold a lead through three games, and the first team to lose each of its first three games by 14+ points since the ... Dolphins in 2019.
Tampa Bay Buccaneers quarterback Baker Mayfield dislocated the thumb on his throwing hand at the end of the Week 3 loss to the Minnesota Vikings . He was seen writhing on the ground in pain and heard screaming as he grasped at his right hand. Mayfield eventually walked off the field with trainers and went straight to the locker room.
The MRI Mayfield had on Monday revealed there was no fracture, no ligament nor tendon damage, per ESPN , and Todd Bowles said he's expected to miss three weeks.
Missing three games is more ideal than missing the rest of the season, but the Bucs are in the danger zone. This is their first 0-3 start since 2014, and Mayfield's backup is undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels . Just an absolute nightmare start for the Bucs, and it's fair to hypothesize that Bowles is on the hot seat.
The New York Giants already lost quarterback Jaxson Dart for the rest of the season, and now, they will be without one of their stars on the other side of the ball.
Pass rusher Brian Burns suffered a torn ACL during the Week 3 victory over the Tennessee Titans , meaning Kayvon Thibodeaux will be asked to pick up the slack. Or, maybe rookie Arvell Reese sees some snaps on the edge. Burns racked up a career-high 16.5 sacks last season.
What's more frustrating than losing a star player for the rest of the year is that Burns probably shouldn't have been playing. He didn't practice all week due to an ankle injury, but fought to suit up on the soggy Meadowland turf Sunday. Now, he's forced to shift his focus to 2027.
New York Jets running back Breece Hall injured his right quad in the fourth quarter against the Detroit Lions , and is considered week to week, per ESPN . Hall rushed for 102 yards and a touchdown in the season-opening win vs. Tennessee, but hasn't crossed 33 rushing yards since.
Hall is still an important piece of this Jets offense, so it's good news he won't miss much time. Braelon Allen and Isaiah Davis are the backups.
Vikings wideout Justin Jefferson suffered an ankle sprain during Sunday's win over the Bucs, and he's going to be just fine. There's even a chance he plays this week vs. the 0-3 Dolphins.
"He avoided anything long term. It's just going to be about progressing throughout the week and where we can get him to from a standpoint of getting the swelling out and then what kind of work week he can have," Vikings head coach Kevin O'Connell told reporters, per ESPN . "But I was very encouraged to get that news today."
San Francisco 49ers wideout Mike Evans left Sunday's win vs. the Arizona Cardinals with a rib strain. NFL Media reports he's day to day.
The future Hall of Famer has caught 12 passes for 137 yards and two touchdowns in three games played for his new team.
Las Vegas Raiders wide receiver Jack Bech broke his forearm in the win vs. the New Orleans Saints , but NFL Media reports he could return later this season.
The second-year pass-catcher has caught just five passes for 48 yards and one touchdown this season, but his injury is a hit to one of the weakest wide receiver rooms in the NFL. Tre Tucker leads the team in receiving with 189 yards. The next leading wide receiver is Jalen Nailor , who has 52 yards receiving through three games.
Saints running back Travis Etienne Jr. suffered a hamstring injury vs. the Raiders, and head coach Kellen Moore said he's going to miss some time. How much time remains to be seen. We don't have much clarity there.
Etienne is the Saints' RB1, but they do have Alvin Kamara and Kendre Miller as well. Despite the four-year, $48 million deal he signed this offseason, Etienne has averaged fewer than 60 scrimmage yards per game. You'd rather have him in the lineup, but Chris Olave , Juwan Johnson and Devaughn Vele are the ones carrying the Saints' offense right now with Tyler Shough .
Washington Commanders linebacker Leo Chenal underwent season-ending neck surgery on Monday after being carted off the field during the Week 3 win against the Seattle Seahawks .
Chenal was starting alongside rookie Sonny Styles in place of Frankie Luvu , who has been out with a groin issue. This unit is pretty thin right now. With that said, Kain Medrano did have a pick six of Sam Darnold on Sunday!
The Baltimore Ravens earned a wild victory over the Dallas Cowboys in Brazil on Sunday, but they suffered a few notable losses as well. Starting center Jovaughn Gwyn was carted off with an ankle injury, and his replacement, Ethan Pocic , suffered a knee injury. Head coach Jesse Minter said both are going to miss some time. All this comes after the team lost Danny Pinter in training camp.
It looks like first-round pick Vega Ioane is going to move from right guard to center, and then Andrew Vorhees or Emery Jones Jr . will start at right guard.
Sunday was disastrous for the Carolina Panthers . Not only did they lose to the Cleveland Browns , but Pro Bowl cornerback Jaycee Horn suffered a "significant quad injury," while Mike Jackson suffered a groin injury. These are the Panthers' top two cornerbacks, who headlined a room that has zero depth. Losing both for even a few games is very concerning -- especially when you consider that this is statistically one of the worst defenses in the NFL.
The Panthers will now look at rookie Will Lee III , Akayleb Evans and Chau Smith-Wade . Corey Thornton , DeVonta Smith and Zion Childress are on the practice squad.
There's a surprising bright spot on the 0-3 Titans, and that's the play of the offensive line. Tennessee has famously boasted some horrific offensive lines over the past few years, but that's not the case this season. However, there's some concern at the right guard spot now.
Rookie Fernando Carmona came in and grabbed the starting right guard spot in training camp. He left the Week 3 matchup against the Giants early with an ankle sprain, and will miss a few weeks, per Jordan Schultz . What's worse is that backup Jackson Slater suffered a "significant" foot injury on Sunday as well. That could throw Atonio Mafi or rookie Pat Coogan into the starting lineup.
Cam Ward is struggling behind a decent offensive line. What's it going to look like if this unit starts to crumble?
