title: Winners and losers from the Ravens’ Week 3 win over the Cowboys
summary: With just seven seconds left in a tied game against the Cowboys, Lamar Jackson delivered a missile to Zay Flowers for a 27-yard gain, leading to a walk-off 56-yard field goal for Tyler Loop to send the Ravens home victorious from Brazil. Winners Tyler Loop: Nobody has been under more scrutiny than Loop in Baltimore […]
full_text: RIO DE JANEIRO, BRAZIL - SEPTEMBER 27: Tyler Loop #33 of the Baltimore Ravens runs off the field after defeating the Dallas Cowboys at Maracana Stadium on September 27, 2026 in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil. (Photo by Buda Mendes/Getty Images) | Getty Images With just seven seconds left in a tied game against the Cowboys, Lamar Jackson delivered a missile to Zay Flowers for a 27-yard gain, leading to a walk-off 56-yard field goal for Tyler Loop to send the Ravens home victorious from Brazil. Winners Tyler Loop: Nobody has been under more scrutiny than Loop in Baltimore since missing a game-deciding kick against the Steelers that would have sent the Ravens to the playoffs last season. The second-year kicker’s moment for redemption presented itself on Sunday in Brazil against Dallas. With just one second on the clock after Jackson’s pass to Flowers, Loop nailed a 56-yard field goal to win the game. Loop finished 2/2 on field goals and 4/4 on extra points against the Cowboys. Lamar Jackson: The Ravens’ superstar quarterback came up big in multiple moments against Dallas. Jackson hit rookie tight end Matthew Hibner for a touchdown to take a three-point lead with a minute and a half left to play. After the Cowboys marched down the field to tie the game, Jackson took the field with just seven seconds left, finding Flowers for a 27-yard pickup and quickly calling a timeout to keep one second on the clock for Loop’s field goal. Jackson finished the day with just five incompletions and two touchdowns. Zay Flowers: It was unknown if Flowers would play in Week 3 with a lingering hamstring injury, but Baltimore likely would not have won without their top receiver. Flowers showed how important he is to the offense, leading the team with 84 receiving yards and finishing with the clutch catch to set up the game-winning field goal, while playing just 21 snaps on a pitch count. Vega Ioane: The rookie first-round guard was forced over to center after both Jovaugn Gwyn and Ethan Pocic exited the game with injuries. Ioane held his own at the position in the two most important drives of the game for the Ravens’ offense. Whether Ioane will remain at center if both Gwyn and Pocic miss extended time remains to be seen. Carson Vinson: Baltimore entered the game without their starting left tackle Ronnie Stanley, leading to Vinson’s first career start in the NFL. The second-year tackle performed admirably protecting Jackson’s blindside, allowing zero pressures throughout the game, according to PFF. Derrick Henry: Henry found the end zone twice on Sunday while rushing for 89 yards on 26 carries. His two touchdowns moved him past Ray Rice for the second-most rushing touchdowns in franchise history, trailing only Jamal Lewis. Henry also passed Eric Dickerson to become the ninth all-time leading rusher in NFL history with 13,356 rushing yards. Justice Hill: Hill provided a nice change of pace from Henry against Dallas, rushing for 33 yards on five carries. Hill’s burst was apparent on several carries, most notably on his longest run of 11 yards, where he would have scored if he were able to keep his balance and stay in bounds after turning the edge. Chris Moore: Moore rebounded from a poor game a week ago to catch Jackson’s first touchdown pass against the Cowboys. Matthew Hibner: The rookie tight end’s first touchdown catch came in a massive moment to give the Ravens the lead near the end of the game. Hibner finished the game with 23 yards to go with his touchdown on two catches. Nnamdi Madubuike: Madubuike’s return to the field for the first time in a year from a potentially career-ending neck injury makes him a winner regardless of what he actually did on the field in Brazil. Madubuike played 47 snaps in his first game back and had two pressures, according to PFF. Keondre Jackson: Jackson has made play after play on special teams since joining the team as an undrafted free agent in 2025 and made another massive one against Dallas with a blocked field goal. Jackson’s play ultimately made the difference in a game won by three points. Nate Wiggins: Wiggins had a tough matchup against CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens, but with the game on the line, Baltimore’s top corner stood his ground. Wiggins was the victim of a controversial pass interference call against Lamb in the end zone on the Cowboys’ final drive that led to a fresh set of downs for Dallas at the two-yard line. Wiggins was targeted on the very next play while guarding Pickens in the corner of the end zone but was in position to force an incompletion. The Cowboys had to settle for a field goal after failing to get into the end zone on the next two plays. Kyle Hamilton: Hamilton shows every week why he is considered one of the best players in the NFL. He had two pass breakups to go with eight tackles, including two tackles for loss against Dallas. Hamilton continues to be the ultimate chess piece on defense, aligning at all three levels of the field throughout the game. Trenton Simpson: Simpson continued his strong start to his contract season in Week 3 with seven total tackles and two tackles for loss. Simpson’s downhill ability has been on full display through the first three weeks of the season, routinely defeating blocks with violence and making tackles for little or no gain. Calais Campbell: The 40-year-old defensive lineman led the team with six pressures in Week 3, according to PFF. Campbell showed that he still has juice as he regularly found himself closing in on Prescott in the backfield. Losers John Simpson: Simpson had a rough outing in Week 3, allowing the most pressures on the offensive line with three, according to PFF. The bigger issue for Simpson against the Cowboys was the penalties — something that has been an issue throughout his career — as he was flagged for three false starts. The Ravens need better from their veteran free-agent acquisition. Marlon Humphrey: Like Wiggins, Humphrey had the difficult assignment of guarding Lamb and Pickens. Humphrey had a strong first two games to start the season, but he struggled on Sunday, allowing 95 yards on five catches, all to Lamb and Pickens. Defensive front: While a few individual players in Baltimore’s front seven may have had solid performances, the group as a whole was not at their best against Dallas. The Cowboys rushed for 148 yards. Javonte Williams led the way with 98 yards and a touchdown on 19 carries, averaging 5.2 yards per carry. While it was expected to give up some yards on the ground in order to limit the damage of the deep passing game, the Ravens need to play better up front. The unit also had a difficult time getting to Prescott, sacking him just once on an unblocked blitz by Roquan Smith.
author: Dustin Cox

title: Ravens Snap Count Analysis, Week 3: Nnamdi Madubuike makes season debut, offensive line roulette
summary: Offense Carson Vinson played all 64 snaps in his first start at left tackle, as did four of the other five starters. Injuries at center late in the game threw a wrench into the equation. Jovaughn Gwyn left the game after 46 snaps and Ethan Pocic suffered a knee injury following just 10 plays. That […]
full_text: Football - NFL - Baltimore Ravens v Dallas Cowboys - Estadio Maracana, Rio de Janeiro, Brazil - September 27, 2026 Dallas Cowboys' Javonte Williams in action with Baltimore Ravens' Nnamdi Madubuike and Roquan Smith REUTERS/Sergio Moraes | REUTERS Offense QB: Lamar Jackson 64 RB: Derrick Henry 43, Justice Hill 21 WR: Rashod Bateman 56, Chris Moore 33, Zay Flowers 21, Devontez Walker 17, LaJohntay Wester 11 TE: Durham Smythe 34, Mark Andrews 33, Matthew Hibner 32, Josh Cuevas 16 OL: Carson Vinson 64, Vega Ioane 64, Roger Rosengarten 64, John Simpson 64, Jovaughn Gwyn 46, Ethan Pocic 10, Andrew Vorhees 8, Emery Jones Jr. 3 Carson Vinson played all 64 snaps in his first start at left tackle, as did four of the other five starters. Injuries at center late in the game threw a wrench into the equation. Jovaughn Gwyn left the game after 46 snaps and Ethan Pocic suffered a knee injury following just 10 plays. That forced Vega Ioane to play center for the last handful of offensive plays, which saw Andrew Vorhees plug in at right guard. Emery Jones Jr. also took three snaps. Derrick Henry more than doubled Justice Hill’s snap count (43 to 21) and took a heavy workload with 26 carries. Hill had his most effective game of the year with 33 yards on five carries. At tight end, Durham Smythe had the most snaps with 34 after Mark Andrews was sidelined mid-game with a hand injury. Andrews returned and finished with 33 snaps. Rookies Matthew Hibner and Josh Cuevas each played their highest snap counts of the year and had three combined catches. Hibner caught the go-ahead touchdown in the fourth quarter. Zay Flowers was limited to 21 snaps in his return from injury and still easily led the team in receiving with five catches for 84 yards. Flowers also had 20 rushing yards and fell just a couple yards away from scoring. Rashod Bateman played 56 snaps with two catches, and Chris Moore retained a surprisingly big offensive role (33 snaps). Moore continues to play a lot more than Devontez Walker, who took 17 offensive reps. Defense DL: Nnamdi Madubuike 47, Travis Jones 42, Calais Campbell 32, Broderick Washington 26, John Jenkins 12 EDGE: Tavius Robinson 58, Trey Hendrickson 45, Zion Young 26, Mike Green 22 ILB: Roquan Smith 74, Trenton Simpson 46, Teddye Buchanan 3 CB: Nate Wiggins 69, Marlon Humphrey 64, Chandler Rivers 32, Chidobe Awuzie 15 S: Malaki Starks 73, Kyle Hamilton 67, Jaylinn Hawkins 61 Nnamdi Madubuike made his long-awaited return to action and was not limited in playing time. Madubuike led all defensive linemen with 47 snaps. Calais Campbell’s 32 snaps saw him lead the team in quarterback hits with three in his most impactful game of the year so far. Aeneas Peebles was a healthy scratch instead of Broderick Washington and John Jenkins, who combined to play 38 snaps. Tavius Robinson again paced the edge rusher room (58 snaps), followed by Trey Hendrickson at 45 snaps. Zion Young’s snap count increased again and he out-snapped Mike Green 26 to 22. At inside linebacker, Roquan Smith played every defensive snap, the only defender in the game to do so. Teddye Buchanan’s return from injury saw him on the field for only three plays. Trenton Simpson played 46 snaps and doesn’t appear at risk to losing his starting role. In the secondary, Nate Wiggins and Marlon Humphrey were not on the field for nearly every play again. Chidobe Awuzie played a season-high 15 snaps, as did Chandler Rivers with 32 snaps. Rivers seemingly has a strong hold on the nickel cornerback spot over Keyon Martin now for the second straight week. Kyle Hamilton exited the game for a few plays after suffering an injury but quickly returned. Malaki Starks retained a near every-down role with 73 snaps and Jaylinn Hawkins saw his snap share decrease slightly but still played 61 snaps.

title: Carolina Panthers 2027 NFL Draft Prospect Profile: Kade Pieper
summary: The 2027 NFL Draft feels like forever away, and we’re all caught up in the start of the NFL season. Regardless, it’s never too early to look ahead to the Draft. This weekly series will take a closer look at some of the prospects the Carolina Panthers could select in the 2027 iteration of the […]
full_text: IOWA CITY, IA - SEPTEMBER 13: Iowa right guard Kade Pieper (58) as seen before a college football game between the Massachusetts Minutemen and the Iowa Hawkeyes on Sept. 13, 2025, at Kinnick Stadium, in Iowa City, Ia. (Photo by Keith Gillett/Iconsportswire) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The 2027 NFL Draft feels like forever away, and we’re all caught up in the start of the NFL season. Regardless, it’s never too early to look ahead to the Draft. This weekly series will take a closer look at some of the prospects the Carolina Panthers could select in the 2027 iteration of the Draft. In this series, we’ll only be looking at prospects the Panthers could seriously consider. This week our profile will focus on Iowa Hawkeyes interior offensive lineman Kade Pieper Bio Kade Pieper (6’4”, 290 lbs.) is the stereotypical farm-boy-turned-offensive-lineman. After literally growing up on a farm in Nebraska, Pieper earned a three star rating playing both sides of the line as a senior. Just before the 2023 season, he flipped his commitment from North Dakota State to Iowa. After redshirting his freshman season, he was a backup his second year. Finally, in 2025, Pieper took over the starting job at right guard as a redshirt sophomore. He performed extremely well, allowing just one sack and ten pressures while drawing a single penalty across 13 games, earning First Team All-American honors. Iowa’s offensive line took home the Joe Moore Award as the best offensive line in the country. Strengths/Weaknesses Pieper is often considered one of, if not the best run blocker in the entire draft, regardless of position. On top of the dominant run blocking, he is an effective pass blocker as well (a pass block grade in the mid to high 70s from PFF). He has that “farm boy strength” and above average athleticism for an interior lineman. He was originally recruited as a tight end, so his mobility allows him to effectively hit the second level. That mobility is largely due to his small frame. At just 290 lbs., he’s one of the lightest interior linemen in this year’s draft. This lack of size combines with his occasional habit of playing high to reduce his functional strength. Pieper will need to work on leverage while fine tuning his pass blocking technique. Projection Pieper is an exceptional athlete with good strength. Interior linemen often fall down draft boards due to positional importance, but Pieper is one that could sneak into the end of the first round. He’ll definitely be a Day 2 pick at the absolute lowest. The Panthers have a ton of cap space invested in the interior of the offensive line, and their starters at guard are expensive and getting old. Though Robert Hunt, the older of the two, only turned 30 last month, the Panthers have seen how important depth at the position has been the last several seasons. Hunt could even be a cap casualty next season, with the team potentially saving $13 million while suffering $10 million in dead cap. If the Panthers truly want to run the football and protect Bryce Young long term, they’ll need to start investing in the interior of the offensive line with higher draft picks instead of just money. What do you think, Panthers fans? If Kade Pieper is available when the Panthers select in the 2027 NFL Draft, should they take him? Sound off in the comments!
author: Daniel Belton

title: Jaycee Horn out indefinitely with torn quad
summary: According to NFL news breaker Ian Rapaport, Carolina Panthers cornerback Jaycee Horn is out indefinitely with a torn quad. Rapaport notes in his tweet that Horn is going to get multiple opinions, but injuries of this severity are almost always multi-month recoveries, especially if it’s a full tear. If it’s not a complete tear and […]
full_text: CHARLOTTE, NORTH CAROLINA - SEPTEMBER 13: Jaycee Horn #8 of the Carolina Panthers readies at the line of scrimmage during the game against the Chicago Bears at Bank of America Stadium on September 13, 2026 in Charlotte, North Carolina. (Photo by Jared C. Tilton/Getty Images) | Getty Images According to NFL news breaker Ian Rapaport, Carolina Panthers cornerback Jaycee Horn is out indefinitely with a torn quad. Sources: #Panthers star CB Jaycee Horn suffered a torn quad and is out indefinitely. One of the game's best. Horn will seek a second opinion, but he's headed for Injured Reserve and could be lost for the season. pic.twitter.com/HINTtlOEtp — Ian Rapoport (@RapSheet) September 28, 2026 Rapaport notes in his tweet that Horn is going to get multiple opinions, but injuries of this severity are almost always multi-month recoveries, especially if it’s a full tear. If it’s not a complete tear and more of a strain, Horn could avoid surgery and be back before a the end of the season. That said, the way this has been reported does not seem promising. Horn has established himself as one of the best corners in the game and had started to shake the injury prone label after missing a total of just three games in the two seasons prior to this one. Now he’ll be headed back to injured reserve, and the Panthers will have to try to make do without him. His running mate Mike Jackson is also dealing with a groin injury, so it might get really ugly in the secondary for the next few weeks at least.

title: NFL Week 4 Power Rankings: Biggest September Surprises
summary: With Week 3 wrapping up, the NFL will turn the calendar to October as it heads into Week 4. Although the opening month of the season is over, there’s still plenty to learn about all 32 teams around the NFL. Week 2 brought key quarterback injuries, leading to multiple backups making starts and further clouding […]
full_text: SANTA CLARA, CALIFORNIA - SEPTEMBER 27: Brock Purdy #13 of the San Francisco 49ers reacts after throwing a touchdown pass to George Kittle #85 against the Arizona Cardinals in the fourth quarter at Levi's Stadium on September 27, 2026 in Santa Clara, California. (Photo by Thearon W. Henderson/Getty Images) | Getty Images With Week 3 wrapping up, the NFL will turn the calendar to October as it heads into Week 4. Although the opening month of the season is over, there’s still plenty to learn about all 32 teams around the NFL. Week 2 brought key quarterback injuries, leading to multiple backups making starts and further clouding things for certain teams. With October on the horizon, here’s how our WCG Week 4 Power Rankings shake out. 1. Buffalo Bills (3-0) Biggest Surprise Through September: Continuity exists, despite a change at head coach. Is this the boost the Bills needed to get over the hump? Maybe this isn’t a huge surprise to some, but so far, Joe Brady has his team playing at as high a level as, if not higher than, former head coach Sean McDermott did. Quarterback Josh Allen is the frontrunner for MVP, and for the most part, they’ve looked like the best team in football. 2. San Francisco 49ers (3-0) Biggest Surprise Through September: Despite more injuries (no surprise), they are a perfect 3-0, and the defense looks worthy enough to be considered Super Bowl caliber. Nick Bosa is hurt again. Their defensive line is in shambles. Mike Evans left with a rib injury on Sunday. Despite that, the 49ers are 3-0, and they look more complete than they did a year ago. There’s no reason to think that won’t continue. 3. Kansas City Chiefs (3-0) Biggest Surprise Through September: How quickly a 31-year-old Patrick Mahomes has returned to form is a credit to hard work, and of course, modern medicine. Not only are the Chiefs undefeated through September, but their star quarterback looks like he’s back to his normal self. Things got a little dicey against Miami, but Mahomes has a 7-2 touchdown-to-interception ratio, a 68% completion rate, and he’s averaging 270 yards per game. Life is good in Kansas City again. 4. Minnesota Vikings (3-0) Biggest Surprise Through September: Despite more chaos at quarterback, the Vikings are a perfect 3-0. Will it last? Coming back against the Packers at home was one thing. Smoothing a high-scoring Bears offense was another. Now their defense has smothered a third team, and things look great for the Vikings so far in 2026. All of this, despite starting two quarterbacks through three games. All that bad luck from last year appears to be reversed this season. 5. Seattle Seahawks (2-1) Biggest Surprise Through September: Their lone loss came with Sam Darnold playing all 60 minutes. Make no mistake, the Seahawks are one of the best teams in football. They’re also at their best when Darnold is under center. That said, it’s mildly surprising that their only loss of September came with Darnold at quarterback, and with the Jayden Daniels-less Commanders being the ones to do it. 6. Cincinnati Bengals (2-1) Biggest Surprise Through September: For the most part, the defense looks Super Bowl caliber. If that holds, the Bengals will be dangerous. Even with a disappointing loss to the Steelers on Sunday, fans have to feel good about the direction the Bengals are headed. Dexter Lawrence has helped transform this defense, and if everyone on the offense stays healthy, this will be a team no one wants to face all year. 7. Baltimore Ravens (2-1) Biggest Surprise Through September: The defense isn’t quite fixed under first-year head coach Jesse Minter, despite a highly paid and highly talented unit. To nobody’s surprise, the offense is back to looking like it normally does with Lamar Jackson under center. First-year offensive coordinator Declan Doyle has done a great job of keeping things explosive. Defensively, they still leave a lot to be desired. While they might be improved, it’s fair to wonder if they’ve improved enough to get back into the Super Bowl contender conversation. 8. Jacksonville Jaguars (2-1) Biggest Surprise Through September: The Jaguars and Trevor Lawrence are quickly proving last year’s impressive run wasn’t a fluke. Jacksonville was one bad second half against the Broncos from being a perfect 3-0. Head coach Liam Coen became the quickest head coach to 15 wins in franchise history, and for the most part, everything is trending in the right direction. Quarterback Trevor Lawrence can also be included in that conversation. He’s playing at the highest level of his career. 9. Las Vegas Raiders (3-0) Biggest Surprise Through September: How real is their hot start? Eventually they’ll turn to Fernando Mendoza, but so far, Kirk Cousins has been more than up to the task. The most surprising team in the league through three games? The Las Vegas Raiders at a perfect 3-0 under first-year head coach Klint Kubiak. I’m not sure whether the offense under Cousins or their defense (which has given up just 54 points) has been more impressive. I’m not sure it’ll last, but Raiders fans have to be over the moon heading into October. 10. Chicago Bears (2-1) Biggest Surprise Through September: No Caleb Williams… No problem? Despite a disastrous Week 2 that cost the team three to four games with Williams out, Case Keenum helped deliver a winning month. It would have been easy to write the Bears off after last weekend against Minnesota simply. The offense looked anemic; they lost their starting quarterback, and overall, spirits seemed down heading into a pivotal early-season matchup against the undefeated Eagles. Instead, they have ridden two great defensive performances and a lifetime-from-Keenum performance to come out of September at 2-1 and in good shape moving forward. 11. Philadelphia Eagles (2-1) Biggest Surprise Through September: Saquon Barkley is still not himself, and because of that, the Eagles’ offense continues to teeter in the middle. Despite a 2-0 start, it was easy to look at the quality of their opponents, how they won those games, and wonder what was going on. The defense is no longer elite, but still plenty good enough. Although the offense isn’t “bad” by any stretch of the imagination, it still lacks the same pop we saw from a few years ago. They’re still in good shape moving forward in the NFC East, but it’s worth wondering if Sean Mannion is the answer at offensive coordinator. 12. Detroit Lions (2-1) Biggest Surprise Through September: Despite their third new offensive play caller in as many seasons, the Lions’ offense is still pretty damn productive. It hasn’t looked the same as it did during Ben Johnson’s heyday, but they have scored exactly 31 points in each of their first three games. The bigger concern is the defense, which continues to give up far too many points, leading to a -2 point differential despite averaging 31 points per game offensively. 13. Denver Broncos (2-1) Biggest Surprise Through September: Despite being 2-1, offensive regression has hit, and the Broncos have been left searching for consistency. Some will blame it on first-year play caller Davis Webb, while others will point to a bad start from quarterback Bo Nix. Regardless of how you cut it, it stands to reason that head coach Sean Payton could take back play-calling if things don’t improve drastically soon for more than one half at a time. We’ll see if they can string together a full game of good offense soon. 14. Pittsburgh Steelers (2-1) Biggest Surprise Through September: Despite a new head coach and a 42-year-old quarterback, the Steelers look like a playoff contender. Count me as shocked as anybody. AFC North games are always close and usually ugly, but being able to pull out a win against the Bengals was an impressive feat. Hell, I’d even argue that it was Aaron Rodgers’ best game of the young season. Now, we’ll see if the offense can do enough to keep them well-rounded. 15. Los Angeles Rams (1-2) Biggest Surprise Through September: That vaunted…

title: Bears vs. Eagles: Inside the Snap Counts, Stats, and a Sucker Sneak
summary: Yeah, that rainy game last week was the anomaly, because with a 27 to 7 win over the Philadelphia Eagles, the Chicago Bears are who we thought they were. While many expected (including me) the Bears to dust off an old-school ground-and-pound game plan to protect 38-year-old Case Keenum, Chicago went the other direction and […]
full_text: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - SEPTEMBER 28: Case Keenum #11 of the Chicago Bears dives into the endzone for a touchdown during the fourth quarter of the NFL game against the Philadelphia Eagles at Soldier Field on September 28, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Todd Rosenberg/Getty Images) | Getty Images Yeah, that rainy game last week was the anomaly, because with a 27 to 7 win over the Philadelphia Eagles, the Chicago Bears are who we thought they were. While many expected (including me) the Bears to dust off an old-school ground-and-pound game plan to protect 38-year-old Case Keenum, Chicago went the other direction and aired it out. They called more pass plays than run plays and showed complete trust in their third-string quarterback. Ben Johnson’s offensive game plan last night was brilliant. A season ago, he ran all over this talented Eagles front, but this time, it was the quick passing game that diced up Vic Fangio’s Philadelphia defense, and that caught the Eagles off guard. The Bears had more total yards (375 to 248), more first downs (24 to 14), and had the time-of-possession edge (36:53 to 23:07). That 23:07 is the Eagles’ second-lowest time of possession in their last 42 games, worse than only last year’s Black Friday game against the Bears (20:42). Let’s look at the Bears’ playing time breakdowns and a few individual stats from the game. OFFENSE Case Keenum is now 4-0 when playing against a Vic Fangio-coordinated defense. Keenum was a perfect 10 for 10 when the Eagles blitzed him for 140 yards, a +1.18 EPA/dropback, and a 90% success rate. Keenum now holds the record for the oldest player to score a rushing touchdown in Bears history, and he did it on a play designed by a former Bears’ offensive coordinator. “That’s a Mike Martz special right there,” Ben Johnson said about the TD. “That’s the old sucker sneak, and I think that they were a little bit tight initially, and then they stemmed out at the last second, which gave us the green light to get to that play, and, you know, it’s an old play but a good play right there.” False Pulling the Guards to Sneak your 38yr old QB 😂😂😂 pic.twitter.com/b3sO4d6HrI — Coach Dan Casey (@CoachDanCasey) September 29, 2026 DEFENSE I was told all offseason that there would be a turnover regression, but Chicago’s defense had three more takeaways, including safety Dillon Thieneman’s first career interception. Again, last week was the anomaly, because in Week 1 they also had three takeaways. Austin Booker had a Peanut Punch, and Dayo Odeyingbo had a sack! T.J. Edwards had a pick and a career-high 3 passes defended. Dennis Allen’s defense has now stacked two good games in a row after getting lit up Week 1. They held the Eagles to 2 for 9 on third-down attempts (22.2%) and stopped Philly on both of their fourth-down tries. SPECIAL TEAMS* *The above image has players who only played in the third phase. Cairo Santos hit all three extra points and both field goals, but he missed the landing zone on another kickoff, resulting in a penalty. You have to assume he’s being coached to try and dirty kick these short to mess up the timing of the returns, but he needs to get this right. Tory Taylor had 2 punts for a 52.5 average (38.5 net) with 1 inside the 20. He nearly had a second down near the goal line, but a rookie mistake by Sam Roush turned it into a touchback. Zavion Thomas had a 32-yard kickoff return. Elijah Hicks had 2 special teams tackles. New (old) long snapper Scott Daly was perfect on all his snaps. To check out the complete Bears vs. Eagles box score, I find ESPN’s site is easy to navigate. All statistics and snap counts, as well as the accompanying pictures, are taken directly from the NFL’s Game Statistic and Information System.

title: Bears show resilience in primetime win over Eagles
summary: Coming into Monday night after a 9-3 loss to the Vikings, with third-string quarterback Case Keenum thrust into a starting role, the Bears had several question marks around them in Week 3. They answered those questions in about as decisively as you could possibly imagine. The Bears trounced the Eagles 27-7 on Monday night, excelling […]
full_text: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - SEPTEMBER 28: Case Keenum #11 of the Chicago Bears calls a play against the Philadelphia Eagles during the first quarter of the game at Soldier Field on September 28, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Michael Reaves/Getty Images) | Getty Images Coming into Monday night after a 9-3 loss to the Vikings, with third-string quarterback Case Keenum thrust into a starting role, the Bears had several question marks around them in Week 3. They answered those questions in about as decisively as you could possibly imagine. The Bears trounced the Eagles 27-7 on Monday night, excelling on both sides of the ball in a win to improve their record to 2-1 for the season. Keenum looked impressive in his first start since 2023, and Chicago got back on its feet to get back into the win column. In a game where many doubted the Bears, they bounced back and showed the nation what they’re capable of. Here are some of my takeaways from Monday’s victory. Case Keenum: Unc still got it Upon initial review, Case Keenum finished with a 79.1 PFN QB Impact grade on Monday. Among Week 3 performances, that’s better than the likes of Matthew Stafford, Josh Allen, Jordan Love, and Drake Maye. That’s not too bad for a third-string quarterback who has just four NFL starts since 2020. Keenum was decisive and poised in Ben Johnson’s offense, scoring three touchdowns with no interceptions while throwing for 247 yards with a 110.8 passer rating. He got the ball out quickly and accurately, he sensed pressure well in the pocket, and he kept the Bears’ offense playing on time. He connected well with the likes of Kalif Raymond and Luther Burden in particular, the former of whom continues to be one of the biggest surprises of Chicago’s season thus far. The Bears’ passing attack was humming all evening. The pass protection was strong, the receivers got open, and Keenum got them the ball in a timely manner. Johnson adjusted his offense to get the ball out quicker and on shorter passes than what he usually calls with Caleb Williams, and in this game, it worked wonders. Dennis Allen masterclass Johnson wasn’t the only Bears coach in his bag on Monday. Defensive coordinator Dennis Allen was extremely efficient in disrupting the Eagles’ offensive momentum, relying heavily on the blitz to get to the quarterback quickly and penetrate the backfield. Allen’s blitz looks were extremely varied, though. You saw your fair share of double-mug blitz looks, but both linebackers didn’t end up rushing the passer every time. T.J. Edwards had one dropped interception where he showed a blitz pre-snap but dropped back into coverage at the last second, and he eventually had an interception in that same assignment later in the night. Dayo Odeyingbo and Montez Sweat both had sacks. The Bears allowed just 141 net passing yards to Jalen Hurts on Monday, and they picked off him and Andy Dalton once each. Allen kept Hurts guessing all night with the looks he was showing before the snap, and that confusion helped Chicago limit the Eagles to just one score for the game. Dillon Thieneman continues to impress In addition to Edwards, the other aforementioned interception the Bears had in Week 3 came from Dillon Thieneman, which marked the first interception of his NFL career. He also added six tackles into the stat sheet to complement his pick, a total which led the team on Monday. Thieneman has been a bright spot for the Bears’ defense through the first three weeks of the season. His sense of urgency, his quick processing, his electric athleticism on the back end, and his versatility as a coverage threat and a downhill tackler has seen him live up to expectations early in his career. The 2026 first-round pick has been everything Chicago hoped of him and more, and it was encouraging to see the rookie safety continue his strong start to his career.

title: Case Keenum finds Fountain of Youth as Chicago Bears Dominate Philadelphia Eagles
summary: On a Monday night at Soldier Field that felt more like a statement than a surprise, the Chicago Bears took a 2-0 Philadelphia Eagles team that had been talking about unfinished business from last November and buried them 27-7, turning primetime into a Case Keenum clinic on old-man football, and a much-maligned defense with a […]
full_text: On a Monday night at Soldier Field that felt more like a statement than a surprise, the Chicago Bears took a 2-0 Philadelphia Eagles team that had been talking about unfinished business from last November and buried them 27-7, turning primetime into a Case Keenum clinic on old-man football, and a much-maligned defense with a statment to the NFL – all at once. Coming off a grim 9-3 Week 2 slog in Minnesota, Chicago controlled the ball for nearly 37 minutes, forced three turnovers, never coughed one up, and watched a 38-year-old backup quarterback throw for two scores, run for a third, and look every bit the veteran who still knows how to win a football game. Luther Burden punched in the opener, Kalif Raymond took a 41-yard strike to the house, Cairo Santos did the rest, and by the time Keenum walked in from a yard out in the fourth, the only thing left for the Windy City was to enjoy a rare, clean, 20-point Monday night beatdown of a supposed NFC contender. Let’s get into it, Bears fans! Box Score for Bears 27, Eagles 7 from ESPN . 1st Quarter It is clear from the outset that Case Keenum has complete control of this offense as he makes efficient play after efficient play. The only deficiencies in his game are physical – he has the mental game on lock. Swift, who struggled against the Vikings, including a fumble, comes out rejuvenated in this game. He is running with confidence and elusiveness. Luther Burden has arrived in this game – as Keenum targets him multiple times and he shows his YAC superpower over and over again. We get some 4th-and-1 redemption for Sam Roush, as Ben Johnson dials up a play for the tight end that gets the first down and more. Unfortunately, Roush gives back the redemption with a bad play on the Tory Taylor punt to the one where he foolishly covers it, and the ball comes out to the 20. But Booker picks up the rookie with a big turnover as he Peanut Punches the ball out on the Eagles’ possession, and Xavier Woods recovers it for Bear ball within the Red Zone. 2nd Quarter Colton Loveland appears to have the touchdown live, but upon review it is clear he is a few inches short of the touchdown. On the next play, Swift loses 2 yards, and then on 3rd down, it looks like Rome has an easy touchdown, but he takes the ball off of his facemask, and while he secures it on the second try, he doesn’t get both feet down. Come on, Rome. 4th down his a missed pass to Burden and Bears turn it over. Gooch note: I really struggle to understand why these carries don’t go to Monangai on short-yardage and goal-to-go situations. On the ensuing Bears possession, we commit a bad penalty that lets the Eagles out of the shadow of their end zone. They are running the ball down our throat on multiple downs. The Eagles get it deep into Bears territory. Then on a play where Sweat is clearly held (flag goes down) Hurts scrambles to his right and is running for the 1st down marker. D. Jackson comes with the big hit right at the marker – and the Striped Ones call it “unnecessary roughness” despite the fact that Hurts had a foot in bounds at contact and was clearly a runner. Penalties offset. Hurts has to leave the game as the overhead observers force a tent visit. Andy Dalton comes in for the Eagles. Bears make a goal line stand. The Eagles are pushed back from the goal line when JVDB pushes his man 3 yards into the backfield, and Bush cleans up the play by tackling Barkley for a loss. And the drive then ends in a Thineman INTERCEPTION of Andy Dalton. Bears ball on the 20-yard line. After the Bears punt, the Eagles drive the length of the field. On a pass play that should have ended the half, the Eagles, somehow, get set, and instead of a spike, Hurts does the Tush Push for a touchdown. Controversy ends the half. Clock showed zeros when Hurts got the ball. Questionable whether they got the snap off but it’s 10-7 Bears at the half. HALFTIME GOOCH Observations: Well, Case Keenum has been everything we could have hoped for in the first half. He has protected the ball. He has been efficient and an excellent decision-maker. He has put the Bears in good position executing BJ’s game plan. Frankly, the Bears dominated the first half and the 10-7 score doesn’t illustrate how well the Bears played. On defense, the Bears were opportunistic, but the Eagles and Barkley gashed them in the run game. 3rd Quarter The Eagles start with the ball in the third quarter and the Bears earn their first three-and-out as TJ Edwards drops a sure interception on third down when Austin Booker’s pressure forces Hurts to throw the ball blind into the flat. Still – Eagles punt. Bears drive the ball and get a field goal to move the score to 13-7. On the next Eagles possession, the Bears defense again looks good. Perhaps Dennis Allen made some halftime adjustments that are coming into play. JJ avoids a blocker and spikes Makai Lemon for a three yard loss. And TJ Edwards (man, I have to apologize for my TJ hate don’t I) again shows up to force the Eagles again into a punting situation. GOOCH Observation: It is clear that BJ came in with a plan of playing inverse to the Eagles’ expectations, given we had our 3rd QB starting the game. BJ correctly anticipated the Eagles would expect a run-heavy approach, so BJ has spammed the play action in pretty much every run down-distance scenario, and the Eagles haven’t had an answer. The Bears with the ball and Monangai is finally getting his touches and making the most of them as the Bears get first down after first down. Then Case Keenum hits Kalif Raymond on the crosser and it is 41 yards and in! Touchdown! Touchdown Bears! Cairo Santos continues to have kickoff problems as his kick hits short of the 20 and the Eagles start with great field position. They get it out almost to the 50. Bears shut them down and force a 4th and short. For some reason, Nick Sirano does NOT go for it on 4th down – instead tries to force the offsides and takes the delay of game and punts. From a win probability perspective, that’s an insanely dumb decision by the Eagles head coach. As we go into the 4th quarter, the Bears lead the Eagles 20-7. 4th Quarter My notes are rather sparse in the 4th quarter as I spent quite a bit of it high-fiving and dabbing up my son. Nonetheless, a few notes. On the Eagles’ possession, TJ finally gets his interception on third down, and it’s a TJ kind of night, as he torches his former team on the defensive side of the ball! As the Bears have the ball on the one foot line the clock is expiring – just as it was in the first half when Hurts got his tush push touchdown – and right as the clock goes to zeros – Keenum takes the snap and sneaks it into the endzone as the ultimate: “anything you can do, I can do better.” Bears go up 27-7 and the rout is on. On the ensuing Eagles drive the Bears defense again shows up, and a MOTIVATED DAYO gets the sack on Hurts. Bears Ball. Bears Win. William (my son) to WCG: “WILLY IS EXCITED!!!!” Bear down, my guys. We are 2-1 on the season, and we have thirty-eight-year-old Case Keenum to thank for it. As Case said: Give glory to God. Gooch out.
author: Donald Gooch

full_text: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - SEPTEMBER 28: Dillon Thieneman #31 of the Chicago Bears celebrates with teammates after intercepting a pass thrown by Jalen Hurts #1 of the Philadelphia Eagles in the end zone during the second quarter of the game at Soldier Field on September 28, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Michael Reaves/Getty Images) | Getty Images Chicago Bears rookie Dillon Thieneman just came up big. The first-round safety’s first career interception couldn’t have come on a more clutch occasion: swiping Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Andy Dalton in the red zone to take away a potential touchdown and maintain the Bears’ 7-0 lead in the second quarter. (In case you’re wondering, starting quarterback Jalen Hurts was momentarily out of the game while being evaluated for a possible concussion after a late hit by linebacker D’Marco Jackson, which is why Dalton, the former Bears quarterback, was in the game.) What a moment, on Monday Night Football, to make such a huge play. The young safety has quietly been one of the Bears’ most consistent players early in the season, which is simultaneously good and concerning. (Your safety shouldn’t be your leading tackler coming into Week 3 in an ideal world.) Still, it’s nice to know the guy brought in to be an immediate difference-maker has proven to be just that. And now, he’s checked off a big box on his resume: “first career interception.” Thankfully, Dalton made it easy for him. Dillon Thieneman. First career INT 🚨 @PHIvsCHI on ESPN Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/GQhn7Oz1ZK — NFL (@NFL) September 29, 2026 The nice part: this pick wasn’t just “a meatball sub,” in the words of Tom Brady from last week. It also helped the Bears maintain a lead not many people expected them to have at this point against the Eagles with Keenum at quarterback. In fact, funnily enough, it stole points off the board for the Eagles after the Bears had failed on 4th and goal with a chance to go up two touchdowns. As a safety, Thieneman probably won’t top too many people’s lists for Defensive Rookie of the Year, especially if the Bears continue being a largely “mid” defense. But make no mistake: so far, the youngin has done his job on the back end of the defense. Here’s to many more interceptions to come.

title: Vikings Trade JJ McCarthy, making it one of the worst picks this century
summary: With Jaxson Dart out for the season, it’s no surprise the New York Giants were looking for help in their quarterback room. Jameis Winston was the only viable QB other than Dart, and after watching him play two games, viable seems like a stretch. On Monday, the Giants sent a 5th-round pick to the Minnesota […]
full_text: MINNEAPOLIS, MN - AUGUST 22: Minnesota Vikings quarterback J.J. McCarthy (9) looks on before the NFL preseason game between the Baltimore Ravens and the Minnesota Vikings on August 22nd, 2026, at U.S. Bank in Minneapolis, MN. (Photo by Bailey Hillesheim/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images With Jaxson Dart out for the season, it’s no surprise the New York Giants were looking for help in their quarterback room. Jameis Winston was the only viable QB other than Dart, and after watching him play two games, viable seems like a stretch. On Monday, the Giants sent a 5th-round pick to the Minnesota Vikings for QB JJ McCarthy. With the move, McCarthy becomes one of the worst draft picks in the history of the NFL. Now, you can think McCarthy is already a bust, or you can still have faith in him and maybe somehow, despite the odds, he still ends up having a solid NFL career. But any future successes that McCarthy may have will not be in a Vikings uniform, and from Minnesota’s perspective, it’s hard to imagine many selections that aged worse than McCarthy. I think when you invest time, money, and draft capital into a QB, and it doesn’t work out, those missed picks hit harder than missing on a first-round offensive lineman or a first-round defensive back. With that premise, the selection of a QB is a far bigger miss than a different position. This century, only three other first-round QBs have started 10 or fewer games for the team that drafted them. McCarthy started 10. Trey Lance started 4 for the San Francisco 49ers. Paxton Lynch started 4 for the Denver Broncos. Johnny Manziel started 8 for the Cleveland Browns. When you look at those four picks, Trey Lance is the worst of the group because the 49ers spent 3 first-round picks to move up to 3 to select him. Brock Purdy has saved that franchise in so many ways you can’t even count. Denver moved up a few spots to take Lynch, but it only cost them a 3rd-round pick to do it. The Browns also moved up a few spots for Manziel, but that also only cost them a 3rd. The Vikings moved up with the Jets to select McCarthy using a fourth- and fifth-round pick to do it. There’s always an extra crushing blow the higher draft pick you use. So while McCarthy is arguably a more crushing blow than Manziel or Lynch (both picked in the 20s), it’s not as bad as Lance, who went 3rd overall. But there are other QBs that have to make this list as well. JaMarcus Russell is famously a bust and was a first overall pick. Zack Wilson going 2nd overall is a massive bust for the New York Jets. The other argument that can be made is for Josh Rosen, who was also selected 10th overall and was traded the next season, but the Cardinals were able to get a second-round pick for him. Since the Cardinals were able to get more back for Rosen, I think it makes the McCarthy pick more egregious. So if we are to look at the worst picks of this century. And if we start with the premise that investments in QBs in round 1 that miss are more impactful than other position players, that means the top 5 or so worst picks will all be QBs. I think, since he was a first overall pick, the top spot still belongs to Russell. I think, when you consider the capital used to move up to select him, Trey Lance becomes the next worst pick this century. I think, since he went 2nd overall, I think Zack Wilson owns the 3rd spot. So don’t worry, Vikings fans, JJ McCarthy is not one of the 3 worst NFL draft picks this century. I do think, however, he comes in fourth. Again, this isn’t about what McCarthy may or may not become as a QB; it’s simply what the Vikings got out of the pick. I think Manziel is probably 5th (because his crash and burn was so public) and Paxton Lynch probably rounds out the top of the list at 6th, with Rosen coming in 7th. The Chicago Bears have had some bad draft selections at quarterback in the first round this century, but Mitch Trubisky still led them to a playoff berth, Justin Fields turned in some electric performances before falling apart, and heck, even Rex Grossman helped (did he help?) the Bears get to a Super Bowl. None of those misses are as bad as the Minnesota Vikings and JJ McCarthy.

title: The Good, The Bad and The Ugly from the Bengals’ 30-27 Loss to the Steelers
summary: Well, that one had pretty much everything you could want from a Bengals – Steelers game — except the result Cincinnati wanted. The Bengals walked into Acrisure Stadium at 2-0, traded punches with Pittsburgh for four quarters, and had the ball with a chance to win late. Instead, they walked out with their first loss […]
full_text: Well, that one had pretty much everything you could want from a Bengals – Steelers game — except the result Cincinnati wanted. The Bengals walked into Acrisure Stadium at 2-0, traded punches with Pittsburgh for four quarters, and had the ball with a chance to win late. Instead, they walked out with their first loss of the 2026 season, falling 30-27 after Chris Boswell’s 33-yard field goal with 2:15 remaining. There were plenty of positives to take from this one. There were also some very familiar problems. Here’s the good, the bad, and the ugly from Cincinnati’s Week 3 loss. The Good: Joe Burrow and the passing game Joe Burrow was really good Sunday. He completed 28 of 37 passes for 282 yards and three touchdowns, finishing with a 123.9 passer rating. He also opened the game by completing his first 14 throws and was 18-of-21 for 152 yards and two scores at halftime. More importantly, Burrow consistently made plays when the Bengals needed them. Ja’Marr Chase hauled in nine passes for 98 yards and a touchdown, while Tee Higgins added six catches for 90 yards and a touchdown. Mike Gesicki also came through with a 25-yard touchdown grab on fourth-and-2 in the fourth quarter to put Cincinnati ahead 27-24. Chase also crossed the 7,000-yard mark for his career, becoming just the fourth player in NFL history to reach that milestone in 81 games or fewer. That’s quite the receiving duo. And despite all the talk about Pittsburgh’s defense coming into this one, the Bengals moved the football. Cincinnati finished with 365 total yards, including 282 through the air. The offense did enough to win this game. The Good: Dexter Lawrence re-announces himself If anyone was wondering what the Bengals were getting when they acquired Dexter Lawrence, Sunday provided another pretty good answer. Lawrence recorded four tackles and two sacks of Aaron Rodgers, with both sacks coming on third down in the red zone. He also hit Rodgers three times and was a major reason Pittsburgh had to settle for field goals on its final two scoring drives. This was Lawrence’s first Bengals-Steelers game, and he certainly made an introduction. The defense ultimately gave up 30 points, but Lawrence and the defensive front were giving Cincinnati opportunities to survive some of the mistakes happening elsewhere. The Bad: The explosive plays allowed The Bengals’ defense had some really good moments. It also gave up some plays that simply can’t happen late in a close game. The biggest examples came on Pittsburgh’s go-ahead drive. Darnell Washington caught a pass and turned it into a 47-yard gain, and Jaylen Warren followed it with a 26-yard run. Those two plays moved Pittsburgh from its own 8-yard line all the way down to the Cincinnati 6 and set up Boswell’s go-ahead field goal. Warren finished with 127 rushing yards on 17 carries, while the Steelers produced 430 total yards. A trademark physical day from the Steelers. The Bengals’ defense was able to stiffen in the red zone, but continually allowing explosive plays is eventually going to catch up with you. It did Sunday. The Ugly: Special teams This is where things really started to unravel. The Bengals had a 20-17 lead in the third quarter when defensive end Cedric Johnson was flagged for roughing the punter, extending a Pittsburgh drive that eventually ended in a Steelers touchdown. Then, with Cincinnati leading 27-24 in the fourth quarter, Ke’Shawn Williams muffed a punt, giving Pittsburgh the ball at the Bengals’ 14-yard line. Ten Pittsburgh points came directly from those two special teams mistakes. That’s a massive swing in a three-point game. Joe Burrow and the offense shouldn’t have to be perfect, but when you’re playing an AFC North rival on the road, you can’t keep handing the other team short fields and extra possessions. The Ugly: The final drive Unfortunately, this is what seemingly everyone will remember. After Pittsburgh took a 30-27 lead, Cincinnati got the ball back with 2:08 remaining and still had a legitimate chance to win. The Bengals eventually moved into Steelers territory, but a pass to Chase Brown for minus-4 yards started to derail things. With 44 seconds remaining and facing a 3rd-and-8, Burrow dropped back from the Pittsburgh 38-yard line looking for a shot at the end zone. Derrick Harmon got to him, punched the ball out and Sebastian Joseph-Day recovered. Ballgame. Burrow said afterward that the Bengals were trying to take a shot into the end zone while avoiding a sack because they were already in field-goal range. It’s tough to put the entire loss on that play. There were plenty of mistakes before it. But that’s the play that ultimately ended Cincinnati’s final chance. The Bottom Line The Bengals lost a game they absolutely had a chance to win. That’s frustrating, especially because there was a lot to like. Burrow played well. Chase and Higgins were excellent. The offensive line did a strong job against T.J. Watt. Lawrence looked every bit like the defensive centerpiece Cincinnati hoped he would be. But the Bengals also committed six penalties for 40 yards , made two costly special teams mistakes, and allowed Pittsburgh to hit them with too many explosive plays. As Burrow put it after the game: “We just can’t shoot ourselves in the foot like that. You can’t win in this league when you do that.” That’s probably the simplest way to describe it. At 2-1, the Bengals aren’t suddenly a bad football team. But they just got a pretty good reminder of how little room for error there is against a divisional opponent — particularly when you’re playing on the road. And now comes the important part: seeing how they respond.
author: Anthony Cosenza

title: Bengals Tuesday Trenches: A bump in the road or is the sky falling?
summary: I’m an optimist. Obviously, things aren’t always black and white. Optimists aren’t always optimistic, pessimists aren’t always pessimistic. But generally speaking, I think you can lump most people into one of those two categories. The Cincinnati Bengals did just about everything they could on Sunday in Pittsburgh to lose. On paper, it was set up […]
full_text: Cincinnati Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow (9) covers his ears as he listens for a play call in the fourth quarter of the NFL Week 3 game between the Pittsburgh Steelers and the Cincinnati Bengals at Acrisure Stadium in Pittsburgh on Sunday, Sept. 27, 2026. The Bengals fell to 2-1 on the season with a 30-27 loss on the road. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co I’m an optimist. Obviously, things aren’t always black and white. Optimists aren’t always optimistic, pessimists aren’t always pessimistic. But generally speaking, I think you can lump most people into one of those two categories. The Cincinnati Bengals did just about everything they could on Sunday in Pittsburgh to lose. On paper, it was set up perfectly for the Bengals. The Steelers’ offense was borderline anemic heading into Week 3, while the Bengals’ defense was coming off a show of force in Houston, where they held the Texans to just six points. We knew Joe Burrow and the Bengals’ offense were going to score their points, and it felt like Cincinnati was on its way to a 3-0 start for the first time since 2015. Nope. The defense generated virtually no pass rush and allowed 42-year-old Aaron Rodgers to run around in the backfield like he was 15 years younger. Rodgers is a first-ballot Hall of Fame quarterback, so the fact that he led the Steelers to a victory isn’t shocking. The way he avoided pressure like he was Burrow’s age, though, certainly was. Special teams, which we almost never talk about outside of Evan McPherson—and that’s usually a good thing—was a disaster . The punt return unit essentially cost the Bengals 10 points. Pittsburgh scored a touchdown after Cedric Johnson’s roughing-the-kicker penalty extended a drive, then added three more after a muffed punt from Ke’Shawn Williams set the Steelers up at Cincinnati’s 14-yard line. Then, just when Burrow got the ball back with plenty of time to lead a game-winning drive, he was sacked for the first time all afternoon. And he fumbled. Game over. The loss isn’t going to kill them. We’re only through Week 3, and this was their first division game. If they finish the regular season 5-1 in the division and 16-1 overall, they’ll obviously have the No. 1 seed and would be among the favorites to win the Lombardi Trophy. That’s how you can look at this if you’re an optimist. That’s how I look at it, and it’s how I’ve always been. It’s probably one of the reasons I haven’t gone insane as a Bengals fan, although I’ll admit I can occasionally drift into borderline delusion. To me, this is just a bump in the road. The idea that the Bengals were going to go undefeated—even within the division—was always unrealistic. The AFC North is brutal. These four teams know each other intimately, and because of that, almost every divisional game turns into a slugfest. Every team, no matter how good, typically has an ugly loss or two during the regular season. If the Bengals were going to have one, maybe it’s better to get it out of the way early. Of course, that’s the optimist talking. How about you? Do you see this as a bump in the road during what could still be a championship season, or has the sky already fallen? Sound off. Random thoughts about the game: Amarius Mims was outstanding against future Hall of Fame edge rusher T.J. Watt. Watt’s star may be fading while Mims’ is rising, but regardless, the Bengals’ right tackle didn’t allow Watt to even sniff the quarterback. For the vast majority of the game, the offensive line looked pretty good. The sack at the end just happened to come at the absolute worst possible time. The run game, especially when Burrow was under center, looked explosive again. It’s a shame the Bengals got themselves into a position where they had to play catch-up and move away from it. The Bengals’ defense came into the game tied for the league lead in sacks, while the Steelers were starting a new right guard and right tackle. You certainly wouldn’t have known it from watching Sunday. I am still very much anxiously awaiting my first look at Landon Robinson on the field. He was a healthy scratch again. I’m concerned about the secondary. DK Metcalf and Michael Pittman Jr. are obviously NFL-caliber receivers. They aren’t in the same league as Ja’Marr Chase and Tee Higgins, though, and the Bengals’ secondary—which practiced against the best wide receiver duo in football all summer—looked lost at times. Covering tight ends continues to be an issue, and so does tackling. I know Darnell Washington is a massive human being, but Bengals defenders were bouncing off him like he was made of rubber. Defenses are not going to let Burrow beat them deep with Chase and Higgins, but that has opened up the underneath passing game—which can essentially serve as an extension of the run game—as well as the middle of the field. I’d like to see Dohnte Meyers get more involved. Getting the ball in his hands in space could force defenses to think twice about devoting so much attention to Chase and Higgins. The Bengals’ run defense was incredible against the Texans, but Jaylen Warren and the Steelers gashed Cincinnati all afternoon. Warren averaged 7.5 yards per carry and finished with 127 yards. Rodgers completed passes of more than 20 yards to five different receivers. That’s… not ideal. I think it’s becoming clear that the Bengals are thin at linebacker and in the secondary. We knew that heading into the season, but I’m surprised it may be coming back to bite them this early. Now the Bengals come home to face a Jacksonville Jaguars team that just dropped 35 points on New England’s vaunted defense. If Cincinnati’s defense doesn’t look more like the unit we saw in Week 2, the Bengals could be in trouble. We may be looking at a shootout. Hopefully, for my blood pressure, we aren’t. Relative Song Lyrics: The sun’s gonna rise tomorrow Somewhere on the east side of sorrow You better pack your bags west Stick out your chest, and then hit the road The sun’s gonna rise tomorrow Somewhere on the East side of sorrow Don’t give it a reason to follow Let it be, then let it go

title: Bengals Film Room: Cincinnati defense struggles vs. Pittsburgh Steelers
summary: From the very first play of the game, it felt like the Cincinnati Bengals defense might have been buying their own hype a bit too much after the win over the Houston Texans. Going back to the first week of the season against Tampa Bay, this Bengals defense is still getting gashed when teams get […]
full_text: From the very first play of the game, it felt like the Cincinnati Bengals defense might have been buying their own hype a bit too much after the win over the Houston Texans. Going back to the first week of the season against Tampa Bay, this Bengals defense is still getting gashed when teams get the ball to a running back in the passing game. Making the linebackers and safeties tackle out in space so much is a concerning trend for this unit. The Steelers immediately went to Jaylen Warren for a big gain to start the game by doing just that. Warren gashed the Bengals defense all game long. He finished with 127 yards rushing, going for 7.5 yards per carry on the game. He added 49 receiving yards on the day, including the big play below that started the game for Pittsburgh. Bad start to the game with Knight taking a bad angle and Friermuth blowing up Bryan Cook for a big play from Warren. Warren feasted against the Bengals defense all game long. pic.twitter.com/MOJp5exSDB — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) September 28, 2026 The first touchdown for the Steelers came on a deep pass to Roman Wilson. The Bengals defensive backs were lined up close together, and Dax Hill coming across off the snap appeared to confuse Jalen Davis a bit. It was like his controller was disconnected momentarily on a game of Madden, and he was cooked off the line for an easy touchdown for Pittsburgh. Jalen Davis cooked off the line for the Steelers first touchdown of the game. Might end up regretting not bringing in Kenny Moore. pic.twitter.com/JmPYI3jpXB — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) September 28, 2026 There were a couple of bright spots for the Bengals defense on Sunday. One of those was the play of rookie edge rusher Cashius Howell. He was one of the only defensive ends to consistently generate pressure and make things uncomfortable at times for Aaron Rodgers throughout the game. It felt like Cashius Howell was one of the only edge guys that consistently got pressure today. pic.twitter.com/I0VZnDmg3l — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) September 28, 2026 Another pressure from Cashius Howell helps hold the Steelers to a field goal. pic.twitter.com/6QKKPs2tOI — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) September 28, 2026 If Cashius Howell starts converting some of these pressures into sacks, watch out. Dude creates immediate pressure even when the Bengals are rushing 3 guys. pic.twitter.com/ld2431aYl9 — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) September 28, 2026 Howell also has been playing solid against the run. He was able to hold his ground on the edge for a stop near the line of scrimmage on a run during the first half. I don’t see how the Bengals keep him off the field. He is playing like their best edge rusher, even over veteran addition Boye Mafe. More snaps should continue coming his way as the season progresses. We need to more snaps for Cashius Howell. pic.twitter.com/1DigDojseO — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) September 28, 2026 One theme of the day for the Cincinnati defense was their inability to make the initial tackle, and that turned into a first down. Jordan Battle came in way too high on Darnell Washington during the first half of this one. Washington also powered through them later in the game, which we will get to. There is no reason to come in like this against the 300-pound tight end, and the results were as expected. I mean what the hell do you expect to happen when you come in this high against Darnell Washington?!? pic.twitter.com/YVbljhMdLl — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) September 28, 2026 This is the second week in a row that I thought Barrett Carter struggled. The missed tackles continue to be an issue for Carter. He’s made some splash plays this year, but he has been way too inconsistent overall. If this doesn’t get cleaned up, the Bengals should consider at least making a call to Bobby Wagner. Wagner isn’t going to give you a lot in coverage, but at least he has been a reliable tackler during his career. Too many Barrett Carter missed tackles again this season. Cedric Johnson getting in on it here too. pic.twitter.com/61f6b9NjUV — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) September 28, 2026 It was another up-and-down performance from Dax Hill on Sunday. He did make a great play on third down to force a Steelers punt. Unfortunately, this was the play right before the muffed punt by Ke’Shawn Williams. This Hill play could have been a much bigger difference maker in the outcome of the game, but the special teams play let the defense down again. Dax Hill with great coverage to force a punt by the Steelers pic.twitter.com/QlWIeg7Wx3 — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) September 28, 2026 The most inexcusable defensive play of the game came during the last drive for the Steelers. The game was tied 27-27, and the Bengals let Darnell Washington get loose down the sideline for a 47-yard catch-and-run. The initial missed tackle came once again from linebacker Barrett Carter. Then, you saw a plethora of players decide they didn’t want to even make an attempt to truly bring down Washington in the open field. Tacario Davis couldn’t get around wide receiver Germie Bernard. DJ Turner just completely stopped running toward him as he got free down the sideline. Jordan Battle was doing who knows what on his attempt to make contact with Washington. Kyle Dugger eventually brought him down, but the damage was done. These guys get embarrassed by Darnell Washington every single time we play Pittsburgh. pic.twitter.com/GDgLGvYNQ4 — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) September 28, 2026 The Bengals defense was able to get a stop and hold the Steelers to just 3 points on the possession. Dexter Lawrence recorded his second sack of the game and allowed the Bengals offense to take the field with over 2 minutes and a chance to tie or win the game. Unfortunately, Joe Burrow and the offense would eventually fumble away their opportunity to pull out a win and a 3-0 start to the season. Dexter Lawrence getting to Rodgers again to force a field goal. Steelers go up 30-27, but now the Bengals offense had a chance to tie or win the game with a little over 2 minutes left. pic.twitter.com/eGpRIcjgnB — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) September 28, 2026 A frustrating team loss 30-27 with all three phases contributing to it. This revamped Bengals defense will have to right the ship quickly for the Bengals to get a win during week 4 against Jacksonville. The Jaguars beat the defending AFC Champion New England Patriots 35-6 on Sunday. How concerned are you about this defense after they allowed 411 total yards to a Pittsburgh Steelers offense that had been struggling prior to Sunday? Sound off in the comments.

title: Dalton Risner praises Erick All’s effort to recover fumble but admits the Steelers got it
summary: The Cincinnati Bengals did about everything they could to ensure they lost to the Steelers on Sunday. Special teams snafus gave the Steelers 10 points, the defense suddenly couldn’t pressure the quarterback or stop the run, and on the final offensive play of the game, quarterback Joe Burrow was sacked (his only sack) and fumbled […]
full_text: The Cincinnati Bengals did about everything they could to ensure they lost to the Steelers on Sunday. Special teams snafus gave the Steelers 10 points, the defense suddenly couldn’t pressure the quarterback or stop the run, and on the final offensive play of the game, quarterback Joe Burrow was sacked (his only sack) and fumbled the ball away. Pittsburgh’s Sabastian Joseph-Day recovered the ball, and the game was over. Right guard Dalton Risner, who had a solid game otherwise, was credited with giving up that sack on Burrow. While he knew it was recovered by the Steelers immediately, he also saw something that showed how tough the 2026 Bengals are, even when they lose. Risner said he had a good view of the play and Joseph-Day clearly recovered the fumble, was down and being touched, and the play was over. It’s what happened afterward that made him call tight end Erick All “one tough SOB.” All and Tanner Hudson claimed the former recovered the ball , but Risner admitted the Steelers got it first. “Erick All comes running from downfield and finds a little crevice in that pile and literally jumps in there,” Risner said. “After about two minutes of being on the ground, he comes up with the football, bro. Like Erick was the last person on that pile, somehow managed to get in there and take it from a defensive tackle. And that’s just who he is; I love that guy.” The play officially went under review to make sure who recovered the ball, and while it ultimately went to the Steelers, All created a moment where the game wasn’t over yet. It may have been futile, but a player’s willingness to try to make something happen in such circumstances says a lot about their character on the field. Hopefully Sunday was just a minor bump in the road, and the Bengals are back to winning in Week 4. Dalton Risner on whether the #Bengals actually recovered Joe Burrow’s fumble. pic.twitter.com/h5NPnHRWKO — Jay Morrison (@ByJayMorrison) September 28, 2026

title: Bengals injury updates on Bryan Cook, Colbie Young, and Kyle Dugger
summary: The Cincinnati Bengals got bit by the injury bug in Sunday’s 30-27 loss to the Pittsburgh Steelers. It started early, when rookie wide receiver Colbie Young exited the game with a knee injury early in the first quarter. Young caught one pass for a two-yard gain before limping to the sideline and not returning. With […]
full_text: CINCINNATI, OHIO - JULY 29: Zac Taylor the head coach of the Cincinnati Bengals talks to the media during the Cincinnati Bengals Training Camp at Kettering Health Practice Fields on July 29, 2026 in Cincinnati, Ohio. (Photo by Andy Lyons/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Cincinnati Bengals got bit by the injury bug in Sunday’s 30-27 loss to the Pittsburgh Steelers. It started early, when rookie wide receiver Colbie Young exited the game with a knee injury early in the first quarter. Young caught one pass for a two-yard gain before limping to the sideline and not returning. With Andrei Iosivas out, Young could have been in line for a bigger role. While hopeful it isn’t a long-term injury, head coach Zac Taylor did confirm that Young will miss Week 4 vs. the Jacksonville Jaguars. The safety room took a hit as well. In the first half, Bryan Cook left the game with an ankle injury, but remained on the sidelines and came back into the game for a few plays, with his right ankle taped up. He tried to gut it out, but the injury was apparent. Kyle Dugger, who replaced him, also got banged up and could be seen limping on the field between plays. Both players will be monitored throughout the week, per Taylor. A tough break for several defensive backs, who will be tasked with slowing down a Jaguars offense that scored 35 points on the New England Patriots in Week 3. Hopefully, they can all suit up this week, but they are definitely names to watch as the week progresses.

title: Tacario Davis could see more work following Jalen Davis injury
summary: The Bengals may have a little more on their plate to figure out at the nickel cornerback spot heading into Week 4. Veteran defensive back Jalen Davis left Sunday’s 30-27 loss to the Steelers with a hamstring injury, and while the Bengals initially listed him as questionable to return, the injury could have an impact […]
full_text: CINCINNATI, OH - AUGUST 22: Cincinnati Bengals cornerback Tacario Davis (20) walks off the field before the preseason game between the Chicago Bears and the Cincinnati Bengals at Paycor Stadium on August 22, 2026 in Cincinnati, OH. (Photo by Ian Johnson/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Bengals may have a little more on their plate to figure out at the nickel cornerback spot heading into Week 4. Veteran defensive back Jalen Davis left Sunday’s 30-27 loss to the Steelers with a hamstring injury, and while the Bengals initially listed him as questionable to return, the injury could have an impact beyond the remainder of the game. That could mean an opportunity for rookie cornerback Tacario Davis. Jalen’s injury occurred early in the third quarter. He’s been the primary backup behind Dax Hill at the nickel spot, while Tacario has seen limited defensive action through the first three games. During his Monday press conference following Sunday’s loss, head coach Zac Taylor did not give a definitive update on Jalen, saying only that he will be monitored this week. As for Tacario, Taylor offered this: “He’s got room for improvement, but he’s got a good attitude about it.” The immediate indication is that Tacario will see more snaps for as long as Jalen is sidelined. And frankly, this is exactly the kind of opportunity the Bengals were hoping their young defensive backs would eventually get. However, it’s not the scenario (injury) that they would have hoped for. Tacario showed enough during the preseason to earn his way onto the roster, including a strong showing in the preseason finale against Philadelphia. Now, with a veteran potentially out, the rookie could be asked to take on a much larger role than he has had to this point. The Bengals already have Dax Hill, DJ Turner II, and others available in the secondary, but losing Jalen would remove another experienced option from Al Golden’s defensive puzzle. Josh Newton was a healthy scratch on Sunday, so expect him to be active if Jalen misses time. We’ll have to see how serious the hamstring issue is before knowing just how much this changes the rotation. But if Jalen misses time, Tacario should get a chance to show that his preseason promise can translate when the games actually count. And that’s a pretty important opportunity for the rookie.

title: 3 things we learned from the Bengals’ sloppy loss to the Steelers
summary: Let’s be honest. Deep down, we all knew this was entirely possible. The Pittsburgh Steelers (2-1) were a wounded animal coming into Sunday, while the Bengals (2-1) were riding high on top of the AFC North. Now they have the exact same records. Here’s what we learned from a sloppy Bengals performance in Pittsburgh. There […]
full_text: Sep 27, 2026; Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, USA; Pittsburgh Steelers defensive tackle Cameron Heyward (97) sacks Cincinnati Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow (9) during the fourth quarterv at Acrisure Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Barry Reeger-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Let’s be honest. Deep down, we all knew this was entirely possible. The Pittsburgh Steelers (2-1) were a wounded animal coming into Sunday, while the Bengals (2-1) were riding high on top of the AFC North. Now they have the exact same records. Here’s what we learned from a sloppy Bengals performance in Pittsburgh. There are some serious coaching issues You can put the blame for the muffed punt directly on Ke’Shawn Williams if you want. But it’s not clear why he was entrusted with that role to begin with (especially when Cincinnati previously had a perfectly reliable returner in Charlie Jones on the roster). But then there was also a roughing the punter penalty on Cedric Johnson, when going for a block wasn’t necessary. And the Bengals committed another six penalties, bringing their season total to 25. Cincinnati’s offense looked stronger than it had all season, but even that fell apart to a familiar theme (an o-line breakdown) on the most important play of the game. Zac Taylor has a serious problem with finishing close games and is now 6-51 when trailing after the third quarter. It’s not easy to come from behind in the NFL, but this seems alarming. The Bengals are 6-51 when trailing after three quarters in the Zac Taylor era. h/t @ByJayMorrison pic.twitter.com/5M3D3Ly7Sx — Chatterbox Sports (@CBoxSports) September 27, 2026 Relying on the heroics of Joe Burrow, Ja’Marr Chase, and Tee Higgins isn’t a real plan. Something needs to change quickly if this team wants to content for a Super Bowl. Dexter Lawrence can’t single-handedly fix the defense Though it honestly felt like that his first two weeks on the Bengals. The big nose tackle had yet another stellar game, this time finally getting official credit for a couple of sacks. Watching Darnell Washington FINALLY be utilized today as a legitimate playmaker was so refreshing to see. Teams are SCARED to tackle him: pic.twitter.com/i8ozTCfRRq — Logan Arblaster (@ArblasterLogan) September 27, 2026 But the overall tackling was back to 2023 and 2024 levels for major stretches of the game, with Jaylen Warren, Darnell Washington, and Roman Wilson all getting receptions of 30 or more yards and Warren also ripping off a 35 yard run. There is no clear favorite in the AFC North Yes, it’s just three weeks, but, to put things in perspective, the Bengals are now tied with the Cleveland Browns for the best record in the division (and, of course, the Steelers and the Baltimore Ravens). At least three of the teams are serious threats to contend for the division title, but, more importantly, all four will absolutely feel like they can win against any of the other three. The Steelers came into the Week 3 matchup against the Bengals with Aaron Rodgers looking like he was already mentally checked out. Meanwhile, Warren hadn’t even reached 50 rushing yards in his first two games. All of a sudden, both looked like stars on Sunday, which is largely because of Mike McCarthy’s game plan, but also the adrenaline boost Steelers players get when they go up against their hated rivals. In case there was any doubt, Cincinnati cannot take any opponent, especially an AFC North one, lightly.
