title: Packers will face rookie QB Jalen Daniels for Buccaneers in Week 4
summary: On Monday, the Tampa Bay Buccaneers confirmed what football fans expected: Baker Mayfield will miss the team’s Week 4 matchup with the Green Bay Packers due to a dislocated thumb. Bucs head coach Todd Bowles confirmed the injury to the media in his Monday press conference, and said that they expect Mayfield to be out […]
full_text: JACKSONVILLE, FLORIDA - AUGUST 28: Jalon Daniels #10 of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers runs the ball during the second quarter of their preseason matchup against the Jacksonville Jaguars at EverBank Stadium on August 28, 2026 in Jacksonville, Florida. (Photo by Parker S. Freedman/Getty Images) | Getty Images On Monday, the Tampa Bay Buccaneers confirmed what football fans expected: Baker Mayfield will miss the team’s Week 4 matchup with the Green Bay Packers due to a dislocated thumb. Bucs head coach Todd Bowles confirmed the injury to the media in his Monday press conference, and said that they expect Mayfield to be out “a minimum of three weeks.” Tampa Bay had just two quarterbacks on their 53-man roster, along with one on the practice squad. Jalon Daniels, an undrafted rookie out of Kansas, had backed up Mayfield through the first three games and is expected to start in Sunday’s game against Green Bay, while Easton Stick, a veteran journeyman, is likely to get called up from the practice squad as Daniels’ backup. So what exactly is Daniels? For those who did not follow the Jayhawks the last few years and did not take a deep dive into the depths of this year’s draftable quarterbacks, here’s a quick primer. Daniels is a short, mobile quarterback, who made his name for the Jayhawks as a dual threat. At the 2026 NFL Combine, Daniels measured in at just under 6-foot-1 and 219 pounds, and he ran a 4.65-second 40-yard dash, which illustrates his scrambling ability. Daniels enrolled at Kansas for the 2020 season and he started six of their nine games as a true freshman in the COVID-shortened campaign. He only managed 718 passing yards, then split the starting job as a sophomore in 2021. He eventually took over the starting job in 2022 and despite dealing with some injuries then on (particularly in 2023, when he only played in three games), the job was his when healthy and he stayed in Lawrence for all six of his college seasons. In the 2022, 2024, and 2025 seasons, Daniels started 9, 12, and 12 games and passed for at least 2,000 yards and ran for 400-plus each year, demonstrating his mobility. Interestingly, however, the Jayhawks’ best season in that span came in 2023, the year when he was injured for much of the season, when they finished 9-4 and ranked 23rd in the final AP poll of the season. That Jayhawks team ran the offense through running back Devin Neal, while senior Jason Bean stepped in for the injured Daniels to lead the team to a win over UNLV in the Guaranteed Rate Bowl. NFL.com’s Lance Zierlein’s prospect notes indicate Daniels has “enough arm talent” to make some deep throws and highlights his athleticism and mobility as strengths. However, accuracy and reading coverages appear to be issues, and Zierlein notes that Daniels’ footwork “unravels on occasion, even without heavy pressure.” With a player like this under center for the opposition, expect Packers defensive coordinator Jonathan Gannon to get creative with his pressure schemes. Mayfield took a whopping 13 sacks over the first three games of the season, and although he tends to have a moderately high sack rate for his career, a 12% rate is absurd and indicative of a line that is allowing significant pressure. Meanwhile, Daniels entered Sunday’s game against Minnesota late, going 0-for-3 passing with an interception. A quarterback matchup like this could be just what the doctor ordered for the Packers’ defense to bounce back after an abysmal showing last Thursday night against the Atlanta Falcons.
author: Evan "Tex" Western

title: A history of Mekhi Becton, the Packers’ latest offensive line addition
summary: The Packers are making a big move in signing Mekhi Becton, but then again, every move involving Becton is big. He’s a massive human being even in a game dominated by other massive human beings. That’s the book on Becton: he’s monstrously big, but the eternally open question is whether or not he can parlay […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PA - JANUARY 12: Mekhi Becton #77 of the Philadelphia Eagles lines up before the snap during an NFL football wild card playoff game against the Green Bay Packers at Lincoln Financial Field on January 12, 2025 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Packers are making a big move in signing Mekhi Becton , but then again, every move involving Becton is big. He’s a massive human being even in a game dominated by other massive human beings. That’s the book on Becton: he’s monstrously big, but the eternally open question is whether or not he can parlay that size into effective work on the offensive line. It worked out at times with the New York Jets. It worked wonderfully well for the Philadelphia Eagles. It failed in spectacular fashion with the Los Angeles Chargers. What will the Packers’ phase of Becton’s career hold? Becton was a three-year starter for the Louisville Cardinals, ending his career having appeared in 35 games over three seasons. Though he got the ultimate offensive line honor in 2018 ( a specially called big man touchdown play ), his 2019 effort earned him the biggest accolade of his career: a first-team All-ACC nod for his work in the Cardinals’ 8-5 season. Declaring early for the 2020 NFL Draft, Becton was a much-debated prospect. Though his athleticism and physical upside was never in doubt ( he posted a 9.85 Relative Athletic Score ), scouts were split on his technical abilities. Bleacher Report called him “ the biggest boom-or-bust prospect in the 2020 draft class ” for that reason, while Pro Football Network questioned whether or not he had the foot speed to make it as a left tackle in the NFL . But he had his backers, too, preeminent draft scout Dane Brugler of The Athletic among them. He correctly predicted Becton would land with the New York Jets , who took him with the 11th overall selection, banking on his athletic ability to overcome whatever sloppy tendencies might exist in his game. Early on, Brugler looked prescient. Becton appeared in 14 games as a rookie, starting 13 — all at left tackle — and he graded out fairly well, too. Pro Football Focus ranked him as the 30th best tackle (out of 60) to play at least 500 snaps in 2020. That’s not a world-beating ranking, but it’s solid enough for a rookie going against NFL athletes for the first time. Unfortunately, that would be the high point for Becton’s Jets career. An early season injury in practice limited him to a single game in 2021, and an avulsion fracture in 2022 ended his season in training camp. Then, in 2023, Becton had a front row seat to Aaron Rodgers’ torn Achilles tendon. (He wasn’t to blame, having switched to right tackle by that point, but was one of the two players closest to Rodgers when it happened.) Predictably, Rodgers’ injury tanked the Jets’ season, and Becton left town the next offseason, a free agent for the first time in his NFL career. He’d land in about the best possible situation, signing with the Philadelphia Eagles and beginning the comeback arc of his career. Originally signed as a swing tackle option, an injury to guard Tyler Steen opened the door at right guard, and Becton stepped through. The move might not have happened had the Eagles’ offensive line coach not been Jeff Stoutland, w ho’d tended toward playing bigger-than-average players at guard . Though initially skeptical, having never played guard before, Becton embraced the move and thrived. “I’m having fun learning as much as I can about what Stout [Jeff Stoutland] wants from us. He pushes us to be the best, to bring out the best in us. That’s what I want,” Becton said . His size, atypical at guard, was an asset. Center Cam Jurgens, facing the tall task of replacing Jason Kelce, loved having Becton next to him at guard. “Mekhi’s got long arms, insanely long arms and he’s able to use them really well,” Jurgens said . “It’s super helpful, especially when you’re going into the run game and he’s able to put those long arms on people and keep people at a distance.” Counting playoffs, he’d play 1,158 snaps at guard for the Eagles across 19 games, starting every single one. That included two wins over the Packers and, even more importantly, a Super Bowl championship. And his mass paid dividends in the ground game; he posted a run blocking grade of 70.3 in 2024, per PFF — higher than any of the guards the Packers played that year, and higher than that of Aaron Banks, for that matter, then a member of the San Francisco 49ers. Becton parlayed his solid season and Super Bowl title into a two-year, $20 million contract with the Los Angeles Chargers, where things promptly fell apart again. Becton played 794 snaps in 15 games (with 14 starts), but posted career-worst grades overall, as a pass blocker, and as a run blocker. The Chargers cut him this spring, saving $9.7 million against the cap in the process. However, there’s more to the story of his 2025 season. The Athletic’s Matt Schneidman reports Becton was dealing with an undiagnosed torn labrum in Los Angeles , which required surgery this past March, which may explain both why he played so poorly last year and why nobody showed any interest in him in the first waves of free agency. It’s worth noting, though, that Belton never appeared on the injury report with a designation tied to his shoulder; it was only knee issues and a concussion that popped up during the course of the season. I’m not saying Becton wasn’t hurt, for the record, but rather that we should have a healthy grain of salt when looking to the injury as a potential factor in his poor play. Becton is also reportedly down to 345 pounds, which would be the lightest listed weight of his career, but still heavier than any other player on the Packers’ offensive line. The Packers have consciously tried to get bigger up front over the past couple of seasons, and if that’s still the goal, you can’t do much better than Becton, even at a lighter weight. Our Justis Mosqueda identified Becton as a potential cap casualty to watch back in March, and his prognostication has ultimately come to pass. Whether or not the former first round pick can resurrect the offensive line remains to be seen, but as with the Laken Tomlinson signing, the Packers aren’t exactly in a position to turn down any help.
author: Jon Meerdink

title: Packers keep adding veteran offensive linemen by signing Mekhi Becton
summary: At least this can be said for the Green Bay Packers’ front office: they are trying to do something to address the team’s issues on the offensive line. A few days after signing former Pro Bowl guard Laken Tomlinson off the Dallas Cowboys’ practice squad over the weekend, the Packers are adding another former first-round […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PA - JANUARY 12: Mekhi Becton #77 of the Philadelphia Eagles lines up before the snap during an NFL football wild card playoff game against the Green Bay Packers at Lincoln Financial Field on January 12, 2025 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images At least this can be said for the Green Bay Packers’ front office: they are trying to do something to address the team’s issues on the offensive line. A few days after signing former Pro Bowl guard Laken Tomlinson off the Dallas Cowboys’ practice squad over the weekend, the Packers are adding another former first-round draft pick to the roster. Joining Tomlinson in Green Bay will be Mekhi Becton, a six-year NFL veteran and the 11th overall pick in the 2020 NFL Draft out of the University of Louisville. Jeremy Fowler of ESPN reported that Becton worked out for the Packers on Monday morning and then signed with the team almost immediately. Becton has been a primary starter for three different teams over the last three years, spending 2025 with the Los Angeles Chargers after starting at right guard for the Super Bowl-winning Philadelphia Eagles during the 2024 season. He started his career with the New York Jets, but he missed almost all of the 2021 season with a torn ACL. He then injured the same knee in training camp the following season and missed the entirety of the 2022 campaign before returning to play 16 games in 2023. With the Chargers, Becton struggled a bit, but he played 16 of the team’s possible 18 games with 15 starts, all at right guard. Becton also played against the Packers twice as an Eagle in 2024, playing every snap at right guard in the Eagles’ Week 1 and Wild Card victories. The 6-foot-7, 360-pounder becomes a real candidate to step in and get immediate playing time, possibly competing with Tomlinson for snaps at guard. Interestingly, Becton and Tomlinson overlapped as teammates with the Jets for two seasons, during the 2022 and 2023 seasons. As noted earlier, Becton missed the entire 2022 campaign, but the two started at left tackle and left guard, respectively, during the 2023 season. Also involved in the Jets’ organization that year were a slew of former Packers: former Green Bay offensive coordinator Nathaniel Hackett held the OC and playcalling duties in New York, while wide receivers Allen Lazard, Randall Cobb, and Malik Taylor and quarterback Tim Boyle were on that team as well. There was one other notable former Packer on the Jets’ roster that year: 2023 was the year that the Packers traded Aaron Rodgers to the Jets as well, though his season ended just a few plays into Week 1 when he tore his Achilles tendon. The signings of both players will likely appear on the NFL’s transaction wire on Monday afternoon. Expect the Packers to make room for these two players on the 53-man roster by placing Zach Bako-Bewele and Jayden Reed on injured reserve. UPDATE: Tomlinson’s addition to the Packers’ 53-man roster was made official on Monday, as was Becton’s signing. However, the Packers have signed Becton to the practice squad, not to the 53-man roster, at least for the time being. This means that the Packers only needed to free up one spot on the 53 for Tomlinson, which they did by placing Bako-Bewele on injured reserve.

title: Packers vs. Buccaneers odds: Opening lines for Week 4 matchup
summary: Before the Tampa Bay Buccaneers played the Minnesota Vikings on Sunday in Week 3, the Green Bay Packers looked like they might be headed out on the road in week 4 as underdogs. The Bucs had not been a good team through their first two games, starting out 0-2, but then again neither had the […]
full_text: TAMPA, FLORIDA - SEPTEMBER 27: Baker Mayfield #6 of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers is sacked by the Minnesota Vikings during the second half of the game at Raymond James Stadium on September 27, 2026 in Tampa, Florida. (Photo by Mike Carlson/Getty Images) | Getty Images Before the Tampa Bay Buccaneers played the Minnesota Vikings on Sunday in Week 3, the Green Bay Packers looked like they might be headed out on the road in week 4 as underdogs. The Bucs had not been a good team through their first two games, starting out 0-2, but then again neither had the Packers, who fell to 1-2 with an abysmal loss in their home opener on Thursday Night Football in Week 3. But then, the Bucs went and lost to the Minnesota Vikings at home on Sunday afternoon, losing starting quarterback Baker Mayfield to a dislocated thumb late in that game. Even with Mayfield playing for most of the game, however, the Buccaneers’ offense gained just 243 net yards and went 2-for-17 on third down. With undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels expected to make his first NFL start, the Vegas line now swings in favor of the Packers against a struggling 0-3 Buccaneers team. As of Monday morning, FanDuel Sportsbook has the Packers favored by 3.5 points in Week 4. For a Packers team that has mightily struggled on offense, this might seem to be a shock. But the Bucs’ quarterback situation and their anemic offense in general is the reason for this projection, more so than even the Packers’ own struggles. Still, the books expect a less-than-exciting, low-scoring affair on Sunday, with the total points line set at just 39.5. Mayfield isn’t the only key player dealing with injury for the Bucs. Rookie first-round pick Rueben Bain, Jr. missed Sunday’s game with a groin injury, while linebacker Josiah Trotter also was ruled out with a shoulder issue. Keep an eye on Mayfield’s injury throughout this week, however, as he will likely be the biggest single factor for the spread. If he is able to play in Week 4, that would surely shift the line significantly back towards a more even matchup. History isn’t overly kind to the Packers in recent meetings with the Bucs, however. The Packers are 2-3 in their last five road games against the Buccaneers, dating back to 2008, and they are 1-3 in their last four overall, including a playoff loss in the 2020 NFC Championship Game. However, Green Bay did win 14-12 in the most recent meeting at Raymond James Stadium back in 2022. Go Pack Go—wherever you go! summary: The Green Bay Packers have been hammered by injuries to start this season, particularly on the offensive line. full_text: TAMPA, FLORIDA - SEPTEMBER 27: Jalon Daniels #10 of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers makes his NFL debut with a pass attempt against the Minnesota Vikings during the second half of the game at Raymond James Stadium on September 27, 2026 in Tampa, Florida. (Photo by Mike Carlson/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Green Bay Packers have been hammered by injuries to start this season, particularly on the offensive line. That has led to a 1-2 start with Jordan Love taking 8 sacks through three games — a number that could well be more with how much pressure his line has allowed in front of him. However, a pair of factors over the next two weeks could actually make the Packers’ matchups with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers and Chicago Bears an opportunity to get their season back on track. First, both opponents’ quarterbacks are dealing with injuries. Baker Mayfield and Caleb Williams look like both could miss the upcoming games against the Packers, leaving Green Bay’s defense to face some inexperienced quarterbacks. Jonathan Gannon will surely dial up some creative pressures in these next two games in that case to try to force mistakes. Meanwhile, those two teams have some of the worst pass rush groups in the NFL. An easier pair of matchups is something the Packers’ offensive line desperately needs after giving up those 8 sacks, 20 QB hits, and a whopping 37 pressures through the first three games, according to Pro Football Reference. Green Bay needs to win these next two games if they have any hope of turning this season around. Thankfully, the situation looks a lot more favorable for them, if they can get their own issues a bit better sorted out. title: Houston Texans Opening Odds vs Dallas Cowboys
summary: The Texas-sized showdown of the Houston Texans (0-3) against the Dallas Cowboys (1-2) is more exciting on paper than in reality. These two teams have struggled out of the gate and are desperate to turn their seasons around in Week 4. FanDuel has you covered whether you’re from Texas or just looking for some additional […]
full_text: The Texas-sized showdown of the Houston Texans (0-3) against the Dallas Cowboys (1-2) is more exciting on paper than in reality. These two teams have struggled out of the gate and are desperate to turn their seasons around in Week 4. FanDuel has you covered whether you’re from Texas or just looking for some additional action this weekend. Below are the Spread, Moneyline, and Over/Under heading into the game against Dallas. The Spread: Texans -2.5 Considering the Texans are 0-3 and haven’t looked competent on offense since the first half of the first game of the season, this is an astonishing line. I cannot imagine Reliant Stadium will be rocking. If anything, this could be a stadium quick to turn on the team if they fall behind. The Cowboys, though 1-2 entering the contest, have scored 20, 37, and 31 points. Houston hasn’t proved it can move the ball against even the weakest of defenses, as seen against the Colts, which doesn’t bode well against a high-powered offense. Until the Texans win a game, take the opponent and the extra points for insurance. Moneyline: Texans -136 The Texans are 3-4 all time against the Cowboys. Given their recent struggles and lack of anything expected to change, It’s hard to believe the Texans can steal a win against the Cowboys. DeMeco Ryans on his coaching impact & if they have any plans to make changes on the offensive side of the ball including Nick Caley calling plays: “Nope my impact is just fine.” “Nope, we’re all in this thing together.” pic.twitter.com/a2AIzDvfbA — Houston Stressans (@TexansCommenter) September 28, 2026 What will be interesting to watch is if the defense can keep a lid on the Cowboys passing attack. Derek Stingley Jr. and Kamari Lassiter have not impressed and are concerning when paired up against CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens. At this juncture in the seasons, it’s difficult to believe the Texans will outright beat an opponent. Wait till they are, hopefully, on a role before taking them straight up. Over/Under: 47.5 The Texans went well under last week’s line of 44.5 against the Colts as well as the 45.5 mark against the Bengals, but managed to blow out the Over/Under against the Bills in a high-scoring matchup. This Over/Under is a tad elevated compared to the two previous lines, most likely due to the high-octane offense in Dallas. That said, Houston’s current offensive form doesn’t bode well to betting the over. If Nico Collins is back in the lineup, then the over is something to consider. Collins’ presence unlocks the passing game and lessens the pressure on the run. The Cowboys defense have allowed a bevy of points thus far. They’ve given up 28, 20, and 34 points in their three matchups. Given how porous their defense has been AND if Nico Collins is set to go Sunday, then take the Over in a competitive and integral matchup between two teams vying to keep their seasons alive early in the 2026 campaign.

title: The Day After the Day After: Houston Texans fall 19-17 to the Indianapolis Colts
summary: The Day After the Day After…when the raw, immediate emotions from the aftermath of a game diminish into the realm of clarity and the proverbial (or literal) hangover no longer haunts the mind. With that, a review of Week 3: Is Ed Ingram that critical to the O-line? Nico Collins’ absence the past two games […]
full_text: INDIANAPOLIS, INDIANA - SEPTEMBER 27: Keenan Allen #10 of the Indianapolis Colts reacts after catching the ball for a first down during the first half of the game against the Houston Texans at Lucas Oil Stadium on September 27, 2026 in Indianapolis, Indiana. (Photo by Johnnie Izquierdo/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Day After the Day After…when the raw, immediate emotions from the aftermath of a game diminish into the realm of clarity and the proverbial (or literal) hangover no longer haunts the mind. With that, a review of Week 3: Is Ed Ingram that critical to the O-line? Nico Collins’ absence the past two games is undeniable, as Stroud is sans his biggest weapon/security blanket, especially in the red zone. Yet, maybe a bigger loss is Ed Ingram. Also out these past two games, the right side of the line has been mediocre at best and beyond horrid at worst. The big 4th down stuffs in the past two games came from defensive penetration along the right interior of the line on short-yardage run plays. Ingram is not the best pass blocking guard out there (reference how badly he got beat against Buffalo on that final drive of the game), but the Texans did have success running the ball that game. Maybe it was Buffalo’s defense, but Houston rushed for 124 total yards in that game on 32 rushes. Houston has totaled only 130 yards on 30 rushes in the two games since he went out. He might return next week, but groin injuries can be a bit difficult to project. The Final Minutes (again): The difference between victory and defeat is incredibly small in the NFL. The Texans could feel justified in thinking they should be 2-1 vs. 0-3. However, it was actions or inactions in the final minutes that doomed the Texans (again). After going up 17-16 on Marks’ short TD run, the Colts had more than enough time to get into range for the go-ahead FG. Being indoors, they probably wouldn’t need much in total yardage. They got one bonus when Fairbairn could not land his kick short of the end zone. It was close, but the Colts’ returner caught the ball with enough of his body still in the end zone. Thus, the Colts started at the 35. Then, the defense, which had played its best game of the season to date, gave up a 20-yard gain that put the Colts right in FG range. With around a minute left in the game, Houston having all 3 timeouts and the Colts going a bit conservative, Ryans curiously decided to hold on to those, eschewing taking a timeout until 29 seconds left. Ryans seemed to hope for a big defensive stop (not as likely at this point) or a FG miss (not as likely either). Perhaps he takes the timeouts and the Colts still move the ball, but he did his mercurial offense no favors by reducing their possession time. Then the Colts forced Houston to return a kickoff, killing more time. Houston did have the timeout and moved the ball to midfield, but subsequent play-calling and the Colts’ defense limited Houston to a Hail Mary attempt. Much like the Buffalo, Houston had its chances to win at the end, but it didn’t happen on this day….again. Kickoffs…still a work in progress for Houston: Fairbairn is still more prone to kick the ball to the end-zone, generating touchbacks that gives offenses the ball at the 35. If he could get the ball to fall within the landing zone, that increases the chances that Houston could pin opponents further back. Then again, Houston’s kick coverages haven’t been as stellar as in years past. Concurrently, a Houston’s returner had an awkward situation in the first half when he allowed a kick to bounce in the landing zone, but then corralled the ball to take a knee in the end zone. Houston only got the ball at the 20 for that, which did not help the offense. These are small things, but it is small things adding up to the 0-3 start. The Critical Play: 1st Quarter, 9:47, HOU Ball, 4th and 1 at the IND 31 (Montgomery rush to the right for no gain) Another 4th and short inside the opponent’s territory. This coming after Will Anderson Jr. gave Houston its first forced turnover inside Colts’ territory. Three plays got Houston 9 yards, bringing them to 4th and 1. Given where the ball was on the field, the Texans could have gone for the FG (a projected 48-yarder indoors). However, you could understand going for the jugular and making a statement. Instead, the Colts’ defensive interior blew up the play for no gain. Indy used the subsequent possession to take a 3-0 lead and strategic control of the game. Yes, this was early in the game, and Houston did come back to take a brief lead late, but that play represented so much wrong about the team right now. The Texans are 0-for-5 in their last five 4th Down attempts. Weren’t Smith, Teller, Montgomery, et al supposed to fix this? FUN WITH NUMBERS: 53%: Combined conversion percentage by the Colts on 3rd/4th down attempts. The Colts went 7 of 15 on 3rd downs and 2 for 2 on 4th downs. This kept drives alive, helped in time of possession, field position…basically all of the big numbers. Those extra conversions helped the Colts run 20 more plays than Houston, making a significant impact on the game. 1: Number of NFL teams all-time that made the playoffs starting 0-4 . Think this upcoming game against Cowboys wasn’t big enough? If the Texans lose this game, they fall to 0-4. In the Super Bowl era, only 1 team ever started 0-4 and made the playoffs: The 1992 San Diego Chargers, who started 0-4, then went on to win 11 of their last 12 to make the postseason. Houston is the only squad this century to start 0-3 (twice) and make the postseason. Matching that Chargers team wasn’t part of the plan coming into the year…oh, and that Chargers team? Lost in the Divisional Round. GAME BALLS: DE Will Anderson, Jr. 7 total tackles (5 solo)/2.5 sacks/3 TFLs/2 FFs/1 FR. After a relatively slow start against Buffalo, Anderson is back to full-on nightmare mode. Houston doesn’t take the lead in the 4th without his forced fumble. Had Houston held on to win, that play would have been the critical moment. Colts PK Spencer Shrader: 4 for 4 on FG, including two 50+ yarders, 1/1 on XPs. On a day when the Colts desperately needed to snap their 9-game losing streak (and 4-game home losing streak to Houston), he gave them 13 points….and all with an injured groin, and coming back from a missed season due to an ACL/MCL injury. SHOULD BE FORCED TO LISTEN TO THE B-SIDE TRACKS OF ALL OF THE LATE JIM IRSAY BAND’S GREATEST HITS ON REPEAT WHILE ONLY EATING FROM MRBEAST BURGER. C Evan Brown: The Houston O-line interior, notably the right interior, did not represent itself well in this game, especially in the 1st half. The Colts’ defensive interior had their way with that side of Houston’s O-line, from the key 4th down stuff in the 1st Quarter to surrendering three sacks. The play somewhat improved in the second half, with even some of the best Texans’ runs coming along the right side of the line. However, Brown had more bad than good to his ledger. HC DeMeco Ryans: This season seems to showcasing the worst of Ryans’ coaching style. Questions about his decision-making related to 4th downs and timeouts are getting magnified for a team with championship aspirations. Then, he had some curious post-game comments about a unified locker room. Perhaps the standard coach-speak, but for a team that is once again 0-3, you wonder if there are some other issues bubbling underneath (especially with recent comments from Stroud about the offense). If there are divisions or locker-room grumblings at 0-3, they generate news. At 0-4, they become the headlines. Now 0-3 and 0-1 in the division, Houston returns to Reliant to resume their interstate (or interregional battle) with the Dallas/Deep Southern Oklahoma/Deep Southwestern Arkansas Cowboys in a must-win game for both teams for so, so many reasons. Kickoff is slated for this coming Sunday at noon CDT on Fox.

title: Horsepower or Horseplay? Individual highlights from Week 3’s big victory vs. Texans
summary: The Indianapolis Colts (1-2) picked up their first win of the 2026 regular season and against their AFC South divisional rival, the also still winless Houston Texans (0-3), no less. The Colts led nearly the entire way until with 4:45 left in regulation, Texans edge Will Anderson Jr. strip-sacked Colts starting quarterback Daniel Jones again, […]
full_text: INDIANAPOLIS, IN - SEPTEMBER 27: Indianapolis Colts cornerback Justin Walley (27) looks on during the NFL game between the Houston Texans and the Indianapolis Colts on September 27, 2026, at Lucas Oil Stadium in Indianapolis, Indiana. (Photo by Michael Allio/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Indianapolis Colts (1-2) picked up their first win of the 2026 regular season and against their AFC South divisional rival, the also still winless Houston Texans (0-3), no less. The Colts led nearly the entire way until with 4:45 left in regulation, Texans edge Will Anderson Jr. strip-sacked Colts starting quarterback Daniel Jones again, which led to the Texans taking the lead, 17-16, on an ensuing scoring drive that was capped off by Houston running back Woody Marks’ 1-yard touchdown run. To their credit, the Colts didn’t quit though. Jones made a big 20-yard completion to veteran wideout Laquon Treadwell, and after consecutive Jonathan Taylor runs, found Keenan Allen for a 6-yard reception that set up kicker Spencer Shrader for the game-winning 53-yard field goal with a little over 15 seconds left to spare. Without further ado, here are our individual performances to highlight, both good and bad: HORSEPLAY Colts Offensive Line: Make no mistake about it, the Texans are a formidable defense foe. The Colts offensive line had their hands full with their front seven featuring the star pass rushing edge pairing of Will Anderson Jr. and Danielle Hunter. Jones was pressured on 46.3% of his dropbacks, which was the 3rd most in the NFL during Week 3 t0-date. In particular, starting right tackle Jalen Travis, despite an initial solid start to the 2026 campaign, clearly struggled containing Anderson Jr. in pass blocking. Specifically, Travis surrendered 3.0 sacks, 11 QB pressures, 7 hurries, and 1 QB hit in pass protection for what was clearly a long afternoon for the Colts’ first-year full-time starter at right tackle. Rather than single out Travis individually here though, I was a bit disappointed that the Colts also couldn’t get the run game going either. Colts star running back Jonathan Taylor, was largely bottled up all afternoon, averaging just 3.0 yards per carry on 23 carries, with his lone big run being called back because of a Laquon Treadwell hold. The Texans are really good up front, but even with the mismatch in pass blocking, and conceding that the Texans are elite in getting after the quarterback off the edges, I expected the Colts to be a bit better in the offensive trenches, particularly in run blocking collectively as a unit. QB Daniel Jones: I’ll hedge a bit here, as see below. However, Jones threw a duck under duress that that Texans safety Reed Blankenship easily intercepted early in the 3rd quarter , and had 3 fumbles on the afternoon, two of which were caused by Anderson Jr. strip-sacks (see above) and lost to Houston. It’s hard to simulate being physically hit in the moment, but ball security has been a consistent issue for Jones, even dating back to his days as a franchise quarterback hopeful with the New York Giants. He has to anticipate or better feel that incoming pocket pressure and either throw the ball away or go down safely and protect the football (like Peyton Maning infamously used to do). He can’t put the ball on the deck that many times, let alone commit three turnovers entirely. It’s typically hard to win that way. HORSEPOWER QB Daniel Jones (Contd.): To his credit, when under constant pressure (which was 46.3% of his dropbacks), Jones completed 9 of 15 pass attempts for 115 total passing yards, a passing touchdown, and an interception , meaning he largely performed well when actually pressured (aside from the lone ill-advised thrown duck). Opposing defenses have been bringing the heat against him since really around midseason of last season and forced the Colts to adjust. It was really a mixed bag for Jones on the afternoon collectively, but after another critical strip-sack from Anderson, he did successfully navigate the Colts into scoring position for Shrader’s game-winning field goal with seconds left after two big completions to his wideouts. Colts Wide Receivers: With Alec Pierce out, Downs had a big afternoon for the Colts, catching 5 receptions for 77 total receiving yards with a career high 172 air yards . His teammate, veteran wideout Keenan Allen also stepped up, and showed that he wasn’t two more games from retirement—as it was starting to look the Colts debuting 34-yard wideout had lost another step through his first two starts in Indianapolis. Rather, Allen had 6 receptions for 63 total receiving yards and Indy’s lone TD reception . Colts Defensive Tackles : Colts Pro Bowl veteran defensive tackle DeForest Buckner was a menace in this one, with 7 tackles, 1.5 sacks , a tackle for loss, and 2 QB hits. His defensive tackle counterpart, Ade Adebawore, gave the Texans fits as a sub-package speed pass rushing defensive tackle, finishing with 1.5 sacks , a QB hit, and a QB hurry. That DT duo appears to pretty fearsome pass rushing so far this season. CB Justin Walley: Having clearly endured a lot of growing pains to begin his pro career, and picked on in coverage, Walley had his best game to-date with a number of key pass breakups. He was targeted 6 times against the Texans on Sunday, allowing 4 receptions for just 30 total receiving yards and 2 pass breakups— including a big one in the end zone near midway through the 4th quarter. PK Spencer Shrader : Despite battling a groin injury suffered in pregame warmups, the Colts placekicker was “money” on Sunday afternoon, going a pristine 4 for 4 with makes from 39 yards, 58 yards, 37 yards, and the game-winning 53 yard field goal kick with 16 seconds left in regulation. Shrader not only won the game for the Colts, gutting it out through injury, but arguably saved their season, by avoiding an incredibly challenging 0-3 start that would’ve been difficult to overcome to keep Indy’s AFC playoff hopes very much alive.

title: Jaguars Winners & Losers From Week 3: Jags Deliver Knockout Against New England
summary: How about that for an ass-kicking? After a ho-hum showing against Denver last weekend, the Jacksonville Jaguars and its fans had to spend the entire week debating whether or not this team was cooked just two games into the season. Admittedly, I fell victim to some of that chatter based on how lifeless the team […]
full_text: JACKSONVILLE, FL - SEPTEMBER 27: Runningback Bhayshul Tuten #33 of the Jacksonville Jaguars is defended by Cornerback Charles Woods #22 of the New England Patriots on a running play during the first half of the game at EverBank Stadium on September 27, 2026 in Jacksonville, Florida. (Photo by Don Juan Moore/Getty Images) | Getty Images How about that for an ass-kicking? After a ho-hum showing against Denver last weekend, the Jacksonville Jaguars and its fans had to spend the entire week debating whether or not this team was cooked just two games into the season. Admittedly, I fell victim to some of that chatter based on how lifeless the team looked in Mile High. All the Jags did in response was beat the brakes off of visiting New England , 35-6, getting defending Super Bowl runner-up quarterback Drake Maye benched in the process. Everything that went right against the Cleveland Browns went right Sunday. Basically everything that went wrong against the Broncos corrected itself. The Jags that played Sunday demoralized a team that had aspirations of making it back to the biggest game in sports, doing so from the very moment the two teams both took the field. There’s much to celebrate after that victory. Especially considering it came against THAT franchise. Outside of a dropped pass and a missed field goal, it really couldn’t have gotten much better for the Jags against the Patriots over the weekend. Victory Monday is going to feel a little sweeter this time around. WINNERS Trevor Lawrence There must be something about the river breeze that Trevor Lawrence likes, because he has been nothing short of animalistic when playing in Jacksonville recently. Lawrence balled out against the solid Patriots defense, going 19-29 for 182 and three touchdowns. Despite passing for more yards a week ago (189 versus 182), Lawrence was in complete control for basically the entire game. He was throwing the ball around the yard in ways that he did against Cleveland that not many quarterbacks can. He also essentially opted out of a rushing score which could’ve further bolstered his stat line. In Jacksonville through two games, Lawrence has seven passing touchdowns to just one interception. Maybe it’s the Prowler uniforms. Maybe it’s just the home crowd. But Lawrence is playing some really solid football at home this year. Now he just has to take it on the road next weekend. Most games with 3+ touchdown passes (including playoffs) in Jaguars history: 13 – Trevor Lawrence 12 – Mark Brunell 9 – Blake Bortles 8 – David Garrard pic.twitter.com/b7ZFdnxeKj — Gus Logue (@gus_logue) September 27, 2026 Bhayshul Tuten The beneficiary of Lawrence’s infamous kneel down was Bhayshul Tuten, who has been a sort of quiet portion of this Jags offense thus far. Tuten has put together some bruising, long runs prior to Sunday but hasn’t had a real signature moment. That moment came when he punched in a one-yard score for his second rushing touchdown of the year which put the nail in the coffin of one of the worst losses suffered by the Pats in recent history. The second-year man Tuten led the Jags running backs with a season-high 73 yards on 15 touches. By himself, Tuten came just 10 yards shy of the entire rushing output from New England. He was helped by solid play along the offensive line and a dominant passing game, but he nonetheless played well in his own right. Tuten is coming into his own as a full time starting running back. Early returns are positive for him, even if he isn’t going for over 100 yards every weekend. More touches and more responsibility on offense will probably only serve to help the young starter. At the very least, it’s still very fun to say “toot toooot” anytime he touches the ball. Bhayshul Tuten Week 3 – 48% snaps – 15 carries, 73 yds, TD (4.9 YPC) – 8 routes – 2 targets, 2 catches, 17 yards Continues to be highly productive. Just needs more work to hit on that lofty upside — Michael F. Florio (@MichaelFFlorio) September 27, 2026 Parker Washington If you look at Parker Washington’s stat line and just see the numbers — three catches, 40 yards and one touchdown — you might miss just how good that line was. Washington made back-to-back circus catch plays that resulted in his second touchdown of the season. After making a You Got Moss’d level catch in the back of the end zone that was called back due to a penalty, Washington plucked a bomb of a ball from Lawrence off the ground and caught it across the goal line for six points. This guy is WR1 material. Week after week he continues to make mind-blowing plays all over the field. Chop wood, carry water, catch touchdowns. Which TD catch is better by Parker Washington? pic.twitter.com/FoR45hgvLK — Fitz (@LaurieFitzptrck) September 27, 2026 The Offensive Line It would be hard to give credit to this offense without giving it to the offensive line. The front five for Jacksonville did its job well on Sunday, keeping Lawrence upright and giving the offense enough time to work. Last week, that was seemingly an impossible task. This week against another good front, the Jags excelled. The Jags rushed for over 100 yards and beat a team by 29 points. You don’t do those things without solid line play. For fun, watch Anton Harrison chuck Christian Gonzalez downfield on that Lawrence kneeldown run. Trevor Lawrence really kneeled it at the goal line with over 8 mins left in this game 😂 👀 Anton Harrison just tossed Gonzalez pic.twitter.com/9B6rbcdYEB — Fitz (@LaurieFitzptrck) September 27, 2026 The Defensive Tackles I didn’t think this would be a position group myself or anyone would be talking about anytime soon. But after Sunday’s game it’s hard not to mention both DaVon Hamilton and Ruke Orhorhoro. During the week I wondered aloud if Sunday could be a get-right game for the Jags along the defensive line following a nonexistent showing at Denver. Somewhat randomly, it was the team’s two defensive tackles who accounted for 1.5 sacks and not Travon Walker on Josh Hines-Allen, who I was hoping for big games out of. Orhorhoro was second on the team in tackles with six to go along with a sack. Hamilton was third on the team in tackles with five to go along with half a sack and a fumble recovery. These two dudes were in the middle of everything New England was doing and were a large part of the troubles the Patriots offense was experiencing. The Pats have solid running backs, but ended the days with 83 yards on the ground and no run longer than nine yards. Cleveland and Denver both rushed for more yardage than New England was able to muster Sunday. A big reason why things changed was the big nasties in the middle. The whole defense played great. But a special shoutout has to go to the guys in the middle for getting the work done. Ruke Orhorhoro said he knew this one could be different from the first practice of the week. 💪🏈 #jaguars #duuuva pic.twitter.com/Gt0ZDyanU5 — Action Sports Jax (@ActionSportsJax) September 27, 2026 Liam Coen Though Coen will probably never say it aloud, it has to feel good to beat the piss out of the guy that stole Coach of the Year honors away from you last season. In all facets, Coen’s team dogwalked Vrabel’s. The Jags were leaps and bounds more put together than New England. Neither team played a truly clean game, but Jacksonville did commit less penalties and turned the ball over fewer times. The coach whose team does that typically wins. Coen is the fastest coach in franchise history to reach 15 wins, doing so in just 20 games. That is absolutely bananas to think about considering how many coaches the Jags have had through the years. This team found the right guy. In turn, he is putting the right product on the field. Let him tell you just how well his team played in this clip: That one feels good, Coach 🔥 pic.twitter.com/vNiuMCz7XT — Jacksonville Jaguars (@Jaguars) September 27, 2026 Josh Cameron I’m not sure that when you look at the Jags’ roster, you see a glaring need for wide receiver. Take into account…

title: AP NFL Power Rankings Week 4: Jaguars crash Top 5
summary: New challenge unlocked for quarterback Patrick Mahomes and the Kansas City Chiefs: drive down the field for a game-winning field goal in seven seconds or less, as the Baltimore Ravens accomplished on Sunday in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, against the Dallas Cowboys. The Brazil tilt was the first game in NFL history in which both teams […]
full_text: (Photo by David Rosenblum/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images New challenge unlocked for quarterback Patrick Mahomes and the Kansas City Chiefs : drive down the field for a game-winning field goal in seven seconds or less, as the Baltimore Ravens accomplished on Sunday in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, against the Dallas Cowboys . The Brazil tilt was the first game in NFL history in which both teams scored in the final 10 seconds of a regular-season game. It headlined another wild week of NFL action, which whittled the remaining unbeaten down to only five. And they were all who we expected, right ? Among the 3-0 unbeatens are the Chiefs, Buffalo Bills and San Francisco 49ers —solid franchises of the past decade. Joining the unbeaten club are two of the more surprising teams (represented in our power rankings as such, as they have shot up the rankings)— the Las Vegas Raiders and Minnesota Vikings . I think I speak for all of Chiefs Kingdom when I say it’s fun to look forward to a Chiefs-Raiders matchup again, as they’ll clash in Week 4. The rivalry is more fun when there are stakes and both teams are competitive. But let’s not get too far ahead of ourselves. Let’s see how the AP power rankings shook out this week. Biggest risers: Pittsburgh Steelers, Jacksonville Jaguars , and Cleveland Browns +7 Biggest fallers: New England Patriots and Green Bay Packers -8 This week, along with myself, staff voters were: Caleb James, Ron Kopp Jr., Rocky Magana, and Jared Sapp . 1. San Francisco 49ers (3rd) I’m going to take the low-hanging fruit here. Brock Purdy has looked purdy nice to start this season. He currently holds the second-highest MVP odds. 2. Buffalo Bills (2nd) Five turnovers and still coming away with the win is tough to do. 3. Kansas City Chiefs (4th) I give myself headaches trying to do the mental gymnastics of the haters who believe the conspiracy theories of the refs favoring the Chiefs. 4. Jacksonville Jaguars (11th) In true Jaguars fashion, they aren’t getting the respect they probably deserve. The top two storylines I saw coming out of this one? Josh Hines-Allen fighting a ball boy for Travis Hunter’s first career interception ball. And Trevor Lawrence oddly kneeling down at the 1-yard line instead of scoring a touchdown with eight minutes left. 5. Seattle Seahawks (1st) The return of quarterback Sam Darnold did not spell victory for the ‘Hawks. They suffered their first loss since November 2025. 6. Baltimore Ravens (7th) The flight from Rio back to Baltimore was about 10 hours. The Ravens took possession with seven seconds left in the fourth quarter to win. This means Ravens’ players could have watched their game-winning drive 5,142 times on the flight home. 7. Cincinnati Bengals (5th) The quarterback who supposedly has ice running through his veins falls up short in the 4th quarter—once again. Burrow sure gains a lot of national respect from that Super Bowl loss, checks notes, five years ago. 8. Philadelphia Eagles (6th) This team reminds me of the 2025 Kansas City Chiefs. A team that looks tired, bored, and like the league has figured them out. They need some sort of shakeup. 9. Minnesota Vikings (9th) A 3-0 start, and they shipped quarterback JJ McCarthy to New York for draft capital. The McCarthy selection will go down as one of the biggest blunders in their franchise history. 10. Los Angeles Rams (8th) I’d be livid as a Rams fan over that pass interference call that negated a game-sealing interception in the fourth quarter. But also, maybe don’t give a 16-point halftime lead or throw a pick-six to put you in that do-or-die spot? 11. Chicago Bears (10th) Although Caleb Williams was on the sideline in a hoodie, the Bears still looked like one of the top teams in the NFC with journeyman Case Keenum. 12. Las Vegas Raiders (18th) Alright, respect where it’s due. The Raiders have looked solid to start the year and have already matched their 2025 win total. But enough of that…. IT’S RAIIIIIDERS WEEK. 13. Detroit Lions (14th) Jahmyr Gibbs is an absolute cheat code on the football field. 14. Denver Broncos (13th) How long can this team survive by winning bizarre games with absurd fourth-quarter comebacks? 15. Dallas Cowboys (16th) Such an insane and hilarious way for the Cowboys to lose a football game. 16. Pittsburgh Steelers (23rd) Credit where credit is due. Pittsburgh delivered a solid divisional win. Now they must repeat on a short week against Cleveland. 17. Indianapolis Colts (22nd) The Colts achieved their first win on American soil in almost a full calendar year! 18. New Orleans Saints (17th) Tyler Shough impresses even in the loss. The Saints could really go on a run and surprise some folks. Their next six opponents are the Falcons, Vikings, Giants, Steelers, Browns, and Panthers. A fairly favorable schedule. 19. New York Giants (21st) If your starting quarterback goes down, it’s favorable to have the Tennessee Titans on your schedule the following week. 20. New England Patriots (12th) What is wrong with Drake Maye? Talk about regression. 21. Arizona Cardinals (24th) What would you give up for the Chiefs to acquire Marvin Harrison Jr.? 22. Cleveland Browns (29th) Browns fans really are an unlucky bunch. They’re upset if they lose, yet upset if they win because they hate their current quarterback. 23. Green Bay Packers (15th) Dreadful performance in front of the home crowd at Lambeau. Does head coach Matt LaFleur make it through the season? 24. Houston Texans (19th) This has to be one of the least-talked-about teams in the NFL. On paper, one of the league’s top defenses. But for the second season in a row, they’re 0-3. 25. Atlanta Falcons (31st) An offensive explosion at Lambeau has reignited faint hope in Atlanta. When Bijan Robinson and Drake London are both hot, and they get competent quarterback play, this offense will be tough to slow down. 26. Carolina Panthers (20th) Honestly, I was shocked to find out the Panthers will be gracing our television screens in primetime next week. 27. Washington Commanders (28th) The team is the lowest in our power rankings and is coming off the most solid win in Week 3. But there isn’t much to be excited about with this team. 28. Los Angeles Chargers (25th) Chiefs fans honestly couldn’t lose with the matchup on Sunday. Either the Bills were embarrassed at home by the 0-2 Chargers or the AFC West offseason champs fell to 0-3. I’ll take this result. 29. New York Jets (27th) The Jets honestly look to be improved this season. But from the outset, it is obvious they are already looking forward to 2027. 30. Tampa Bay Buccaneers (26th) Baker joins the list of starting quarterbacks to miss time this season. What a brutal season for the Bucs, and one has to wonder how long head coach Todd Bowles has a job. 31. Miami Dolphins (32nd) With Devon Achane going down for the season, 0-17 may legitimately be in the cards. 32. Tennessee Titans (30th) This season will produce the most depressing country songs ever written in Nashville.

title: Chiefs Mailbag: When will Cyrus Allen see the field?
summary: Welcome back to the Arrowhead Pride Mailbag! Throughout the season, keep watching The Feed for an opportunity to submit your questions about the Kansas City Chiefs! The box score and advanced metrics paint a prettier picture than the Chiefs’ Week 3 24-10 victory over the Miami Dolphins felt as the actual game unfolded. Let’s see […]
full_text: (Photo by Scott Winters/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Welcome back to the Arrowhead Pride Mailbag ! Throughout the season, keep watching The Feed for an opportunity to submit your questions about the Kansas City Chiefs ! The box score and advanced metrics paint a prettier picture than the Chiefs’ Week 3 24-10 victory over the Miami Dolphins felt as the actual game unfolded. Let’s see what’s on our readers’ minds ahead of an unexpected showdown of 3-0 teams Sunday against the Las Vegas Raiders . John 1963 asks: Has quarterback Patrick Mahomes lost faith in wideout Xavier Worthy? Or is he not getting open? Only two targets Sunday. The Chiefs ran only 49 offensive plays on Sunday, making it a difficult sample to determine who the staff may be fading on or who simply didn’t factor into a truncated game plan. I think there is evidence that Tyquan Thornton has more trust on deep routes than Worthy does. Worthy still seems preferred to his fellow speedster on short and intermediate routes, although second-year man Jalen Royals is trending up in that category. Worthy’s 17-yard catch on Sunday was one of the better routes we have seen him run in 2026, and he came down with a high pass from Mahomes. But right now, if the deep throws are going to Thornton and Rashee Rice, and Travis Kelce is getting so much intermediate work and racking up yards after the catch, where is Worthy’s ceiling to improve on a dismal showing so far this season? Worthy and Mahomes both spent the offseason recovering from major surgery, so it’s still a bit early to write off his season. But if he isn’t a more effective piece of the offense coming out of the Week 5 bye, I think you could see his snaps start trending down dramatically. FoxBot2021 asks: If Rashee Rice stays on this kind of pace for 1k and maybe 5-6 TDs, and IF he can walk the straight and narrow, do the Chiefs give Rashee a short 2-3 year deal like they did with Tyreek Hill? The ship has sailed on Rice signing an extension as Hill did in 2019. Hill signed a three-year extension after his final season on his original rookie contract. So the Chiefs really had four seasons to pay off what was then a very controversial three-year deal. Ultimately, the Chiefs traded “The Cheetah” ahead of the extension’s final season in 2022. Rice is now three games into the final season of his rookie deal and set to be one of the most interesting free agent cases next offseason. He is currently on pace for 1076 receiving yards and six touchdowns, with his targets increasing each week. With Rice coming off of his own offseason surgery, I expect his production to rise further from what we are seeing. With running back Kenneth Walker getting significant check-down work in the passing game, Rice’s current 6.4-yard average depth of target would easily set a career high if it holds. That said, the Chiefs will need to have some serious conversations about his future. The wide receiver franchise tag for 2027 is currently estimated ( per Over the Cap ) at $30.9 million. Even if Rice becomes Kansas City’s first 1000 yard wide receiver since 2021, will that really be due to his transcendent talent — or a product of the Chiefs’ offense? Ultimately, I predict that Rice will be a Chief somehow in 2027. I don’t think the Chiefs will eat the salary cap room to use the tag — but I also don’t think teams will line up to pay him as a No. 1 wideout. If he has to prove himself — on and off the field — for one more season, I think Rice will ultimately decide the Chiefs give him the best chance to put up numbers that eventually get him paid. AzDiamond asks: Is defensive coordinator Steve Spagnuolo going to going to give cornerback L’Jarius Sneed the Daniel Sorenson and Ben Nieman treatment or will he play Chris Roland-Wallace and/or rookie Jadon Canady in the slot? The last two weeks, offenses have thrown quick passes to Sneed to mitigate anything the Chiefs might do to pressure the quarterback. His lowest passer rating allowed through three games is 89.6 in Week 1. I am not sure it will become the frustrating situation Chiefs fans saw with Sorensen and Nieman in the past. Spagnuolo clearly has an affinity for Sneed, but that is true for multiple players in the current secondary. With safety Chamarri Conner likely to return in Week 4, I am wondering whether he will take on some of the rotational third-safety role and let Roland-Wallace absorb some of Sneed’s slot work. Roland-Wallace played only 12 defensive snaps on Sunday but led the team’s defenders with a 93.2 coverage grade per Pro Football Focus . One solution I am wondering we’ll see after the bye is Nohl Williams taking on some of the slot work, with veteran Kristian Fulton rotating in outside. After playing the first two weeks in relief of rookie Mansoor Delane heavily, Fulton did not see the field against Miami. Canady has played in more than two-thirds of the special teams snaps the last two weeks, and I am not sure the team can currently spare him unless absolutely necessary. I expect the fourth-round pick to have a learning year in 2026 and compete next summer for a significant defensive role. ChiefTigerfan24 asks: When will we see rookie wide receiver Cyrus Allen get some more offensive snaps? I would like to start working him in to see if the pre-season hype is real or not. I expected Allen to defy expectations and carve out a bigger role early in his rookie season. One complicating factor has been the usage of Royals, who I wasn’t totally sure would even make the team six weeks ago. Royals only has three catches for 17 yards, but all have come in three moments. One went for a touchdown, and his other two catches have yielded first downs. Whenever Allen’s first real action comes, I think it will be unexpected and the result of the Chiefs seeing something they feel he can exploit. With the chance to enter the bye at 4-0 and alone in first place in the AFC standings, I won’t be surprised if they find a situation to use him against the Raiders in Week 4. KaneMarko asks: Pass rush….where has it been the last 2 weeks? As the following two slates have unfolded, I truly believe that the Denver Broncos entered Week 1 with a terrible offensive game plan that made the Chiefs’ pass rush look more ready than it truly was. This is a young defense, and you should expect ups and downs. Pass rush and coverage tend to work hand in hand. The Chiefs are giving up too many frustrating third-down completions. A more dependable linebacker would also help mitigate the success teams are having against Kansas City on play-action. It was concerning to see Dolphins quarterback Malik Willis enter the game as the league’s most sacked quarterback and for the Chiefs not to get to him. It is also still early, and the Chiefs have less mobile quarterbacks on tap for their next two games in Kirk Cousins of the Raiders and the Los Angeles Chargers ’ Justin Herbert. Chief Among Them asks The Vikings, Bills, Raiders, and 49ers all went 3-0 this Sunday, playing 0-3 and 1-2 teams in one-score games. Why is everyone acting like the sky is falling for the Chiefs, who was one of only three teams this week to win by more than one score? There’s really no way to explain to someone who didn’t watch the game why fans are mad. The Chiefs covered a 10-point spread, allowed only three points after halftime. Per Next Gen Stats , Kansas City never had less than a 76% win probability (and never less than 86% in the fourth quarter). Watching the game (and reading real-time reactions), I was reminded of another Week 3 contest against a seemingly terrible opponent. The eventual Super Bowl LVII champion Chiefs traveled to face the Indianapolis Colts for their third game — only to lose 20-17 to a team that ultimately finished the 2022 season 4-12-1. You can acknowledge that the past two weeks have raised some early concerns for the Chiefs while also appreciating that defeating any team by 14 points is a difficult…

Sloppy Wins Are Becoming A Kansas City Calling Card | Yahoo! Sports But there’s another side to this. After that, though, the Chiefs get the Seattle Seahawks and a road tilt against the Denver Broncos, and if Kansas City isn’t executing the way they did during that first win over the Broncos, those little things will suddenly matter a lot more. Kansas City Chiefs HC Andy Reid gives latest injury updates on Josh Simmons, Chamarri Conner after Week 3 win vs. Miami Dolphins | A to Z Sports “I’ll tell you what,” Reid began. “I will let you guys know when Josh (Simmons) is coming back. I’ll be the first to tell you. So we’ll just see how that all works out.” Chiefs fans want to know whether Simmons will make his debut in Week 4, mainly because if he doesn’t, the team will have missed a chance to place him on injured reserve. NFL rules require players placed on injured reserve to miss at least four weeks before they can return to practice, be designated to return, and play in a game. 10 Quick Facts Following the Chiefs Week 3 Win Over Miami | Upon Further Review | The Mothership Quarterback Patrick Mahomes moved past Joe Montana in terms of career touchdown passes. Mahomes tallied his 274th career touchdown pass on Sunday, moving him past Joe Montana for 20th on the all-time list. It all helped Mahomes earn his 115th career start (including the playoffs), matching Tom Brady for the most victories through 150 starts in NFL history. Mahomes also now has 83 career games with multiple touchdown passes, which leads the NFL by eight games since 2018. Ex-Chiefs star expected to make ‘full recovery’ after scary injury | Chiefs Wire The former Wisconsin Badgers standout was a member of Kansas City’s Super Bowl LVII and LVIII rosters and played a key role in Steve Spagnuolo’s defense between 2022 and 2025. NFL insider Jordan Schultz shared the latest update on Chenal’s status in a post to his official Twitter account on September 28: According to Schultz, Chenal has feeling in all of his extremities, which bodes well for his recovery timeline. Around the NFL Case Keenum surprises in Bears’ win. What’s wrong with Eagles’ offense? | The Athletic Keenum, 38, filling in for the injured Caleb Williams, was impressive in his first NFL start since 2023, completing 24 of 34 passes for 247 yards and TDs to Luther Burden III and Kalif Raymond. His 1-yard run in the fourth quarter put the game on ice. The Eagles held the Bears’ running game in check after getting run over in a Black Friday loss last season, but Keenum beat them through the air. The last time he had more passing yards was Sept. 23, 2019, when he finished with 332 for Washington in a loss to the Bears. Giants trade for Vikings QB McCarthy but say Winston is QB1 | ESPN Giants coach John Harbaugh said after Sunday’s victory over the Tennessee Titans that Jameis Winston would remain the Giants’ starter even if the team added another quarterback. He reiterated that Monday after the trade for McCarthy. The Giants host the Arizona Cardinals on Sunday. “Jameis is starting. You guys asked me that [Sunday] night. He’s our starting quarterback, and that’s how we’re rolling,” Harbaugh said. “We’ll be ready to play this next game and going forward. Excited about Jameis. … I’m looking forward to seeing where we go, and as we go we’ll get a chance to build around Jameis’ strengths.” What happened to Drake Maye? Why his Year 3 collapse is getting harder to explain away | CBS Sports The difference is that Maye’s 2025 season was considerably more convincing. He wasn’t simply amassing stats. His EPA improved substantially, his turnover-worthy plays went down, and the deep ball became a real weapon: Maye completed 61.8% of his throws 20-plus yards downfield, one of the highest rates in the league. That looked like legit franchise-QB development, not a false positive. The biggest difference so far isn’t that Maye suddenly can’t make NFL throws. He can. It’s the mistakes that largely went missing last season that have come back, almost as if they’re making up for lost time. In case you missed it on Arrowhead Pride 5 things we learned from the Chiefs’ Week 3 victory in Miami Mansoor Delane will have his rookie moments, but… Dang, he is just a good football player. I feel like it took Delane a couple of drives to really get his feet wet and get into the rhythm, but once he did, he was a difference-maker on this defense. When you combine him and Nohl Williams on the outside, it’s going to be hard for opposing perimeter wide receivers to have much success against the Chiefs. title: The Chiefs look like a different team than they did last September
summary: Through three games last season, the Kansas City Chiefs were searching for an identity. Losses to the Los Angeles Chargers and Philadelphia Eagles left them 0-2, and a 22-9 win over the New York Giants offered relief more than reassurance. This year, they have beaten the Denver Broncos 31-10, survived the Indianapolis Colts 33-30 in […]
full_text: (Photo by Chris Arjoon/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images). | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Through three games last season, the Kansas City Chiefs were searching for an identity. Losses to the Los Angeles Chargers and Philadelphia Eagles left them 0-2, and a 22-9 win over the New York Giants offered relief more than reassurance. This year, they have beaten the Denver Broncos 31-10, survived the Indianapolis Colts 33-30 in overtime and handled the Miami Dolphins 24-10. The scores tell part of the story. The Chiefs have scored 88 points through three games, compared with 60 at the same point last year. Their offense has gained 1,249 yards, up from 947 across the first three games in 2025. Those totals reflect a team that can now create yards in more than one way. Here are three thoughts about the hot start compared to last year: 1. Kenneth Walker has changed the equation Last September, quarterback Patrick Mahomes often had to supply the offense’s rushing spark himself. He ran for 57 yards against the Chargers and led Kansas City with 66 against the Eagles. The Chiefs won in Week 3 with 105 rushing yards as a team, but no running back topped Isiah Pacheco’s 45. Now Kenneth Walker III has 360 rushing yards in three games. His 173 yards against Denver helped turn a close opener into a decisive win. He followed that with 117 rushing yards against Indianapolis, then scored both on the ground and through the air in Miami. Walker gives Kansas City a way to dictate terms without asking Mahomes to rescue every stalled possession. The Colts game showed that a stronger run game has not come at the expense of the pass. Kansas City produced 152 rushing yards and 371 net passing yards in the same game. Mahomes threw for 382 yards and three touchdowns. Even when Indianapolis forced the Chiefs into a shootout, they could still win. 2. The offense has more answers around Mahomes Mahomes’ return from his knee injury did not make for a flawless Week 1 passing performance: he completed 15 of 27 attempts against Denver. Three games in, though, he has thrown for 812 yards and seven touchdowns. Travis Kelce has 231 receiving yards, Rashee Rice has 190, and Tyquan Thornton has supplied downfield plays, including two crucial catches in the overtime win against the Colts. The difference shows up in how Kansas City has won. Walker powered the opener. Mahomes’ arm carried much of the game against the Colts. In Miami, the Chiefs scored on their first possession, endured a long quiet stretch, then put together an 80-yard fourth-quarter drive before Kelce’s touchdown sealed it. The offense has had uneven stretches, but it has found different ways to put points on the board. 3. A better start still leaves questions Kansas City’s defense has allowed 50 points, compared with 56 through three games last season. The 31-10 win over Denver was its clearest statement: the Broncos managed only 176 yards. But the Colts scored 30, and Miami gained 329 yards despite scoring just 10 points. It is too early to declare the defense as “consistent.” That distinction matters when comparing the two starts. Last year’s Chiefs also showed they could shut down an opponent, holding the Giants to nine points in Week 3. They lacked enough offense to overcome their rougher afternoons against the Chargers and Eagles. This year, the Broncos game showed Kansas City can win comfortably with defense and a punishing run game; the Colts game showed it can win when the defense has a difficult night. The bottom line Three games cannot settle what this team will become. They do show a meaningful change from last September. The 2025 Chiefs entered Week 4 trying to build momentum after their first win. The 2026 Chiefs enter it unbeaten, with Walker giving the offense a threat it can lean on and Mahomes still capable of taking over when the game demands it.
author: Maurice Elston

title: Why Travis Kelce was wide open to start the Chiefs’ win in Miami
summary: Through three games, Kansas City Chiefs tight end Travis Kelce is reminding the football world why he is at the top, or near it, on many all-time lists. Before “Monday Night Football” caps Week 3, the Chiefs’ leading receiver this season ranks second among all NFL tight ends in receiving yards (231). That ranks 12th […]
full_text: (Photo by Alie Skowronski/Getty Images) | Getty Images Through three games, Kansas City Chiefs tight end Travis Kelce is reminding the football world why he is at the top, or near it, on many all-time lists. Before “Monday Night Football” caps Week 3, the Chiefs’ leading receiver this season ranks second among all NFL tight ends in receiving yards (231) . That ranks 12th among all league players. He is averaging 16.5 yards per reception over 14 catches. He has multiple catch-and-run plays that lasted roughly 50 yards. In Week 1 against the Denver Broncos , quarterback Patrick Mahomes caught the Broncos’ defense in a blitz, delivering the ball with chemistry that turned the play into a 59-yard scamper. To open the Week 3 contest against the Miami Dolphins, he found a lot of room to run again, but it wasn’t possible without a nonchalant adjustment on the fly by Mahomes. In his post-game press conference, the quarterback explained how the Dolphins’ defense helped get Kelce open in a roundabout way. “I think the fact that I scrambled out to the right got him open, which it wasn’t necessarily supposed to happen like that,” Mahomes said. “I was supposed to pull up, but how the defensive line stunted, I was able to get outside.” Mahomes talked about the opening play to Kelce post-game, saying the DL stunting one way got him open by forcing Pat to move right instead of pull up in the pocket That's a blown-up play by the D against most QBs, but Pat casually slings it across his body pic.twitter.com/vof76znZnM — Ron Kopp Jr (@RonOnChiefs) September 28, 2026 Mahomes also pointed out the depth that Miami’s high safety had to stay on top of wide receiver Tyquan Thornton’s deep route. “I think what got him open the most is Tyquan running down the field,” Mahomes shared. “You have that speed running at you down the field; the safety got depth, the run game, the play action brought the first level, second level up. Then all of a sudden Travis is right there behind everybody. Got him the football there and he made a big play.” Thornton’s impact on the play gave Kelce the space to gain 48 yards in all, but the initial throw is one only elite gunslingers can make. Most quarterbacks would be thwarted by the initial pressure, rolling right and never considering a throw back across the field. That’s what makes Mahomes different. After a couple of nonchalant steps out to avoid the pressure, he ripped a pass back across the field and both hash marks. The Dolphins’ defense naturally flowed away from Kelce; this throw isn’t factored into the game plan when the coaches put it up on the whiteboard. The Kenneth Walker effect Patrick Mahomes completed all 14 of his play-action attempts for 201 yards and a TD Sunday, tied for the most attempts without an incompletion by any player in the last 20 seasons💯 KC ranks 1st in play-action usage this season (36%) after ranking 13th… pic.twitter.com/1Om2p8EP7t — ESPN Insights (@ESPNInsights) September 27, 2026 It all stems from an initial run action out of a formation with three tight ends, a trend Kansas City is mastering with each week. Sunday was Mahomes’ most efficient performance yet off under-center play-action throws. With Kelce on the receiving end, someone who could be considered one of the all-time greats at finding soft spots in coverage, the Chiefs are in a strong position to continue generating explosive plays with scheme (and Mahomes being Mahomes).
author: Ron Kopp Jr.

title: Andy Reid points out Chiefs’ offense didn’t have a ton of plays in Miami
summary: The Kansas City Chiefs’ offense was clicking on all cylinders against the Miami Dolphins, averaging over seven yards per play for most of the game and opening things up for quarterback Patrick Mahomes to deliver an incredibly efficient performance. The performance may have been masked by the 24 points on Kansas City’s side of the […]
full_text: (Photo by Chris Arjoon/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images). | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Kansas City Chiefs ’ offense was clicking on all cylinders against the Miami Dolphins , averaging over seven yards per play for most of the game and opening things up for quarterback Patrick Mahomes to deliver an incredibly efficient performance. Patrick Mahomes had an 83.3% completion percentage against the Dolphins in Week 3 His 20/24 performance is his highest single game completion percentage since Week 15 of 2022, per @SumerSports — Shawn Syed (@SyedSchemes) September 27, 2026 The performance may have been masked by the 24 points on Kansas City’s side of the scoreboard, an underwhelming total considering how easy things looked for the Chiefs’ offense at times. On Monday, head coach Andy Reid answered questions from reporters on a video conference call. He shared a reason Kansas City couldn’t match the scoring outputs of Weeks 1 and 2. “I thought we handled the pass game pretty well,” Reid said. “We didn’t have a ton of plays; we were in the 40s on that, and normally you’re up a little higher in the 60 or 70 area.” Time of possession was key for the underdog Dolphins to stay in the fight. Miami had nearly 10 more minutes with the ball. Still, the Chiefs’ offense finished enough of the opportunities given to win by two touchdowns. “I thought the way it balanced out… [Kenneth Walker] was still able to have a productive day in the run game and the pass game,” Reid continued. “But it opened up some things in the pass game that we were able to take advantage of with some bigger plays.” Reid shared a note on the team’s top two wideouts by snap count: Rashee Rice and Xavier Worthy. The former had a game-high seven catches for 88 yards with 55 coming after the catch. “It was good to see him get a couple of catches in there that were physical, good, strong catches,” Reid said about Rice. “He is so good with the ball after he gets it and so physical… It’s almost like having a running back at a wide receiver spot where, when he gets it, he’s going to bring it, and that’s always good.” Worthy, leading the team in snaps for the second consecutive week, had just one highlight: a 17-yard completion on the sideline. “He had one that was sort of an intermediate throw there, and he did a nice job with it,” Reid reflected. “We’ll just see how it all works out for him as we go forward. He’s busting his tail, and I think, every week, he’s feeling better with the shoulder issue and doing a good job there.” Speaking of feeling better, it’s hard to imagine Mahomes is yet after a penalty for roughing the passer was called on Dolphins edge rusher Chop Robinson for an obliteration of a hit. The quarterback is likely sore today, but it didn’t seem to slow him down for long on Sunday. “It was more than a chiropractor could do,” Reid joked. “I think every bone in his body cracked on that one, but he got back up and kept firing.”
