title: Chiefs Week 3 snap count analysis: L’Jarius Sneed, the blitzer
summary: Welcome to Arrowhead Pride’s weekly snap-count analysis! So let’s see what we can figure out about the Kansas City Chiefs when taking a closer look at playing time during the 24-10 win over the Miami Dolphins in Week 3. The starting lineups are courtesy of NFL Game Stats and Information, and the snap-count data comes […]
full_text: (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images Welcome to Arrowhead Pride’s weekly snap-count analysis! So let’s see what we can figure out about the Kansas City Chiefs when taking a closer look at playing time during the 24-10 win over the Miami Dolphins in Week 3. The starting lineups are courtesy of NFL Game Stats and Information, and the snap-count data comes from Pro Football Focus’ premium stats. Starters (offensive): LT Kahlil Benson, LG Kingsley Suamataia, C Creed Humphrey, RG Trey Smith, RT Jaylon Moore, QB Patrick Mahomes, WR Tyquan Thornton, RB Kenneth Walker, TE Travis Kelce, TE Noah Gray and TE Jake Briningstool. Starters (defensive): DE George Karlaftis, DT Chris Jones, DT Khyiris Tonga, DE Felix Anudike-Uzomah, LB Nick Bolton, LB Drue Tranquill, LB Jack Cochrane, CB Mansoor Delane, CB L’Jarius Sneed, S Alohi Gilman and S Jaden Hicks Did not play: CB Kristian Fulton, QB Justin Fields Inactive: TE Jared Wiley, QB Garrett Nussmeier (Emergency third QB), S Chamarri Conner (Knee), DE Jack Pyburn, DE Tyreke Smith, OT Diego Pounds, LT Josh Simmons (Back) The big takeaway: L’Jarius Sneed’s playmaking utilized The Chiefs’ main trio of cornerbacks in Miami featured rookie Mansoor Delane, Nohl Williams and L’Jarius Sneed. 33 of Sneed’s 53 snaps were aligned in the slot. On seven plays, Sneed was sent after the quarterback as a blitzer, according to Pro Football Focus . NFL Next Gen Stats credited Sneed with five quarterback pressures, a career-high mark for the seventh-year defensive back. He also caused a turnover that was pivotal in the Chiefs securing victory on Sunday in Miami. Defensive coordinator Steve Spagnuolo wants Sneed on the field for a reason, and it mostly has to do with his playmaking around the ball. The Offensive takeaway: (Some of) The Auxiliary receivers step up Tight end Noah Gray played the fewest offensive snaps (33) he has in any game this season against the Dolphins, but he saw the second-most catches (3) on the team, including a 24-yard reception on the sideline that put the Chiefs in the red zone late in the contest. His young teammate at the position, second-year tight end Jake Briningstool, earned his first career start by taking the field on the first play of the game. Kansas City presented a 13-personnel set that featured Kelce, Gray and Briningstool on the field at the same time, setting up a play-action pass to Kelce. He played six snaps. Second-year wide receiver Jalen Royals made his season debut last week against the Indianapolis Colts and played two more snaps than he did in Miami (10), but Royals recorded a catch for 11 yards that moved the chains for the Chiefs in the second half. It was good to see the offense get impactful plays from the pass catchers below quarterback Patrick Mahomes’ top shelf of playmakers. However, rookie wide receiver Cyrus Allen recorded one snap; he has played just five snaps for Kansas City’s offense this season. The Defensive takeaway: Peter Woods outsnaps Khyiris Tonga Up front on defense, the Chiefs’ youth movement is taking over more and more with each game. Nose tackle Khyiris Tonga (30 snaps) started on Sunday, but rookie defensive tackle Peter Woods out-snapped the veteran by five. On 23 of Woods’ 35 plays on the field, the Dolphins ran a pass play; on one of those snaps, Woods dropped into coverage. Edge rusher R Mason Thomas also wasn’t the “starter”; fourth-year defensive end Felix Anudike-Uzomah began the game on the field, but the rookie from Oklahoma played 41 snaps compared to Anudike-Uzomah’s 31. Rookie defensive tackle Bryson Eason also made his Chiefs debut in Miami, playing seven snaps. Offensive Snaps Defensive Snaps Special teams snaps

title: Chargers Power Rankings Roundup: Bolts’ downward slide continues at 0-3
summary: The Chargers were as close as they have been all year to earning their first win this past Sunday. Five takeaways by the defense usually means victory is assured. Yet somehow, that wasn’t the case by the time the clock hit zero at Highmark Stadium. When it was all said and done, the Chargers held […]
full_text: ORCHARD PARK, NEW YORK - SEPTEMBER 27: Head Coach Jim Harbaugh of the Los Angeles Chargers looks on from the sidelines during the third quarter of the game against the Buffalo Bills at Highmark Stadium on September 27, 2026 in Orchard Park, New York. (Photo by Kathryn Riley/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Chargers were as close as they have been all year to earning their first win this past Sunday. Five takeaways by the defense usually means victory is assured. Yet somehow, that wasn’t the case by the time the clock hit zero at Highmark Stadium. When it was all said and done, the Chargers held a +4 advantage in the turnover battle while still leaving on the wrong end of a 24-16 result. The offense scored just 10 points off those five turnovers which was nowhere near enough cushion to hold off the Bills by the time they got their act together. Understandably so, that debacle has led to the Chargers dropping even further down this week’s NFL power rankings. Let’s check out how bad the damage is. CBS Sports – #24 “They played in desperation mode on the road against the Bills, and it still wasn’t good enough. The schedule is brutal, and a 0-9 start is possible.” – Pete Prisco Sports Illustrated – #27 “Column on the Chargers, who should be investigated for wire fraud .” – Conor Orr ESPN – #27 “ Expectations were high for the 2025 first-round pick, given how running backs have thrived with OC Mike McDaniel at other stops. But Hampton has been a disappointment so far. He was the 12th running back in ADP, but his 31 points ranks 22nd. Hampton also saw a decreased workload in Week 3 after struggles in his first two weeks. As the Chargers move forward, this could become more of a split backfield with Hampton and Keaton Mitchell, who averaged 6.5 yards per carry to Hampton’s 3.7 in Buffalo.” — Kris Rhim Sporting News – #29 ‘‘The Chargers were more active defensively to turn over the Bills multiple times. But Jim Harbaugh saw more awful offense with Justin Herbert failing to stop his own giveaway woes. They, like the Texans, are straight-up bad at this point.” – Vinnie Iyer Pro Football Talk – #29 “ Justin Herbert has replaced Joe Burrow as the ‘veteran QB most likely to change teams in 2027.”’ – Mike Florio USA Today – #29 “ The last time they were 0-3 was 2017, when Philip Rivers was the quarterback, and the team was playing in a suburban L.A. soccer stadium. An 0-3 start has them swimming for a life raft with one unlikely to appear since the Seattle Seahawks, Denver Broncos and Kansas City Chiefs are next on the docket.” “ Surprisingly, the Chargers’ biggest disconnect can be found on offense, where quarterback Justin Herbert isn’t executing Mike McDaniel’s offensive scheme. ” “ This past offseason, McDaniel’s hire was viewed as one of the league’s best, because he brought a proven track record as a play-caller. Instead, the Chargers are in disarray, Herbert is playing poorly and the unit ranks among the league’s bottom-feeders in total offense.” — Brent Sobleski The Athletic – #29 “ This was supposed to be Justin Herbert’s year. (Or was that last year? It’s hard to keep up.) The Chargers’ two heralded tackles aren’t playing great, and they’re having to start a rookie at center, but this is Year 7 for Herbert, who has more interceptions than touchdowns (4-to-3) and the third-worst passer rating in the league (73.4). Offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel was supposed to fix this, but it hasn’t happened yet, and the Seahawks, Broncos, Chiefs and Rams are next.” – Chad Graff and Josh Kendall

title: Los Angeles Chargers news: Bolts add Indiana WR in new 2027 mock draft
summary: The Chargers came into the 2026 season with a young wide receiver group that seemed poised to breakout a bit given the Mike McDaniel hire and the type of offense that they were now expected to run. Through three weeks, that offense is nowhere to be seen and the receiver room is a far cry […]
full_text: BLOOMINGTON, INDIANA - SEPTEMBER 19: Charlie Becker #80 of the Indiana Hoosiers runs the ball during the game against the Western Kentucky Hilltoppers at Memorial Stadium on September 19, 2026 in Bloomington, Indiana. (Photo by Michael Hickey/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Chargers came into the 2026 season with a young wide receiver group that seemed poised to breakout a bit given the Mike McDaniel hire and the type of offense that they were now expected to run. Through three weeks, that offense is nowhere to be seen and the receiver room is a far cry from those preseason expectations. Enter Indiana’s Charlie Becker, whom the Chargers are paired with in a recent 2027 mock draft from Sports Illustrated. The 6’4, 210-pound Becker has been lighting up the college football world thus far this season with six touchdowns and 370 yards on 19 receptions through four games. “ I’m not here to start another Justin Herbert debate. He, obviously, needs to play better, and he could do that by getting better weapons. (See what I did there?) Becker has been the breakout star of the young college football season. Initially, I was hesitant to go all in on Becker despite all of the positive intel I received on him before the season. I needed to see it again after his sensational playoff performances that came out of nowhere last season. After three games, I’m sold on the 6’4″, 209-pound Becker, who can do it all with his high-level route running and reliable hands. He already has a whopping six touchdown receptions. ” What would you all think about the Chargers adding a player like Becker in the first round of next year’s draft? Yay or nay? title: Chargers Week 3 PFF Grades: Genesis Smith, Joe Alt lead the way for Bolts after elite outing
summary: The defense came to play against the Bills and almost got it done all by themselves with five takeaways. The offense, on the other hand, was barely there and may not have completely got off the bus. What a shame to waste such a performance by Chris O’Leary’s unit, and specifically rookie safety Genesis Smith […]
full_text: INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA - SEPTEMBER 20: Joe Alt #76 of the Los Angeles Chargers in action against the Las Vegas Raiders at SoFi Stadium on September 20, 2026 in Inglewood, California. (Photo by Luke Hales/Getty Images) | Getty Images The defense came to play against the Bills and almost got it done all by themselves with five takeaways. The offense, on the other hand, was barely there and may not have completely got off the bus. What a shame to waste such a performance by Chris O’Leary’s unit, and specifically rookie safety Genesis Smith who picked off Josh Allen twice for his first two career interceptions. Sorry, rookie. The other side of the ball owes you some gifts. One positive note from the offense is Joe Alt’s performance who got back to looking like one of the league’s best tackles. After a Week Two that saw him get flagged over and over again, this was refreshing to see. Let’s take a look at this week’s grades. Offense Best OT Joe Alt – 83.6 RB Keaton Mitchell – 78.9 WR Tre’ Harris – 75.1 OT Travis Burke – 72.1 WR Ladd McConkey – 67.7 Alt rebounded with his best game of the season. He earned an elite 90.0 run block grade and a very good 79.5 in pass blocking. Mitchell was leaned upon more this week compared to the first two games and he turned in a solid performance behind a 79.5 rushing grade. Harris showed some serious hands on a great pluck out of the air against the Bills when the team needed a clutch play in the second half. He was solid and is overtaking Quentin Johnston as the team’s WR2. Burke got work as an extra offensive lineman against the Bills. He was above average in both run blocking (67.1) and pass pro (70.1) while leading the team in both receptions (six) and yards (76). McConkey played most of the snaps on offense but was rather unproductive based on his normal standards. He finished second on the team with four catches and 66 yards. Worst OG Cole Strange – 30.1 TE Oronde Gadsden II – 38.6 TE Hayden Rucci – 47.4 QB Justin Herbert – 51.1 RB Omarion Hampton – 52.0 Strange had his worst game of the season Sunday and that’s saying something when he has yet to have a game grade above 47.1. His 33.2 in pass blocking was somehow just second-worst behind Trevor Penning (24.6). Gadsden was underwhelming as a run blocker with a 54.6 in tha area. His receiving grade of 45.7 was also worst among all players. Rucci’s grade was sunk by a 29.6 in pass protection but his run block grade of 68.0 was third on the team. He actually was very solid and had a great sequence with Joe Alt where he sealed the edge for Mitchell to score the team’s lone touchdown on Sunday. Herbert’s interception was one of the worst balls he’s thrown in some time. It was an egregious decision in a massively pivotal moment. Hampton was bottle up all day and that showed in his 52.0 rushing grade. Defense Best S Genesis Smith – 95.1 CB Donte Jackson – 81.4 S Tony Jefferson – 81.1 CB Tarheeb Still – 75.9 LB Del’Shawn Phillips – 75.4 What a day for Smith who was coming off a rough outing against the Raiders. He picked off Allen twice, including a circus pick where the ball fell on his stomach after ricocheting off several players. Jackson was yet again the team’s best corner but unfortunately left the game with a concussion in the first half. Still forced one of the game’s fumbles which was recovered by Jefferson. He was weak in tackling and run defense but came through in coverage for most of the day. Phillips was top five in both tackling (80.4) and run defense (71.1), finishing as the team’s best linebacker against the Bills. Worst CB Rodney Shelley – 25.1 EDGE Bud Dupree – 45.5 LB Troy Dye – 52.6 EDGE Akheem Mesidor – 54.7 LB Daiyan Henley – 54.7 Just like it was a great day for Smith, it was equally a bad day for Shelley who was picked on the moment he entered the game for Donte Jackson. Right now, Shelley is acting as the team’s third cornerback due to Deane Leonard seemingly only playing special teams now. That’s not good! Mesidor had the best sack of the day where he cleanly beat left tackle Dion Dawkins with an excellent hand swipe en route to bringing down Josh Allen for his first career full sack. However, his 47.5 in run defense is what sunk his grade into the bottom five. Henley allowed three receptions on four targets his way to be completed for 46 yards, including 35 after the catch. He’s squarely on pace to have one of his worst seasons as a pro. His coverage grade is an abysmal 38.7 through three games.

title: 2 winners, 3 losers from Chargers-Bills: Chris O’Leary’s unit came to play
summary: The Chargers had a decent amount of good come against the Bills but it all happened to come via the defense who recorded a whopping five takeaways from Josh Allen and the league’s best offense through two weeks. Unfortunately, the Chargers needed six or seven to apparently beat the Bills and earn their first win […]
full_text: ORCHARD PARK, NEW YORK - SEPTEMBER 27: Genesis Smith #22 of the Los Angeles Chargers celebrates after intercepting a pass from Josh Allen #17 of the Buffalo Bills during the second quarter of the game at Highmark Stadium on September 27, 2026 in Orchard Park, New York. (Photo by Bryan M. Bennett/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Chargers had a decent amount of good come against the Bills but it all happened to come via the defense who recorded a whopping five takeaways from Josh Allen and the league’s best offense through two weeks. Unfortunately, the Chargers needed six or seven to apparently beat the Bills and earn their first win of the season because the offense was still just as lost and disconnected as they looked in Weeks One and Two. Three weeks into the season, there’s still so many more questions than answers. sigh…. Here are this week’s winners and losers. Winners S Genesis Smith Smith rebounded from a rough outing against the Raiders to pick off one of the league’s best quarterbacks not once, but TWICE(!) on Sunday when the Bolts visited the Bills. The first was a beautiful undercut of a slot post intended for wideout D.J. Moore and the second was a circus catch that started with Smith and Moore both ricocheting the ball off their hands at the catch point only for it to fall gently onto Smith’s stomach while he was still sliding on the ground. It was a tough break for Allen, but Smith still kept his head about him enough to clamp down on the ball before it could hit the turf. Talk about a confidence booster for the rookie moving forward. Genesis Smith picks it off and the Chargers have forced two turnovers in the first quarter @LACvsBUF on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/ZPNmigdnpQ — NFL (@NFL) September 27, 2026 EDGE Akheem Mesidor After recording a half sack in Week Two, Mesidor earned his first career full sack in emphatic fashion by winning cleanly against Bills left tackle Dion Dawkins (one of the best in the league) to bring down Josh Allen. The rookie has been showing more and more promise with each regular season game and it helps that Chris O’Leary is finding his groove earlier than we all initially thought. Losers QB Justin Herbert Herbert and the offense looked like the same unit from their first two games despite the notion that they had their best week of practice going into Sunday. They were unable to capitalize much at all on their five takeaways by the defense and Herbert’s lone interception thrown was just plain ugly. After looking at the defense before the snap, Herbert seemingly forgot that safety C.J. Gardner-Johnson was hovering in the middle of the field when he fired a ball to Marquez Valdez-Scantling in the end zone. CGJ read it the whole way and grabbed one of the easier interceptions of his career. It was an indefensible throw by Herbert and a real gut punch to his defenders frosixm the past two weeks. After a lot of wrong going on around him, Herbert only fanned the flames by making such a huge mistake in a pivotal point of the game. RB Omarion Hampton Hampton was stifled all day by the Bills top-10 run defense and it forced Mike McDaniel to try and get some going behind Keaton Mitchell and his speed. He finished with 56 yards on 15 carries (3.7 YPC) and no receptions on one target. On the other hand, Mitchell had 52 yards rushing for 52 yards (6.5 YPC) and received three targets (albeit he caught them all for -5 yards). The interior of the offensive line was simply unable to get any movement Mitchell’s speed was the only thing working as the Bolts needed to get him on the edge fast with their edge players doing a good job of making their ball carriers bounce it back in. Hampton only has a harder task coming with the Seahawks’ sixth-ranked run defense set to greet him in Week Four. WR Quentin Johnston Johnston left Sunday’s loss with season-highs in catches (three) and yards (40) but even with those middling stats, it was a much worse day in reality. First, over half those 40 yards came on a play at the end of the half where the Bills defense lined up halfway down the field to allow anything underneath. It was the easiest 21 yards he’ll get in his entire career. Secondly, he had another egregious drop on a perfect pass from Herbert. It was also on a third down during a drive the Chargers needed to cash in on. I’m not sure what to think about Johnston now. We know what he looks like at his best, but this is a really, really unfortunate stretch for him. Part of it seems to be how he fits in McDaniel’s offense, but his fit doesn’t change how he catches and if neither of things are going well, then what in the world is going on? If there’s anyone that needs a shot of confidence right now on the Chargers, it’s him.

title: Could tight end injuries lead to debut of Rams rookie?
summary: Cornerback Jaylen Watson is not expected to play when the Los Angeles Rams face the Philadelphia Eagles in Week 4. The defensive back was carted off of the field on Sunday against the Denver Broncos when he dislocated his shoulder. Rams head coach Sean McVay addressed Watson and other injuries during his Monday press conference. […]
full_text: Cornerback Jaylen Watson is not expected to play when the Los Angeles Rams face the Philadelphia Eagles in Week 4. The defensive back was carted off of the field on Sunday against the Denver Broncos when he dislocated his shoulder. Rams head coach Sean McVay addressed Watson and other injuries during his Monday press conference . “He’ll probably be out for this week, and (it’s) something that we’ll see if we can kind of get him strengthened and harness it,” McVay said. “It’s something that he’s dealt with before, but not something that we’ve discussed, IR.” Watson signed a three-year, $51 million contract this offseason after playing his first four years in the league with the Chiefs. With Watson playing in the first half of the game, the Rams held the Broncos to 67 total yards and zero points. In the second half, with Watson on the sideline and his arm in a sling, the Broncos gained 197 yards and scored 30 points. Tight ends Colby Parkinson and Terrance Ferguson were also injured during Sunday’s loss to the Broncos. McVay said that Parkinson is day-to-day with a AC joint sprain in his shoulder. “We’ll see what that looks like for him,” McVay said. Ferguson has a medial ankle sprain and likely will miss Sunday’s game against the Eagles, per reports. This was an aggravation of an existing injury. Parkinson has played 61 percent of the team’s offensive snaps this season, and Ferguson 43 percent. The Rams’ run game suffered in the second half with Parkinson and Ferguson banged up. One interesting wrinkle to the tight end injuries is whether or not it could mean the debut of second-round rookie Max Klare this week. Klare has been a healthy scratch in all three games, but if Ferguson and Parkinson are both ruled out then he could be the next-best option for McVay’s 13 personnel. Coach McVay provides injury updates following Week 3. pic.twitter.com/KA9MTT015r — Los Angeles Rams (@RamsNFL) September 29, 2026 Puka Nacua, Kamren Kinchens updates: Two-time All-Pro WR Puka Nacua has missed the past two games with a lingering hip/groin issue, but McVay has hope that he will return to the team against the Eagles. “We’ll continue to see,” McVay said. “But if he is able to progress the way that we hope, there’s optimism that he’ll be able to play this week.” Here’s Puka Nacua working out on the side with a trainer during practice. pic.twitter.com/bNsaFPwe3p — Sarah Barshop (@sarahbarshop) September 25, 2026 The Rams sorely miss Puka’s presence on offense . Finally, Kamren Kinchens continues to rehabilitate his hamstring injury suffered during the 49ers game in Week 1 and his status is the one we don’t have any new information on from the coach.

title: Jaylen Watson may be back for the Rams after Week 4
summary: Jaylen Watson appeared to be seriously hurt in Week 3 when he was helped to the sideline, and road a cart to the locker room, but apparently the Los Angeles Rams are not considering putting him on IR. Now, Watson’s injury may still be serious, but the good news for the Rams is that he […]
full_text: INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA - SEPTEMBER 21: Trent McDuffie #22, Jaylen Watson #35 and Quentin Lake #37 of the Los Angeles Rams celebrates a defensive stop against the New York Giants during the second quarter of the game at SoFi Stadium on September 21, 2026 in Inglewood, California. (Photo by Sean M. Haffey/Getty Images) | Getty Images Jaylen Watson appeared to be seriously hurt in Week 3 when he was helped to the sideline, and road a cart to the locker room, but apparently the Los Angeles Rams are not considering putting him on IR. Now, Watson’s injury may still be serious, but the good news for the Rams is that he may be expected back sooner than later. It would be ideal for the Rams to see their team healthy with Myles Garrett, Puka Nacua and now Watson, but that hasn’t been the case. Instead, this team has been injured and their 1-2 record has been disappointing. The season isn’t over and the Rams haven’t looked helpless, but they’ve looked lesser in two out of three weeks. Hopefully the Rams get Watson and others back in time to make a push. Injury Updates: McVay says Terrance Ferguson (ankle) and Jaylen Watson (shoulder) likely out for Week 4 at Eagles; latest on Colby Parkinson (shoulder) and Puka Nacua (hip) (therams.com) “WOODLAND HILLS, Calif. – Rams head coach Sean McVay on Monday said cornerback Jaylen Watson sustained a dislocated shoulder in Sunday night’s loss to the Broncos. While Watson “probably” will miss this Sunday’s Week 4 road game against the Eagles, according to McVay, he will not be placed on Injured Reserve and that isn’t something they have talked about. “He’ll probably be out for this week, and (it’s) something that we’ll see if we can kind of get him strengthened and harness it,” McVay said. “It’s something that he’s dealt with before, but not something that we’ve discussed, IR.” Watson’s injury occurred around the 3:04 mark of the second quarter. He was carted back to the locker room after being evaluated in the medical tent. Prior to exiting with that injury, he had recorded two total tackles (one for loss) and two passes defensed.“ Rams get mixed bag update on Jaylen Watson after scary shoulder injury (sports.yahoo) “Rams head coach Sean McVay revealed Monday that Watson suffered a dislocated right shoulder late in the first half of Sunday night’s 30-26 loss to the Denver Broncos and will miss multiple games. There was at least one encouraging wrinkle: Los Angeles does not plan to place Watson on injured reserve, which would require him to miss a minimum of four games. McVay also indicated Watson has suffered a similar injury before.“ Rams Week 3 snap counts: How LA overcame several injuries vs. Broncos (ramswire) “The Los Angeles Rams suffered their second loss of the season on Sunday night, and this one was much different than the first. They blew a 16-point lead to the Denver Broncos , losing by a score of 30-26 on the road. Injuries have piled up for the Rams, forcing Sean McVay and Chris Shula to dip into their depth on each side of the ball. As a result, the snap counts look quite different than they did in Week 1 when Puka Nacua, Myles Garrett, Kamren Kinchens and Jaylen Watson were all fully healthy. Below is a breakdown of the playing time from Sunday night’s loss, including some separation at running back and a deeper rotation in the secondary.“ Broncos hang on to beat the Rams, who blow multiple leads and are a disappointing 1-2 to start this season (sports.yahoo) “Stafford has played a lot of football and he wasn’t fazed. He hit Konata Mumpfield for three straight completions, gains of 21, 9 and then a 48-yard touchdown to take back the lead. Mumpfield beat cornerback Riley Moss and was wide open downfield for Stafford’s pass. The Rams led 26-23. That just meant it was the Broncos’ turn to answer. Nix hit Bryant for 39 yards and Troy Franklin for 21, putting Denver in position to at least tie the game with a field goal. Two penalties, including a questionable one on Wallace, kept the drive alive. That led to the Nix touchdown, and the Rams couldn’t answer despite getting inside the red zone at the end. The Broncos are happy to be 2-1 after a rough Week 1 loss at Kansas City . The Rams aren’t quite as pleased with their start to the season.“ McVay, Rams won’t make excuses after pass interference call (espn.com) “[It] doesn’t really matter,” McVay said Monday. “It is what it is. That was the call that was made and there was a lot of opportunities that we had to be able to close the door on that game. … But I wouldn’t have any additional coaching points for how Josh [Wallace] plays through the cycle of the snap. But I’m not going to make excuses either and we’re not going to play the victim card.” The Rams were called for five penalties in the final two minutes of the fourth quarter, tied for the most by any team in a game since 2000, according to ESPN Research. Referee Bill Vinovich’s crew had thrown the second-fewest flags in the final two minutes of a game in the 2024 and ’25 seasons. The group threw only one flag in the last two minutes across the entire 2024 season.“ Terrance Ferguson Injury Could Force Rams to Change Their Offensive Identity (si.com) “The Los Angeles Rams received some injury updates on Monday following their loss on Sunday night to the Denver Broncos. During the game, tight end Terrance Ferguson left with an ankle injury while Colby Parkinson was clearly hampered. “Colby didn’t have any setbacks with his knee injury, but he did have an AC sprain to his shoulder. We’ll see what that looks like,” said head coach Sean McVay. “Terrance Ferguson had a medial sprain to his ankle. We’ll see what that looks like moving forward for him.” McVay: Medial ankle sprain for Terrance Ferguson (nbcsports) “Ferguson briefly departed after injuring his ankle in the team’s Sunday Night Football loss to the Broncos, returning for two snaps prior to departing again after his lone reception of the evening. The ankle injury now appears likely to cost the talented young tight end at least one game, with the potential for the absence to linger if the sprain is “more high than low.” McVay also relayed that fellow tight end Colby Parkinson suffered an AC sprain and is considered day-to-day. Veteran Tyler Higbee would be in line to operate as the primary receiving tight end after amassing 62 yards and a touchdown on eight receptions in Week 3, should both miss. Higbee should be added in all formats as a potential TE1 in the immediate future.“ NFL Week 3 Sunday aftermath: Tyler Loop’s heroics, Drake Maye concerns, Brock Purdy’s MVP form (nfl.com) “Football’s ability to inspire never ceases. Ravens kicker Tyler Loop rode a rocky path during his rookie campaign, culminating in a season-ending miss in the team’s Week 18 loss to the rival Steelers with the AFC North title (and the accompanying playoff berth) on the line. That pushed 44-yard kick attempt set in motion an offseason of change in Baltimore. Loop fended off questions about his future, keeping his job despite the immense fallout. A blocked attempt in Week 2’s disappointing loss to the Saints revived questions about the 2025 draft pick. Then, on Sunday in Rio de Janeiro, Loop got his shot to brush away the haze of the past. After the Ravens’ defense bowed up and kept Dallas out of the end zone late in the fourth quarter, seven seconds remained in 31-31 game. Lamar Jackson rocketed a missile that Zay Flowers leaped to snag for a 27-yard gain , with the receiver immediately getting down as Jackson called a timeout with 1 second remaining and the ball now at Dallas’ 38-yard line. Loop lined up the 56-yard attempt and calmly banged it through, with CBS Sports’ Jim Nantz eloquently calling the game-winning boot “a trio in Rio.” Ravens players celebrated with their sometimes-maligned kicker as they pulled off a last-second victory despite stumbles along the way.“ NFL news roundup: Jaycee Horn out indefinitely; Justin Jefferson, Breece Hall avoid serious injuries…

title: Rams snap count review: Can the special teams be repaired?
summary: Closing out an action-packed fourth quarter, a Los Angeles Rams last-second pass was intercepted in the end zone, resulting in a 30-26 loss on the road to the Denver Broncos. In the final 15 minutes, Sunday Night Football viewers were treated to 24 points, an interception return for a score, and numerous explosive plays along […]
full_text: DENVER, COLORADO - SEPTEMBER 27: Josh Wallace #30 of the Los Angeles Rams makes an interception against the Denver Broncos during the fourth quarter at Empower Field At Mile High on September 27, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Justin Edmonds/Getty Images) | Getty Images Closing out an action-packed fourth quarter, a Los Angeles Rams last-second pass was intercepted in the end zone, resulting in a 30-26 loss on the road to the Denver Broncos. In the final 15 minutes, Sunday Night Football viewers were treated to 24 points, an interception return for a score, and numerous explosive plays along with some questionable referee calls. L.A. jumped out to a 16-0 half time lead, out-gaining Denver 273 yards to 67, but having to settle for three field goals. The Rams came out flat in the second half and the Broncos took advantage of poor special teams play to board 16 unanswered points setting up the furious fourth quarter. For Rams fans, it’s a recurring bad trip. To the point where fans can expect the L.A. special teams to allow the opposition to not only flip the field, but flip the momentum as well. Sunday night was tragicomedy of errors. On coverage, substandard lane integrity/spacing, pursuit angles, and tackling. On returns, almost zero delay of opposing gunners on punts, zero lanes on kickoffs. and little creativity by the returners. The mayhem didn’t start until the second half. For the first 30 minutes, the Rams pretty much had their way in all phases, After trading three-and-outs, L.A. punted to Denver for their second possession. The punt coverage team lost outside leverage and allowed a return of 28 yards down the sideline and the Broncos turned the short field into a score. On the Rams next possession, midway through the third stanza, Ethan Evans boomed a punt and Grant Stuard made a fine tackle, pinning Denver back at their own nine yard line. But it was all for nothing, gunner Emmanuel Forbes was pushed out of bounds and decided to run down the field out of play rather than return to it, resulting in a penalty that negated a pair of fine efforts. The re-kick was a shank, so instead of inside their own 10, the Broncos started at midfield and as often happens, took advantage of the short field and tied the score. The momentum had swung. Rams players, their snap counts, and play percentage in bold. Quarterback Matt Stafford (86, 100%) It’s not news that in the NFL, a team’s fortunes generally rise or fall with the play of their quarterback. Stafford has always been a volatile performer, prone to wild swings between big-time throws and poor decisions. Monday night was no exception. Running back Kyren Williams (61, 71%) Blake Corum (25, 29%) 23 carries is not a paltry total, but it’s interesting that the Rams didn’t run more considering the early success. Williams showed why he’s the Rams RB#1. Heart, toughness, and the ability to make the first tackler miss. In a physical game like this, his competitiveness and “banger’s mentality” led to his getting the lion’s share of reps. In a game where the Rams game plan was to throw the football, Corum wasn’t able to garner enough touches to get a lather up. A dropped pass early in the game was likely enough to limit his snaps. Wide receiver Davante Adams (71, 83%) Konata Mumpfield (63, 73%) Xavier Smith (38, 44%) Jordan Whittington (21, 24%) Adams stacked a second straight stellar outing, this one primarily against Patrick Surtain, one of the NFL’s premier corners. If you’re into “what if’s”, he twice got open well behind the Denver defense but Stafford missed him. It was obviously Mumpfield’s best game as pro. He ran some really nice routes and Stafford was looking his way late in the game. A good sign. Neither Smith nor Whittington were targeted. Konata Mumpfied #Rams Caught behind break 4th QTR – second conesecutive target pic.twitter.com/jwLiEoHqjf — Matt Waldman (@MattWaldman) September 28, 2026 Tight end Tyler Higbee (61, 71%) Colby Parkinson (37, 43%) Davis Allen (36, 71%) Terrance Ferguson (22, 26%) Good to see Higbee can still produce when needed. Had the Rams won, he would have been the lead. After the first couple series, it appeared that Allen was going yo join Higgs as a two-headed monster, but poof!, he disappeared from the passing game. First half injuries to Ferguson and Parkinson limited their production and led the Rams away from “13 “sets in the second half. 27.8 percent usage in the final 30 minutes, down from 45.7% in the first. Rams TE Terrance Ferguson (ankle) probably out against Eagles, McVay said. TE Colby Parkinson (shoulder) to be determined. — Gary Klein (@LATimesklein) September 28, 2026 Offensive line Alaric Jackson (86, 100%) Steve Avila (86, 100%) Coleman Shelton (86, 100%) Kevin Dotson (85, 99%) Warren McClendon (86, 100%) Beaux Limmer ( 1, 1%) A mixed bag, but not good by any stretch. Late blitzing and stunts seem to give the unit trouble. 55 pass attempt is a lot and all had their moment of ignominy. Special teams Kicker Harrison Meevis came back from last week’s miss to be, for all intents and purposes, one of the Rams most effective offensive weapons. Long snapper Joe Cardona got downfield and made a tackle. Punter Ethan Evans Ethan was serviceable. Defensive line Kobie Turner (41, 61%) Braden Fiske (35, 52%) Aaron Donald (35, 52%) Poona Ford (21, 31%) Tyler Davis (20, 30%) Ty Hamilton (9, 13%) In the face of a loss, the Rams defense actually played pretty well. Denver didn’t do anything on the ground, 25 carries for 78 yards and one of those was 14 yard reverse where a tackle was flat out missed well behind the line of scrimmage. Pass rush pressure was not outstanding against a very good offensive line, but they did keep Denver QB Bo Nix off kilter most of the game and batted down a couple of passes at the line. Edge Byron Young (59, 88%) Josaiah Stewart (52, 78%) Wesley Bailey (13, 19%) Desjuan Johnson (12, 18%) While he only has one sack to his credit, Young is 12th in the NFL in pressures and has 21 percent pressure rate after three weeks. Stewart had a quiet game, but I did see him lining up at off-ball linebacker. Don’t know if this a one-off for this week or if it has legs going forward. Nothing noteworthy on Johnson or Bailey. While the pass rush didn’t get a lot of quarterback hits or sacks, they did harry the Giants passing game into a 50 percent completion rate and kept Broncos from consistently attacking downfield. Linebacker Nate Landman (59, 88%) Omar Speights (40, 60%) It seems that on a regular basis, the Rams leave the flats completely uncovered and opposing offenses exploit this to their advantage. Not sure if this is scheme, blown assignments, or the linebackers inability to get out there. Landman was very quiet, while Speights led the team in tackles and had a sack. Safety Quentin Lake (67, 100%) Kamren Curl (66, 99%) Jaylen McCollough (25, 37%) Lake seemed to be all over the place, he’s really at home as a true safety. DC Shula can still move him around the formation but he strikes me a a much better player when he faces the action. Curl was quiet, but the Rams primarily lined him up deep and the Broncos passing game was based around the line of scrimmage, not much downfield action. McCollough subbed in and lined up where the linebackers are usually positioned. Cornerback Trent McDuffie (66, 99%) Emmanuel Forbes (39, 58%) Josh Wallace (58, 87%) Jaylen Watson (20, 30%) McDuffie was again, quite good. Played mostly in the slot this week. Wallace was in the eye of the storm with mixed results. He played outside corner for the first time in a long while. His coverage was tight, had the interception and also batted down a pass on third down, both huge at the time. He also actually got a second INT, but was called for a phantom pass interference penalty. Negatively, late in the game he apparently left his zone wide open and Denver hit the spot for a huge gain. Forbes had a couple of major penalties. He also ran into a teammate and lost track of…
author: Venie Randy Soares

title: The Rams need Puka Nacua more than Puka needs them
summary: It wasn’t long ago that Sean McVay expressed that Puka Nacua had to prove himself as a reliable person before the L.A. Rams would consider extending him like an irreplaceable player, but three weeks into the season it has become apparent that McVay and Matthew Stafford probably need Puka more than he needs them. Puka […]
full_text: It wasn’t long ago that Sean McVay expressed that Puka Nacua had to prove himself as a reliable person before the L.A. Rams would consider extending him like an irreplaceable player, but three weeks into the season it has become apparent that McVay and Matthew Stafford probably need Puka more than he needs them. Puka Nacua will be a number one receiver no matter where he goes and there will be no shortage of teams ready to backup the Brinks for him as a free agent, so it appears that no amount of bad behavior could change the fact that star players have all the leverage. Even when Nacua isn’t on the field he’s making an impact. It’s more apparent than ever that the Rams are just not a good enough team without him, that Stafford’s deep shots aren’t threatening to any defense, so will the front office commit to him now or risk losing him forever? Could his absence even be related to his lack of a commitment? ProFootballTalk’s Mike Florio, for all his flaws, addressed the elephant in the room that nobody else seems to want to talk about : Even if Nacua is legitimately injured, it behooves him to wait this out as long as possible because the Rams haven’t given him a contract extension. “Yes, Nacua’s contract has been delayed by his off-field issues. But with no financial security beyond this year, Nacua surely doesn’t want to risk aggravating the injury and missing even more time. Likewise, he doesn’t want to perform in a way that will reduce the perception that he deserves to be paid among the best in the league at the position.” Because if Nacua plays zero more games this season but is a free agent with a clean bill of health in 2027, it has been proven over and over again that teams will ignore the red flags and pay up like he’s as good as ever. If Nacua could sign with another team today, there’s no question that there are teams out there willing to pay him as the highest-paid receiver in the NFL. That would be at least $42.2 million per season. It doesn’t sound like a very good investment for a player who already had an injury history before and is now set to probably miss his third game in a row, if he even avoids surgery that would keep him out a minimum of six weeks. Puka Nacua (hip, groin) update, via @RapSheet : "I would say sooner rather than later just may not be next week." — Underdog NFL (@UnderdogNFL) September 28, 2026 However, what if Nacua would rather sit out and have surgery BECAUSE the Rams are paying him $5 million instead of $45 million? Wouldn’t you err on the side of caution if playing might cost you $40 million? Or $100 million? Jaxon Smith-Njigba got a $120 million guaranteed from the Seattle Seahawks. Nacua is looking for at least that much and he would deserve it too because some team out there will pay it. They just will. If the Rams don’t pay it, somebody will. If the Rams don’t pay it now, Nacua is motivated to not play for the Rams, knowing that another team is waiting for him when his contract is over. And he knows it. Puka Nacua: “The organization does not believe surgery in this situation will be needed, but it’s also not entirely off the table if Nacua doesn’t show signs of improvement.” Either he returns in Week 4 or he misses 6 weeks due to a sports hernia surgery. Yeah that’s what I… https://t.co/ku5EISZ9rR — Jesse Morse, M.D. (@DrJesseMorse) September 27, 2026 Puka Nacua knows that the Rams have invested in the 2026 season as if it’s their last: Trade for Myles Garrett Trade for Trent McDuffie Bring back Aaron Donald Sign Jaylen Watson He knows that being 1-2 is an embarrassment for the Rams and he knows that L.A. needs him more than ever. How bad would it look if the Rams did all this work only to upset their biggest star and finish 10-7? And don’t get it twisted: Nacua IS the Rams’ current biggest star. For all his faults, his self-inflicted wounds, and his inability to play right now, Nacua is bigger than the reigning MVP, the reigning Defensive Player of the Year, and Aaron Donald. He’s bigger than all of them. This felt especially true on Sunday night, as Stafford struggled for the second time in three games, often launching “Puka balls” up the sidelines or on one of his classic crossing routes, only to find no Puka there to catch it. (I know we’re going to talk about numbers for Davante Adams and Konata Mumpfield, but I’m not talking about just pure receiving yards.) Per Next Gen Stats, the Rams have averaged a full yard per play more when Nacua is on the field compared to when he isn’t. An entire yard PER PLAY. Stafford completed just 54% of his attempts against the Broncos and needed 55 throws to get to 390 yards. On passes of 20 or more yards this season, Stafford is 4-of-12 for 162 yards, one touchdown and two interceptions. Last year, Stafford had 10 touchdowns and only one interception on those throws. His passer rating on deep passes is 70, compared to 122 during his MVP campaign, and is anyone going to argue that Nacua has nothing to do with that? Or McVay’s reputation as one of the NFL’s best offensive coaches, a label that got significantly better again after Nacua was drafted in 2023? Running 13 personnel is a lot easier to do when you have the NFL’s best receiver. And Adams is not the NFL’s best receiver, nor is he 25. Yes, Adams 166 yards per game without Nacua. Mumpfield almost had 100 last night. That’s a far cry from Nacua’s impact of changing how a defense plans for your offense like he does, and the Rams still only scored 26 points (only 10 in the second half, only one drive went longer than 63 yards, and only 2/12 drives resulted in a touchdown) despite all those YARDS. Yes, the Rams beat up the Giants in Week 2 without Puka, but L.A.‘s schedule is only getting harder from there. The Rams have yet to play the Seahawks, have another game against the 49ers, plus Eagles, Bills, Chiefs, Cowboys, and so on. Puka looks at that schedule and knows how thin the margins have become after starting 1-2. The Rams can’t expect to go into another playoffs as a wild card and emerge on the other end as Super Bowl winners. Winning three road playoff games in a row is nearly impossible. That would mean L.A. needs to go 13-1 over the rest of the season to match or come close to the same record that the Seahawks had last year. Maybe 12-2 is just good enough, but any worse than that could be pushing it. So who needs who more right now? Puka Nacua , who — even if he doesn’t take another snap this season — could get $45 million per season from multiple teams as a free agent in 2027. Or… The Rams , who need to rebound from losing to both of the only two good teams they’ve faced so far this season, and the MVP, who launched 166 passes in 2025 to Nacua because that’s how much confidence he has in him? A lot of people tried to play off Nacua as “replaceable” because he does have red flags, both in how he has conducted himself off of the field and how his physical playing style puts him in danger on the field. However, one thing cannot go unsaid: The healthy version of Nacua is more important to the Rams than the unhealthy version of the Rams is important to Nacua.

title: Rams’ Super Bowl hopes might already be in jeopardy
summary: The Los Angeles Rams’ loss to the Denver Broncos on Sunday night was inexcusable and might’ve put their season and Super Bowl hopes in jeopardy. If that’s too much of an overreaction just three games into the season, let me ask you this: Have the Rams resembled a contender at any point through the first […]
full_text: DENVER , CO - SEPTEMBER 27: Matthew Stafford (9) of the Los Angeles Rams leads a drive during the second quarter against the Denver Broncos at Empower Field at Mile High in Denver, Colorado on Sunday, September 27, 2026. (Photo by AAron Ontiveroz/The Denver Post) | Denver Post via Getty Images The Los Angeles Rams’ loss to the Denver Broncos on Sunday night was inexcusable and might’ve put their season and Super Bowl hopes in jeopardy. If that’s too much of an overreaction just three games into the season, let me ask you this: Have the Rams resembled a contender at any point through the first three weeks? And beating up on a Giants squad playing a backup quarterback for much of the game doesn’t count! After getting blown out by the 49ers in the season opener, this was the team’s chance to find redemption and beat a talented, albeit highly flawed Broncos team. Instead of doing that, they allowed Denver to: Outscore them 30-10 in the second half, despite the Rams outgaining them by 225 yards. Become the first team in NFL history to rebound from a scoreless first half when down by double digits, and score over 30 points after halftime in back-to-back seasons. Let an inconsistent Bo Nix survive a mostly dreadful performance, only to have him orchestrate a miracle comeback sent straight from the football gods later. Say what you want about the officiating — which was indeed pure crap — or injuries to key playmakers Terrance Ferguson and Jaylen Watson, the Rams blew it. Short-handed or not, it never should’ve gotten to that point whatsoever. But it did, and LA is now reaping what it sowed as it works to get back into the win column. @nfloncbs This is NOT what we expected #nfl #football ♬ original sound – Meme Effect Only – Meme Effect Only The Rams have certainly navigated slow starts and major injuries before, but this time it feels different. Puka Nacua has already missed more time in the first three weeks than he has all of last season. Myles Garrett , the team’s prized offseason acquisition, hasn’t played since the opener and might not play for a while longer. Almost everything that could go wrong this season has, and we’re not even a quarter of the way through yet. It’s almost fair to wonder if the Rams squandered their best chance in 2025. LA did everything possible to return to the Super Bowl, including getting an MVP performance from Matthew Stafford , but it still wasn’t enough, as they fell short in the NFC Championship. They doubled down (and then some) this offseason to fix their trouble areas, and it might not be enough either. The Rams are no longer the overwhelming Super Bowl favorite they were heading into the 2026 season. According to FanDuel Sportsbook , LA has now fallen behind the Bills, who have +650 odds to hoist the Lombardi Trophy, compared to the Rams’ +700. The Ravens are not too far behind with +950 odds. In fact, Los Angeles has five teams currently in the top 10 of Super Bowl odds left on its schedule, including the Eagles, Bills, Chiefs, a rematch with the 49ers and two late-season matchups with the Seahawks. If that doesn’t turn your already nervous stomach in the slightest, you might want to check your pulse. The Rams have plenty of work to do to get back into the good graces of fans and oddsmakers. Three games generally do not define an entire season. The bad news is that LA has already used up too much of its margin for error. That can always change, as injured players return and the rest of the team finds its rhythm. However, after three games, the Rams don’t look anything like the title contender they were expected to be. Until that changes, it’s fair to wonder whether Los Angeles is already in a fight to save a season they believed had a good chance of ending with another Super Bowl title.

author: Evan Craig

title: Pass protection is more valuable than ever for Matthew Stafford and the Rams
summary: Matthew Stafford did not have his finest game against the Denver Broncos. It wasn’t a complete disaster by any means for the reigning NFL MVP in Week 3. He completed a subpar 54.5% of his passes for a gaudy 390 yards and a pair of touchdowns, but it took him 55 attempts to get there […]
full_text: DENVER , CO - SEPTEMBER 27: Matthew Stafford (9) of the Los Angeles Rams looks at the clock as the last seconds tick off during the third quarter of the Denver Broncos' 30-26 win at Empower Field at Mile High in Denver, Colorado on Sunday, September 27, 2026. (Photo by AAron Ontiveroz/The Denver Post) | Denver Post via Getty Images Matthew Stafford did not have his finest game against the Denver Broncos. It wasn’t a complete disaster by any means for the reigning NFL MVP in Week 3. He completed a subpar 54.5% of his passes for a gaudy 390 yards and a pair of touchdowns, but it took him 55 attempts to get there and he also threw a pair of interceptions, both of which came in the fourth quarter (one of which was returned for a touchdown, one of which was on the final snap of the game). When you dive into the advanced numbers, it’s more of the same. In the loss, Stafford posted just .03 EPA/play, a success rate of just 43% and -0.1 completion percentage over expectation ( all according to RBSDM.com ). Through three weeks, Stafford’s PFF grade is a flat 60.0 , dead-on average by their grading scale. Now, PFF’s grading has always been flawed and is especially unreliable now given what that company has gone through in the last year, but a middling grade at least somewhat matches the eye test through three games. There is one distinct and easy-to-grasp area in which the Rams and their star quarterback are struggling mightily, and it came to a head against the Broncos: pressure. Talanoa Hufanga's 66-yard pick six swung the @Broncos ' win probability by 55.4 percentage points. 🔸 Before INT: 16.3% 🔸 After INT: 71.7% 🔸 WP Swing: +55.4% #LARvsDEN | #BroncosCountry pic.twitter.com/mLmDq82zBe — Next Gen Stats (@NextGenStats) September 28, 2026 According to Next Gen Stats, when under pressure on Sunday night, Stafford was just 5-of-18 passing for 61 yards with the first interception of the night and he was also sacked four times. From a clean pocket, his fortunes couldn’t have been farther in the opposite direction, save for one play. He went 25-of-35 when kept clean, throwing for 329 yards and two touchdowns plus the desperation pick to close the game. That’s 3.4 yards per attempt while under pressure, 9.4 yards per attempt from a clean pocket. It’s easy to understand why that is so devastating to an offense. Obviously, no quarterback in the NFL is ever going to be free from pressure on every snap throughout a game, let alone a season. You have to deal with pressure constantly, especially going up against the league’s best defenses (a group you can still consider the Broncos to be included in). But when the disparity in success is that enormous, it puts even more emphasis on holding the line for your quarterback. Things were even more stark in the second half when Denver made its comeback. The Broncos pressured Stafford on 57.7% of his second-half dropbacks this weekend, compared to just 23.5% in the first half (again from Next Gen Stats). It goes without saying that this is something the Rams have to clean up going forward. Concerningly, this has been a trend through the first sixth of this season. Against the San Francisco 49ers in Week 1, Stafford was pressured on 44% of his dropbacks, the highest pressure rate he had faced since Dec. 2024. No one is going to tell you the offense was spectacular or even good in the opener, and no one is going to tell you they were impressed by the offense in the second half of Week 3. Generate pressure on Matthew Stafford and he is not the same QB. If you cannot generate pressure on the Rams, Stafford will slice and dice you up. Difference between the first and second half of this game. Broncos need to keep Stafford uncomfortable in the pocket. *stats shown… https://t.co/pc7IiDZcDC pic.twitter.com/26wS85EJQl — Investments & Sports Club (@StocksSportsRE) September 28, 2026 Against the Giants in Week 2, by the way, Stafford only faced pressure on five dropbacks and torched that defense. The offensive line was one area that drew some concern, or at least some sideways glances, leading into the season. There’s time to improve and it’s not like they’re wholly lacking talent. But this is a legitimate concern and one that needs to be fixed as quickly as possible. With an aging quarterback who’s not exactly fleet of foot, keeping him upright needs to be addressed urgently. It’s too early to throw in the towel on this team, even at 1-2. That should be a given. But if there’s anything that can derail a title-contending season, your quarterback falling under constant siege and suffering the consequences of it would be at the top of the list.
author: Brendan Dzwierzynski

title: The refs didn’t give up a second and twenty, the Rams did
summary: You can blame the officiating for the latest Los Angeles Rams loss to the Denver Broncos, but I think that misses the point. The Rams had a 16-0 lead lost, retook the lead, late and had the Broncos deep in their own territory on a second and twenty after a holding call against the Broncos. […]
full_text: DENVER, COLORADO - SEPTEMBER 27: Head coach Sean McVay of the Los Angeles Rams shakes hands with head coach Sean Payton of the Denver Broncos after the game at Empower Field At Mile High on September 27, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. The Broncos defeated the Rams 30-26. (Photo by Justin Edmonds/Getty Images) | Getty Images You can blame the officiating for the latest Los Angeles Rams loss to the Denver Broncos, but I think that misses the point. The Rams had a 16-0 lead lost, retook the lead, late and had the Broncos deep in their own territory on a second and twenty after a holding call against the Broncos. The Rams allowed the Broncos to convert easily, keeping them in the game. BIG PLAY PAT BRYANT pic.twitter.com/WeWDOu8xa1 — MileHighReport (@MileHighReport) September 28, 2026 A great game is a story and a great story isn’t about one chapter, but the entire novel. One play didn’t cost the Rams. A number of plays did. The officiating didn’t cost the Rams the game, the Rams put the game in the hands of the officials by not sealing the deal when they were up 16-0. They let the Broncos back in the game, the Broncos won. That’s math. You can find silver linings such as the Rams built the lead in the first place, they played without Puka Nacua, the defense at times looks so much better than last year with Trent McDuffie, the running back room is solid, the special teams didn’t miss a field goal Sunday Night, but the Rams lost. It should hurt for the team and for the fans who take this sport too seriously (like me). This is supposed to be a fun game, but it’s hard to find any fun after that loss, and if you’re paying attention, some of the same problems from 2025 are showing up in 2026. The biggest issue, the failure to close out games while leading. If teams didn’t know they were in a Rams game until the very final whistle, they do now. Blame the refs, blame McVay, blame the pick-six by Matthew Stafford, blame me! I was there! But it doesn’t change the fact that THE RAMS lost. The Broncos won, and in the history books, that’s the part that’ll matters most in the NFL. This season isn’t over, but it’s off to a rough start and this particular loss should sting. If the Rams don’t want to feel this way again, they need to play better. That’s math. Broncos turn lopsided first half into wild back and forth finish vs. Rams (milehighreport) “In the first half, the Los Angeles Rams were in such complete control of the game that it surely looked like a blowout was in full effect. At one point, the Rams were on pace to drop nearly 600 yards of offense. However, the Denver Broncos defense did one good thing and that was limiting them to field goals all through the second quarter. Down 16-0, Bo Nix and the Broncos charged back in the third quarter with two touchdown drives and converting both two-point conversions to tie the game. Then an absolutely wild fourth quarter where both teams would make big plays before Nix and the Broncos drove down the field in the final four minutes to take the lead in the final minute.“ Rams clap back on narrative of Sean McVay ditching media after collapse vs Broncos (sports.yahoo0) “This caused a stir amongst media members as the Rams head coach seemingly ditched the postgame press conference. Nate Atkins of The Athletic revealed how shocking the move by McVay was in a post on X. “Sean McVay ducked out of his press conference before Rams media could get into it, only 10 minutes after the final whistle. Not sure I have ever seen that in this league before,” Atkins wrote . Rams Vice President of Communications Artis Twyman quickly countered the senior NFL writer on X. “Again Nathan, I will not let you get on here and not represent the truth. In the press box, they announce that media that want to attend the post game news conference, leave at the five-minute mark. You chose to stay until the end of the game, which made you late,” Twyman wrote .“ When will Garrett, Nacua return for Rams? (nbcsports) “Mike Florio and Chris Simms assess the timeline for Myles Garrett and Puka Nacua to return from injury, and for the latter, how contract negotiations may affect it.” Bo Nix and Talanoa Hufanga lead the Broncos past the Rams 30-26 in a Sunday night thriller (espn.com) “Nix’s keeper from inches outside the goal line with 47 seconds left capped a wild final five minutes that included a 66-yard pick-6 by Hufanga, a quick touchdown response by Los Angeles and a game-sealing second picked-off pass by Denver’s do-everything safety. “I actually had to have a pep talk with myself,” after dropping two interceptions earlier in the game, said Hufanga, who finished with a sack, a tackle for loss, a quarterback hit and three pass breakups to go with his pair of interceptions.“ Matt Stafford-Taylor Swift cameo, explained: Why Rams QB is appearing in star’s latest music video (sportingnews) “Swift showcased her new music video while accepting the inaugural Artist Director Honors at the 2026 MTV Video Music Awards show on Sunday. While the Rams were busy taking on the Broncos , Stafford went viral for making a surprise cameo, wearing a tuxedo in the background. Dakota Johnson and Colin Farrell joined Stafford among the notable faces in the video:“ From the Podium: Sean McVay, Matthew Stafford and Josh Wallace recap Rams narrow loss to Broncos on Sunday Night Football (therams.com) “DENVER — With three lead changes in the final five minutes of the game, Sunday Night Football between the Rams and Broncos went down to the final play. Unable to score on the final play of the game, Denver ultimately prevailed, 30-26. Rams head coach Sean McVay, quarterback Matthew Stafford and cornerback Josh Wallace gave their thoughts on the game from the podium.“ ‘No panic but there’s frustration.’ Rams blow 16-point lead in stunning loss to Broncos (latimes.com) “DENVER — Mile sigh. A heavy one. The what-the-heck-just-happened kind. That’s how the stunned Rams felt Sunday night. Coach Sean McVay and his team came here aiming to put together a second consecutive impressive prime-time performance. And through the first half against the Denver Broncos, it looked like the Rams would do just that.“ HIGHLIGHTS: Rams top plays in Week 3 vs. Broncos | Josh Wallace’s INT, Tyler Higbee’s TD & more (therams.com) “Watch the Los Angeles Rams’ best plays from the Week 3 matchup against the Denver Broncos on Sunday Night Football.” Broncos vs. Rams final score: Bo Nix caps second-half comeback with late TD as Denver stuns L.A. (cbssports) “The Rams dominated the first half and showed no ill effects of being without the reigning Defensive Player of the Year and a superstar wide receiver. The absences of Myles Garrett and Puka Nacua were a relative afterthought while Los Angeles constructed a 16-0 lead. They out-gained the Broncos 256 to 72 before the break, and they were in total control. But then the Broncos flipped the game on its head. On the other side of the halftime break, Bo Nix connected with Pat Bryant II and Nate Adkins for back-to-back touchdowns and converted the two-point conversion on both of them to level the score before the third quarter had even expired. Denver’s defense also stepped up, as it held the Rams to a meager 19 yards in the frame.“ 2026 NFL season, Week 3: What We Learned from Sunday’s games (nfl.com) “ Rams feel Puka’s absence. A week after Davante Adams turned back the clock and scorched the Giants for 195 yards and a pair of touchdowns, he was stellar again. He racked up game-highs of 137 yards and seven receptions — his 332 yards over the last two weeks are the highest two-game total in his career. But the absence of Puka Nacua , one of the game’s best receivers, was surely felt. By game’s end, Stafford had 390 yards on 30-of-55 passing, but when the Rams offense lulled, it was apparent how beneficial having a second elite WR option would be. Konata Mumpfield had the game of his short career with four grabs for 93 yards and a 48-yard TD catch. But three of…
author: Danny Stone

title: Bill Vinovich is simply awful!
summary: Bill Vinovich has officiated multiple Super Bowls and numerous conference championship games, and the league has repeatedly assigned him to some of its biggest games. But experience and reputation do not make an official immune from criticism when the calls on the field become game-changing. And on Sunday night, Vinovich and his crew once again […]
full_text: DENVER, CO - AUGUST 28: Referee Bill Vinovich looks on in a preseason game between the Denver Broncos and the Minnesota Vikings at Empower Field at Mile High on August 28, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Justin Edmonds/Getty Images) | Getty Images Bill Vinovich has officiated multiple Super Bowls and numerous conference championship games, and the league has repeatedly assigned him to some of its biggest games. But experience and reputation do not make an official immune from criticism when the calls on the field become game-changing. Bill Vinovich will be the referee for Broncos-Rams on Sunday Night Football. Denver has a 5-11 lifetime record in games officiated by Vinovich, including a 1-6 mark at home. Vinovich's crew called 14 accepted penalties in Week 2, about 18% above the NFL average. pic.twitter.com/fYmDcbbuyc — Zack Kelberman (@KelbermanNFL) September 23, 2026 And on Sunday night, Vinovich and his crew once again found themselves at the center of a controversial finish involving the Los Angeles Rams. The Rams lost to the Denver Broncos 30-26 , but one particular decision late in the fourth quarter deserves enormous scrutiny. With Denver facing third-and-6 at the Los Angeles 11-yard line with 1:15 remaining, Bo Nix’s pass intended for Pat Bryant fell incomplete. Josh Wallace was flagged for defensive pass interference , giving Denver an automatic first down. The official play-by-play confirms the penalty and the fact that the play was wiped out. this was called DPI… thoughts? pic.twitter.com/ea6STqux1i — SleeperNFL (@SleeperNFL) September 28, 2026 From the Rams’ perspective, it was an absolutely brutal call. Wallace appeared to make a play on the football, and the replay created an even bigger question about whether Bryant was the player who actually initiated the contact. If anything, the Rams had a legitimate argument that the penalty should have gone the other way for offensive pass interference. Instead, Denver received a fresh set of downs. That changed everything. Rather than forcing the Broncos to face fourth down in the red zone, the penalty allowed Denver to continue the drive. The Broncos subsequently moved closer to the end zone and completed their comeback, turning what could have been a potential Rams victory into a devastating four-point loss. And this is where Vinovich’s history becomes relevant. The most infamous example came in the 2018 NFC Championship Game between Sean Payton’s New Orleans Saints and Sean McVay’s Rams. With the Saints driving late, Rams defensive back Nickell Robey-Coleman made significant contact with Tommylee Lewis before the ball arrived. No pass interference penalty was called. The NFL subsequently acknowledged that the officiating crew missed defensive pass interference and a helmet-to-helmet penalty on the play. Vinovich was the referee for that game. That missed call ultimately helped send the Rams to Super Bowl LIII. Nearly eight years later, Vinovich was again at the center of a critical Rams game — and once again, an officiating decision became a defining moment. To be clear, the Rams made plenty of mistakes themselves. Matthew Stafford threw a pick-six, Denver produced a massive 39-yard conversion on second-and-20, and Stafford’s final pass was intercepted. This was not a perfect Rams performance. But that does not make the Wallace penalty any less significant. Had the interception stood, or had the play been ruled differently, Denver’s drive would have ended in Los Angeles territory. Instead, the Broncos received new life and ultimately completed the comeback. For Rams fans, that is going to make the Vinovich name awfully familiar again — and not for the right reasons.

title: PFF grades: The short-handed Rams really need someone to step up
summary: If you’re looking for silver linings with the Los Angeles currently 1-2 and tied for last place in the NFC West, you probably won’t find them in this week’s grades from Pro Football Focus (PFF). Sunday night’s loss to the Denver Broncos was heartbreaking all around. LA is short-handed. Usually reliable contributors are not performing […]
full_text: DENVER, COLORADO - SEPTEMBER 27: Davante Adams #17 of the Los Angeles Rams runs downfield against Pat Surtain II #2 of the Denver Broncos during the second quarter of the game at Empower Field at Mile High on September 27, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images) | Getty Images If you’re looking for silver linings with the Los Angeles currently 1-2 and tied for last place in the NFC West, you probably won’t find them in this week’s grades from Pro Football Focus (PFF). Sunday night’s loss to the Denver Broncos was heartbreaking all around. LA is short-handed. Usually reliable contributors are not performing up to their individual standards. The Rams desperately need someone to step up and alter the course of the season . So far that hasn’t happened. The team will seemingly continue on this unfortunate trajectory with upcoming tough games against the Eagles, Bills, better-than-expected Cardinals, and the 3-0 Raiders. What can we glean from Sunday night’s shortcomings? Top five grades on offense 1 – Kyren Williams, RB: 85.0 Williams rushed 15 times for 88 yards. He averaged 5.9 yards per carry. He also added six catches for 70 yards through the air. The only thing he did wrong was not carry the ball more, and that is on the offensive play caller. The Rams were quick to shift away from the run and it didn’t play out in their favor. 2 – Tyler Higbee, TE: 81.0 Higbee received a large workload with both Terrance Ferguson and Colby Parkinson limited because of injury. The veteran tight end caught eight of his 11 targets for 62 yards and a score. It’s nice that, even when short-handed, the Rams can turn to a quality and dependable tight end like Higbee. He’s probably not someone you want to run your offense through, however. 3 – Warren McClendon, RT: 69.5 While McClendon led the offensive line in PFF grading, it wasn’t a clean night for the right tackle. He allowed seven pressures in pass protection and was flagged two times. Kevin Dotson was the lowest performer of the group with three pressures. 4 – Davante Adams, WR: 68.0 Adams received the highest target total on offense with 13, although he finished behind Higbee in catches with seven. The veteran ripped off 137 yards in a tough matchup against Patrick Surtain. 52 of Adams’ yards came after the catch point. He dropped one pass. 5 – Konata Mumpfield, WR: 65.9 Second-year receiver Konata Mumpfield came out of nowhere to catch a 48-yard wide open touchdown when his team needed him the most. Mumpfield caught four of his eight targets for 93 yards. He also dropped one pass. Other notes on offense Matthew Stafford finished with a grade of 60.0, which was ninth on the offense overall. Through three weeks, Stafford is PFF’s 27th quarterback in offensive grade and 24th in passing grade. Interceptions have been a major concern. He’s tied for second in the NFL with four behind Drake Maye. More concerning is that the Rams offense has found very little success on the deep ball. Stafford is just 5/13 for 194 yards with one touchdown and three interceptions—good for a PFF passing grade of 58.3. That ranks him 30th in the NFL. How do we explain Stafford’s drop off from last season? Is this late-career decline? Could there be something systemically wrong with LA’s approach? No matter, the Rams need Matthew Stafford to perform better and fast. Top five grades on defense 1 – Omar Speights, MLB: 89.8 Speights earned an impressive sack on Bo Nix that came at an opportune time. He notched two pressures on six pass rushing attempts. His run defense grade of 90.3 led the defense and he recorded two stops. 2 – Jaylen Watson, CB: 83.5 Watson played only 20 snaps before injuring his shoulder and exiting the game. The Rams defense had the Broncos bottled up until that point, and there was a clear drop off when his replacements came in. LA must cross their fingers that Watson doesn’t miss much time moving forward. 3 – Josh Wallace, CB: 78.7 Put the controversial defensive pass interference call aside, Josh Wallace was still stingy in coverage. He allowed a single catch on three targets for 27 yards and caught an interception on a pass disrupted by Kobie Turner. If Watson misses time, Wallace should be the next man up. 4 – Quentin Lake, DB: 78.4 Lake allowed three catches on four targets, but he minimized the damage in terms of yards with 15. He’s started the season off well and added another two pass break ups in this game. 5 – Byron Young, EDGE: 77.4 Young led the Rams with seven pressures. The next closest total was two and there were four players: Speights, Aaron Donald, Josaiah Stewart, and Braden Fiske. Kobie Turner and Tyler Davis each had one. That production isn’t good enough. All attention will be on slowing down Young while Myles Garrett is out. Someone else needs to step up. Other notes on defense It wasn’t the best night for Trent McDuffie, although he faced a tough matchup in Jaylen Waddle. McDuffie finished eighth in defensive grading and allowed two passes on five targets for 48 yards with a pass break up. Nate Landman earned a coverage grade of 62.9 but allowed a passing touchdown on his lone target.

title: Rookies Mike Washington, Zeke Masses come up big in Week 3 win
summary: Here is a look at how the Las Vegas Raiders’ 2026 draft class (eight of the 10 picks are on the 53-man roster) fared in a 35-27 Week 3 win at the New Orleans Saints and what to look for Sunday at home against the Kansas City Chiefs: Fernando Mendoza:The No. 1 overall pick served […]
full_text: (Photo by Morgan Simmons/Getty Images) | Getty Images Here is a look at how the Las Vegas Raiders’ 2026 draft class (eight of the 10 picks are on the 53-man roster) fared in a 35-27 Week 3 win at the New Orleans Saints and what to look for Sunday at home against the Kansas City Chiefs: Fernando Mendoza: The No. 1 overall pick served as Kirk Cousins backup. He did not play. But he’s on a streak. Mendoza hasn’t been part of a team that has lost since 2024. Treydan Stukes: The Raiders’ second-round pick was out because of a concussion he suffered in Week 2. He is expected to be back this week and the Raiders need him against Travis Kelce. Trey Zuhn: The third-round pick played five offensive plays after playing two plays in Week 2. He was even lined up in an H-back role Sunday. Coach Klint Kubiak is finding ways to get his players involved. Jermod McCoy: The fourth-round pick played 12 special teams snaps, but none on defense. He played 18 defensive snaps in Week 2. Mike Washington: The fourth-round pick played 16 percent of the snaps after playing 19 percent of the snaps in the first two games. Washington made his snaps count as he had a 36-yard touchdown run in the third quarter to get the Raiders back in the game as they finished the game with 19 unanswered points. He has 102 rushing yards on 15 carries. Dalton Johnson: The fifth-round pick safety was a healthy scratch for the third straight game. Him being inactive with Stukes out isn’t a great sign. Zeke Masses: The fifth-round pick is now a clear starting cornerback. He started for an injured Darien Porter in Week 2. Porter was healthy in Week 3 and Masses still started. Masses made a big interception in the fourth quarter at the Saints and he has three interceptions in the past two games. He’s an exciting playmaker. Malik Benson: The sixth-round pick played four offensive snaps and two on special teams. He was targeted once with no catches and had one punt return for 13 yards.
