title: Geno Smith’s fumble ruins strong outing and costs New York Jets a win
summary: The 2026 season couldn’t have started any better for the Las Vegas Raiders, who wrap up September with a perfect 3-0 record. Like last week, the Raiders aren’t missing any of their offseason losses so far, but let’s check in on a few old friends to see how Week 3 fared for them. Geno Smith […]
full_text: (Photo by Nic Antaya/Getty Images) | Getty Images The 2026 season couldn’t have started any better for the Las Vegas Raiders , who wrap up September with a perfect 3-0 record . Like last week, the Raiders aren’t missing any of their offseason losses so far, but let’s check in on a few old friends to see how Week 3 fared for them. Geno Smith Score: 31-24 Jets lose Stats: 31/37 (83.8%), 321 yards, 3 TDs, 0 INTs Smith played pretty well against the Detroit Lions, carving up the Lions’ defense for the first 300-yard game he’s had since his Raiders’ debut in last year’s season opener . The veteran quarterback also helped rookie tight end Kenyon Sadiq announce himself to the league, with Sadiq hauling in seven passes for 105 yards and a score. New York even tied it up with about four minutes left in the fourth quarter. However, Smith was sacked five times and fumbled in scoring territory on the last one, ending any comeback hopes. GENO SMITH FOR THE WIN 🔥 pic.twitter.com/E2U1MIQGP5 — BrickCenter (@BrickCenter_) September 27, 2026 Dylan Parham Score: 31-24 Jets lose Staying in New York, Parham seems to have found new life with the Jets this season. Heading into the game, he was Pro Football Focus’ highest-graded guard with an elite mark of 92.8 through two weeks (h/t Jets Media on X/Twitter ). However, Week 3 was a different story for Parham. Before PFF’s review, he had an ugly 47.1 grade and really struggled as a run blocker (46.1). On top of that, he suffered a knee injury and was “quickly ruled out”, according to The Athletic’s Zach Rosenblatt . At the time of writing, there’s no word on the severity of Parham’s injury. Darren Waller Score: 21-18 Panthers lose Stats: 5 catches, 51 yards Truth be told, Waller should have been featured in last week’s check-in. He had a pair of touchdowns against the Atlanta Falcons in Week 2, but this past Sunday was his highest receiving total of the campaign so far. Waller also finished as Carolina’s second-leading receiver, finding the Fountain of Youth after turning 34 years old earlier in the month. Additionally, he’s becoming one of Bryce Young’s favorite targets, with a team-leading eight passes coming his way against the Browns. As a side note, don’t look now, but Cleveland is 2-1 with back-to-back wins!
author: Matt Holder

title: Brock Bowers returns with vengeance in Las Vegas Raiders’ Week 3 win vs. New Orleans Saints
summary: It’s been a while since Las Vegas Raiders fans have had this much to cheer about at the end of September. Five years, to be exact, as the Raiders’ Week 3 win over the New Orleans Saints improved their record to a perfect 3-0 for the first time since 2021. It wasn’t the prettiest game, […]
full_text: (Photo by Morgan Simmons/Getty Images) | Getty Images It’s been a while since Las Vegas Raiders fans have had this much to cheer about at the end of September. Five years, to be exact, as the Raiders’ Week 3 win over the New Orleans Saints improved their record to a perfect 3-0 for the first time since 2021. It wasn’t the prettiest game, with Las Vegas having to overcome a fourth-quarter deficit to pull off the upset on the road. But the Silver and Black embraced Al Davis’ “Just win, baby!” mantra and got the job done, leading to a positive tune for this week’s winners and losers. WINNER: Brock Bowers Sunday was not only Bowers’ season debut, but also his first game in 273 days after ending last year on injured reserve, and he reminded everyone why he’s so great. The tight end hauled in 10 catches for 116 yards and a touchdown and was the team’s leading receiver by a wide margin, with six more grabs (nine more targets) and 73 more yards than any other Raiders pass-catcher. What’s even more exciting is that Klint Kubiak is using Bowers all over the field, with 39% of his pass snaps coming as a slot receiver, another 39% out wide and 17.1% as an in-line tight end against the Saints, per Pro Football Focus . That’s part of what can make Las Vegas’ offense scary moving forward, as the team ranks tied for seventh with 29.3 points per game and Kubiak has only had his best chess piece for one game. Good morning pic.twitter.com/wYRAqA1VQ1 — Ian Hartitz (@Ihartitz) September 28, 2026 WINNER: Malcolm Koonce The Raiders have been waiting for Koonce to take the next step, signing him to “prove-it” contracts in back-to-back offseasons. He was solid in the first two games of the campaign, but really came alive in New Orleans. The 2021 third-round pick tied Maxx Crosby for the team lead with six pressures and did it on just 21 pass-rush snaps while Crosby had 39 rushes, per PFF . On top of that, most (if not all) of Koonce’s production came when it mattered most: the fourth quarter. He helped fuel the Raiders’ comeback effort and close the door on the Saints, coming up with a strip-sack that set up Las Vegas’ go-ahead touchdown and a quarterback hit that caused an interception and led to another score to go up eight points. That helped Koonce earn the second-highest PFF pass-rush grade ( 91.6 ) among edge rushers in Week 3, pre- Monday Night Football . LOSER: Jackson Powers-Johnson To be fair, the entire Raiders’ offensive line has struggled in the running game since the season opener. But Powers-Johnson has been one of the unit’s biggest problems, failing to record a PFF run-blocking grade above the baseline (60.0) in all three games. He hit a new low against the Saints with an ugly 34.6 mark . Additionally, the third-year pro has battled injuries throughout his career and exited Sunday’s game early. It was only five total snaps and just four in the running game, but backup Caleb Rogers — who JPJ was competing for a starting spot with in training camp — posted a 74.9 grade as a run blocker. Again, it’s a small sample size. But between Powers-Johnson getting banged up and struggling on the field, plenty of signs point to Kubiak making a change at right guard in the near future. WINNER: Nakobe Dean Nakobe Dean, the turnover machine! The free-agent signing has become arguably Las Vegas’ most-impactful defender, forcing a fumble in each of the team’s first three games of the season. He also led the team in tackles (12) , again, and made plenty of plays near the line of scrimmage with five ‘ defensive stops ’, tied for the sixth-most among Week 3 linebackers according to PFF . Three of those came in coverage , and Dean added a PBU to his stat line, earning an elite 90.4 overall mark from PFF. #Raiders LB Nakobe Dean had 3 forced fumbles in 4 seasons with the Eagles. He has three forced fumbles in the first three games with Las Vegas. He has a league-high 22 solo tackles, as well. pic.twitter.com/vXcCYGEvcX — Ryan McFadden (@ryanmcfadden_) September 28, 2026 LOSER: Isaiah Pola-Mao It’s safe to say that the Raiders have missed starting free safety Treydan Stukes, who left the Chargers game early with a concussion and didn’t clear the NFL’s protocol in time to suit up this past Sunday. Meanwhile, Pola-Mao had a bad coverage break in Los Angeles, and his issues carried over to New Orleans, allowing five completions on five targets for 39 yards and three of the Saints’ four touchdowns . The good news is that he’s just a backup. But the bad news is that the Raiders are clearly thin at safety and could be in trouble if Stukes has to miss more time or suffers another injury down the line. WINNER: Kirk Cousins After a shaky performance in Week 1, Cousins has silenced the doubters over the last two games. He tossed three more touchdowns and was two yards shy of having back-to-back 250-yard performances. Also, it was clear that having a reliable intermediate target in Bowers helped the quarterback have a more efficient outing and gave him a safety valve. Plenty of people (understandably) want to see Fernando Mendoza make his NFL debut. However, they’re going to have to be more patient if Cousins continues to play like this. LOSER: Eric Stokes Stokes might be the luckiest corner in the league right now, as he’s still yet to force an incompletion, per PFF . He was targeted seven times by the Saints and only gave up four catches for 40 yards. But one of the passes that hit the ground was a missed deep shot by Tyler Shough, where the wide receiver, Bryce Lance, was wide open for an explosive play. Additionally, the veteran corner bit on a play-action fake that left tight end Noah Fant open in the flat, allowing Fant to secure the catch and run the ball into the end zone. Through three games, Stokes has been targeted 10 times and given up 113 yards for two touchdowns . All of those numbers are the most among the Raiders’ cornerbacks, and he gave up 28 receptions on 50 targets for 261 yards and just one score in 16 games last year. With Hezekiah Masses rising and Darien Porter playing well in the season opener, Rob Leonard might have to make a change in the secondary if Stokes doesn’t turn things around quickly.
author: Matt Holder

title: We’re witnessing a different breed of Raiders as team drops Saints 35-27
summary: How easy would it have been for the Silver & Black to wilt after the opposition not only scored a touchdown to take the lead, but recovered the fumble on the ensuing kick off, and two plays later, made another end zone visit. But Klint Kubiak, his coaching staff, and players apparently don’t like to […]
full_text: (Photo by Chris Graythen/Getty Images) | Getty Images How easy would it have been for the Silver & Black to wilt after the opposition not only scored a touchdown to take the lead, but recovered the fumble on the ensuing kick off, and two plays later, made another end zone visit. But Klint Kubiak, his coaching staff, and players apparently don’t like to do things “easy”. For the third straight game on the young 2026 season, Kubiak’s Las Vegas Raiders stared down adversity in the face, smirked, got the job done. This time, it was on the road against the New Orleans Saints, and instead of succumbing to quick-sand situations the Raiders were well-accustomed to do in year’s past, Las Vegas answered the ball, rose to the occasion, and earned an impressive 35-27 victory. Once more we saw complementary Raiders football where the defense picked up the offense and vice versa, despite special teams gaffes. Instead of collapsing under the immense pressure — on the road against a quailty New Orleans squad, Las Vegas persevered and won. The performances and results harken on the old adage: Once is an accident, twice is a coincidence, three times is a pattern. The first time the Raiders showcased resolve to win in the season opener against the Miami Dolphins was eyebrow raising. The second time they did it by beating the Los Angeles Chargers piqued interest. Doing it for the third time at New Orleans certainly firmly establishes a pattern. And it harkens on this: We’re witnessing a different breed of Silver & Black with Kubiak at the helm. RAIDERS FORCE ANOTHER FUMBLE AND CALL GAME ‼️ pic.twitter.com/oGMruwoPuT — NFL (@NFL) September 27, 2026 After trading touchdowns in the second quarter to knot the score at 13, Las Vegas moved the ball into the red zone during a two-minute drill and hit a field goal to take a 16-13 lead into halftime. The potential double-dip was thwarted, however, as the Raiders did receive the second-half kick off only to go three-and-out. And this began the downward spiral for the Silver & Black. Kellen Moore’s Saints offense went on an impressive 12-play, 87-yard touchdown drive that chewed 6:50 off the clock. And with 20-16 lead in hand, New Orleans scooped up in inexplicable fumble by Las Vegas running back and kick return man Dylan Laube. Like noted above, two plays and 32 yards later, Saints quarterback Tyler Shough found tight end Noah Fant for a 16-yard touchdown, 27-16 New Orleans. Instead of wallowing in the series of unfortunate events, however, Kubiak’s offense ran five plays culminating in rookie running back Mike Washington Jr. finding daylight and immolating New Orleans defense on a 36-yard touchdown run. Trailing just 27-22 after the two teams traded punts to close the third quarter, the Saints went on a spiral of their own. As our Matt Holder noted shortly after the game, all four of the Saints’ possessions in the fourth quarter ended in turnovers . That great equalizer gave the Raiders ample runway for two final stanza touchdowns — a four-yard touchdown strike from quarterback Kirk Cousins to wide receiver Cody White and four-yard dime from Cousins to tight end Brock Bowers, 35-27 Las Vegas. Brock Bowers came back and immediately looked like Brock Bowers again. 10 REC, 116 REC YDS, 1 TD vs Saints Can Bowers help push the Raiders into the playoffs? https://t.co/cvv8di0xYV pic.twitter.com/uNetudtQdk — Football Performances (@NFLPerformances) September 27, 2026 Let’s hit the quick slants as fast as Rob Leonard’s Raiders defense took the ball away from the Saints: —Cousins went 22 of 33 for 248 yards with three touchdowns , no interceptions, while getting sacked three times against the Saints. The veteran quarterback has thrown three touchdown passes in the first trio of games validating Kubiak’s decision to roll with the 38-year-old signal caller over No. 1 pick Fernando Mendoza. —“Brock-tober Fest” arrived early as Bowers’ had an outstanding season debut with 10 catches for 116 yards and one touchdown. The tight end lined up all over the formation from traditional in-line and split tight end and even in the slot and perimeter that’s normally reserved for a wide receiver. —Raiders starting running back Ashton Jeanty carried the rock 19 times for 56 yards and a paltry 2.9 yards per carry average. One has to wonder if his ankle is 100 percent but Washington provided juice of his own with five carries for 54 yards including the scintillating touchdown. —Linebacker Nakobe Dean is proving the Raiders wise for giving him a big-money deal in free agency as the veteran paced the team with 12 total tackles, a stop for loss, and a forced fumble to slam the door on the Saints collective faces. This after he forced a key fumble to help Las Vegas win last week. —Leonard’s defense forced four turnovers from the Saints. A trio were forced fumbles — two on sacks; one from defensive end Malcolm Koonce and the other from strong safety Jeremy Chinn — and the other an interception by rookie cornerback Hezekiah Masses (his third pick on the young season). Fair to say Raiders LB Nakobe Dean has been a good signing 27 tackles, 1.5 sacks, 3 FF & 3 Wins pic.twitter.com/uJWmuVzp24 https://t.co/zPO8QG05Su — Clint Goss (@NFLDraftDome) September 27, 2026 —Getting rookie safety Treydan Stukes back in the Raiders secondary can’t happen soon enough. Inactive due to a concussion sustained in Week 2, veteran Isaiah Pola-Mao got the start and the Saints picked on him frequently as he was charted giving up three of Shough’s four touchdown passes. Quotes of Note “When I hit him, I saw the ball come up. I thought the ball was going forward so I just assumed it was a strip sack. It was very rewarding. We knew whole time (in) the second half, we knew the defense was going to have to show up.” —Las Vegas Raiders defensive end Malcolm Koonce on his forced fumble “We knew we had to rally back, we had to start back playing our type of football. And that’s our style of play, taking the ball away. We got a goal every week, ‘How many takeaways are we going to get?’ We had none in the first half, so we had to come back in the second half strong.” —Las Vegas Raiders middle linebacker Nakobe Dean on defense’s mentality Up Next It’s a battle of AFC West unbeatens next Sunday when the Raiders (3-0) host the unbeaten Kansas City Chiefs (3-0) who picked up their first road win of the season with a 24-10 victory over the Miami Dolphins this past Sunday. Powered by Patrick Mahomes efficient afternoon and running back Kenneth Walker III’s two-touchdown outing (one rushing, another receiving) the Chiefs sit atop the division alongside the Raiders. It’s an AFC West that features Kansas City and Las Vegas on top, the Denver Broncos at 2-1 and the Los Angeles Chargers at 0-3.
author: Ray Aspuria

title: Raiders News: Week 3 AFC West roundup, stage set for Las Vegas-Kansas City battle for 1st place

That sets the stage for a huge matchup next Sunday, where the top spot in the division is on the line against the 3-0 Kansas City […]
full_text: (Photo by David Eulitt/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Las Vegas Raiders managed to end September undefeated, taking down the New Orleans Saints 35-27 in Week 3 to remain tied for first place in the AFC West. That sets the stage for a huge matchup next Sunday, where the top spot in the division is on the line against the 3-0 Kansas City Chiefs. But before that, let’s also check in on how the Los Angeles Chargers and Denver Broncos fared on Sunday. Chiefs vs. Dolphins Score: 24-10 Chiefs win Key Stats: QB Patrick Mahomes: 20/24 (83.3%), 246 yards, 2 TDs, 1 INT RB Kenneth Walker III: 18 carries, 70 yards, 1 TD, 1 receiving TD WR Rashee Rice: 7 catches, 88 yards LB Nick Bolton: 11 tackles, 1 TFL, 1 PD CB Mansoor Delane: 10 tackles, 1 TFL, 1 PD It seemed like Kansas City was pretty much on cruise control in Miami. Mahomes hit Travis Kelce for a 48-yard gain on the Chiefs’ first play from scrimmage, setting up a Walker touchdown to go up 7-0 on the opening drive. The Dolphins did answer with a touchdown drive of their own, but that was the closest the game got, as the Chiefs came right back and scored the next time they had the ball. It’s safe to say Mahomes and the Chiefs are back, winning two out of three contests by multiple possessions. But the Raiders have done the same, heightening the stakes for next week’s matchup. Chargers vs. Bills Score: 24-16 Chargers lose Key Stats: QB Justin Herbert: 20/34 (58.8%), 226 yards, 1 TD, 1 INT RB Omarion Hampton: 15 carries, 56 yards WR Tre’ Harris: 6 catches, 76 yards LB Daiyan Henley: 9 tackles, 2 FRs EDG Tuli Tuipulotu: 6 tackles, 1.5 sacks, 1 TFL, 2 QB hits The Chargers Chargered. Los Angeles had a legitimate chance to pull off a major upset on the road. Next week: @ Seahawks Broncos vs. Rams Score: 30-26 Broncos win Key Stats: QB Bo Nix: 17/34 (50.0%), 186 yards, 2 TDs, 1 INT, 1 rushing TD RB J.K. Dobbins: 17 carries, 49 yards WR Pat Bryant: 2 catches, 44 yards, 1 TD (1 2pt conversion) S Talanoa Hufanga: 5 tackles, 1 sack, 3 PDs, 2 INTs DT Zach Allen: 2 tackles, 1 sack, 5 QB hits This game looked like a snooze fest in the first half before the Broncos finally woke up in the third and fourth quarters. Denver’s offense couldn’t get anything going, with no points heading into the locker room, before putting up 30 to pull off the come-from-behind win. Still, the Broncos offense is struggling to find its footing under new play caller Davis Webb. They only put up 257 yards and were outgained by 225 yards in the contest. Through three weeks, Cousins has proven that he can still sling it, which makes this a dangerous team. At the rate things are going, Fernando Mendoza might not start a game all year.”

title: Miami Dolphins’ Most Valuable Player | Week Three | Protection is key
summary: The Miami Dolphins didn’t defeat the Kansas City Chiefs in week three — they lost 24-10 — but they held their own against one of the best teams in the National Football League for much of the contest. It’s a moral victory for a team that has struggled through three weeks of the 2026 NFL […]
full_text: MIAMI GARDENS, FL - AUGUST 20: Miami Dolphins center Aaron Brewer (55) speaks to the media during a New York Giants and Miami Dolphins joint practice at the Miami Dolphins Training Camp on August 20 2026, at the Baptist Health Training Complex in Miami Gardens, FL. (Photo by Doug Murray/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Miami Dolphins didn’t defeat the Kansas City Chiefs in week three — they lost 24-10 — but they held their own against one of the best teams in the National Football League for much of the contest. It’s a moral victory for a team that has struggled through three weeks of the 2026 NFL season. If Miami continue to show incremental improvement as the year rolls on, the foundation that new general manager Jon-Eric Sullivan and new head coach Jeff Hafley have talked about wanting to establish will prove beneficial to future versions of Dolphins teams. One area the Dolphins needed to show improvement in was protecting the quarterback. Malik Willis had been sacked nine times through Miami’s first two games — 5 times against the Raiders in week one and 4 times against the 49ers in week two. Against the Chiefs, improvement was made — as Willis wasn’t sacked a single time on the afternoon. Miami Dolphins Week Three MVP – OC Aaron Brewer A major reason why Willis was able to avoid Kansas City’s pass rush was the play of Miami’s starting center Aaron Brewer. Brewer was the Dolphins’ highest graded offensive lineman by Pro Football Focus in week three — earning a 72.6 overall grade. Obviously Brewer did not give up a sack against the Chiefs — no one did — but through three games in 2026, Brewer has not allowed an opposing defender to bring his quarterback down a single time. With running back De’Von Achane being lost for the season due to an ACL tear, the Dolphins will need every single remaining healthy player to take a step forward if they want to continue make positive developments in 2026. Brewer is now Miami’s most impactful offensive player. His play this season will go a long way towards determining how many notches the Dolphins can put in the win column in 2026 and beyond. MVP TRACKER Week One – WR Caleb Douglas Week Two – LB Jacob Rodriguez Week Three – OC Aaron Brewer

title: Miami Dolphins Fans Take On Game Three
summary: While losing 24–10 is certainly a decisive defeat, many Miami Dolphins fans likely expected a much worse outcome against the Kansas City Chiefs. Regardless, this marks another frustrating loss, and the situation is compounded by the news that the Dolphins’ standout best player, De’Von Achane, will miss the remainder of the season with a torn […]
full_text: MIAMI GARDENS, FLORIDA - SEPTEMBER 27: Malik Willis #2 of the Miami Dolphins runs the ball against the Kansas City Chiefs during the first quarter at Hard Rock Stadium on September 27, 2026 in Miami Gardens, Florida. (Photo by Alie Skowronski/Getty Images) | Getty Images While losing 24–10 is certainly a decisive defeat, many Miami Dolphins fans likely expected a much worse outcome against the Kansas City Chiefs. Regardless, this marks another frustrating loss, and the situation is compounded by the news that the Dolphins’ standout best player, De’Von Achane, will miss the remainder of the season with a torn ACL. While sidelining Achane during a rebuilding season may be pragmatic, I worry the new front office will struggle to properly evaluate Malik Willis without enough quality playmakers around him to show his true capabilities. Following yesterday’s game against the Chiefs we asked the following question: Below are some of your thoughts on this game and the state of our Miami Dolphins- ImRightYoureWrong was already fearing what we now know. Achane feared to have a serious knee injury Get better son, there’s always next year…… Csouza breaks down the different things they saw across the roster as far as growth or lack there of. My overall thoughts: Offensive Line- Showed a lot of improvement in pass protection. Saw some good communication in passing off stunts as well. Only consistent pressure is when KC blitzed. Run blocking can still use some work, but that also might be reflective of Gordon not being the most intuitive back Willis- Unfortunately, as a Florida Gators fan, he is starting to remind me of Anthony Richardson. Great athleticism and arm, but the mechanics fall apart leading to inaccuracy. This is something that can be worked on, but hard to break bad habits when you’re used to letting your arm make up for issues. DL- Showed some improvement from previous games. After getting gashed in the first half, the yards were harder for Walker in the second with multiple tackles behind the line of scrimmage. Some pressure, but nothing consistent enough to actually effect a qb like Mahomes. DB- They are all young and inexperienced. The zone defense is simply not working. There is a lack of communication and players are not passed off the way they should be leading to all of these wide open players. I understand the philosophy of keeping everyone in front and forcing the team to work their way down the field; however, this is failing the team. The line gives too much time to the quarterback. This team needs to be more man to man. That plays to the strengths of our cbs, rather than embracing a philosophy that is doomed to failure. Good coaching adapts to the players you have, rather than forces them into a system. StanleyDoyle1 has several legit concerns and also some signs of hope. The comments after the game indicate that we are grading on a curve in a class of 1, given that just about everyone is straining to point out that a few players did well today. But I am concerned for a few reasons, none of which relate to the loss this game: We’ve invested an inordinate amount of draft picks in the defensive line over the past few years, and at this stage we should expect this to be the dominant or at least competent unit. It’s not, and none of the DTs or DEs has stood out. To the contrary, they are worse than last year. OK, so Robinson and Uche had 2 or 3 pressures? Are we really celebrating this, given that the team has ZERO SACKS after 3 games? This looks like a scheme and a coaching problem. Or maybe I’m just avoiding the horrifying truth that it’s a talent issue. Willis is exactly who I — and maybe two or three others who withstood a barrage of criticism on this site for being unpatriotic — thought he would be. The O-line gave him time this week. With a couple exceptions, he was slow to process, made occasional poor decisions, and made inaccurate throws downfield. Wait, I thought he was supposed to be this super-accurate long-ball thrower? As predicted before the season started, he’s obviously not the solution. If we were playing Madden, it might be fun to watch him use his great athleticism to run 5 yards. We’re not playing Madden. It’s not fun. The playcalling has been atrocious. The offense is entirely predictable. Maybe that’s because we have young players and need to keep it simple. Three touchdowns in three games. I can’t see how Slowak survives this offseason. The reason for hope: Rodriguez, Taafe, Bell, Proctor and most of the rest of the rookie class. They deserve better coaching. surfla8 believes things are headed in the right direction. Just one takeaway: It should be apparent at this point that the team is improving. With money and a few good picks, 2027 could be watchable. Zen4Phins sees week over week improvment. Defense did well against the run. 6 tfl and 5 qb hits. Willis was flinging the ball, held it less and no sacks allowed. Rodriguez was awesome. Special teams tackling was good again. Coleman looked sharp on returns. Thought we could’ve tried a long fg, gonna need a few of those. Pass coverage was spotty. Dropped a few passes today. Still too many penalties. Overall thought they looked good. I’ve been drinking aqua, orange, white, blue, and sometimes black kool aid for years and this year has a different taste. Each week feels like a slightly better taste than last. IWLU272 points to a mistake that has stuck with me as well. I don’t understand that gamble at that point of hte game. Hafley should be called out, especially by himself, for the decision to go for it on 4th and 6 from their own 47 yd line with 6:00 left in the game. They had 2 timeouts left plus the 2 minute warning and were down by 7 points. Punt the ball and pin them deep. By not punting the ball, he told his defense that he has zero confidence in them. Of course they did not get the first down and KC took over at Miami’s 47 and the rest is history. Really a bone headed call by Hafley, IMO. MIAMI235 is not associating the injury with the new deal or are they? Good thing we gave that big contract for the 127 yards Achane got so far. REALLY good player, but how many times have we seen the payday contract, quickly followed by a big injury. Mattylady seems pleased with the improvement overall. Actually, it wasn’t that bad. Expected a higher scoring game from the chiefs,Miami D,held them pretty good until the fourth quarter. Probably their best game so far,except for the dumb penalties on both sides of the ball,had TD,negated due to a penalty, a big 4th down stop onKC,which gave them another opportunity to score and kC did.Clean up those penalties, and Ollie looked great,hopefully Archane won’t be out for long,nothing serious I hope. Spok507 is another who has seen some steady improvement. This team, while young and inexperienced, has managed to improve with each game. This was not an easy win for the Chiefs. They got stopped on 4th down, had another turnover, and the defense held them back quite a few times. I wish Haf would’ve trusted them to maybe make another stop instead of going on 4th down at midfield with 6 minutes and two TOs left. Jacob Rodriguez is a stud. We have no secondary, but the line and linebackers are good. It’d be nice to find a pass rush outside of Chop, tho. The offense, even without Achane and Douglas, looked improved. They moved the ball and the play calling was a lot more inventive than before. There were mistakes, but correctable ones that will change with experience. Ollie Gordon, Bell, Washington and Uchich really stepped up. All in all, they were competetive and managed to stay in the game for 3 quarters. Eliminate the bogus shift call that took a TD away, and this might have ended differently. I’m optimistic they can keep improving. The Vikings, despite being 3-0, don’t look very good— especially with Kyler Murray playing. We should look better against them. Left Shark sees a team that is learning to win. I see progress from week to…

title: Miami Dolphins excluded from the NFL Coat of Arms
summary: I watched yesterday’s game where the Miami Dolphins fell to the KC Chiefs 10-10 and the NFL referees 14-0. The combined score was KC/NFL Refs 24 – Miami/out of favors 10.  I can’t even talk about the Dolphins performance until I unpack the completed slanted officiating. Unless the “anointed team” completely no shows, the refs […]
full_text: OTTAWA, CANADA MARCH 8:The official seal of the United States is displayed outside the U.S. Embassy, in Ottawa, Ontario, Canada, on March 8, 2025. (Photo by Artur Widak/NurPhoto via Getty Images) | NurPhoto via Getty Images I watched yesterday’s game where the Miami Dolphins fell to the KC Chiefs 10-10 and the NFL referees 14-0. The combined score was KC/NFL Refs 24 – Miami/out of favors 10. I can’t even talk about the Dolphins performance until I unpack the completed slanted officiating. Unless the “anointed team” completely no shows, the refs in every sport will put their hoofs on the scales of justice to benefit whatever team is anointed. I remember the Heat beating the Chicago Bulls in Jordan’s heyday at the old Miami Arena. I was in attendance. Steffi Graf, Jack Nickalus, Cal Ripken, Jr. and I think Ferdie Pacheco were also there to watch the GOAT. However, Rex Champman hit like 7 or 8 3-pointers and the Heat beat down the Bulls. If the game would’ve been closer, the refs would have carried the Bulls over the finish line as they usually did for MJ. We saw this in full effect today. The NFL officiating is the biggest embarrassment in the history of the American experience. There is no attempt to improve it. It really makes you think that the NFL decides who will win each game before the season begins in some type of Star Chamber (check out this Michael Douglas movie if you can). In the olden days in England, powerful folks would meet outside at night under the stars to decide the guilt or innocence of some individual and then they would carry out the sentence(hence the term Star Chamber). It makes you think the powers that be have money on the game. I could literally write a hundred pages on how many garbage calls have went against the Dolphins over the last 40 years. I know other teams get screwed too but our pendulum is stuck to the bad. Many of these calls are simply inexplicable. And if you complain, the NFL punishes you. I still do not understand how the NFL gets aways with this, KNOWING they have an anti-trust exemption from the U.S. government. In what other American endeavor outside of sports can a member of that organization NOT criticize a corporation publicly? If I worked at Acme and criticized them, yes they would fire me and rightfully so and I can go public if I have evidence of their wrong doing However, again Acme does not have an anti-trust exemption or at least that is what the Coyote told me 😊. There is NOTHING less American than the NFL stifling free speech. The NFL practices in gross negligence and then has the buffoonish broadcasters and their “so called officiating expert” Gene Steratore come out and bless every single call. For those of you who don’t know, Steratore was the absolute buffoon moron who screwed the Dolphins against the Steelers in Miami (2010, I think) where the Steelers fumbled the ball in the end zone, THE FINS RECOVERED THE DAMN BALL, and this complete moron said there wasn’t a clear recovery and gave the ball back to the Steelers. It turns out this guy grew up in Pittsburgh and was allowed to ref an NFL with the Steelers. How in the name of God can this happen? So, this is the buffoon who was asked about the sissy roughing the passer call against Chop Robinson? This was a total garbage call because what was Chop supposed to do, sack Mahomes and use his “Homelander” super powers to fly away at the last nano-second? Momentum and gravity made Chop land on Mahomes, not intent. But Mahomes is the anointed one by the NFL, just like Brady was. It you launch an “air biscuit” against Brady or Mahomes it is an automatic 15-yard penalty. They cannot be touched. Period. So Steratore weighed in on that one but where was Steratore when Malik’s helmet was pulled off? Nowhere to be found. Where was Steratore when the player pulled Achane’s facemask on the play where he was hurt? Nowhere to be found. The NFL officiating cannot be criticized and it NEVER makes a mistake. In the legal world, attorneys must avoid EVEN the appearance of impropriety. Not the NFL. In my many travels to London, I noticed many stores (usually the elite ones like Harrod’s) have these shields up on the top corner of the store entrances. I asked what those were and I was told there was an official process to apply for the shield. These shields let the general public know that this business is preferred by the royal family; I just read that they had to be updated for the transition to King Charles. So I want to figure out how the Dolphins can earn the NFL preferred shield? Do we need to run ads with Malik’s and Devon’s shirts off? Maybe Jacob Rodriguez can appear on the cover of Men’s Fitness magazine with his shirt off? I am wide open to suggestions. Maybe I will reach out to King Charles?

title: Fins Up, Fins Down | Winners and losers from Miami Dolphins week three loss
summary: The Miami Dolphins showed signs of life against the Kansas City Chiefs — keeping the deficit to just one score until a late touchdown pass from Patrick Mahomes to Travis Kelce sealed their fate. Unfortunately, “keeping it close” doesn’t amount to a hill of beans in the win/loss column. However, like head coach Jeff Hafley […]
full_text: LAS VEGAS, NEVADA - SEPTEMBER 13: Chris Bell #18 of the Miami Dolphins warms up before the NFL game at Allegiant Stadium on September 13, 2026 in Las Vegas, Nevada. The Raiders defeated the Dolphins 27-13. (Photo by Christian Petersen/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Miami Dolphins showed signs of life against the Kansas City Chiefs — keeping the deficit to just one score until a late touchdown pass from Patrick Mahomes to Travis Kelce sealed their fate. Unfortunately, “keeping it close” doesn’t amount to a hill of beans in the win/loss column. However, like head coach Jeff Hafley has preached since he took the job in Miami, this year isn’t necessarily about winning or losing — it’s about showing growth, building a solid foundation and getting better every time the team takes the field. I believe they did that against the Chiefs. So, whose stock is up and whose stock is down after week three’s loss to Kansas City? FINS UP Our Fins Up player from Miami’s week three loss is rookie receiver Chris Bell. Fellow standout rookie Caleb Douglas sat out this week’s game due to an ankle injury, giving Bell an opportunity to shine. He did just that — nabbing four receptions for a team leading 67 yards receiving — nearly 1/3 of quarterback Malik Willis’ 210 yards passing. Bell’s quick return to action following a late-season ACL tear last November while playing in college at Louisville is nothing short of astounding. He’s shown flashes of the player who was talked about as a late first-round selection in the 2026 NFL Draft prior to his knee injury, and as he continues to work his way back to full strength, the Dolphins will continue to benefit from his solid play. I don’t think we’re too far away from Bell’s first touchdown grab as a member of the Miami Dolphins. Can he find paydirt this weekend against the Minnesota Vikings? Stay tuned! FINS DOWN Through no fault of his own, running back De’Von Achane earns this week’s Fins Down designation. On just his third carry of the game against Kansas City, Miami’s electric running back went down with a seemingly innocuous knee injury. Unfortunately, it was anything but. Achane wouldn’t return to the game — further hampering Miami’s already wounded rushing attack. The Dolphins would amass just 46 yards rushing from players not named Achane or Malik Willis for the rest of the tilt against the Chiefs. Following the loss, Hafley said the early outlooks regarding Achane’s knee “ do not sound very optimistic. ” Those are not the words any Dolphins’ fan wants to hear when it comes to the team’s most dangerous weapon.
author: Marek Brave

title: De’Von Achane injury: What free agents are available for Miami Dolphins?
summary: The Miami Dolphins lost running back De’Von Achane to a torn ACL on Sunday, ending the season for the team’s top rusher and a 2025 Pro Bowl selection. Miami currently has two running backs, Jaylen Wright and Ollie Gordon II, on the 53-man roster, with Jarquez Hunter and Carlos Washington, Jr., on the practice squad. […]
full_text: LAS VEGAS, NEVADA - JANUARY 04: Kareem Hunt #29 of the Kansas City Chiefs warms up before the game against the Las Vegas Raiders at Allegiant Stadium on January 04, 2026 in Las Vegas, Nevada. The Raiders defeated the Kansas City Chiefs 14-12. (Photo by Candice Ward/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Miami Dolphins lost running back De’Von Achane to a torn ACL on Sunday, ending the season for the team’s top rusher and a 2025 Pro Bowl selection. Miami currently has two running backs, Jaylen Wright and Ollie Gordon II, on the 53-man roster, with Jarquez Hunter and Carlos Washington, Jr., on the practice squad. Miami could look to move forward with that group, but they could also look to add a veteran free agent. But who is available? Miami is not going to break the bank to sign someone, but they could look to add a veteran on a minimum deal, making sure they have the depth needed to get through the season. The Dolphins’ running game is the focal point of the offensive system, and they are going to need increased depth at the position without Achane. Kareem Hunt The former Kansas City Chiefs running back was a Pro Bowl selection in 2017 as a rookie when he led the league in rushing yards. He finished last year with 163 carriers for 611 yards and eight touchdowns. He is not a direct replacement for Achane, but could provide another power option with Gordon, serving as a compliment to Wright’s speed. He would not be a workload carrying running back at this point in his career, but he could be a good veteran rotation guy who can handle 10 carries a game. Raheem Mostert Could Miami bring back former Dolphins runner Mostert to solidify the group? Mostert has bounced around the league throughout much of his career, but had extended periods with the San Francisco 49ers (2016-2021) and Miami (2022-2024). He was selected to the Pro Bowl in 2023 when he led the league in rushing touchdowns with Miami. In 12 games with the Las Vegas Raiders last year, he recorded just 22 carries for yards. He clearly would not be the number one option, but could serve as a rotational player when Wright and Gordon need a break. Joe Mixon The Dolphins could look to add Mixon if he clears the medical concerns that cost him the entire 2025 season. If his foot is healthy, and that is obviously a question mark, he could still be the played that picked up 1,016 yards in 2024 with the Houston Texans. He could be a workhorse, taking a large number of carries, but he is not going to be a direct replacement for Achane. Miami could consider him as the second option, letting Wright lead the group. Nick Chubb Chubb just re-signed with the Cleveland Browns to ceremony retire as a member of the team, but the Dolphins could look to sign him for the remainder of the year. Wright would likely remain the top option for Miami, but Chubb could be a more physical rotational playe with him. He might slide ahead of Gordon on the depth chart once he is fully engaged in the offense. Chubb sustained a knee injury in 2023 and did not return to full form in 2024 or 2025. He only has 224 carries and 838 yards the last two seasons. Cam Akers Akers is only 27 years old, so there is potential to still land a running back with potential to reach. However, after being a second-round pick in 2020, he has played for five different teams in seven different stretches. He was at his best with his first team, the Los Angeles Rams, from 2020 through 2023, and he has a great combination of speed and power. But, in 2025, he only appeared in three games with no carries for Seattle. He would only be a rotational player with the Dolphins, giving Wright a break when needed. Other options Other players Miami could consider include Dalvin Cook, Antonio Gibson, D’Onta Foreman, Ronald Jones II, Alexander Mattison, and Miles Sanders. Would you consider any of them? Was there someone not on the list you would consider?

title: De’Von Achane injury: Dolphins lose running back for season
summary: Miami Dolphins running back De’Von Achane left the team’s Week 3 loss to the Kansas City Chiefs in the first quarter with a knee injury. He was soon ruled out of a return to the game, then head coach Jeff Hafley said after the game he was not “optimistic” about the injury. On Monday morning, […]
full_text: MIAMI GARDENS, FLORIDA - DECEMBER 28: De'Von Achane #28 of the Miami Dolphins walks off the field after beating the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in an NFL football game at Hard Rock Stadium on December 28, 2025 in Miami Gardens, Florida. (Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images) | Getty Images Miami Dolphins running back De’Von Achane left the team’s Week 3 loss to the Kansas City Chiefs in the first quarter with a knee injury. He was soon ruled out of a return to the game, then head coach Jeff Hafley said after the game he was not “optimistic” about the injury. On Monday morning, that lack of optimism was confirmed with Achane’s injury confirmed. According to ESPN’s Adam Schefter and NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport, Achane sustained a torn ACL and will be out for the remainder of the season. Achane was the center of the Dolphins’ offense this year as they work their way through a rebuild. As Miami focuses on the development of their younger players, including rookie wide receivers Caleb Douglas, Chris Bell, and Kevin Coleman, Jr., Achane provided a veteran stabilizing presence to the attack. Miami will now have to figure out how to replace the man around who they built their entire offensive system. Achane was selected to his first Pro Bowl after last season when he tallied 1,350 rushing yard. He was injured as he was tackled on an 11-yard run. Kansas City Chiefs safety Alohi Gillman tackled Achane by his head, twisting the running back’s body awkwardly around his left leg. The running back slowly got up from the field and slowly walked off the field, flanked by trainers. He spent time walking on the sideline before heading back to the locker room. He eventually returned to the sideline during the game, but was never able to get back on the field. Miami’s running back group is now headlined by Jaylen Wright and Ollie Gordon II. Wright missed the team’s Week 3 game with a stringer and foot injury. Wide receiver Malik Washington was used as a running back to provide relief to Gordon following Achane’s injury. Running backs Jarquez Hunter and Carlos Washington, Jr., are on Miami’s practice squad. The team could also look to sign a free agent to provide depth at the position. Achane will likely be on a timeline to return during training camp or just before the regular season in 2027, depending on how he recovers from surgery. This story will be updated with more information as it is available.

title: Vikes Views: Nincompoop of the Week – Week 3 Vikings at Buccaneers
summary: Your Minnesota Vikings went on the road to defeat the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, 23-16. 3-0 never felt so unsatisfying, so if you’re not done complaining yet, let’s talk about who was terrible this past Sunday. Kyler Murray Murray being on this list might be a little harsh, but it’s the NFL. Murray’s start to his […]
full_text: MINNEAPOLIS, MINNESOTA - SEPTEMBER 13: General manger Nolan Teasley of the Minnesota Vikings looks on before a game against the Green Bay Packers at U.S. Bank Stadium on September 13, 2026 in Minneapolis, Minnesota. (Photo by Stephen Maturen/Getty Images) | Getty Images Your Minnesota Vikings went on the road to defeat the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, 23-16. 3-0 never felt so unsatisfying, so if you’re not done complaining yet, let’s talk about who was terrible this past Sunday. Kyler Murray Murray being on this list might be a little harsh, but it’s the NFL. Murray’s start to his Minnesota tenure has not been ideal. The Buccaneers should’ve been put away long before they were and it’s the offensive incompetence in Minnesota that kept them in the game. I’m not ready to give up on Murray after one full game as the starter, but . his start to his Minnesota tenure hasn’t exactly inspired confidence. Vikings Offensive Line The Vikings’ OL did not do Kyler any favors on Sunday. The offensive tackles might have been the weakest spots on the line. Christian Darrisaw allowed a sack and committed a holding penalty. O’Neill couldn’t block anyone in the run game. Tampa’s defensive line is good, but they’re not that good. Keith Carter’s squad is going to have to regroup after a rough performance. Josh Metellus The Vikings allowed quite a few chunk plays on Sunday and it seemed Metellus was at the center of it. He seems to be struggling to find his place on this defense. Metellus has been a weak spot on the defense all three weeks so far. Theo Jackson At some point, potential has to turn into production. Jackson has been given a larger role in the defense this season and continues to be the player opposing offenses seem most interested in testing. Missed tackles, bad angles, and almost zero impact plays from Jackson. Nolan Teasley I am not the biggest J.J. McCarthy fan in the world, but he has shown some promise. He wasn’t completely awful, and he’s still very young. The Vikings have no clear long-term direction at quarterback right now, and it seems silly to pass up any potential solution for a fifth-round draft pick. Teasley’s first major move feels like a gamble the Vikings didn’t need to make. There are too many quarterback injuries around the league and too much uncertainty within the organization to move on from a former first-round pick for a Day 3 selection. From where I sit, the Vikings should have gotten more in return or held onto McCarthy a little longer. It’s the Nincompoop of the Week, it’s not that serious, it’s just football.

title: Vikings 3-0: J.J. McCarthy Traded, Kyler Murray Wasn’t the Problem, Defense Is Record-Breaking
summary: Vikings trade J.J. McCarthy to Giants for a fifth-round pick; Forness breaks the bust label, All-22 on Kyler Murray, and O’Connell’s second-half collapse. — Tyler Forness and Dave Stefano of The Real Forno Show (a Vikings 1st & SKOL production) opened with the news that Minnesota dealt 2024 first-rounder J.J. McCarthy to the New York […]
full_text: TAMPA, FL - SEPTEMBER 27: TAMPA, FL - SEPTEMBER 27: Minnesota Vikings quarterback Kyler Murray (1) prepares to throw before a game between the Tampa Bay Buccaneers and the Minnesota Vikings, Sunday, September 27, 2026 at Raymond James Stadium in Tampa, Florida (Photo by Ricky Bowden/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Vikings trade J.J. McCarthy to Giants for a fifth-round pick; Forness breaks the bust label, All-22 on Kyler Murray, and O’Connell’s second-half collapse. — Tyler Forness and Dave Stefano of The Real Forno Show (a Vikings 1st & SKOL production) opened with the news that Minnesota dealt 2024 first-rounder J.J. McCarthy to the New York Giants for an unconditional fifth-round pick. Forness said the lack of escalators “really tells you where the value was in the trade market,” comparing it to Antonio Brown’s modest return at his peak. He argued the move “does right by McCarthy” by sending him to a team that once considered him at No. 6 and now needs a quarterback after Jackson Dart’s knee injury. Multiple matching reports from Alec Lewis and others about process inconsistency and off-field “eccentric” traits, Forness said, put McCarthy below the “hot crazy line”: talent existed, but “the play wasn’t good enough to match some of the behind the scenes stuff.” He called McCarthy “probably the biggest bust in Vikings history outside of maybe Demetrius Underwood,” while wishing him well as a backup to Jameis Winston. The hosts then turned to Sunday’s ugly offensive tape versus Tampa Bay. Forness, after watching All-22, insisted “Kyler Murray was not bad” even if stats looked poor. Early chunk plays (dagger to Justin Jefferson, corner and post to Jordan Addison) worked; the second half collapsed because Todd Bowles’ heavy fronts and deep linebackers clogged the intermediate windows Kevin O’Connell’s scheme lives on. “O’Connell got his ass absolutely handed to him by Todd Bowles,” Forness said, citing missing mesh, shallow crosses, and spacing concepts that could have baited linebackers. Protection was mostly clean (fastest sack 5.3 seconds), three batted balls were not height-related, and miscommunications with T.J. Hockenson and Addison were chemistry issues seen with prior quarterbacks. The defense, meanwhile, is “historic”: Forness cited a ~71% blitz rate on Baker Mayfield dropbacks and called it the highest ever recorded. Key Points: McCarthy traded Monday for a raw fifth-rounder; talks accelerated after Dart’s injury. No conditions surprised Forness; market simply wasn’t there once the league knew Minnesota was done. Giants offer a fresh start with John Harbaugh familiarity and Joe Schoen’s prior interest. Murray’s first-half 5-of-8, ~100 yards, TD vs. second-half drought blamed on play-calling, not the QB. Worst offensive success rate in 20 years; defense’s unique, repeatable blitz packages are the bright spot. Fifth-rounder may be flipped for a tight end (Josh Oliver torn bicep) or running back depth. Next: home vs. Dolphins and Malik Willis; Jefferson’s MRI “looked good.” Listen: Or on your favorite podcast aggregator. Watch: The Vikings sit 3-0 with an elite defense and an unresolved quarterback future. Forness’s All-22 take will fuel debate all week. Listen to the full Real Forno Show for the unfiltered tape study, trade context, and what O’Connell must fix before Sunday. Fan with Us!!! So here’s questions for you: What would you have done with McCarthy—and do you buy that Murray wasn’t the problem? Are you buying the historic defense as a legitimate Super Bowl foundation, or do the offensive concerns worry you more than the 3-0 record suggests?

title: Vikings Autopsy: Daily Norseman Week 3 Postgame Roundtable (A 23-16 win over the Buccaneers)
summary: Hello everyone, and welcome to the Week 3 Minnesota Vikings postgame roundtable here at Daily Norseman. The Vikes are coming off a nail-biter in Tampa, beating the Bucs 23-16, and remain alone atop the NFC North at 3-0. Where does the offense go from here? Ostensibly…up, right? How quickly can the Vikings have a Brinks […]
full_text: TAMPA, FLORIDA - SEPTEMBER 27: Kyler Murray #1 of the Minnesota Vikings passes during the game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Raymond James Stadium on September 27, 2026 in Tampa, Florida. (Photo by Mike Ehrmann/Getty Images) | Getty Images Hello everyone, and welcome to the Week 3 Minnesota Vikings postgame roundtable here at Daily Norseman. The Vikes are coming off a nail-biter in Tampa, beating the Bucs 23-16, and remain alone atop the NFC North at 3-0. Where does the offense go from here? Ostensibly…up, right? How quickly can the Vikings have a Brinks truck backed up to Brian Flores’ house with a lifetime contract and ALLLLL the money? Let’s talk to it: Question 1: Let’s freestyle for a minute — get your initial thoughts out about the Vikings beating the Bucs in Week 3, 23-16. Brandon Warne : I feel like a broken record, but damn….it wasn’t pretty. But at the end of the day, a win is a win, and it still kinda feels like a Black-and-Blue Division win against the Bucs, even if there isn’t an NFC Central anymore. Anyone else agree? No? The offense remains spotty, but I think I’m less worried about it than I usually would be given a few factors that I’ll get into as we progress here. Nobody in the NFC North has looked flawless, and if you weren’t feeling great about beating the Packers, who lost to the Falcons, maybe it feels a bit better to know the boys beat the Bears, who took down the mighty Eagles on Monday Night Football. Christopher Gates : Thank goodness for Brian Flores, because if that guy wasn’t running this defense and doing absolutely maniacal things to opposing offenses, I don’t know where this team would be right now. The offense is, honestly, a bottom-three offense in the NFL for any number of reasons, but this defense keeps dragging the team to victories somehow. It’s obviously not sustainable over the long term, but it will work against teams like the Buccaneers that are also having issues on offense. They’ll need to pick it up at some point. Are they capable of it? Ehhhhhhhhhhhh… Warren Ludford : It was a win on the road, so that was great, but it’s frustrating that the offense isn’t playing better. Losing Justin Jefferson after the first drive was more of a game-planning loss than people think. Not only did the Vikings lose their best player on offense, but they also had a game plan built around running the passing game through Jefferson. So, when he was lost after the first drive, receivers had to be given different roles, and perhaps different plays, etc., and they had to improvise plays they hadn’t practiced during the week, etc., etc. If Jefferson was out all week, they could have come up with a game plan without him, but losing him after the first drive forced them to improvise the rest of the game with stuff the receivers hadn’t practiced. The Bucs eventually doubled Addison too, and the other receivers didn’t get open much, and there isn’t any chemistry between Murray and them. The Bucs defense is pretty good too, but being down Jefferson (and Jordan Mason) has had an effect. Craig Williams : Why is it that when this team starts a season great, it never feels good? The offense is obviously worrisome. They also gave up a few big plays on defense. A better team would’ve beaten the Vikings on Sunday. Shawn C. : Fortunate. But 3-0 is 3-0. But make no mistake: this team has a definite ceiling with the current offense; I don’t care if our defense ends up being the 1985 Bears. It must get fixed. The passing game is anemic by 1970s standards. Sam Buegler : A win is a win is a win, but oof. That was not a fun watch. Brian Flores, I will personally make sure you never have to buy a drink in Minnesota again, even if it bankrupts me. ————— Question 2: Who was your Vikings MVP? BW : I have the benefit of reading everyone’s answers before my own, so how about I go off-script just a little bit…let’s give some love to Johnny Hekker. Sure, he has some name value — inasmuch as a punter can in this day and age outside of Pat McAfee — but to come off the street and punt eight times, average more than 46.0 yards per boot with a couple inside the 20 and a long of more than 60 yards? In a day where the offense was playing like the conditions were similar to a week earlier, I think that has a ton of value. CG : Who else but Will Reichard? It’s strange not to have an overwhelming sense of dread every time a Minnesota Vikings kicker takes the field, but Reichard has become so automatic that seeing him trot out onto the field is almost comforting at this point. I’m sure there’s absolutely no chance expressing that sentiment will come back to bite me later in any way, shape, or form. Honorable mention to Myles Price, who finally managed a long return and didn’t have it called back by a ridiculous penalty. WL : I’ll say Will Reichard, although Myles Price or Jordan Addison are contenders too. Reichard had 11 points total, including two field goals from 50+, which made the difference. CW : Vikings MVP Will Reichard always comes through and was perfect again. The 56-yarder was massive. Eric Wilson had a great day and was saved by a no-call on a facemask. SC : Could be a handful of players on defense, but I’ll go with Myles Price, as he continues an early-season All-Pro trajectory, and his touchdown won the game for the Vikings. SB : Reichard. He is the definition of consistency no matter what, and he just proves it again and again. Price also housing the punt was something we have been waiting for, and it was so nice to finally see it happen. But nailing three kicks and a few extra points again forces my hand in giving it to Will the Thrill. ————— Question 3: Who was your Vikings LVP? BW : I have a hard time saying anyone else other than Kyler Murray, though I think his performance on the Josh Freeman scale is still only like a 40/100. His accuracy was scattershot, and his wheels saved him from perhaps an even worse day than it already was, but it was functionally his first/only full game with the team on the heels of suffering a concussion early in Week 1. Lord knows we all deserve some grace, but if Murray still looks like this in a couple weeks…we’ve got problems. CG : It’s Kyler Murray. Yes, it’s one game, and Justin Jefferson got hurt and this and that and whatever. I was told Murray was the “veteran presence” who would help elevate Kevin O’Connell’s offense to the level we saw with Sam Darnold or Kirk Cousins behind center. All I saw was a guy with happy feet, even when the offensive line gave him plenty of time, who seemed scared to use the mobility that was supposed to separate him from other potential options the Vikings had at the position. He was awful on Sunday, no two ways about it. WL : I’ll go with Josh Metellus. It looked like he gave up the long TD to Ted Hurst, which was big for the Bucs, who otherwise couldn’t generate many points. He’s been the weak link in the secondary so far this season- and that was predictable. CW : Kyler Murray looked bad in his debut. The OL also struggled. The entire offense outside of Addison, I guess, would be my answer. So KOC? SC : Kyler Murray. I do think the loss of Justin Jefferson early threw the entire game plan out of whack, but his overall performance was still poor. The numbers are what the numbers are. I expect improvement over the next two weeks. I mean, there has to be, right? SB : The Vikings’ rushing attack. Aaron Jones had a few good runs, but otherwise no one could get anything going. Dallas and Claiborne combined for three yards. We need to bring in another back, or find a new way to get someone other than Jones going, because we can’t work him the way we did last week. It’s unsustainable. ————— Question 4: Where do you stand on Kyler Murray right now? BW : As I said earlier, I’m still cautiously optimistic. If Murray still looks like this in a few weeks, it’s time to start watching some college football to see who we like in the upcoming draft. My early thought? It’s a solid…

title: Justin Jefferson Avoids Serious Injury, Could Play Sunday
summary: In what has been an already full news day for fans of the Minnesota Vikings, it appears that their star player has dodged a pretty significant bullet on the injury front. Numerous reports have come down saying that wide receiver Justin Jefferson suffered an ankle sprain in Minnesota’s 23-16 victory over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers […]
full_text: TAMPA, FL - SEPTEMBER 27: Minnesota Vikings wide receiver Justin Jefferson (18) runs ahead during a game between the Tampa Bay Buccaneers and the Minnesota Vikings, Sunday, September 27, 2026 at Raymond James Stadium in Tampa, Florida (Photo by Ricky Bowden/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images In what has been an already full news day for fans of the Minnesota Vikings, it appears that their star player has dodged a pretty significant bullet on the injury front. Numerous reports have come down saying that wide receiver Justin Jefferson suffered an ankle sprain in Minnesota’s 23-16 victory over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Sunday afternoon, but that he avoided any serious injury and that there’s even a chance that he could play this coming Sunday when the Vikings face the Miami Dolphins at U.S. Bank Stadium. Jefferson caught two passes on the Vikings’ opening drive against the Buccaneers, the second of which was a screen pass that set up a Will Reichard field goal to give the Vikings the first points of the game. On the play, Jefferson went down awkwardly and went to the blue medical tent, where he was deemed questionable to return with an ankle injury. He stayed on the sideline until just before halftime, when he went back to the locker room. He did not come back out with the team for the second half and was ruled out for the game shortly thereafter. My guess is that we won’t know for sure whether Jefferson will play until the final injury reports come out on Friday afternoon, but at least we know that, at least for now, this doesn’t appear to be a long-term injury for the Vikings’ star wide receiver. Given the way the Vikings’ offense looked at Raymond James Stadium without him on the field, that can only be seen as a good thing for their hopes going forward.

title: Vikes Views: Sunday King – Vikings at Buccaneers
summary: The Minnesota Vikings won on the road in Tampa Bay, in an ugly game. There were 17 punts, 3 Interceptions, and 17 penalties. Three different times, the teams combined for five consecutive possessions ending in punts. The teams averaged less than 17 yards per possession in a defensive battle. The two defenses are stout, but […]
full_text: TAMPA, FLORIDA - SEPTEMBER 27: Myles Price #4 of the Minnesota Vikings is congratulated after a touchdown in the first half during the game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Raymond James Stadium on September 27, 2026 in Tampa, Florida. (Photo by Mike Ehrmann/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Minnesota Vikings won on the road in Tampa Bay, in an ugly game. There were 17 punts, 3 Interceptions, and 17 penalties. Three different times, the teams combined for five consecutive possessions ending in punts. The teams averaged less than 17 yards per possession in a defensive battle. The two defenses are stout, but they were assisted with some questionable offensive play by both teams’ QB and OL. The team is 3-0 overall, 2-0 in the NFC North, and 2-0 on the road. It’s a great start and we’ll just have to hope the offense figures things out eventually. Here are my nominees for Player of the Game. Eric Wilson It was another fantastic defensive performance and Eric Wilson was at the center of most of the action. He was flying around the field yesterday. Wilson led the team with 10 total tackles and added 1.5 sacks. Jordan Addison Addison was the lone bright spot on offense. He has been open quite often this year and hasn’t received the service he deserves. He took advantage of his opportunity after Jefferson went down with 5 catches for 90 yards and a beautiful 41-yard touchdown. He almost pulled down another bomb later in the game, but he was unable to corral an underthrown deep ball. Myles Price Sometimes all you need is a spark. Price’s punt return touchdown gave the Vikings the breathing room they needed to keep the pressure on Tampa’s offense all day. Price looked electric on punts and kicks all day. If he finds a crease, he’s dangerous. Will Reichard Another week, another perfect day for Will Reichard. Will is a weapon and the way this team is playing, they’re going to be needing him a lot this season. Kyle Van Noy Van Noy had his first sack for the Vikings in the 2nd quarter. It was part of four consecutive three-and-outs (2 for each team). He also had a couple of more tackles for loss in the run game. Van Noy has quickly become another weapon in Brian Flores’ arsenal. Honorable Mention: Johnny Hekker – Hekker was solid all day, nothing insanely good, but solid. Great on holds too! Jalen Redmond – another solid performance from Redmond. His deflection almost resulted in an interception. Dallas Turner – Turner was disruptive all game once again. At some point we’re going to run out of ways to say he’s playing great football. Blake Cashman – he could’ve been listed up there with Eric Wilson, but his best pass breakup was friednly fire on the ball that was tipped by Redmond.

summary: Last week, I briefly talked about how the nonsensical trade rumors had started surrounding Minnesota Vikings quarterback J.J. McCarthy. McCarthy #9 of the Minnesota Vikings celebrates with Justin Jefferson #18 after his touchdown pass against the Dallas Cowboys during the fourth quarter at AT&T Stadium on December 14, 2025 in Arlington, Texas. title: The Vikings Could Be Without Josh Oliver For A While
summary: The Minnesota Vikings lost a significantly underrated part of their offense on Sunday, and the fear is that he could be out for a long time. . .potentially for the remainder of the season. Ian Rapoport of the NFL Network is reporting that the Vikings believe that tight end Josh Oliver may have suffered a […]
full_text: MINNEAPOLIS, MN - JANUARY 04: Minnesota Vikings tight end Josh Oliver (84) warms up before the NFL game between the Green Bay Packers and Minnesota Vikings on January 4th, 2026, at U.S. Bank Stadium in Minneapolis, MN. (Photo by Bailey Hillesheim/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Minnesota Vikings lost a significantly underrated part of their offense on Sunday, and the fear is that he could be out for a long time. . .potentially for the remainder of the season. #Vikings TE Josh Oliver is feared to have suffered a torn biceps in Sunday’s game and will have an MRI today determine if that is the case, sources say. Oliver would be out indefinitely if the testing confirms. pic.twitter.com/pHZG0hj8kX — Ian Rapoport (@RapSheet) September 28, 2026 Ian Rapoport of the NFL Network is reporting that the Vikings believe that tight end Josh Oliver may have suffered a torn bicep in Sunday’s victory over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, and that the injury may require surgery. If that’s the case, he could be out indefinitely. Oliver has been one of the best blocking tight ends in football for quite a while now, and signed a new three-year contract extension with the team in 2025. If the Vikings are without him for any length of time, it will impact a running game that has already had its issues through the first three weeks of the season. In Oliver’s absence, the role of the second tight end would likely be filled by Gavin Bartholomew. Bartholomew was the Vikings’ seventh-round pick in the 2025 NFL Draft, but did not play at all in his rookie season while dealing with a back injury that left him on the Physically Unable to Perform List for the majority of the year. Bartholomew has played just four snaps on offense through the first three games this season. The Vikings also have former Cincinnati Bengals tight end Cam Grandy on the practice squad, though Grandy has mostly been a special teamer to this point in his NFL career. Here’s hoping that the injury to Josh Oliver isn’t as severe as the Vikings are fearing that it is and he’ll be back in the fold sooner rather than later.

full_text: A 1-2 start to the 2026 season has left many questions for New England Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel to try and answer. The biggest? Getting Drake Maye back on track. Through three games, Maye has thrown six interceptions in addition to losing a fumble. Decision-making seems to be the biggest issue early on for the quarterback, who was pulled in the fourth quarter of Sunday’s 35-6 blowout loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars. “I think quarterbacks want to make plays. I think they want to throw touchdowns. I think sometimes when Greg and I go golfing, we really want to make a good score, right? Sometimes we’re so focused on it, we try to choke the life out of the golf club, and we’re squeezing it so damn tight that the ball has no choice but to go sideways,” Vrabel said Monday morning on WEEI’s The Greg Hill Show . “We need to stop trying to choke the life out of every single play. We need to relax. We need to settle in and go play football and not try to force things that aren’t there.” Later in the day, Vrabel was asked how he goes about addressing that issue while also raising Maye’s confidence level. “Confidence comes from your preparation, and it comes from going out there. I can’t manufacture confidence. I can’t just say, ‘Hey, be confident.’ You have to practice. You have to hit those plays in practice, and you have to feel good about it,” Vrabel said. “Sometimes you want to do something so badly. It’s like the tighter you hold the golf club, the more crooked it goes when you hit it. We just have to be able to make sure that we’re on the same page, that everybody knows what is expected of them, have a few details and then go play football.” Following Sunday’s game, Maye said there was nothing wrong with his right shoulder that was injured in last year’s AFC Championship Game. However, the quarterback didn’t say there weren’t lingering effects from the hit. Vrabel, meanwhile, said he was not aware of any ongoing injury concerns before adding he doesn’t “anticipate that being an issue going forward.” Now, with the head coach looking for answers ahead of next Sunday’s showdown with the Buffalo Bills, Vrabel was asked if simplifying the offense is necessary. “When you have games like that throughout the entire team – how do you fix some things? You get back to the basics,” Vrabel said. “Again, we want to continue to impress upon the importance of what our identity is. We still have to build it. You have to put it out there. Before you can protect something, you have to build it. And we have to get back to the basics. “So, some of that is, do you do less and try to do it better? Or do you go and you try to scheme up a bunch of stuff and hope you hit it? I think at the end of the day, there’s a great balance. I thought we had a couple of good scheme plays and we didn’t hit them. They made it and we didn’t. … So, I think to your question, you never want to go into a game when a guy is unsure, right? But how much we do, we’ll look at that, and we’ll look at everything that we can do to help us win here on the road.”
