title: NY Giants news: Brian Burns out for the year, Giants acquire J.J. McCarthy, more
summary: Good morning, New York Giants fans! Here are the stories you need to know the day after the Giants acquire QB J.J. McCarthy and lose Brian Burns for the year. NFL trade deadline grades: J.J. McCarthy to the Giants | ESPN.com Giants grade: C. But the Giants’ front office should look in the mirror over […]
full_text: Good morning, New York Giants fans! Here are the stories you need to know the day after the Giants acquire QB J.J. McCarthy and lose Brian Burns for the year. NFL trade deadline grades: J.J. McCarthy to the Giants | ESPN.com Giants grade: C. But the Giants’ front office should look in the mirror over its bungling of the Winston situation. It’s not unreasonable for the Giants to be aggressive in finding a better replacement given how much time is left in the season. But they clearly shouldn’t have signed Winston to an extension right before the season if this is how they feel about him! Even though Murray is a free agent at the end of this season, McCarthy’s ship had already sailed in Minnesota after he couldn’t beat out Wentz. If he wasn’t going to be the Vikings’ backup quarterback, his value would likely have continued to drop. To get a fifth-round pick while saving a few million across his remaining 2026 and 2027 compensation (not nothing!) makes sense. They have uncertainty at quarterback in 2027, yes. But that was true whether McCarthy was there or not. McCarthy throws against Dallas, Washington So many cutups against the Cowboys and Commanders. Yeah I’m all in. LETS RUN IT @jjmccarthy09 pic.twitter.com/whFFmwj8Ep — Anthony (@AnthonyGros13) September 28, 2026 Giants made the one QB trade that offered hope, even if it doesn’t guarantee anything | Yahoo Sports! Yet it at least has a chance to work, which is likely better than you can say about the other options the Giants had. Most of them were short-term rentals. Most of them were older and more experienced, but there was a reason they were either unemployed or available by trade. That’s a reminder of where McCarthy was prior to the trade: the third QB option on a team that ranks last in the NFL in total yards, pass yards and first downs. It should also serve as a warning for any Giants fans counting on this saving their season. Giants to waive QB Jake Haener, intend to re-sign him to practice squad | Pro Football Talk With the Giants trading for J.J. McCarthy, the club will make another roster move to keep just two quarterbacks on their 53-man roster. Per Mike Garafolo of NFL Network, New York will waive Jake Haener but intend to re-sign him to the team’s practice squad. Haener was promoted to the active roster on Saturday after Jaxson Dart suffered a long-term knee injury last Monday night. Haener, 27, joined the Giants in August after spending some time with the Chiefs during the offseason program. QB Report Cards for 2026 NFL Week 3 | Bleacher Report Grade: D. Jameis Winston didn’t do enough for the New York Giants to beat the Tennessee Titans. That’s OK. He didn’t to. The Giants benefited from a ground-and-pound approach, a strong defensive effort and multiple Titans mistakes. Tennessee didn’t pieced together a drive longer than three plays until the team’s seventh offensive possession. Winston simply needed to avoid a significant mistake, which he did. Will the Giants trick themselves in the wake of Jaxson Dart’s injury? | The Athletic The concerns following the Giants entering the season — the availability of Dart, Cam Skattebo and Malik Nabers, plus the maturity of Dart/Skattebo — were mostly realized in less than two games. But the key questions that followed the Giants into this season will follow them into 2027 as well. They should not assume those questions will be answered to their liking. The evidence so far suggests some of the team’s biggest bets carry even greater risk. Harbaugh on losing Dart, Burns "We got our quarterback one week and probably our top defensive player the next week is shocking. But you've got to overcome the shock" John Harbaugh talks about the loss of Brian Burns for the season pic.twitter.com/xgLv0pjVnV — SNY Giants (@SNYGiants) September 28, 2026 Giants in survival mode after losing the irreplaceable Brian Burns for the season | SNY.tv If New York’s quarterback was the team’s most important offensive player, Burns held that role for the defense. He is a monster on the field, evident by his 16.5 sacks a season ago. He’s an elite edge rusher and solid against the run, but more than anything, the heart-and-soul and emotional leader of that side of the ball. So many players treat this as a job – justifiably so. Burns took everything that happened on the field to heart. When the Giants blew a late lead to the Broncos last season, it was Burns who sat in his locker stall after the game, in full game uniform, crying. Teammates gravitate toward that level of emotion, care. It’s why they elected him captain the last two years. Jason Pierre-Paul pitches Giants reunion after crushing Brian Burns injury | New York Post The 37-year-old — who played three games for the Buccaneers last season after being away being away from football for nearly two years — tagged the Giants in a post on X that said, “@Giants what’s up.” Pierre-Paul signed with the Bucs’ practice squad in December 2025, and was activated for three games late in the season. Rookie was a force on Sunday Arvell Reese was flying around the field against Tennessee. 12 TKL, 9 SOLO, 1 TFL, 1 PD vs Titans The rookie linebacker continues to flash as one of the most exciting young pieces on New York’s defense. https://t.co/UMG5nOAliR pic.twitter.com/5Zx9aA1QRV — Football Performances (@NFLPerformances) September 28, 2026 Giants’ Arvell Reese on Week 3 performance: I had a ‘chip on my shoulder’ | USAToday.com New York Giants rookie linebacker Arvell Reese responded to a disappointing performance last week with a game-high 13 tackles on Sunday against the Tennessee Titans. “After a loss, you always want to self-reflect and see what you could be doing better,” Reese said. “So I just self-reflected on that and came out this weekend with a chip on my shoulder. title: Fantasy Football 2026: Waiver wire, Week 4 edition
summary: Welcome to the Fantasy Football Waiver Wire for Week 4. Injuries continue to be a big story in 2026. Newsflash to those who are new to fantasy football: This is how it goes almost every season. The cold reality is that the show must go on and fielding a healthy and productive lineup only gets […]
full_text: Next man up: Allen | Getty Images Welcome to the Fantasy Football Waiver Wire for Week 4. Injuries continue to be a big story in 2026. Newsflash to those who are new to fantasy football: This is how it goes almost every season. The cold reality is that the show must go on and fielding a healthy and productive lineup only gets harder once the Bye weeks hit (which starts in Week 5). The Waiver Wire can be a lifeline when the injury bug bites your squad. The Process : Each week, I try to identify the top Waiver Wire targets and evaluate the short- and long-term prospects of those players. I also do my best to reveal which players who are coming off a big week are fool’s gold. Finally, I look at streamers who might help you in a pinch (this is usually more important during bye weeks). Note that I’m writing this column BEFORE the Week 3 Monday night game (PHI @ CHI). Some players discussed won’t be available in your league. I try to list players who are available in more than 50% of leagues. But what does that even mean? A 10-team league with six bench spots will have a much larger Free Agent pool than a 14-team league with eight. Most leagues fall somewhere in between. This isn’t “one size fits all.” By way of example, I won’t list Tyler Shough , Bryce Young , Jordan Addison, or Woody Marks this week, among others who probably aren’t available in any of your leagues. One quick strategy point: There are no byes this week, but four teams have a bye in Week 5. If you have the roster space, it’s always a good idea to look ahead and grab what you need a week early (this is most relevant for the “onesie” positions – QB, TE, PK and D/ST). One quick reminder: People overreact to early season failure and make mistakes. Keep an eye on who gets dropped this week. You might find a player who can make a difference for you later in the season if/when they revert to form. WEEK 4 BYES: NONE Week 4 Waiver Wire Quarterback: If you need a second quarterback in a Superflex format, or a streamer in a 1-QB format, three old veterans who might be able to help you are Geno Smith , Kirk Cousins (who I recommended last week), and Aaron Rodgers . Laugh all you want, and yeah, I know their combined age is well over 100. But all three of these guys are producing and are capable of big games in the right matchups. Fun fact: Cousins has three TD passes in all three of his starts. The schedule is about to get harder, but with Brock Bowers back in the fold he’s worth considering if you need help. Smith’s next two games are against the Bears and Browns, which is a continuation of favorable matchups. Pittsburgh’s schedule is mouth-watering for the next six games: Browns, Colts, Bucs, Saints, Browns again, Bengals (who Rodgers just carved up on Sunday). I’m not a big believer in Michael Penix, Jr. , but he looked good in his return to action and has an elite receiver and running back to help him along. He’s another to consider if you need a second QB or a streamer. Marcus Mariota is a highly capable backup who can be a useful fantasy plug-in, and unlike all the guys mentioned above, he adds points with his legs. But he might only get one or two more starts before Jayden Daniels returns. Running Back: Here is where you might want to spend some FAAB, if you need help at running back. Miami lost star running back De’Von Achane on Sunday to a torn ACL. His season is done. The NFL’s weakest and most inexperienced roster just got significantly worse with the loss of its most talented player. Ollie Gordon got the first shot at first-string reps, and while he wasn’t particularly effective, he did score a TD (a rarity for the Dolphins). But note that presumptive backup Jaylen Wright was inactive on Sunday due to some minor injuries. Neither Miami back is a home run. The team has a good chance to be historically bad and has yet to break 13 points in a game. Still, it’s hard to find RBs mid-season who get significant volume opportunities, and with Achane done for the year, both Wright and Gordon figure to see plenty of touches. But who will “start” and what will the split be? It’s worth noting that neither back was drafted by the current regime. Of the two, I’d prioritize Wright, who was the better and more explosive college talent and has one more year of NFL experience. The team traded up to get him in the third round a few years ago, and I’m sure they’d like to see what he can do as the lead back. I think more fantasy players will target Gordon, because he got the reps against the Chiefs on Sunday, so it might be easier to grab Wright. Braelon Allen is also in line to see a major boost in opportunity, if Breece Hall’s quad injury causes him to miss a few games as expected. The Jets have a good offensive line and their offense is playing decently. Allen is a priority add if he’s available, as he should command a pretty good share of the work in a split with third stringer Isaiah Davis for as long as Hall i s out. Alvin Kamara is probably not available in the vast majority of leagues, but he’s a must-add if available and especially with Travis Etienne, Jr. re-aggravating a hamstring injury on Sunday. It’s an excellent offense and Kamara was getting a good chunk of the touches even before Etienne got hurt. You can also consider Kendre Miller if you’re really stuck. Keaton Mitchell continues to see plenty of snaps, in an annoying three-man backfield. He’s decent bench depth. Wide Receiver There are always multiple names to consider at receiver, and the challenge is figuring out which big performances, and high usage rates, are sustainable after a spike week. I’ll repeat a bunch of names I’ve listed in recent weeks: Rashad Bateman , Denzel Boston , Malik Washington, Tre Tucker, Khalif Raymond , and Dontayvion Wicks . I’ll add a few more if you need to dig down or have bench space for deeper stashes: Keenan Allen , Makai Lemon , Chris Bell , Tre Harris , Konata Mumpfield , and Mack Hollins . If Mike Evans misses time, the 49ers will be down a total of four receivers from what they started with when training camp opened, including the Top-3 on their first July depth chart. The challenge is figuring out who might step up if that’s the case. I haven’t got a clue. Tight End: Kenyon Sadiq is the top name this week, and the rookie has done enough in his first three games to warrant a priority claim if you need help at tight end. It won’t be great every week, but outside of a few players it never is at this position. The injury to Breece Hall could open the door for more quick, easy-button throws and maybe even a few carries for Sadiq, who scored a rushing TD in Week 1. His usage and target share in Week 3, where he recorded his first career 100 yard game, is encouraging. Rookie tight ends usually don’t hit, but Sadiq has a pretty rare athletic profile and the Jets are giving him a chance to step up early. Three more players to consider if you need help: Darren Waller (who has a penchant for scoring TDs), Mike Gesicki , and Brenton Strange . I still like Terrance Ferguson the most among the Rams’ tight ends, but he injured his ankle on Sunday night, and Tyler Higbee stepped up and had a big game. Chasing the performance of L.A.’s tight ends might end up being one of the most frustrating and futile activities for fantasy managers this season as they deploy a lot of them, and once Puka Nacua is healthy it’ll be even more of a crapshoot. That’s all I’ve got. Good luck with your waiver claims! ***This column appears each Monday right here at Big Blue View. Each Thursday, my weekly fantasy preview with my rides, fades and sleepers (start/sit) appears here, and on Fridays you can find my weekly Giants Props of the week, also right here. ***
author: David Hartman

title: John Harbaugh won’t speculate on a Jameis Winston-J.J. McCarthy competition
summary: Now that J.J. McCarthy is a member of the New York Giants, the question of when, or if, McCarthy will take over for Jameis Winston as the team’s starting quarterback has moved front and center. Head coach John Harbaugh wasn’t willing to play the speculation game when he spoke to reporters via Zoom on Monday […]
full_text: J.J. McCarthy | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Now that J.J. McCarthy is a member of the New York Giants, the question of when, or if, McCarthy will take over for Jameis Winston as the team’s starting quarterback has moved front and center. Head coach John Harbaugh wasn’t willing to play the speculation game when he spoke to reporters via Zoom on Monday afternoon. “Our design is to win the next game. Our design is to be 1-0 next week,” Harbaugh said. “In any other conversation, you could ask me who’s going to be the starting quarterback next year or five years from now. I don’t know. What I do know is that we’re going to be playing the Cardinals in six days, and that’s how it works. “So all the other conversation isn’t going to help us beat the Cardinals. So it’s irrelevant. What we’re going to be doing is he’ll [McCarthy] be either the number two quarterback or the number three quarterback Sunday. Jameis will be the starter.” What about whenever McCarthy is up to speed on the Giants’ offense? “Jameis will be the starter for as long as I can see into the future, but I don’t know. Nobody knows,” Harbaugh said. “What I do know is that we’re going to be playing this game against the Cardinals on Sunday, and Jameis will be our starter for sure. And he’s going to play a winning football game. I know that. I have complete confidence that Jameis is going to play a great football game on Sunday and that our guys are going to play great around him.“ Harbaugh said the Giants were “turning over every stone” to find the best quarterback they could to add to the roster once Jaxson Dart suffered his season-ending injury. “I think he’s [McCarthy] a strong young quarterback, has some experience in the National Football League,” Harbaugh said. “Obviously was a very high draft pick, very talented player and is going to make us a stronger football team. So excited about it, think it makes us better.” The Giants, of course, spent a lot of time scouting McCarthy before passing on him in the 2024 NFL Draft. Harbaugh said it was the front office that raised the possibility of trying to acquire McCarthy from the Vikings. “They were the ones that brought him to the table, so to speak,” Harbaugh said. “Our high-level scouts, Joe [Schoen], and then the guys working in that group there all the way down had a lot of recommendations,” Harbaugh said. “We talked about a lot of quarterbacks, and J.J. was right near or at the top of the list in their evaluations. So they felt very strongly that he was going to be a good option, and that was interesting to me.” McCarthy was selected No. 10 overall by the Vikings in 2024. He missed his rookie season with a knee injury, started 10 games in 2025, and was serving as Minnesota’s No. 3 quarterback this year behind Kyler Murray and Carson Wentz. “He’s a talented guy. I mean, there’s just no doubt about it. He’s talente,” Harbaugh said. “He was a top 10 pick for a reason. There’s plenty of good tape even in the NFL out there. So I know he didn’t hold onto that job in Minnesota, and that’s why he’s available. If he had, we wouldn’t be talking, having this conversation right now. It would be somebody else. “He can throw it. He can run it. He can make plays. There’s a lot of things he could do better from what he did, obviously. And we’re going to see where it goes from here. I mean, that’s really what it boils down to. But just from a talent standpoint, I don’t think anybody would deny that J.J. McCarthy is a very talented young quarterback.”
author: Ed Valentine

title: Brian Burns injury: John Harbaugh confirms torn ACL, surgery
summary: New York Giants defensive end Brian Burns is on the road to recovery after tearing his ACL in the team’s Week 3 matchup against the Tennessee Titans. Burns played in just 25 defensive snaps against the Titans before going down with the injury. Now, his season is coming to an end after recording just four […]
full_text: Brian Burns | Getty Images New York Giants defensive end Brian Burns is on the road to recovery after tearing his ACL in the team’s Week 3 matchup against the Tennessee Titans. Burns played in just 25 defensive snaps against the Titans before going down with the injury. Now, his season is coming to an end after recording just four tackles in three games for the team. It’s a big loss for the Giants, who signed Burns to a five-year, $141 million contract ahead of the 2024 season. It’s a big loss for the Giants, as Burns played in all 17 games in each of his first two seasons with Big Blue. He also made the Pro Bowl last season and was on the All-Pro second team. This only adds to the mountain of injuries the Giants are already dealing with this season, headlined by quarterback Jaxson Dart, who also suffered a knee injury in Week 2 against the Los Angeles Rams and won’t return this season. If there’s any silver lining for the Giants, it’s that they have a deep pass rush rotation. Even though Burns is out, the team can rely on former top-5 pick Kayvon Thibodeau to fill that role. He’ll be joined by Abdul Carter, the No. 3 overall pick in the 2025 NFL draft, on the other end. The team also has Tremaine Edmunds and rookie top-5 pick Arvell Reese in the middle, giving the team a high ceiling for the linebacker corps.
author: Jeremy Brener

title: J.J. McCarthy trade: NY Giants acquire quarterback from Minnesota Vikings
summary: The New York Giants are acquiring quarterback J.J. McCarthy from the Minnesota Vikings, per a report from NFL insider Ian Rapoport. Per Jordan Schultz, the Giants are sending a 2027 fifth-round pick to the Vikings for McCarthy. The Vikings have confirmed the trade. The Giants, of course, lost starting quarterback Jaxson Dart for the season […]
full_text: J.J. McCarthy | Getty Images The New York Giants are acquiring quarterback J.J. McCarthy from the Minnesota Vikings , per a report from NFL insider Ian Rapoport. Per Jordan Schultz , the Giants are sending a 2027 fifth-round pick to the Vikings for McCarthy. The Vikings have confirmed the trade . The Giants, of course, lost starting quarterback Jaxson Dart for the season with a knee injury during their Week 2 loss to the Los Angeles Rams. Jameis Winston’s play since has been uninspiring, and the only other quarterback on the roster was journeyman Jake Haener. The Giants had an opportunity to draft the 23-year-old McCarthy out of Michigan with the sixth overall pick in the 2024 NFL Draft. They passed on McCarthy, as well as Bo Nix and Michael Penix, to select wide receiver Malik Nabers. The Vikings took McCarthy No. 10 overall. That, of course, worked out well for the Giants. Nabers had a sensational rookie season, and the Giants were able to move up in the 2025 NFL Draft to select Dart as their quarterback of the future. Things did not go well for McCarthy in Minnesota. McCarthy missed all of his rookie season with a torn meniscus in his right knee. He started 10 games for the Vikings last season, compiling a 6-4 record. He completed 140 of 243 passes (jusy 57.6%) for 1,623 yards with 11 touchdowns, 12 interceptions and a 72.6 passer rating. This offseason, the Vikings signed veteran Kyler Murray as a free agent. McCarthy not only lost a competition with Murray for the starting job, but ended up as the No. 3 quarterback in Minnesota behind Murray and Carson Wentz. Now, he will join the Giants. In his recently-launched Substack, ‘The Sweep’, NFL insider Tom Pelissero said this about why the Giants made the deal: The Giants extensively scouted McCarthy (and the rest of the 2024 quarterback class) before deciding to wait and taking Dart in 2025. McCarthy’s athletic ability and play style is a fit for the offense that OC Matt Nagy and company built for Dart, and he should be capable of running many of the QB movement concepts that figure to be dormant as long as Winston, a pocket passer, is in the lineup. At age 23, McCarthy is less than four months older than Dart. He’s 6-4 as an NFL starter. He’s cost-controlled for 2027. And in the event McCarthy takes over and flourishes down the stretch this season, the Giants have the right to exercise his fifth-year option for 2028. One thing that has been made clear by the J.J. McCarthy trade. #NYGiants coach John Harbaugh cares about the NOW. He'll worry about the future in the future. Whatever it takes to make the Giants the best they can be right now is what will be done. — Ed Valentine (@edvalentine.bsky.social) 2026-09-28T19:08:59.864Z The Giants are now spending a healthy amount of money on quarterbacks who will be backups to Dart after this season. The financials for the #Giants : Just under $1m for McCarthy this season. Next year, they’re on the hook for $3.775m fully guaranteed. They owe Jameis Winston just over $6m fully guaranteed in 2027 as part of his new deal. https://t.co/zV8V3ZmFap — Mike Garafolo (@MikeGarafolo) September 28, 2026 Valentine’s View While I figured the Giants were going to be aggressive in the quarterback market after McCarthy’s injury, this is not a move I expected them to make. The Giants spent a massive amount of time with McCarthy prior to the 2024 draft, concluding in the end that he was not the right quarterback for them. Maybe the Dart injury, and what they saw on the market made them view McCarthy differently. Maybe John Harbaugh had a different impression of McCarthy than Joe Schoen and the Giants’ scouts when the Ravens studied him in 2024. Maybe Harbaugh’s brother, Jim, gave his brother a glowing recommendation of McCarthy. Jay Glazer is reporting that John Harbaugh did speak to his brother about McCarthy before the Giants made the deal. Maybe the idea of adding another 23-year-old quarterback with NFL experience and upside was too good for the Giants to pass up. Both as a hedge against Winston’s ups and downs, and perhaps as a long-term option if Dart doesn’t become what the Giants believe he will. I have mixed feelings about the trade. If McCarthy couldn’t handle Minnesota or succeed with quarterback guru Kevin O’Connell as his coach, what makes the Giants believe he can succeed in New York? Does this open them to questions about whether they full believe in Dart’s future? I can’t blame them for taking a big swing and getting the best quarterback they could get. And, I certainly think this is a better swing than Justin Fields or Gardner Minshew. It just comes with a lot of questions. Vote in the poll and let us know what you think of the move, Giants fans.
author: Ed Valentine

title: J.J. McCarthy trade: Big Blue View staff reacts to NY Giants’ deal for QB
summary: The New York Giants made the surprising move to trade with the Minnesota Vikings for quarterback J.J. McCarthy on Monday morning. We fully expected the Giants to make a move for a quarterback in the aftermath of Jaxson Dart’s season-ending knee injury. However, trading a fifth-round pick for the 10th overall pick in the 2024 […]
full_text: J.J. McCarthy | Getty Images The New York Giants made the surprising move to trade with the Minnesota Vikings for quarterback J.J. McCarthy on Monday morning. We fully expected the Giants to make a move for a quarterback in the aftermath of Jaxson Dart’s season-ending knee injury. However, trading a fifth-round pick for the 10th overall pick in the 2024 NFL Draft came as a surprise. We decided that this was an excellent time to see what the Big Blue View staff thinks of the move. Nick Falato I understand why the Giants made this move. Yes, J.J. McCarthy was bad in Minnesota, and taking on his contract puts some pressure on the Giants’ cap. The fifth-round pick they gave up is valuable. Still, I understand why New York was willing to trade a fifth-rounder for a 23-year-old quarterback who was selected 10th overall just two drafts ago and spent his entire rookie season injured. Jameis Winston hasn’t looked particularly good through two games, and the Giants want a mobile quarterback who can operate in this Nagy/Roman-designed, heavy-personnel offense. It’s a similar offensive structure to the one McCarthy led at Michigan under Jim Harbaugh, where he won a National Championship. That Harbaugh connection is significant, particularly when it comes to McCarthy’s familiarity with the system and the way he was developed. It also helps alleviate some of the concerns surrounding his character. At the end of the day, the Giants bought an asset at a low point while adding another dimension to the quarterback room of a 2-1 team. McCarthy offers something different from Winston, and if he finds some success this season, the possibility of trading him for more value is always on the table. More than anything, the move gives the Giants options. New York has already added two Day 3 picks through the Josh Ezeudu and Daniel Faalele trades earlier this offseason, and the team could potentially recoup a fourth-rounder through the compensatory-pick formula with Austin Schlottmann in Tennessee. However, as things stand, the Giants currently do not have a fourth- or fifth-round pick. Jeremy Brener The Giants are doing something. That’s all people can ask for at this point. Jameis Winston has shown that he can only lead the team so far. Six field goals and zero touchdowns in two games isn’t going to cut it, so bringing in McCarthy is valuable to give the Giants a chance at something. McCarthy could absolutely flop, but that’s okay. The Giants are showing here that they believe this year’s team can still win and they want to give them a chance to be in the best position possible to compete. David Hartman The Giants are 2-1, but they’ve lost their most important players on offense and defense for the season. The team hoped that Jameis Winston was a capable enough backup in the event of a Jaxson Dart injury. But the offense has sputtered with Winston under center, and the team needed to add a player at the position. Today we learned that J.J. McCarthy is that player. The Giants have had 20 possessions since Dart went down and they haven’t found the end zone in any of them. Yes, the weather was a big factor against the Titans. But 18 points (all field goals) across two full games isn’t cutting it. McCarthy, the national championship-winning QB and 10th overall draft pick in 2024, has been a failure so far. He missed his entire rookie year with a knee injury suffered in the preseason and then was so bad in his second season that skeptics accused the Vikings of making up injuries so as to not play him. Now “Nine” gets a second chance, with the Giants. I would’ve loved to listen in on the conversation between the Harbaugh bothers that surely happened before the Giants pulled the trigger and sent a fifth rounder to Minnesota in this deal. I wasn’t a fan of McCarthy coming out of college and am doubtful that he’ll be able to elevate the offense much above where Winston has it, if he gets the chance to start. He’s certainly more mobile, which is a plus, but he hasn’t shown an ability to make good decisions or throw with NFL-caliber accuracy. Most of the standard and advanced stats for him were terrible last season, and that was with Kevin O’Connell, who by reputation is a quarterback whisperer, tutoring him, and very good receiving weapons around him. His 35.6 QBR across 10 games last season is alarming, and ranked 30th among qualifying QBs (and second to last among QBs who started at least eight games). I don’t know that there was anyone better out there, and McCarthy is still only 23. And sure, we’ve seen reclamation projects succeed (Sam Darnold, Baker Mayfield, Geno Smith, etc.). Still, this acquisition doesn’t move the needle much for me, and I won’t be shocked if McCarthy is simply a backup this season, barring an injury to or total collapse by Winston. Quarterback play is going to be a big issue for a Big Blue team that still has a chance to compete, and today’s move doesn’t change that. Tony Del Genio I admit to being puzzled by this move. John Harbaugh came to the Giants extolling the Ravens’ strategy of stockpiling draft picks. So in his first year he (and I do mean he – Joe Schoen is not in charge anymore) gives up multiple picks to move into the third round to get Malachi Fields (which I was fine with) and now gives up a fifth for McCarthy, which I’m not fine with for several reasons. It suggests Harbaugh really thinks this is a playoff-caliber team, which I do not. It flies in the face of quarterback whisperer Kevin O’Connell’s inability to mold McCarthy into a starting-caliber, winning QB. It creates an uncomfortable dynamic with Jaxson Dart and Jameis Winston. Maybe J.J. and Dart can commiserate on meniscus repair surgery and recovery. Barring that, though, I don’t see the long-term upside. Chris Pflum I fully expected the Giants to make a move for a backup quarterback, but I can’t say I saw this move coming. In part because Ed (among several others) was so adamant that it wouldn’t happen, and in part because I expected the Giants to prefer a more veteran option like Jimmy Garropolo or Justin Fields. But, I suppose that ignored two key clues that it was more likely than anticipated. The first is that the Giants simply love to make us wrong. There are times it almost seems like the Giants go out of their way to do the opposite of what we expect. The second are the years McCarthy spent with Jim Harbaugh in Michigan. He’s familiar with Har-ball, the culture that the Harbaughs want to instill, and the type of offense they like to run. It’s possible, even likely, that Jim stumped for the QB with whom he won a National Championship. While McCarthy stands as the biggest miss of my Quarterback Deep Dive series, he has still flashed the traits that made him a high first round pick. In particular, his athleticism and arm strength should allow the Giants to use the QB run game and get explosives off of play action should they need him to see the field. A fifth round pick is also more than I expected them to part with, but it’s also possible that they already intended to draft a developmental QB on Day 3 anyway. If so, McCarthy could have more upside than anyone they would have gotten. Regardless, this is pretty clearly a “Harbaugh” decision, and an upgrade over Jake Haener.
author: Chris Pflum

title: NY Giants rookie report: Arvell Reese, Sisi Mauigoa shine against the Titans
summary: The New York Giants managed to escape a sloppy, rainy Week 3 game against the Tennessee Titans with a win. It’s a win that veterans on the team say they wouldn’t have gotten a year ago, but the 2026 draft class wouldn’t know anything about that. Instead, the draftees only know a scrappy team that […]
full_text: New York Giants linebacker tackles Tennessee Titans running back Tony Pollard. | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The New York Giants managed to escape a sloppy, rainy Week 3 game against the Tennessee Titans with a win. It’s a win that veterans on the team say they wouldn’t have gotten a year ago, but the 2026 draft class wouldn’t know anything about that. Instead, the draftees only know a scrappy team that managed to overcome adversity (more than a bit of it self-inflicted) and pull out a win in adverse circumstances. We’ve been keeping track of the Giants’ rookie class this year, and four of them were key figures in the Giants coming away with a 2-1 record. Arvell Reese (LB) The Giants’ first pick said after the game that he came out with a chip on his shoulder after his performance against the Rams in Week 2. That much was apparent from the tape, as Reese was simply everywhere for the Giants against the Titans and led the Giants in tackles with 12. He played off-ball, came downhill as a blitzer, and lined up on the edge over the course of the game, and was a consistent factor. Hopefully this game was Reese’s coming out party, as he played with the kind of twitch and speed to which we became accustomed to seeing from him at Ohio State. He flew around the field and consistently arrived with bad intentions. On the Titans very first series he knocked an offensive lineman to the ground in run defense and then pancaked running back Tyjae Spears on a blitz. Reese still plays with a slight hesitation when dropping into zone coverage in the middle of the field, though that seems to be improving as well. He simply flies to the ball when playing downhill and his tackle for a loss on a pass to Tony Pollard was particularly impressive. Sisi Mauigoa (G) Mauigoa may have had a rough outing against the Rams’ defense and struggled against Aaron Donald in particular, but he rebounded nicely against the Titans. Sisi gave up zero pressures, hurries, or sacks against the Titans. The Giants may have struggled to throw the ball consistently, but it wasn’t because of their rookie right guard. Mauigoa is quietly having an excellent start to his career, and “quiet” is exactly what you want to see from an offensive lineman in pass protection. He wasn’t quiet, however, when it came to run blocking. Sisi’s power was on full display against the Titans as he consistently distorted the line of scrimmage. Mauigoa was effective on iso blocks, as well as when working with his linemates out double-teams or duo blocks. It’s still early, but Mauigoa has adjusted extremely well to life at guard. Well enough that they might want to start thinking about making it his home for as long as he’s a Giant. Colton Hood (CB) The Giants second-round pick got his second start as Deonte Banks continues to work his way back from the calf injury he suffered back in Week 1. Hood had an uneven game, with some highs, more than a few lows, and his own injury concerns. Hood left the field in the fourth quarter, apparently dealing with a calf issue. He was able to return to the field, but wasn’t quite playing with the same quickness he was earlier in the game. And he was both quick and sticky to start the game. Hood’s coverage wasn’t perfect in the first half, but he did a good job of staying in phase with receivers in man coverage as well as being assignment sound in zone coverage. In the second half, however, the Titans made a point of targeting Hood in coverage, particularly when he was playing off coverage. They seemed to identify a tendency to give a bit too much cushion in zone coverage and exploited that for easy completions. Hood struggled to redirect and close on the ball in off-coverage, perhaps due to a tightening calf, the poor field conditions, or a combination of both. Hood hasn’t played poorly per se, and he’s flashed the traits that had some considering him a potential first round pick. However, he’s still clearly a work in progress at cornerback. Malachi Fields (WR) Fields saw 47 plays on Sunday, 44 on offense and three on special teams. The passing offense wasn’t a big part of the gameplan for the Giants, who opted to keep the ball on the ground for the most part — whether that was due to the weather, a lack of faith in Jameis Winston, or both, remains to be seen. That said, Fields was targeted twice and caught both passes for 19 yards. He isn’t a natural separator, but he is developing a good sense of when and how to settle into voids in zone coverage. Fields’ best work continues to be away from the ball, serving as a blocker on both run and pass plays. His blocks aren’t consistently accurate just yet, but he’s giving good effort and looks for work if he doesn’t initially have anyone to block. Interestingly, the Giants generally kept Fields out wide, using him as either the X or Flanker, as opposed to using him close to the formation and using him as an insert blocker as they did against the Dallas Cowboys. That could be an adjustment to the Titans’ defense, the absence of Jaxson Dart, or simply an evolution of how Fields is used. How Fields is deployed and how the Giants arrange their formation will be something to keep an eye on as the season unfolds. Dominic Zvada (PK) and Ben Mann (LS) The Giants’ UDFA rookie specialists were once again excellent. They have been the brightest of bright spots this year, not just for their highs, but for their consistency. Conditions were miserable on Sunday against the Titans, but you wouldn’t have known it from the kicking operation. Zvada didn’t have to make any long field goals, but he successfully navigated the wind and rain, as well as did his job limiting the Titans’ return game. The Giants moved the ball well-enough against the Titans’ defense to get into scoring position, but their Red Zone offense was horrific. Fortunately, Zvada was there to make sure the Giants came away with points. Four field goals isn’t much in the way of offensive production, but it was just enough to ensure the Giants were able to escape with a win. Mann continues to be rock solid as a long-snapper. Not only are his snaps crisp, consistent, and accurate, but he shows fantastic hustle in getting off his blocks and downfield to defend returns.
author: Chris Pflum

title: Giants-Titans: 5 plays that led to the Giants’ Week 3 victory
summary: The New York Giants improved to 2-1 after their 12-7 victory in the rainy conditions at MetLife Stadium on Sunday. The Giants’ special teams helped secure the win, with Jordan Stout averaging 53 yards on five punts and rookie kicker Dominic Zvada booting all four of his attempts for the 12 points the Jameis Winston-led […]
full_text: The New York Giants improved to 2-1 after their 12-7 victory in the rainy conditions at MetLife Stadium on Sunday. The Giants’ special teams helped secure the win, with Jordan Stout averaging 53 yards on five punts and rookie kicker Dominic Zvada booting all four of his attempts for the 12 points the Jameis Winston-led offense scored. Winston didn’t prove he should be the Giants’ quarterback for the rest of the season, but he did enough to secure the win. The Giants possessed the football for nine more minutes than the Titans, and the Giants were penalized ten times for 88 yards. The Titans ended up outgaining the Giants 262 yards to 238. Both offenses were inefficient on third down; the Giants went 4 of 13 and the Titans 5 of 13 — all five in the second half. Arvell Reese led the Giants with 12 tackles, with Dru Phillips recording 11 and Tremaine Edmunds recording 10. However, the vaunted Giants’ pass rush lost Brian Burns midway through the game to a right knee injury, and the Giants did not sack Ward once in the game. The defense bent badly in the second half after a hot start. It’s something to monitor moving forward. The Giants were lucky enough to escape with a win against the Titans, and here are five plays that were crucial for one reason or another. Play 1: Jevon Holland! Holland has an interception in each game so far this season — none bigger than this game-sealing pick: JEVON HOLLAND CALLS GAME @TENvsNYG on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/ECvOY9ckOt — NFL (@NFL) September 27, 2026 Holland’s patience and vision were exceptional on this play against the second-year signal caller. Holland started to close width on Ward, who was scrambling to the boundary, but the safety read the quarterback’s eyes and sank underneath the route breaking behind him. Holland intercepted the pass and secured the Giants’ second win of the season. Holland is having a fantastic season for the Giants. Play(s) 2: FIVE three-and-outs to start Brian Daboll’s return did not go as planned in the rainy, windy conditions of East Rutherford, N.J. New York’s defense shut down Tennessee’s rushing attack, holding them to 13 first-half rushing yards, an average of 2.2 yards per carry. The first Tennessee drives resulted in three-and-outs, resulting in 32 total yards. Wan’Dale Robinson failed to secure two catchable passes, and the offense struggled to do anything against the Giants until the two-minute drill. The Titans did respond well in the second half. Brian Daboll started attacking the Giants on quick out routes, which allowed Cam Ward to get into a rhythm. The Titans finished the day with a twelve-play drive and two thirteen-play drives. Unfortunately, for Tennessee, it resulted in just one touchdown and the aformentioned Jevon Holland — game-sealing — interception. Play 3: 59-yard field goal try Tennessee drove the football to the Giants’ 41-yard line, and Robert Saleh opted to kick a 59-yard field goal, down 6-0. Joey Slye missed the kick, and the Giants took over with 41 seconds left in the first half. Jameis Winston threw two incompletions and then found Malik Nabers on a quick slant that converted the third-and-10. He then found Darnell Mooney for 7yards to help set up Dominic Zvada’s third field goal, a 39-yarder that gave the Giants a two-possession lead. Play(s) 4: Fourth-down stop The Giants with a big third quarter fourth down stop against the Titans, who remain scoreless. pic.twitter.com/yPcuwexLfx — Nick Falato (@nickfalato) September 27, 2026 The Titans had a 12-play, 62-yard drive that yielded zero points after Cam Ward sailed this ball incomplete. The Giants’ defense bent through the drive, surrendered a 20-yard completion to Carnell Tate and a 12-yard run by Tony Pollard. Still, the Giants defense clamped down with deceptive pressure looks in the red area that resulted in two incomplete passes. Ward missed an open Tate in the end zone on the third-and-goal play. Play 5: Cam Skattebo the receiver The Jameis of all Jameis plays. pic.twitter.com/ImklXwdBv8 — Nick Falato (@nickfalato) September 27, 2026 Points were hard to come by in this sloppy, weathered game, but the Giants broke the 0-0 tie after this third-and-seven conversion by Jameis Winston to running back Cam Skattebo. Matt Nagy called a familiar 3×1 look with the pivot/corner to the three-receiver side and the running back releasing toward the lone receiver side; Skattebo does a great job extending his route downfield, and Winston took a SHOT as he released to the open back. In patented fashion, Skattebo finishes the play with tenacity.
author: Nick Falato

title: Eagles-Bears takeaway: Lackluster play catches up with the Birds in Chicago
summary: You could feel this game coming. In Week 1, the Eagles struggled to beat the Commanders in Washington 24-22. They followed it up with a last-second, 24-20 victory on the road against the Titans, who finished with the NFL’s second-worst record a season ago. The defense had put together two lackluster performances against weaker opponents. […]
full_text: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - SEPTEMBER 28: Head Coach Nick Sirianni of the Philadelphia Eagles gestures during the fourth quarter of the NFL game against the Chicago Bears at Soldier Field on September 28, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Todd Rosenberg/Getty Images) | Getty Images You could feel this game coming. In Week 1, the Eagles struggled to beat the Commanders in Washington 24-22. They followed it up with a last-second, 24-20 victory on the road against the Titans, who finished with the NFL’s second-worst record a season ago. The defense had put together two lackluster performances against weaker opponents. The offense was bailed out by Jalen Hurts playing hero ball. And so last night’s 27-7 shellacking at the hands of Ben Johnson’s Bears in Chicago shouldn’t have been too surprising. Hopefully, it’s a wake-up call. Against an opponent superior to the two they played previously, Hurts couldn’t paper over the offensive line’s continuing and worrisome struggles, and the defensive line’s inability to pressure the quarterback continued despite the return of Jonathan Greenard. Meanwhile, the secondary suffered breakdowns throughout the game and allowed a third-string QB who they beat in the… checks notes… 2017 NFC Championship Game put up a 110.8 rating against them. Giants vs. Eagles will be played on the fifth anniversary of the Vikings vs. Eagles NFC Championship game. 38-7. pic.twitter.com/0kRenhPCOK — Brenden Deeg (@BrendenDeeg_) January 18, 2023 Yup, that was the same Case Keenum throwing for 247 yards, 2 TDs and no interceptions against a Vic Fangio unit that garnered a whole lotta hype in training camp. They’ve given up an average of 23.0 points per game through three outings, 16th in the NFL. They have three sacks thus far and have yet to force a turnover, sitting -5 in the turnover differential. Per Sumer Sports , the Birds are 23rd in EPA/play and 20th in success rate. The safeties and linebacking corps haven’t looked good through three games. Drew Mukuba, Marcus Epps and Michael Carter II have missed tackles and blown assignments. Nakobe Dean’s absence has been felt, with Jihaad Campbell so far failing to replicate his predecessor’s performance. But the real issue stems from the defensive line, who quite simply, hasn’t delivered on their preseason promise. A lot of money has been invested on the defensive line. Jalen Carter signed a 4-year, $152 million contract extension with $107 million in guaranteed money this off-season. Jordan Davis got a 3-year, $78 million deal with $64 million guaranteed. Jonathan Greenard received a 4-year, $98 million extension after his trade from Minnesota, and Jalyx Hunt will likely be the next lineman to follow with a similar mega-deal. Greenard just this week returned to the field following two weeks on the injured list, so it’s unfair to expect peak performance from him as of yet, but there is little excuse for everyone else. Moro Ojomo and Nolan Smith, two young players looking to secure big deals of their own, have been largely silent. One has to think Fangio’s guys will figure this out and get it together, but there is absolutely no excuse for getting shredded in a prime time NFL game by Case Keenum in the year 2026. A defense some believed would be one of the five best units in the sport has been middling through their first three games, and the onus is on the defensive line to make life difficult for opposing coordinators. On the offensive side, preseason concerns about the O-line were well-founded. Landon Dickerson’s inability to return to full health was less than ideal. Fortunately, last year’s 5th-round pick Drew Kendall has held his own thus far at center. The rest of the line has struggled. Tyler Steen has been abysmal at right guard to start the season. Cam Jugens, who shifted from center to left guard with Dickerson out, can’t find any consistency. And Jordan Mailata, one of the highest-priced vets on the team, has simply not been the same player since the 2024 Super Bowl season. Lane Johnson has been fine at right tackle, but he can’t do it all alone. On 1st-and-goal from just outside the one yard line in the 2nd quarter, the offensive line couldn’t generate enough push or open up a single lane to allow Barkley to run the ball into the end zone for the tying score. Instead, they forced Sean Mannion to try a pass play on 3rd-and-goal from the 2 with Andy Dalton, who threw an interception in the end zone. A 95-yard drive ended in no points as a result. Sure, Dalton is terrible, should not be on the roster and should not have been asked to throw a pass in that situation. But the O-line’s inability to get Barkley in the end zone on first and second downs shouldn’t be ignored, either. In the first half against the Bears, the line looked like it was figuring things out. Saquon Barkley broke off some big runs and the running game looked good. Barkley ran for 73 yards on 11 carries before halftime and then came out and rushed four times for nine yards in the second half. Jalen Hurts’ pass protection was OK, but some killer penalties and poor execution on 1st and 2nd downs put him behind the sticks most of the night, resulting in an ugly performance in which he threw for just 153 yards with two turnovers. He was shut out in the 2nd half. He was not helped by his coaching staff. Nick Sirianni’s decision not to go for it on 4th-and-1 near midfield in the 3rd quarter trailing 20-7 reeked of a lack of confidence in his unit. After the game, Sirianni, the team’s CEO head coach who says he specializes in his decision-making in just these kinds of game situations, admitted he made a mistake. He then went for it on 4th-and-5 later in the 4th quarter, after the game had largely been decided. None of it made sense. Play-caller Sean Mannion continues to call screen passes behind the line to Makai Lemon, and receivers weren’t schemed open this week. It had been a bumpy first two weeks for the Eagles, but they had persevered and managed to pull out two victories against lesser opponents/coaching staffs. Against Ben Johnson’s Bears, they did not receive similar fortune. Things won’t get any easier when Matthew Stafford comes to Philadelphia this week, looking to exact revenge in his own personal house of horrors. The Rams, 1-2 to start the season, will be out for blood. Then it’s on to Jacksonville to face a Jaguars team that has given up the fewest points in the league through the first three weeks. If they play like they did last night in Chicago, the Eagles will be staring at a 2-3 record two weeks from now.
author: John Stolnis

title: Eagles vs. Bears: The good, the bad, and the ugly
summary: Halloween is a little over a month away, but the Eagles certainly put on a good show in their version of Black Monday as Chicago Bears’ 38-year-old backup quarterback Case Keenum resurrected the ghosts of Eagles’ past like Joe Webb and Taylor Heinicke. The Eagles’ defense did a fabulous job of disguising Keenum as the […]
full_text: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - SEPTEMBER 28: Case Keenum #11 of the Chicago Bears celebrates after a touchdown against the Philadelphia Eagles during the first quarter of the game at Soldier Field on September 28, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Michael Reaves/Getty Images) | Getty Images Halloween is a little over a month away, but the Eagles certainly put on a good show in their version of Black Monday as Chicago Bears’ 38-year-old backup quarterback Case Keenum resurrected the ghosts of Eagles’ past like Joe Webb and Taylor Heinicke. The Eagles’ defense did a fabulous job of disguising Keenum as the next coming of Joe Montana, John Elway and Tom Brady all wrapped up into one, when he completed 24 of 34 for 247 yards and 2 touchdowns in a thorough beating of the Eagles, 27-7, at Soldier Field on Monday night before a national TV audience. It was Keenum’s first start since December 24, 2023. He scored his first rushing touchdown since December 22, 2019, against the New York Giants when many of the Eagles players were in high school. It was a pure horror show for the Eagles punctuated by a lackluster offensive line, a listless effort, incompetent coaching and a lack of discipline, spearheaded by a season-high 10 penalties, which is more than what the Eagles incurred combined over their first two games, and a team that better begin to self-evaluate before this season spins out of control. The Eagles had been getting away with many mistakes over their first two games against inferior teams because Jalen Hurts bailed them out. There was little Hurts could do Monday night, except for run for his life again, after completing 16 of 25 for 153 yards and rushing TD. Monday night could have been an Eagles’ showcase, a display of strength to the rest of the NFC that they are the team to beat after the defending Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks and Super Bowl favorite Los Angeles Rams fell this past weekend. Instead, they blew it. While the Delaware Valley was laughing over the amazing finish the Baltimore Ravens had over the Dallas Cowboys on Sunday, the rest of the country is having a big belly laugh over the Philadelphia Eagles losing to Case Keenum. Actually, it was Bears’ coach Ben Johnson who beat the Eagles. He was always one million steps ahead of Vic Fangio, who it seems opposing teams have figured out, and Nick Sirianni, who has a very talented paper team that has done little in backing that ability on the field. This game may be a portend. It proved the Eagles, at best, could be a 10-7 or 9-8 team that barely makes the playoffs. We’ll see. With the Rams, Jacksonville, Carolina and Dallas ahead, the Eagles’ five-year postseason streak may be coming to a screeching halt. However, no worries. It’s less than a month before LeBron James and the 76ers begin their season. Many of the Eagles will spend their winter courtside watching them. There was very little good, a pile of bad and an Everest of festering ugly in the Eagles’ 27-7 loss to the Chicago Bears. The Good Hurts’ first half, completing 10 of 13 for 111 yards, hitting six different receivers and scoring on the last play of the half. Last drive of the first half. Hurts, as he has done throughout this season, carried the Eagles to the scoreboard, completing 5 of 6 for 66 yards, and capping the 8-play, 67-yard drive with a one-yard TD sneak on the final play of the half. It saved what had to that point been an ugly first half. Hurts’ 30-yard rope to DeVonta Smith at the Bears’ 19 with 40 seconds left in the first half. Britain Covey’s 26-yard kickoff return after the Bears went up 10-0. Jalyx Hunt getting good penetration in shoving Kyle Monangai back two yards for Zack Baun and Jihaad Campbell to clean it up at the Eagles’ nine on first-and-goal. Corner Quinyon Mitchell deflecting a pass on Bears’ third drive on fourth-and-goal, and coming up pull down D’Andre Swift for a two-yard loss inside of two minutes on second-and-goal at the Eagles’ 11. Mitchell later deflected away another pass on the Bears’ first drive of the second half. The Eagles’ goal-line stop on the Bears’ third possession. It came mixed with a little luck when Rome Odunze flubbed an easy TD catch in the corner of the end zone, but helped along greatly by a Quinyon Mitchell deflection on fourth-and-goal at the Eagles’ three. Jalen Carter nailing D’Andre Swift for a two-yard loss on a second-and-goal on the Bears’ third drive. A good start, that quickly went bad. Rookie Makai Lemon hauling in the first play of the game for a 19-yard gain. The Eagles’ first drive kind of fizzled after that. The Bad Keenum completing 9 passes for 69 yards and a touchdown on his first 11 throws. Cooper DeJean continuing to have his problems. His missed tackle onLuther Burdenon the Bears’ third possession on a second-and-12 on the last play of the first quarter. Hurts nailed for intentional grounding on the fourth play of the Eagles’ first drive. E.J. Jenkins looked like he was in the vicinity of the ball. He wasn’t, drawing a flag. The Eagles went from a third-and-six to a third-and-16 at midfield. Linebacker Zack Baun making a rare mistake, missing rookie tight end Sam Roush , who had no catches prior to Monday night, on a fourth-and-one at the Eagles’ 32. Roush came sliding down, Baun found him 16 yards later, after allowing Roush to slide wide open. Baun actually had a tough game. Time after time, it seemed, Keenum found the middle of the field wide open, where Baun patrols. A sign of things to come. Safety Marcus Epps missing Luther Burden on the first play of the game for seven yards. Epps later blew a coverage when he was handed off by DeJean for a 22-yard reception to Rome Odunze late in the first half to the Eagles’ 33. The Ugly Sirianni and Fangio being systematically outcoached by the Bears’ Ben Johnson. The Bears picked up 24 first downs to the Eagles’ 14, 375 yards of total offense to the Eagles’ 248, and Keenum completed 24 of 34 for 247 yards alone. The Eagles have turned the ball over five times and have no turnovers through the first three games for the first time in franchise history. The Eagles third quarter offense. Of the 11 third-quarter drives the Eagles have had this season, they have gone three-and-out on eight of them. They have been outscored a combined 17-6 in the quarter, and have gained 95 yards and three first downs. Against Washington and Chicago, they went three-and-out on their first three drives and three-and-out on three of four drives. Against Tennessee, the Eagles went three-and-out on two of three drives. Against Chicago, the trend continued for 31 yards of offense and a first down. Andrew Mukuba’s holding call with 9:07 to play, giving the Bears an automatic first down at the Eagles’ nine. It was the fourth time the Eagles’ secondary was flagged and the fourth time the Bears picked up a first down off an Eagles’ penalty. The Eagles’ Moro Ojomo being coaxed offside on a fourth-and-two play with 12:48 left in the game at the Eagles’ 39. The play was typical of the night for the Eagles, who were on their way to 10 penalties. The flag gave the Bears a new set of downs, and allowed them to seal the victory on a Case Keenum 1-yard score. The Eagles exceeded the 9 penalties combined (for 75 yards) over their first two games, with 10 flags for 61 yards against Chicago. Mukuba, or corners Cooper DeJean or Riq Woolen, who had a horrendous game, should have picked up Kalif Raymond down the middle of the field on the 41-yard touchdown with 5:47 left in the third quarter. Woolen lined up against Raymond, then was handed off to cover motion man Luther Burden. But both DeJean and Woolen stayed with Burden, allowing Raymond to run uncovered down the middle. DeJean may have been responsible for Raymond cutting inside, while Woolen picked up the outside motion receiver Burden. Mukuba was positioned halfway to Wisconsin and nowhere to be found. The Eagles first quarter. The Bears had 7 first downs, had the ball for 11:35, converted 3…

title: Eagles-Bears final score: Philadelphia bullied by Chicago again
summary: The Philadelphia Eagles are 2-1 after losing to the Chicago Bears at Soldier Field on Sunday. Final score: 27 to 7. After getting bullied by the Bears in Philly last year, all eyes were on this Eagles defense to be better this time around. They were not. Vic Fangio’s group got owned by Ben Johnson. […]
full_text: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - SEPTEMBER 28: D'Andre Swift #4 of the Chicago Bears runs the ball during the first quarter of the NFL game against the Philadelphia Eagles at Soldier Field on September 28, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Todd Rosenberg/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Philadelphia Eagles are 2-1 after losing to the Chicago Bears at Soldier Field on Sunday. Final score: 27 to 7. After getting bullied by the Bears in Philly last year, all eyes were on this Eagles defense to be better this time around. They were not. Vic Fangio’s group got owned by Ben Johnson. They got torched by 38-year-old Case Keenum, a third-string quarterback who hadn’t played in an NFL game since 2023. Keenum’s final numbers: 24/34, 247 yards, two touchdowns, zero interceptions, and a 110.8 passer rating. And one of those incompletions was Rome Odunze dropping a touchdown. Of Vic Fangio's 42 games with the Eagles, Week 3 of 2026 had the 2nd worst success rate allowed and 5th worst EPA/play allowed, per @SumerSports — Shawn Syed (@SyedSchemes) September 29, 2026 This loss isn’t JUST on the defense. The offense had a chance to take a lead to start the second half … and instead went three-and-out three times in a row. They ran nine plays for just seven yards. One of those drives ended with Nick Sirianni inexplicably deciding to punt from 4th-and-1 at the minus 49-yard line. Sirianni did not have a very good night in terms of strategy. Not to mention that his team didn’t exactly look ready to play on Monday night. Pretty bad and concerning loss. Next up for the Eagles: a home game against the Los Angeles Rams. LA has failed to live up to massive preseason hype but they could very well beat this team. Read on for a recap and stay tuned for BGN’s postgame coverage. Also, check me out the PHLY Eagles postgame show. FIRST QUARTER The Eagles won the coin toss and elected to defer, per usual. The Eagles had Braden Mann as a 12th man on the field for kickoff once again, this time holding the ball on a tee after that was a point of discussion coming out of Week 2. The Bears started at their own 32-yard line. Marcus Epps immediately missed a tackle on the first play from scrimmage. The Bears quickly picked up a first down with a tight end screen. Two straight passes before the Bears’ first running play. Then another Case Keenum completion for a first down into plus territory. The Bears went with a toss to old friend D’Andre Swift to set up 2nd-and-1. Another Keenum completion for another first down … before expedited review revealed the ball hit the ground between Cole Kmet’s legs. Facing 3rd-and-1, the Bears’ run was stopped short of the marker. But then Keenum found a wide open Sam Roush on fourth down for an easy first down. Ben Johnson in his bag early. Facing 3rd-and-2, Keenum flipped shorst to Luther Burden, who was initially stopped before he was pushed by his teammates into the end zone. Not the kind of start you wanted to see from an Eagles defense that got bullied by the Bears last year. Got outmuscled to give up a score. EAGLES 0, BEARS 7. Case Keenum on the Bears opening drive 5/6 45 yards 1 TD His first passing TD since December 17, 2023! pic.twitter.com/nqGrehvWNE — PFF (@PFF) September 29, 2026 The Eagles took over at their own 25-yard line. Jalen Hurts’ first pass was a first down to completion to an open crossing Makai Lemon. Another Lemon target that wasn’t doomed from the start! Nice to see. The Eagles picked up another first down with a Saquon Barkley run to the left edge. Facing 3rd-and-6, Hurts got called for intentional grounding after facing quick pressure. Facing 3rd-and-16, a Hurts dumpoff to … Johnny Mundt … picked up just five yards. Punt from the plus 46-yard line … that went out of bounds at the 16-yard line. Only a net of 30 yards. Bad stuff from Mann but Nick Sirianni might’ve wanted to be more aggressive there in no man’s land. #Eagles have had issues leaving the backside edge unblocked on these boots. Clearly hard to execute this way… https://t.co/mSnlPyeCdq — Deniz Selman (@denizselman33) September 29, 2026 The Bears took over at their own 16-yard line. They quickly moved just shy of midfield before Riq Woolen was flagged for defensive holding. Facing 3rd-and-6 around midfield, the Bears thought they had a free play with Moro Ojomo jumping early … but the refs clearly thought Ojomo didn’t jump offside. Keenum’s downfield pass was incomplete to bring up a punt. The Bears’ punt was downed nicely at the 2-yard line. Jonathan Jones could’ve tried to pick up the ball for a free return since the Bears touched it … but he just watched Chicago down it. Cool. Or not! The Bears actually touched the ball while a player’s foot was on the goal line for a touchback. Lucky break there. The Eagles took over at their own 20-yard line. Unnecessary Tyler Steen holding penalty wiped out a big Saquon Barkley run to the left for a first down and more. Hurts checked down to Tank Bigsby, who fumbled for a Bears recovery. Awesome. Bears force the fumble and recover! @PHIvsCHI on ESPN Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/fUNklyY1xv — NFL (@NFL) September 29, 2026 The Bears took over at the plus 15-yard line. They reached third down to bring up the end of the first quarter. SECOND QUARTER Facing 3rd-and-6, Andrew Mukuba almost came up with a pick on a Keenum throw. But the Eagles’ third down stop was negated by another Woolen penalty that looked weak, just like his first. Next play, Keenum hit Colston Loveland for a score. Upon review, Loveland was just shy of the goal line. Jalen Carter came up with a big TFL to knock the Bears back. Facing 3rd-and-goal, Keenum’s pass to a wide open Rome Odunze was bobbled and incomplete as the receiver fell out of bounds with Nolan Smith in coverage. Phew. Johnson kept his offense on the field … and Keenum’s pass was knocked down by Quinyon Mitchell! Huge stop for a turnover on downs. If I’m getting greedy, a pick six could’ve been pretty nice there. Q said NOPE ❌ pic.twitter.com/BkqcSasoEr — Philadelphia Eagles (@Eagles) September 29, 2026 The Eagles took over at their own 3-yard line and a false start knocked them back a yard. Facing 3rd-and-1, the Eagles lined up in the gun and Hurts hit a crossing DeVonta Smith who was schemed open. Then DeVonta drew a pass interference flag on the Bears to move the offense a little shy of midfield. Barkley broke off a run just shy of the red zone. A Lane Johnson holding penalty was wiped out by a late Bears hit on Hurts out of bounds. Hurts was pulled from the game by a concussion spotter and Andy Dalton came in. Barkley broke off a run to the 1-yard line. Facing 3rd-and-goal after Barkley was stuffed twice, Dalton threw a ball right to a Bears defender. Cool, man. Why the fuck are you passing the ball there?! Do not trust Dalton!!! Bears LB D’Marco Jackson SMOKES Jalen Hurts as he is stepping out of bounds. Hurts is headed to the blue medical tent. 😳 Dirty? pic.twitter.com/LVUs3rSx02 — SPORTSRADIO 94WIP (@SportsRadioWIP) September 29, 2026 Andy Dalton comes into the game as Jalen Hurts gets checked and he is PICKED OFF in the end zone 😳 #NFL pic.twitter.com/7dHe09ppz9 — TSN (@TSN_Sports) September 29, 2026 The Bears took over at their own 20-yard line. Keenum got a big completion to Odunze despite facing quick pressure in his face from Jonathan Greenard. Keenum ripped off another 22-yard completion in a soft spot between Cooper DeJean and Marcus Epps. Facing 3rd-and-10, Keenum made a tight window throw for another first down. Back-to-back TFLs knocked the Bears back to 3rd-and-goal from the 11-yard line. Facing 3rd-and-goal, Keenum couldn’t connect with his target and the Bears had to settle for a field goal. EAGLES 0, BEARS 10. The Eagles took over at their own 33-yard line with 1:46 on the clock and two timeouts to work with. Hurts to Dontayvion Wicks picked up a first down. Hurts to DeVonta down the right sideline was complete with a great contested catch by the receiver. Then Hurts hit Zach Ertz…

full_text: Eric Hartline-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Philadelphia Eagles are on the road again in Week 3 for a Monday Night Football matchup against the Chicago Bears. All eyes will be on how well the Eagles defense can stop Chicago’s run game, not only because that’s the part they failed to stop in 2025, but also because the Bears are relying on QB3 Case Keenum as their starter. Not that Keenum can’t lead this offense, but he’s had only one week to prepare for the occasion, and his last regular season game was in December 2023 — it’s been awhile. Still, the veteran isn’t to be overlooked, and the Eagles defense needs to play more soundly than they’ve done through two games this season. Join Bleeding Green Nation on game day! Stay on top of every Eagles update and debate every snap with other diehard Birds fans. It will also be a big night for the Eagles offense, specifically for the guys up front. Cam Jurgens and Drew Kendall have one more week of reps under their belts in their new roles, and will hopefully continue to develop. New OC Sean Mannion has added some really exciting elements, but the run game still needs a boost to make it a more complete package. title: Jalen Hurts evaluated for a concussion, cleared to return against Bears
summary: The Eagles were finally close to scoring in the second quarter on Monday night against the Bears when quarterback Jalen Hurts took a late hit by D’Marco Jackson. Hurts went flying (further) out of bounds and despite bouncing up and heading back to the huddle, he was ushered off the field to undergo concussion testing […]
full_text: Photo by Michael Reaves/Getty Images | Getty Images The Eagles were finally close to scoring in the second quarter on Monday night against the Bears when quarterback Jalen Hurts took a late hit by D’Marco Jackson. Hurts went flying (further) out of bounds and despite bouncing up and heading back to the huddle, he was ushered off the field to undergo concussion testing in the medical tent before ultimately being cleared to return. #Eagles QB Jalen Hurts got leveled by D'Marco Jackson on a late hit and is now being evaluated for a concussion. Andy Dalton is in. pic.twitter.com/s55XNVqqIc — Ari Meirov (@MySportsUpdate) September 29, 2026 The QB was visibly frustrated as he tried to get back on the field as soon as possible. He showed more emotion than he typically does as he was held out even a few plays longer. Jalen Hurts appeared to be asking to go back in the game before Andy Dalton threw an INT. pic.twitter.com/oxIY76WxUQ — ESPN (@espn) September 29, 2026 🔥 Jalen Hurts comes out of the blue medical tent fired up and yelling pic.twitter.com/r3FoiPMe7G — Jeff Skversky (@JeffSkversky) September 29, 2026 Head coach Nick Sirianni appeared to consider utilizing a timeout to get Hurts back in the game, but instead let Andy Dalton finish the drive. title: Jonathan Greenard ACTIVE for Eagles vs. Bears
summary: The Philadelphia Eagles officially announced the inactives list for their Week 3 game against the Chicago Bears. The big news is that veteran edge rusher Jonathan Greenard is ACTIVE despite being ruled questionable to play. On Saturday, Greenard fully participated in practice for the first time since he suffered a pectoral injury ahead of training […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - MAY 27: Jonathan Greenard #52 of the Philadelphia Eagles looks on during OTA offseason workouts at Jefferson Health Training Complex on May 27, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Mitchell Leff/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Philadelphia Eagles officially announced the inactives list for their Week 3 game against the Chicago Bears. The big news is that veteran edge rusher Jonathan Greenard is ACTIVE despite being ruled questionable to play. On Saturday, Greenard fully participated in practice for the first time since he suffered a pectoral injury ahead of training camp. One would imagine Greenard won’t be playing his normal workload in this debut. But the Eagles’ big offseason acquisition might still provide Philly’s pass rush with a much-needed boost while operating in a limited role. Greenard is one of four active edge rushers with the others being Jalyx Hunt, Nolan Smith, and Arnold Ebiketie. The following Eagles players WILL NOT PLAY: Dallas Goedert, Hollywood Brown, Fred Johnson, Tanner McKee, Cole Payton, and A.J. Epenesa. Goedert, Brown, and Johnson were ruled out on the final injury report. Goedert is dealing with a knee injury that will likely cause him to miss multiple games. In his absence, the Eagles temporarily elevated franchise legend Zach Ertz from the practice squad. It’s unclear how much of a factor Ertz will be in his first game coming back from an ACL injury that ended his 2025 season early. The feeling here is that he could still be a helpful player for this offense. Brown was active for Week 1 but did not play any snaps. The Eagles made an effort to get him a little more involved in Week 2. His absence leaves the Eagles with the following active receivers: DeVonta Smith, Dontayvion Wicks, Makai Lemon, Darius Cooper, Britain Covey, and Elijah Moore. Moore is active for the first time this season after previously being a healthy scratch. Fred Johnson’s absence means that Markel Bell is the swing tackle behind starters Jordan Mailata and Lane Johnson. It also means that rookie Micah Morris is active for the first time in his career. Willie Lampkin, Bell, and Morris are the three backups behind the Eagles’ starting five offensive linemen. McKee is the Eagles’ emergency third quarterback once again with Andy Dalton serving as Jalen Hurts’ primary backup. Payton is the Eagles’ fourth-string quarterback. Unlike McKee, he is ineligible to play in this game. Epenesa is a healthy scratch after being active for the Eagles’ first two games. He was previously fourth in the edge rusher rotation and now he’s fifth with Greenard back. Chance Campbell is active and will make his Eagles regular season debut after being temporarily elevated from the practice squad. The Eagles are entering their second straight game with an open spot on the roster. Philadelphia Eagles inactive list TE Dallas Goedert – Injury. WR Hollywood Brown – Injury. OT Fred Johnson – Injury. QB Tanner McKee* – Emergency third quarterback. QB Cole Payton – Fourth quarterback. EDGE A.J. Epenesa – Fifth edge rusher. Chicago Bears inactive list The Bears ruled Caleb Williams out on Saturday. Chicago is expected to start third-string QB Case Keenum since he was actually able to practice all week, unlike usual No. 2 Tyson Bagent, who missed time while in the concussion protocol. Bagent was ruled questionable to play but he’s active. QB Caleb Williams OL Ozzy Trapilo OL Jordan McFadden DE Jamree Kromah DT Jayden Loving

title: Eagles roster news: Zach Ertz elevated for Bears game
summary: The Philadelphia Eagles officially announced two roster moves ahead of the team’s Week 3 Monday night game against the Chicago Bears. Here’s an overview: Note: teams are permitted to temporarily elevate up to two practice squad players per game. A player can be elevated up to three times in the regular season and an unlimited […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - OCTOBER 14: Zach Ertz #86 of the Philadelphia Eagles celebrates a touchdown during a NFL game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Lincoln Financial Field on October 14, 2021 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Philadelphia Eagles officially announced two roster moves ahead of the team’s Week 3 Monday night game against the Chicago Bears. Here’s an overview: TE Zach Ertz and LB Chance Campbell were temporarily elevated from the practice squad. Note: teams are permitted to temporarily elevate up to two practice squad players per game . A player can be elevated up to three times in the regular season and an unlimited number of times in the postseason. Let’s sort through this news on a player-by-player basis. ZACH ERTZ It was previously reported that Ertz was expected to be available for this game. The Eagles brought the 35-year-old veteran back to Philly to help instantly fill in for the injured Dallas Goedert, who will not be playing against the Bears. Just how many snaps will Ertz play? That much remains to be seen. It’s not easy to imagine he’ll be on the field for a normal TE1 workload since he’s playing in his first real game since getting hurt last year and he’s presumably still catching up on the Eagles’ playbook. But he could see some targets, especially since he’s played with Jalen Hurts in the past. The Eagles have Johnny Mundt and E.J. Jenkins behind Ertz. CHANCE CAMPBELL Campbell is likely being elevated for special teams purposes but making him active does also provide extra depth at off-ball linebacker. Monday will mark Campbell’s first regular season action in an Eagles uniform. And his first regular season snaps of any kind since he suited up for the Tennessee Titans in 2023. OPEN ROSTER SPOT For the second week in a row, the Eagles are entering a game with just 52 players on the active roster.
