title: Eagles-Bears Week 3 prediction
summary: One of the top questions entering this week’s Philadelphia Eagles game was: “Who’s going to start at quarterback for the Chicago Bears?” With Caleb Williams ruled out and Tyson Bagent reportedly set to be a backup tonight after missing practice time due to his concussion, it sounds like it’s going to be Case Keenum under […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PA - NOVEMBER 28: Jordan Davis #90 of the Philadelphia Eagles celebrates during an NFL football game against the Chicago Bears at Lincoln Financial Field on November 28, 2025 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images One of the top questions entering this week’s Philadelphia Eagles game was: “Who’s going to start at quarterback for the Chicago Bears?” With Caleb Williams ruled out and Tyson Bagent reportedly set to be a backup tonight after missing practice time due to his concussion, it sounds like it’s going to be Case Keenum under center. But how much does it matter in this matchup that the Bears are going to be down to their third quarterback? One would certainly think more than not at all. That said, it’s not like Williams played all that well against the Eagles last year. Chicago instead relied on their running game to bully the Eagles’ defense. If Ben Johnson is similarly able to stay one step ahead of Vic Fangio on Monday night, the Eagles could very well be leaving the Windy City with a loss. The onus, then, is on this defense to prove they’ve improved since that showing. It’s on them to live up to the preseason expectations that this could be one of the better — if not the best — defenses in the NFL. So far, we’ve yet to see that from this group. And specifically the defensive line. In their defense (no pun intended), there have been some extenuating circumstances. The Eagles were clearly focused on limiting Jayden Daniels’ rushing production in Week 1, which they did well. Then they had to deal with unusually hot conditions in Week 2. No more excuses in Week 3. It’s time for this pass rush, which could be boosted with the potential return of Jonathan Greenard (even if his playing time is limited), to come alive. And they’re only going to get consistent opportunities to get after the Bears’ quarterback if they can stop the run. That’s the key to this game. After watching the Eagles narrowly win in each of their first two games, I’m not going to sit here and expect this one to be a cakewalk. Johnson is a good coach and the Bears are probably going to be fired up for a primetime home game coming off a disappointing Week 2 loss. The Eagles tend to make things stressful. They also tend to win. So, give me an Eagles victory where they fail to cover the spread once again. title: Steelers Week 3 grades in win over Bengals
summary: The Pittsburgh Steelers did a complete 180 from their performance in Week 2 and saw their offense come to life against the Cincinnati Bengals in a 30-27 win. As they get ready for the Cleveland Browns on a short week, we give you our Week 3 grades as the Steelers improved to 2-1. QB Aaron […]
full_text: (Photo by Joe Sargent/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Pittsburgh Steelers did a complete 180 from their performance in Week 2 and saw their offense come to life against the Cincinnati Bengals in a 30-27 win. As they get ready for the Cleveland Browns on a short week, we give you our Week 3 grades as the Steelers improved to 2-1. QB Aaron Rodgers ​ Jarrett Bailey: Rodgers looked as good as he ever has in a Steelers uniform. He finished the week tied for eighth in EPA per play among quarterbacks, and nearly topped 300 yards with three touchdowns. Had a pass not bounced off Roman Wilson’s hands for an interception, his stat line would have been as close to perfect as it can get. Great bounce back from Rodgers and the offense. Grade: A Joey Bray: Was it the cleanest game from Aaron Rodgers? No, but it was easily one of the better performances we have ever seen from the veteran quarterback in a Steelers uniform. Again, Rodgers was let down by his receivers, who left a few completions on the field. Despite all of the miscommunications and trouble snapping the ball on time, Rodgers threw for nearly 300 yards and three touchdowns. This is the type of performance you should be hoping for every week from your 42-year-old quarterback. Grade: A ​Offensive Line ​ Jarrett Bailey: The Steelers had over 400 yards of offense on Sunday, and that was in no small part due to the upgraded play on the offensive line. Brock Hoffman and Max Iheanachor made their respective first starts of the season, and instantly provided more time for Rodgers to throw and opened more lanes for Jaylen Warren to run through. While we can’t expect them to be perfect each week, this was as close to perfection as it gets. Grade: A+ Joey Bray : It cannot be overstated just how much the offensive line play opened up the Steelers offense in Week 3. Rookie first-round pick Max Iheanachor got his first career start at right tackle, while veteran Brock Hoffman took over for Spencer Anderson at right guard. Both played well, and you could see the difference in the offense this week. Both the running and passing game both saw season highs in terms of production while the offense scored 30 points after scoring just 16 points through the first two weeks. While it’s still hard to imagine we see the offense put up 30 points every week, the changes to the offensive line seem to have made a massive impact on the offense. Grade: A+ ​RB Jaylen Warren ​ Jarrett Bailey: Warren had a career day, putting up a career-best 176 yards from scrimmage. Had his run of north of 80 yards not been taken away due to a ticky-tack penalty, we could be talking about Warren topping 200 yards on the ground. Keep feeding No. 30. Grade: A Joey Bray : This was one of the very best games that Jaylen Warren has played in the NFL. Warren averaged 7.5 yards per carry and had an 84-yard run negated due to a holding call. He also should have at least ten more yards and a touchdown to his total if he weren’t caught by the turf monster. The speedy back had to carry the load with the absence of Ric Dowdle, and proved that he deserves a larger slice of the pie even when Dowdle is back healthy. Grade: A+ WR Roman Wilson Jarrett Bailey: It’s constantly one step forward and another step back for Wilson. He was sprung open for a touchdown on the opening drive, and then had a pass bounce off his hands for an interception later on in the game. Germie Bernard needs more looks. Grade: C+ Joey Bray : Man, I really thought I was going to be able to talk nicely about Roman Wilson after his 38-yard touchdown on the opening drive of the game. However, Wilson is responsible for Rodgers’ interception as the ball bounced right off the hands of the young receiver. Wilson was left on the bench for a good majority of the second half as rookie second-rounder Germie Bernard saw the field more. The inconsistencies of Wilson continue to outshine any bright spot he creates. He continues to be a frustrating player to evaluate. Grade: C ​Pass Defense ​ Jarrett Bailey: I’m not going to crush the Steelers’ secondary. When you face an elite quarterback and two high-caliber receivers, you’re going to give up yards. Burrow was getting the ball out quickly, and both Chase and Higgins had good days picking apart the consistent zone looks from the Steelers. They need to be better as a unit, but it also felt like the plan was to be a bend don’t break defense against an elite passing attack. Grade: C- Joey Bray : I have a tough time being super hard on the secondary considering they are down two of their best players in Joey Porter Jr. and DeShon Elliott. That being said, this was their worst showing of the season. Joe Burrow started the game 14/14 and had a solid game overall. The Bengals, of course, have one of the best receiver duos in the league, which poses its own set of challenges for the Steelers each time they play Cincinnati. It was another zone coverage-heavy game for the defense who was picked apart by an elite quarter and a duo of elite receivers. Grade: D ​Special Teams ​Jarrett Bailey: Sunday felt like a vintage Steelers win, largely due to their luck and playmaking on special teams. A roughing the kicker call on Cam Johnston extended a drive that led to a DK Metcalf touchdown. A muffed punt was then recovered by Ben Skowronek and set up a Chris Boswell field goal, of which he went 3-for-3 on the day. A great day for the special teams. Grade: A Joey Bray : After missing a field goal in each of the first two games, Chris Boswell went 3-for-3 on field goals. Cam Johnston appeared to get hit during a punt but bounced back and turned in a solid performance. Kaden Wetjen has yet to make any impact plays as a return man, but it could only be a matter of time before he breaks one loose. Grade: A Let us know what you think in the comments . title: Week 4 Odds: Steelers open as slim favorites vs. Browns
summary: Coming off a satisfying Week 3 win over their rivals in Cincinnati, the Pittsburgh Steelers are headed on the road in Week 4 for the second straight divisional game on their slate. This week, the Black and Gold will be featured in primetime as they take on the Cleveland Browns on Thursday Night Football. Pittsburgh […]
full_text: CLEVELAND, OHIO - DECEMBER 28: Aaron Rodgers #8 of the Pittsburgh Steelers reacts during the second quarter of the game against the Cleveland Browns at Huntington Bank Field on December 28, 2025 in Cleveland, Ohio. (Photo by Jason Miller/Getty Images) | Getty Images Coming off a satisfying Week 3 win over their rivals in Cincinnati, the Pittsburgh Steelers are headed on the road in Week 4 for the second straight divisional game on their slate. This week, the Black and Gold will be featured in primetime as they take on the Cleveland Browns on Thursday Night Football. Pittsburgh is currently sitting on top of the AFC North due to how tiebreakers shake out this early in the season, but the entire division enters the week with 2-1 records. Yes, even the Browns — who are in a close race with the Falcons for the worst quarterback room in the NFL — have a winning record after a pair of upset wins in back-to-back weeks over the Buccaneers and Panthers. According to our friends at FanDuel Sportsbook , the Steelers are narrow favorites on the road, opening as 2.5-point favorites in this game. I’ll be curious to see how much, if at all, this line moves during the week. Home teams are typically given a slight edge — usually in the ballpark of 3-points — when sportsbooks view the matchup as a close one. The Steelers being favored 2.5-points on the road means FanDuel expects them to win, but not by much. Overall, FanDuel is showing it has little faith in either of these offenses with an over-under line, ie the combined point total of the two teams, set at just 38.5. That’s the lowest over-under total on their books for Week 4. This week’s matchup should prove an interesting barometer for the Steelers this season, as well as the new Mike McCarthy regime. While this is a game Steelers fans should rightfully expect to result in a Pittsburgh victory, Thursday Night Football in Cleveland has been the team’s kryptonite since games began being played on Thursdays. The team is 0-4 all-time in Cleveland on Thursday nights, with losses there in 2009, 2019, 2022, 2024. This week will give them an opportunity to prove whether that was more of a Mike Tomlin problem, or an Achilles’ Heel that will continue under McCarthy. Let us know what you think in the comments . title: 5 takeaways from the Steelers’ 30-27 win over the Cincinnati Bengals
summary: And just like that, the Steelers aren’t bad again. Following a listless performance on offense in Week 2, Pittsburgh won a shootout over the Cincinnati Bengals in Week 3 . As always, there are plenty of takeaways to be had. 1. Steelers show resiliency Following last week’s ugly defeat at the hands of the New […]
full_text: PITTSBURGH, PENNSYLVANIA - SEPTEMBER 27: Roman Wilson #14 celebrates his touchdown with Max Iheanachor #71 of the Pittsburgh Steelers during the first quarter against the Cincinnati Bengals at Acrisure Stadium on September 27, 2026 in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Joe Sargent/Getty Images) | Getty Images And just like that, the Steelers aren’t bad again. Following a listless performance on offense in Week 2, Pittsburgh won a shootout over the Cincinnati Bengals in Week 3 . As always, there are plenty of takeaways to be had. 1. Steelers show resiliency Following last week’s ugly defeat at the hands of the New England Patriots, I wrote that I wanted to see how the Steelers would respond to a loss under the team’s new coaching staff. It’s safe to say the team made the right adjustments under head coach Mike McCarthy. After a horribly incompetent Week 2 on offense, the Steelers dropped 30 points on a Bengals defense that has been surprisingly solid to open the season. That’s not to say it was a perfect showing, but it was a far cry from the unit’s multi-level failures last week. “Resiliency is critical to any type of success, whether it’s playing one division game or overcoming a loss last week.” McCarthy said postgame. “Momentum is a huge part of our game. It’s a hard-working football team. … Once you get through the first of everything as a team, there’s usually bumps that you go through, so, they’ve stayed the course.” While the Patriots loss was an abnormally bad game, it’s fair to say that there was always going to be some turbulence early in the McCarthy era as Pittsburgh adjusted to its first new head coach since 2007. The ride has indeed been bumpy through three games, but the team showed the poise to not let a disaster last week spiral out of control. It’s still difficult to get a read on the 2026 Steelers. But given the improvement this week from the last, that’s a good problem to have at the moment. 2. The offensive line shows up One of the through lines of last week’s loss was how thoroughly Pittsburgh’s offensive front was dominated by the Patriots’ defensive line. Not one player in Pittsburgh’s starting five had a good game. But despite playing against an improved Cincinnati front on Sunday led by all-world nose tackle Dexter Lawrence, the Steelers’ offensive line was largely fantastic in both the run and pass game. Pittsburgh averaged an impressive six yards per rush, while quarterback Aaron Rodgers was sacked only twice — once on a blitz pickup miscommunication, and another on an extended play. Of course, Pittsburgh’s sudden success in this area of the game clearly correlates with a significant change this week, swapping out right tackle Dylan Cook and right guard Spencer Anderson for first-round rookie Max Iheanachor and veteran backup Brock Hoffman, respectively. While I wasn’t able to keep an eye on him on every play, Iheanachor seemed to have a stellar debut. His easy athleticism shines in his mirroring in pass protection and explosion off the ball as a run blocker. His initial charting backed the eye test — according to New Gen Stats, he only allowed three pressures on 36 pass-blocking reps, including a 75% one-on-one rate. look at Iheanachor firing out of his stance https://t.co/ijcIHyJACW pic.twitter.com/9WHq75ZY7X — Nate Tice (@Nate_Tice) September 27, 2026 At guard, Hoffman’s first Steelers start might not have been as flashy, but he still put together a key performance limiting Lawrence’s impact alongside Zach Frazier and Mason McCormick. Despite having two new names on the line, it was the most coordinated the group has looked all season by a mile. And the strong pass protection numbers weren’t juiced by an exceptionally fast time to throw by Rodgers, either. In fact, according to ESPN’s Benjamin Solak, Rodgers’ 3.19-second average time to throw on Sunday was the longest of his Steelers career. The Pittsburgh offensive line finally clicking with Iheanachor in the lineup was great news, not just in the context of the Bengals’ game, but for the long-term prospects of a team that has spent heavy resources trying to rebuild the group in recent seasons. There’s still a lot of football to be played before sweeping pronouncements, of course, but the Steelers’ offensive line looked promising on Sunday. 3. Jaylen Warren is RB1 OK, maybe Jaylen Warren played a little bit too much on Sunday, given his legs were the only thing stopping him by the time the fourth quarter rolled around. Jaylen Warren on his stumble: "I wasn't tired. My body was tired." pic.twitter.com/YGzPYaYkzK — Mike DeFabo (@MikeDeFabo) September 27, 2026 But overall, Warren’s performance in Week 3 showed exactly why he should be getting a larger workload moving forward. Against the Bengals, he finished with 127 rushing yards and a 7.5-yard average, not including an 87-yard run that was taken back due to a questionable holding call. And in the passing game, Warren added another 49 receiving yards, and continued to shine as a pass protector. Boy did PIttsburgh need this. Steelers came into this game averaging the fewest points and yards thru 2 games in Aaron Rodgers career pic.twitter.com/HVJhJxg14g — trey wingo (@wingoz) September 27, 2026 As those long runs showed, Warren’s long speed isn’t enough to take every big break to the house, but his burst and contact balance remain excellent. He’s an every-down threat who continues to deserve more playing time than he’s usually given. Warren remains one of the NFL’s most underrated running backs. He’s also clearly been the Steelers’ best and most consistent skill position player through three weeks. Sunday finally showed what he can do in a bell-cow role. 4. The defense could’ve used Joey Porter Jr. Despite giving up 27 points on Sunday, I’m far from worried about the Steelers defense. The Joe Burrow/Ja’Marr Chase/Tee Higgins/Chase Brown attack was going to be better than anything Pittsburgh had faced up to that point in the season, and sure enough, that elite offensive core made some elite plays on Sunday. If there’s anything to be slightly perturbed by, it should be the Steelers’ pass rush not making much of an impact until later in the game, only sacking Burrow once. Still, Pittsburgh’s edge room is made up of proven players, and having receivers who get open with the ease of Chase and Higgins remains a great antidote to pressure. And those pass catchers might’ve been better minimized if the Steelers had their best cover corner available on Sunday. Pittsburgh clearly didn’t trust its defensive backs in man coverage against the Bengals’ star duo, but instead, Burrow picked them apart in zone. Asante Samuel Jr. put together a respectable effort matching up against Higgins, but clearly couldn’t match the latter’s size and contested catch ability. Samuel was eventually benched for rookie Daylen Everette, who has more traditional boundary corner size. Porter would’ve given the Steelers a bigger presence at corner to match up with Higgins, and his press-man speciality, along with Jamel Dean, would’ve allowed the team to switch up more coverage concepts. Ultimately, the Steelers will want Porter down the line if they want the defense to live up to its potential this season, and the star corner has said he’ll “ definitely ” play at some point — whatever that means. Of course, it’ll be interesting to see what Porter’s return timeline looks like as the Steelers enter a short week ahead of a matchup against the Cleveland Browns. 5. Odds and ends Sample sizes are a funny thing. In two of the Steelers’ three games so far this season, Rodgers has largely played well and done a better job pushing the ball downfield and extending plays than he did in most of 2025. It’ll be interesting what the trend looks like over the rest of the season. Ben Skowronek caught a touchdown pass and recovered a key fumble when the Bengals muffed a punt. One of the most underrated Steelers had an underrated performance on Sunday. For as impressive as…
author: Ryland Bickley

title: The Morning After: Jaylen Warren needs to be the Steelers’ bell cow
summary: When you give the ball to Jaylen Warren, good things tend to happen. The former undrafted product of Oklahoma State had one of the best games of his career on Sunday against the Bengals, compiling a career-high 176 yards from scrimmage (127 rushing, 49 receiving) and was the engine that drove the Steelers’ offense out […]
full_text: (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images When you give the ball to Jaylen Warren, good things tend to happen. The former undrafted product of Oklahoma State had one of the best games of his career on Sunday against the Bengals, compiling a career-high 176 yards from scrimmage (127 rushing, 49 receiving) and was the engine that drove the Steelers’ offense out of the abyss and into relevancy. In Weeks 1 and 2, the Steelers’ ranked 27th in EPA per rush. As we head into the final game of Week 3, they sit comfortably in seventh place out of the 30 that have played thus far. Their yards per rush also skyrocketed from 27th in the league in the first two weeks (3.39) to second (6.0). Warren did this as the sole running back. Rico Dowdle was out with a toe injury he sustained in Week 2, which left Warren to carry the ball 17 times, which is a new career high. And in his first game as a true bell cow back, Warren showed he is more than capable of being the straw that stirs the drink in the Steelers’ backfield. While the Steelers will certainly feature Dowdle when he is healthy – and they should – it should not be a 50-50 split. Warren showed it when he shared a backfield with Najee Harris and he’s showing it now – he is the Steelers most dynamic playmaker when he gets the ball in his hands. Feeding No. 30 should be a priority for Pittsburgh, especially this coming Thursday against a Browns team that ranks 26th in defensive EPA per rush. It’s the morning after game day, and the Steelers have life. Steelers offensive line dominates The offensive line play from Week 2 to Week 3 was night and day. After being the fourth-most pressured quarterback in the NFL across the first two weeks, per Sumer Sports , Aaron Rodgers was the ninth-lowest pressured quarterback of 30 qualified QBs thus far. Despite facing a Bengals defense that is fourth in the NFL in sacks, the Steelers’ offensive line kept Rodgers clean throughout most of the afternoon. Troy Fautanu allowed just two pressures after a shaky performance against the New England Patriots. Zach Frazier and Mason McCormick cleaned up after a sloppy performance, as well, but it was the new right side that was the ultimate game-changer for Pittsburgh. Right guard Brock Hoffman allowed zero pressures on 59 snaps. Rookie Max Iheanachor allowed just two pressures and was not credited with giving up a sack. The extra time allowed Rodgers to push the ball downfield. Two of his three touchdown passes were on deep balls (20+ yards downfield), and he averaged 8.34 yards per attempt when he had a clean pocket to throw from, which was good for ninth in the league. If the Steelers want to get into the playoffs and actually make a run, this is the type of play they will need – keep Rodgers clean, let him push the ball downfield, and balance it out with a dynamic ground game. They just showed they are capable of doing exactly that. Steelers miss Joey Porter Jr This was the first time this season where it was evident the Steelers were missing Joey Porter Jr. The Steelers showed zone on 48 snaps. Joe Burrow went 24-of-31 against zone coverage for 226 yards and. touchdown. Pittsburgh played man on just five snaps, which is where the services of Porter were really missed. Had he been active, the Steelers almost certainly would have felt more comfortable deploying more man coverages with No. 24 lined up on either Ja’Marr Chase or Tee Higgins. Instead, Burrow went a perfect 4-for-4 against man coverage with a touchdown. When you sit in zone all game against a great quarterback, he’ll happily nickel and dime you to death down the field, which is what Burrow and the Bengals largely did. Of their five scoring drives, four featured at least eight plays, and two totaled at least 11 plays in length. The Bengals weren’t incredible explosive, but they didn’t have to be. Burrow was getting rid of the ball in just over 2.5 seconds, which rendered the Steelers’ pass rush completely null and void until the game’s final drive. The Steelers got the win, but it could have been a bit more decisive had Porter been on the field. Quick hitters Robert Spears-Jennings has been a special teams stud. He registered his eighth special teams tackle on Sunday, per Ross McCorkle . That puts him on pace for 45 on the year – an insane number. I’m kind of over the Roman Wilson experience. It’s constantly one step forward, one step back. He sprung open on the pick play on the first drive for a touchdown, and then let a ball bounce off his hands for an interception later on. Germie Bernard then came in and made a difficult sliding grab for a 14-yard gain and a first down. More of 17, less of 14 going forward. This was the most Ben Skowronek game of all time. One catch for a touchdown and a fumble recovery on a muffed punt that led to a crucial field goal. The ultimate blue collar player. DK Metcalf’s struggles will get overshadowed due to him reaching the end zone and the Steelers winning, but three catches for 31 yards marks another slow day. He also had a pair of penalties, one of which negated an 87-yard run. Can’t go without talking about the incredible play by Derrick Harmon (although I’m unsure why they call him DJ). The Bengals were in Steelers territory, Harmon busts through the center of the offensive line and calls game. The future is bright for him and the Steelers’ defensive interior as a whole. Darnell Washington needs to get no less than five targets per game. 90 percent of the time, he catches a five yard pass and turns it into a big gain because no one can tackle him. Why getting him the ball isn’t a higher priority is beyond me. Let us know what you think in the comments . Be sure to bookmark Behind the Steel Curtain for all the latest news, breakdowns, and more! Mike McCarthy’s proactive approach was key component in Steelers Week 3 win Steelers stock report after upset win over Bengals Dallas Cowboys among teams calling Steelers about Joey Porter Jr trade Steelers vs. Bengals: Week 3 picks Steelers place Gennings Dunker on injured reserve

title: Snap Reactions: What playing time says about Seahawks depth chart at skill positions
summary: The defending Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks went on the road in Week 3, facing off against the Washington Commanders, losing for the first time since Week 12 of the 2025 season. While the final score was close, between an ineffective running game and three turnovers that led to 21 points for the commanders, it’s […]
full_text: LANDOVER, MARYLAND - SEPTEMBER 27: Jadarian Price #8 of the Seattle Seahawks runs the ball against the Washington Commanders during the first quarter at Northwest Stadium on September 27, 2026 in Landover, Maryland. (Photo by Scott Taetsch/Getty Images) | Getty Images The defending Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks went on the road in Week 3, facing off against the Washington Commanders, losing for the first time since Week 12 of the 2025 season. While the final score was close , between an ineffective running game and three turnovers that led to 21 points for the commanders, it’s a game the Seahawks will look back on and feel they should have won. On the offensive side of things, Seattle had a solid day outside of turnovers. The run game certainly was not where the team or fans would like it to be, but Sam Darnold showed once again that he is capable of leading an offense even when the run game isn’t working. The offensive snap counts are very interesting for several reasons. Likely the most talked about snap counts on the offensive side of the ball is at right guard, where there was a clean 60/40 split for snaps between Christian Haynes and Beau Stephens. Perhaps more interesting, though, is what the snap counts say about other position groups. Tight end is unquestionably A.J. Barner and then a huge gap before either of Eric Saubert or Elijah Arroyo, both of whom finished with 18 offensive snaps. At receiver All-Universe Jaxon Smith-Njigba is the unquestioned leader of the group, with Cooper Kupp and Rashid Shaheed seeing similar snap counts to the 2025 season. Tory Horton wouldn’t be expected to see a huge amount of work as he continues working his way back into things, but it bears watching whether he earns more snaps in the coming weeks. Another position that bears watching is running back, where former undrafted free agent George Holani and former undrafted free agent Emmanuel Wilson both outsnapped 2026 first round pick Jadarian Price. Similar to Horton, Price wouldn’t necessarily be expected to have a huge workload after leaving the Week 2 win over the Arizona Cardinals due to injury, so at least at this point being outsnapped by more veteran players is likely less of a concern than ball security. On the defensive side of the ball, there weren’t a whole lot of surprises. Nick Emmanwori played 36 defensive snaps in his second game back on the field following surgery in the offseason, while Nehemiah Pritchett played just over half of the defensive snaps in the game. That is noteworthy for Pritchett in that it marks the third time in three games that he has played more than fifty percent of defensive snaps, something he had only done twice in his career prior to this season. And when it comes to special teams, just as it has been in recent seasons, it’s Brady Russell’s world and everyone else just lives in it. Russell led the Seahawks with 28 special teams snaps, while Mike Morris was second at 24 in his first regular season action of the year. Tyrice Knight, Patrick O’Connell and Chazz Surratt all logged 23 special teams snaps to round out the top five for the team. And now it’s on to a second consecutive matchup against a winless opponent, as the Los Angeles Chargers bring their 0-3 record to Lumen Sunday afternoon in search of their first win of the season.
author: John Gilbert

title: 3 questions to think about following Seahawks loss to the Commanders
summary: We’ve had well over 24 hours to digest the Seattle Seahawks daring to lose a regular season football game for the first time in 10 months. They were not at their best against the Washington Commanders and paid a heavy price, losing 33-31 despite comfortably out-gaining Washington on the afternoon. Turnovers will kill you no […]
full_text: LANDOVER, MARYLAND - SEPTEMBER 27: Jeremy Reaves #39 of the Washington Commanders attempts catch against Rashid Shaheed #22 of the Seattle Seahawks during the fourth quarter at Northwest Stadium on September 27, 2026 in Landover, Maryland. (Photo by Patrick Smith/Getty Images) | Getty Images We’ve had well over 24 hours to digest the Seattle Seahawks daring to lose a regular season football game for the first time in 10 months. They were not at their best against the Washington Commanders and paid a heavy price, losing 33-31 despite comfortably out-gaining Washington on the afternoon. Turnovers will kill you no matter how great you area. Myself and Bryce Coutts dissected the game on The Hawks Eye podcast on Monday, and there were a few questions Bryce posed that I think we should pose or at least repurpose to Field Gulls readers. Did the Seahawks make a mistake by not keeping Cody White? Dareke Young left as a free agent to the Las Vegas Raiders, while Jake Bobo had an unfortunate ACL tear in training camp. Cody White stayed on the Seahawks roster throughout preseason and lost out on a roster spot to Montorie Foster Jr, training camp and ‘Hard Knocks’ star. As Mike Macdonald laments the lackluster special teams , Bryce and I wondered aloud ( at 12:13 of the video ) if the Seahawks should’ve kept one of their established special teams standouts. Foster has not played in the last two games, which means the Seahawks don’t have any reserve wide receivers on kick or punt coverage duties. Bryce : “On specials, Cody White was a factor. You lost Dareke Young as a gunner, Irv Charles hasn’t been able to go, Montorie Foster hasn’t given you anything on specials, and your specials have been atrocious. I feel if Cody White was able to be on here, at least you would’ve gotten something out of him on specials because he was one of the better gunners and kick cover guys.” Young, Bobo, and White all being gone is a lot of ST snaps to replace just at the WR position. If Foster isn’t providing anything right now, should Seattle have made more of a push to keep White and try and stash Foster on the practice squad? I think Emmanuel Henderson and Ricky White III should be considered special teams options as the season progresses, along with Irv Charles. Should the Seahawks keep rotating at right guard? Christian Haynes and Beau Stephens split snaps for the second week in a row. I outlined on the show (at 22:02 and 44:26 ) that I am not interested in a midseason competition for backup right guard. Either Haynes should get all the snaps or Stephens gets all the snaps. The fact that Haynes is once again in split duties like he was as a rookie is either a sign that they don’t trust his conditioning or there is something that is lacking in Haynes’ game that makes the coaching staff not want to play him a full game. Bryce : “How much do the Seahawks in the run game miss Anthony Bradford right now? Because he can move people. This is where that rotation with Christian Haynes and Beau Stephens has to get solved. They got to find someone that can move somebody in the run game. They’re not getting as much push as they should off that right side.” Mookie : “I think they had eight carries for -1 running on the right side. That tells you all you need to know, where [Abe] Lucas hasn’t been at his best, and even if Haynes and Stephens are playing to a draw, you want them to actually put people a couple of yards beyond the line of scrimmage, and that’s just not happening. I want them to drop the rotation. Either Haynes is ready for a full game or you start Beau Stephens. My hang-up with this is they did the same rotation thing with Haynes and Bradford when Haynes was a rookie. The fact that we’re still doing this: either Haynes has some sort of conditioning problem that they don’t want to talk about, or they really don’t want to commit to Haynes for a full game for what ever other reason.” Until Anthony Bradford is back, I don’t think there’s any benefit to rotating your offensive line at any position. Is Rashid Shaheed actually a good fit in the Seahawks offense? We’re three weeks into the season and Rashid Shaheed has six catches for 53 yards on 12 targets. Not exactly dazzling numbers for a player who signed a $51 million contract in free agency. Tory Horton barely played on Sunday and had three catches on as many targets for 48 yards. The season is still young and Shaheed’s chemistry has been primarily with Sam Darnold, whom he’s only played with for barely over the equivalent of a full game this month, but does it look like Shaheed actually makes sense for Seattle’s receiver group? It’s been a disappointing start to the season for Shaheed, who was on an 80+ catch pace with the New Orleans Saints before he was traded to Seattle . Perhaps there is a benefit to being a bigger fish in a small pond (albeit one where the biggest fish is Chris Olave), and Shaheed on a more stacked team could get lost in the shuffle. We get into this at 25:35 . Mookie : “So far it’s just JSN, it’s Kupp, and the fact that Horton had more catches than Shaheed in far fewer snaps is not great for Rashid. I’m wondering about his fit as a blocker, his ability to separate in certain route combinations—just because you’re fast doesn’t mean you can separate consistently at an NFL level. There’s a lot to think about here, it’s the only sour point for me in what was the most varied passing game to date under Brian Fleury.” Watch the full episode below! We also review Sam Darnold’s performance, how the defense performed, and whether it was a good decision by the coaching staff to sit Jadarian Price for fumbling again. Video

title: Seahawks safety Julian Love labeled ‘day to day’ by Mike Macdonald, could return vs. Chargers
summary: After missing Sunday’s game against the Washington Commanders with a calf injury he sustained in practice last week, Seattle Seahawks safety Julian Love appears to be trending towards a potential return in Week 4 against the Los Angeles Chargers. According to head coach Mike Macdonald, Love underwent extensive work on Monday morning which yielded positive […]
full_text: After missing Sunday’s game against the Washington Commanders with a calf injury he sustained in practice last week, Seattle Seahawks safety Julian Love appears to be trending towards a potential return in Week 4 against the Los Angeles Chargers. According to head coach Mike Macdonald, Love underwent extensive work on Monday morning which yielded positive results. However, his status for practice this week remains unclear. “As far as Julian goes, it’s a day-to-day thing right now,” Macdonald said at Monday’s press conference. “We’ll see how that shakes out. He did some extensive work this morning and it went well. We’ll see how that translates to Wednesday and move forward.” Should he remain sidelined against Los Angeles, Rodney Thomas II and AJ Finley will presumably continue to fill in. Both opened the season on Seattle’s practice squad but were signed to the active roster following a flurry of injuries to begin the season. Although he was active for the first two games, Finley didn’t see the field but was asked to step up against Washington with Love out. However, he struggled in coverage, was the closest defender on Treylon Burks’ first half touchdown and was flagged for a costly penalty in the fourth quarter that led to a go-ahead field goal. With fellow safety Ty Okada (hamstring) sidelined and without an update on a possible return date, Love’s return would certainly provide a significant boost to Seattle’s shorthanded secondary, who looked like a shell of themselves in Week 3. More information regarding Love’s status should become available on Wednesday evening when the Seahawks release their first injury report of the week.

title: Seahawks special teams are struggling to cover kickoffs
summary: When the Seattle Seahawks slogged their way through a pretty uninspired preseason, the special teams concern was the performance of Jason Myers, who missed five kicks over three games. Myers has been perfect on his field goals and extra points, which is a big relief. But through three weeks of the regular season, the Seahawks […]
full_text: SEATTLE, WASHINGTON - DECEMBER 15: Special teams coordinator Jay Harbaugh of the Seattle Seahawks reacts during the fourth quarter of the game against the Green Bay Packers at Lumen Field on December 15, 2024 in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Jane Gershovich/Getty Images) | Getty Images When the Seattle Seahawks slogged their way through a pretty uninspired preseason, the special teams concern was the performance of Jason Myers, who missed five kicks over three games. Myers has been perfect on his field goals and extra points, which is a big relief. But through three weeks of the regular season, the Seahawks have a different special teams issue that definitely was not a problem in 2025. The Seahawks are one of the worst teams at defending kick returns Last season, Jay Harbaugh’s unit allowed only 24 yards per kick return, tied for fourth-fewest in the NFL and almost two full yards below the league average. Seattle allowed 81 returns (second-most in the league) while Jason Myers had a career-low 17.5% touchback rate, so the Seahawks having a high-scoring offense was only part of the equation. This was a team that was willing to put the ball in play and limit the opposition to much worse field position than a touchback at the 35. According to Stathead , the average starting field position for Seahawks opponents off of kickoffs was their own 28, the worst in the NFL (well, best, if you look at it from Seattle’s perspective). That is not happening in 2026. With Week 3 almost wrapped up, the Seahawks rank 30th in yards per return allowed at 30.1 . They have already allowed five of 11 kickoffs to be run back for at least 30 yards. In 2025, the Seahawks only allowed eight such returns. The average starting field position for Seahawks opponents off of kickoffs is their own 32, which is worse than league average and includes touchbacks and illegal kicks that bring the ball to the 40. I’m no film expert, but the Seahawks look to be having trouble with outside contain and getting off their blocks in the first place. In none of these returns is the returner contacted until they’re just about at the 30. The Seahawks have allowed 5 kick returns of 30+ yards this season on just 11 runbacks. They allowed 8 all of last season. 30.1 yards per return is 3rd-worst in the NFL. They were 4th-best last year. pic.twitter.com/anhin8I0qZ — Mookie Alexander (@mookiealexander) September 28, 2026 I stress that this is only a kickoff return problem, because the Seahawks are the only team in the NFL yet to even allow a punt return. If the Seahawks coverage unit cannot consistently make returns significantly better than a 35-yard line touchback, then Jason Myers might as well just kick more touchbacks when possible. Seattle has been really, close to letting a big return break and the dam might burst sooner rather than later. Losing Dareke Young, Cody White, and Jake Bobo could be looming large The Seahawks didn’t lose too many players from last season’s roster, but 15 of those kick return tackles last year came from current Las Vegas Raiders, Dareke Young and Cody White. Young was second behind Brady Russell in kick return tackles, while White had six before suffering a season-ending injury. Jake Bobo is still on the team but on injured reserve for the year. That’s a combined 407 special teams snaps lost to injury or departures. Seattle usually had at least one of those three receivers on kick coverage duties, and during the playoffs (when White was on IR) the Seahawks had Bobo and Young together. It’s not nothing that Montorie Foster Jr, star of Hard Knocks and one of the preseason standouts over the summer, has been a healthy scratch for two games. Foster played seven special teams snaps (three punts, four kickoffs) and that’s the extent of his action up to this point. Seattle has played two straight games without a receiver covering kicks. Enter Irv Charles? After Week 4, Irv Charles is available to come off injured reserve. There is zero chance he’s going to do anything on offense, not when he’s pushing 30 and has zero career targets. But he was acquired in the offseason because , when healthy, he’s supposed to be a very valuable special teams contributor. In his last healthy season (2024), Charles was part of kick coverage duties on the New York Jets, but kick coverage stats prior to 2025 are a different beast when touchback rates were north of 65 percent under the old rules. The ball is now in play on kickoffs an overwhelming majority of the time, so Charles can justify double-digit snaps weekly upon return. Despite everything I’ve said about the kick returns, the Seahawks have curiously allowed just one touchdown drive after a kickoff, and that was back on opening night versus the New England Patriots. But the knock-on effect of allowing the opposition to start with reasonably good to great field position is, should a punt be forced, you’re most likely backed up. The margin for error for giving up at least a field goal attempt is, at most, 25-ish yards if the other team is anywhere from its own 30 or better. That’s asking too much of any defense, not accounting for when they’re defending their own territory off of turnovers like we saw in the Washington Commanders game. Commanders starting field position: WSH 20 (punt) SEA 21 (TD) WSH 28 (punt) WSH 44 (punt) WSH 40 (TD) WSH 2 (punt) WSH 35 (FG, two-min drill) WSH 34 (punt) SEA 43 (TD) WSH 26 (punt) WSH 44 (punt) WSH 40 (FG) WSH 33 (EOG) Only 4 of their 13 drives were inside their own 30. Bad. — Mookie Alexander (@mookiealexander) September 27, 2026 This is comparatively not a high priority fix for Seattle compared to the run game inconsistencies, pre-snap penalties, and low red zone struggles, but it’s one of those “little things” that is currently not in the Seahawks’ favor.

title: Move over, Colt McCoy: Marcus Mariota is Seattle’s real football tormentor
summary: The Seattle Seahawks lost to the Marcus Mariota-led Washington Commanders on Sunday. While it’s one of the biggest upset losses the Seahawks have suffered in years, maybe we should’ve seen it coming. Mariota didn’t have to do a whole lot, but he made timely, accurate throws (including a couple of passes that were nearly caught […]
full_text: The Seattle Seahawks lost to the Marcus Mariota-led Washington Commanders on Sunday . While it’s one of the biggest upset losses the Seahawks have suffered in years, maybe we should’ve seen it coming. Mariota didn’t have to do a whole lot, but he made timely, accurate throws (including a couple of passes that were nearly caught or caught but marginally out of bounds), and cemented the game with a read-option keeper on a 3rd and long. Three touchdowns, no turnovers, and only one pass that was ever in serious jeopardy of being intercepted. And now, for your double depressing stat of the day, Mariota owns Seattle football teams. He’s had three cracks apiece against the Seahawks and Huskies and come out a winner every single time. Marcus Mariota has never lost to a team from Seattle 3-0 against the Seahawks and 3-0 against the Huskies — Curtis Rogers (@AKidFromKent) September 27, 2026 Marcus Mariota vs. Seattle 2012 (Oregon) : W 52-21 vs. Washington 2013 (Oregon) : W 45-24 at Washington 2014 (Oregon) : W 45-20 vs. Washington 2017 (Tennessee Titans) : W 33-27 vs. Seahawks 2022 (Atlanta Falcons) : W 27-23 at Seahawks 2026 (Washington Commanders) : W 33-31 vs. Seahawks It wasn’t like Mariota was a passenger in any of those games. He had 10 total touchdowns and just one interception against the Huskies, while his three separate starts versus the Seahawks saw him get seven touchdowns (six passing, one rushing) and only two turnovers (both with the Falcons). This is definitely not like when known Seahawks nemesis, Colt McCoy, had modest stats in two of his three winning starts but the games were low-scoring and McCoy could win a game 6-3 or 17-12. McCoy never even played the Huskies when he was at Texas. Mariota has owned Seattle’s two big football teams for almost 15 years. You know what? Tip of the cap. Hopefully the Seahawks never have to play him again.

title: Seahawks vs. Chargers odds: Opening lines for Week 4 matchup
summary: Despite a shocking 33-31 upset loss to the shorthanded Washington Commanders on Sunday, the Seattle Seahawks still open up as heavy favourites against the winless Los Angeles Chargers in Week 4. Seattle opened the season 2-0 and even after dropping an extremely winnable game, Sam Darnold and the offense strung together 437 total yards, leaving […]
full_text: INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA - AUGUST 10: George Holani #36 of the Seattle Seahawks scores a touchdown against the Los Angeles Chargers in the first half during a preseason game at SoFi Stadium on August 10, 2024 in Inglewood, California. (Photo by Ronald Martinez/Getty Images) | Getty Images Despite a shocking 33-31 upset loss to the shorthanded Washington Commanders on Sunday , the Seattle Seahawks still open up as heavy favourites against the winless Los Angeles Chargers in Week 4. Seattle opened the season 2-0 and even after dropping an extremely winnable game, Sam Darnold and the offense strung together 437 total yards, leaving little concern about the team’s production moving forward. According to the current lines at FanDuel Sportsbook , the Seahawks are a 6.5-point favourite (-118) , with their money line set at -335 and Los Angeles’ at +270 . The line for total points is 44.5 , seemingly predicting a higher scoring affair but not quite a shootout Although the Chargers sit at 0-3 with losses to the Arizona Cardinals, Las Vegas Raiders, and Buffalo Bills, they’re still not a team who should be taken lightly. While the offense has struggled to move the ball under new offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel, they’re led by a proven veteran in Justin Herbert and have a strong supporting cast, consisting of Omarion Hampton, Ladd McConkey and Oronde Gadsden II. Defensively, they picked off superstar quarterback Josh Allen twice in their Week 3 loss to the Buffalo Bills and held the dual threat signal caller to 22 rushing yards—even though he found the endzone twice. Regardless, the odds don’t necessarily justify how strong of a team Los Angeles can be. But they’ll have to contain a dangerous Seahawks attack, led by Jaxon Smith-Nijgba, who’s totaled an unworldly 405 receiving yards and six touchdowns across the team’s first three games. The real concern comes with their defense, who just allowed 33 points to a Marcus Mariota led Commanders team. Normally, it’s far from the issue but their secondary took a hit with safeties Julian Love (calf) and Ty Okada (hamstring) sidelined. It’ll be worth monitoring their status’ as the week progresses to see if either are healthy enough to suit up, but given Okada’s been completely sidelined so far this season and head coach Mike Macdonald hasn’t provided an update, they appear on track to be missing at least one of the two starters. The line of 44.5 for total points seems to align with one of two returning and Seattle’s defense improving, especially when taking into consideration they allowed just 17 points across their first two games with Love on the field. The Seahawks loss to Washington is eerily similar to Week 5 of last season, when they dropped a 38-35 offensive thriller to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers while missing several key defensive pieces. However, they bounced back with a win over the Jacksonville Jaguars and expect them to come out firing on all cylinders once again as they look to get back in the win column. 12s, make your voices heard on the SB Nation app! title: The 49ers’ injuries aren’t sustainable, but Brock Purdy might make them survivable
summary: The 49ers dodged several bullets with their injuries in their Week 3 win over the Arizona Cardinals. Having lost defensive end Nick Bosa to a calf injury last week week — with the star pass rusher likely looking at around a month on the sideline — the 49ers saw several other key players go down […]
full_text: (Photo by Thearon W. Henderson/Getty Images) | Getty Images The 49ers dodged several bullets with their injuries in their Week 3 win over the Arizona Cardinals. Having lost defensive end Nick Bosa to a calf injury last week week — with the star pass rusher likely looking at around a month on the sideline — the 49ers saw several other key players go down in a 36-30 defeat of their division rivals on Sunday. Mike Evans suffered a rib injury with two minutes left in the first half and was carted to the locker room, while the second half saw Trent Williams leave the game with a stinger and Dre Greenlaw sustain a quad injury. Yet the saving grace for the 49ers is that, following evaluation, none of those injuries are serious . Evans is day-t0-day with a rib strain, Williams should be ready by Thursday while Greenlaw will be managed throughout the week with a quad contusion. Still, there is an obvious sense of deja vu around the 49ers amid their excellent start to the season. The Niners are winning games despite a remarkable amount of injury adversity, just as they did in 2025. Yet with 16 players already on injured reserve, and with the 49ers electing not to put Bosa on IR in part because of concern about having enough spots to designate players to return, it is clear San Francisco is close to a tipping point with injuries. It is not sustainable for the 49ers to continue suffering injuries so consistently and keep winning. With tough games against the Denver Broncos and Seattle Seahawks on the horizon, fortunes for this injury-ravaged roster may soon change, and the harsh reality is that — even with this impressive start — it is difficult to envisage a roster in this shape seriously contending for the Super Bowl. In this situation last season, the 49ers’ decimated roster unsurprisingly hit a ceiling, and the result was 41-6 divisional round loss to the Seahawks that ended an admirable campaign. Still, for as much as the sheer scale of the injuries has presented significant challenges for San Francisco, outside of Ricky Pearsall, the 49ers have yet to lose a member their roster who could be considered a blue-chip player for the season. That is a crucial difference from 2025, when the 49ers lost Bosa and Fred Warner for the season within the first six weeks and also had to deal with a multi-week injury to quarterback Brock Purdy. And, though their current form amid the injuries doesn’t seem sustainable, the 49ers have hope that it can continue because of the play that is being sustained by two critical components of the offense. Purdy provides hope amid yet more adversity That Purdy’s performance against the Cardinals was arguably his worst of the season so far speaks to how well he is playing. Arizona succeeded in making life a lot more difficult for Purdy than either the Los Angeles Rams or Miami Dolphins did, and there were periods of the game in which the offense sputtered. Purdy did not put up the spectacular completion percentage numbers that defined the first two weeks, but the final stat line still made for very impressive reading. He completed only 55.6 percent of his passes against the Cardinals, but still threw for 297 yards and four touchdowns. Through three games, Purdy boasts a completion percentage of 72.3, has 789 passing yards and leads the NFL with nine touchdown passes while throwing just one interception. Purdy is also first in the NFL in success rate on passing plays (63.9%) and adjusted yards per attempt and adjusted net yards per attempt (both 11.1). He leads the NFL in passer rating (133.1) and QBR (93.8). In terms of Expected Points Added, Purdy’s EPA per play of 0.59 over the first three weeks ranks first of any quarterback since 2016, per Sumer Sports . BROCK PURDY TO MIKE EVANS EXTENDS THE LEAD @AZvsSF on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/ScREsrmsVw — NFL (@NFL) September 27, 2026 Put simply, Purdy is playing at an MVP level right now, with his standard exemplified by three standout plays in Week 3. His 23-yard touchdown pass to Mike Evans was a superb demonstration of the accuracy that has played a substantial role in his high completion percentage, while the sequence that effectively ended the game as a contest was an encapsulation of the upside he possesses as an athlete. Purdy was robbed of an early MVP moment when he saw a 35-yard scramble for a touchdown brought back because of what looked a harsh holding penalty against George Kittle. Two plays later, though, Purdy rolled out after a play-fake and found a wide-open Kittle for a 20-yard score to end Arizona’s comeback effort. Brock Purdy has put up an MVP performance through 3 weeks. Here are two MVP level plays that did not even count pic.twitter.com/y6UwKBxud5 — Gridiron Gold Mine (@GridironGoldM_) September 28, 2026 Asked if any quarterback is playing better than Purdy right now, Kyle Shanahan told his post-game press conference: “I’d be surprised, but I don’t study the other quarterbacks right now, so I don’t really know what anyone else is doing except for the guys that we go against. “I don’t get to see any of that, but I think it’s really hard to play much better than he’s playing right now.” All the numbers indicate you cannot play any better than Purdy is doing right now, but he is being supported by an offensive line that is doing an excellent job through three weeks. Indeed, despite concerns about the makeup on the interior O-Line and the injury to Williams on Sunday, the 49ers have still yet to give up a sack. Piss missile by Purdy on third-and-12 pic.twitter.com/nhDZWhvl2T — Ted Nguyen (@FB_FilmAnalysis) September 28, 2026 Per Pro Football Reference , the 49ers have allowed a pressure rate of just 13.5%, the best in the NFL. Pressures and sacks are a quarterback and offensive line stat, and those hugely impressive numbers reflect a quarterback with an elite understanding of how to move in the pocket and an oft-maligned O-Line making huge strides. The challenge for both Purdy and the O-Line is maintaining that kind of form as the difficulty level ramps up. Of course, there are going to be some down weeks for Purdy and the offensive line is obviously not going to go the entire season without giving up a sack. But the level of play at the quarterback position and in the trenches are primary reasons for hope for the 49ers that this year could be different, and that the injuries don’t necessarily have to limit what they can achieve. The defenses of both Denver and Seattle will severely test the 49ers up front and provide challenges to Purdy that he has yet to face through weeks. If Purdy and the O-Line can rise to these forthcoming challenges and perform at somewhere close to the standard they have each produced so far, then that would provide cause for expectations to rise significantly. San Francisco can’t afford for the injuries to keep piling up, and the 49ers desperately need Bosa back as soon as possible. But Purdy and those protecting him have to this point served as key differentiators from last season. As long as that remains the case, the 49ers have a chance of surviving their adversity and mounting a more serious challenge than their 2025 injuries allowed.
author: Nicholas McGee

title: Why didn’t George Kittle take a knee? Kyle Shanahan didn’t tell him to
summary: The San Francisco 49ers beat the Arizona Cardinals Sunday 36-30 and as the Cardinals went to their onside kick in an attempt to win the game, one question entered my mind: What was George Kittle doing running that final touchdown into the end zone? The touchdown is nice. Especially when Brock Purdy scored one two […]
full_text: SANTA CLARA, CALIFORNIA - SEPTEMBER 27: George Kittle #85 of the San Francisco 49ers celebrates after scoring a touchown during the fourth quarter against the Arizona Cardinals at Levi's Stadium on September 27, 2026 in Santa Clara, California. (Photo by Ezra Shaw/Getty Images) | Getty Images The San Francisco 49ers beat the Arizona Cardinals Sunday 36-30 and as the Cardinals went to their onside kick in an attempt to win the game, one question entered my mind: What was George Kittle doing running that final touchdown into the end zone? The touchdown is nice. Especially when Brock Purdy scored one two downs earlier with a near 50-yard scramble. Unfortunately that touchdown got nullified thanks to a holding call on none other than Kittle. Had Kittle taken a knee, the anxiety of the game possibly getting snatched from the 49ers would be nothing. The Cardinals had no timeouts, and the clock was well below the two-minute warning. A knee on the 1-yard line and the 49ers can run the clock out leading to the game ending 29-27, 49ers. Instead, we got this: Kittle extending the lead 📈 📺: FOX pic.twitter.com/iQXUbg6nGF — San Francisco 49ers (@49ers) September 27, 2026 Now look, no one is disputing the awesomeness of the touchdown itself, especially with the background behind it. That said, why not take a knee? Kittle had just the perfect opening to even go out of bounds. Stops the clock, but at least the 49ers can still tick the thing down, and the Cardinals can never take the field again. Kittle was just doing what he normally does. “Probably should have gone out of bounds,” Kittle told reporters after the game. “We could have just kneeled it out. But no one told me to, so that’s their fault, not mine.” The 49ers head coach shouldered responsibility for not delivering the memo: “That was on me,” Kyle Shanahan said. “I didn’t remind him in the huddle and I don’t expect him to be paying attention to the clock. But I definitely wish I did.” What resulted was the Cardinals trying to move down the field with a minute and change and electing to kick a 49-yard field goal on 2nd and 10 with 34 seconds left. 34 seconds is a sliver of time to get the obvious onside kick and then try to get it in the endzone proper. The plan didn’t work as the kicked ball rolled into the waiting arms of a Deebo Samuel. Leave it to George Kittle—or is it Kyle Shanahan—to leave us glued to the monitor until the very, very end.
author: Patrick Holloway

title: Kyle Shanahan explains why he was impressed with 49ers’ depleted D-Line in Week 3
summary: It’s no secret that the 49ers are extremely thin on the defensive line, and the pressure numbers from their Week 3 win over the Arizona Cardinals reflect that. Per Pro Football Focus, the 49ers managed only 12 pressures of Cardinals quarterback Jacoby Brissett, getting home on two as Ogbo Okoronkwo and Keion White recorded sacks. […]
full_text: SANTA CLARA, CA - SEPTEMBER 27: Keion White #56 of the San Francisco 49ers sacks Jacoby Brissett #7 of the Arizona Cardinals during an NFL game on September 27, 2026 at Levi's Stadium in Santa Clara, CA. (Photo by Matthew Huang/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images It’s no secret that the 49ers are extremely thin on the defensive line, and the pressure numbers from their Week 3 win over the Arizona Cardinals reflect that. Per Pro Football Focus, the 49ers managed only 12 pressures of Cardinals quarterback Jacoby Brissett, getting home on two as Ogbo Okoronkwo and Keion White recorded sacks. It was always likely to be tough sledding for the 49ers’ front from a pass-rushing perspective without Nick Bosa and rookie Romello Height, and with impressive rookie defensive tackle Gracen Halton leaving the game with cramps in the second half. But, speaking in his Monday conference call, head coach Kyle Shanahan explained why he was more than satisfied with the performance of the Niners’ young and depleted D-Line. Said Shanahan: “By no means was it perfect, but I was real proud of how they played. They really competed their asses off. They were running to the ball, working real hard. I thought they did a good job throughout the game. I think they all kind of died out a little bit as the game went, just getting those plays up into the 80s and then losing Gracen to the cramps and stuff, which just took the numbers down some. But, we were able to change up our fronts throughout the game. We asked a lot of them and considering the circumstances for them, I thought it was a real successful game for them.” With Raheem Morris as the defensive coordinator, the 49ers have become more multiple up front. Morris frequently mixes in five-man fronts, and he presented the Cardinals with several different looks last Sunday, with his deployment of Fred Warner as an extra rusher proving successful in speeding up Brissett’s clock. While playing in a variety of different fronts, Osa Odighizuwa (82%), White (69%), Khalid Kareem (62%) and Okoronkwo (55%) all featured on over 50 percent of the defensive snaps. That is a huge mental and physical strain to put on a thin group and, in those circumstances, a return of two sacks and only 90 yards surrendered Jeremiyah Love on the ground represents a solid day from the 49er D-Line. It is not an effort Shanahan will want that group to have to put in regularly, and help is on the way with Height returning to practice following surgery on his broken hand, Matthew Judon being signed to the practice squad and Mykel Williams seeing his practice window opened after starting the year on the PUP list. Reinforcements are on the way ahead of more exacting challenges for the 49ers against the Denver Broncos and Seattle Seahawks in the next two weeks. However, those who held the fort on the defensive side of the trenches against Arizona can afford to hold their heads high.
author: Nicholas McGee

title: Kyle Shanahan puts Brock Purdy in company with former MVP after win
summary: San Francisco 49ers quarterback Brock Purdy has opened the 2026 season playing the best football of his career, as the offense has been on a tear through three games. Purdy has thrown for 789 yards, nine touchdowns, and one interception, while rushing for 93 more yards and another score. He’s completing 72.3 percent of his […]
full_text: SANTA CLARA, CALIFORNIA - SEPTEMBER 27: Brock Purdy #13 of the San Francisco 49ers looks to throw during the third quarter against the Arizona Cardinals at Levi's Stadium on September 27, 2026 in Santa Clara, California. (Photo by Ezra Shaw/Getty Images) | Getty Images San Francisco 49ers quarterback Brock Purdy has opened the 2026 season playing the best football of his career, as the offense has been on a tear through three games. Purdy has thrown for 789 yards, nine touchdowns, and one interception, while rushing for 93 more yards and another score. He’s completing 72.3 percent of his passes and averaging 9.5 yards per attempt, as the 49ers have averaged nearly 33 points a game so far. While there has been some strong quarterback play to start the year, Purdy has quickly put himself in the MVP conversation with the 49ers’ 3-0 start. Over the years, head coach Kyle Shanahan has seemingly put the ball in Purdy’s hands in key situations more often, and he did so again to seal the deal on Sunday, as the 49ers threw their way to victory at the end. Purdy dropped back four times on San Francisco’s game-sealing drive up two with 2:51 to go, which included a 20-yard touchdown pass to George Kittle to put the 49ers up nine with 90 seconds remaining. The quarterback position has long been talked about for the 49ers under Kyle Shanahan, who has been able to field successful offenses regardless of who has been at the helm. But it’s clear he’s easily been the most confident with Purdy calling the shots. Is this the most confident he’s been in a quarterback during his coaching career? “I had that [level of confidence] with Matt [Ryan] in ’16,” Shanahan said after the game. “Had it in [Matt] Schaub way back in the day. And I’ve had it with Brock, I think, four years in a row now.” And that feeling has been echoed throughout the building. “Yes, I think Kyle’s confidence in Brock is incredibly high,” George Kittle said. “Brock’s confidence is incredibly high. It’s different. We can be in a Wednesday practice, and Brock might miss a pass, and I think in years past, Kyle would be frustrated with him for not hitting that pass or another quarterback for not hitting that pass. Now, Kyle is like, ‘nah, he’ll hit it on game day.’ It’s fun to see that in that relationship with them.” “Yeah, it’s electric [watching Purdy play],” safety Malik Mustapha added. “We always knew that Purdy was going to be a top quarterback in this league. I’m glad he’s getting the respect he deserves. We see how he works day in and day out, and I’m just glad he’s getting his flowers.” Even with the injury situation getting dire, the 49ers have looked like true contenders in 2026. And Purdy is the biggest reason for it.

The San Francisco 49ers face the Philadelphia Eagles in January. It would not be surprising to see the Niners meet with the Bears later on in January, either.
