title: Mykel Williams’ practice window set to be opened, 49ers get good news on veteran trio
summary: After a Week 3 victory during which it seemed like the 49ers’ injuries were reaching critical mass, San Francisco got several pieces of good news on Monday. Veteran wide receiver Mike Evans, left tackle Trent Williams and Dre Greenlaw all left the win over the Arizona Cardinals with injuries, adding to the concerns for a […]
full_text: HOUSTON, TX - OCTOBER 26: Mykel Williams #98 of the San Francisco 49ers exits the field during an NFL football game against the Houston Texans at NRG Stadium on October 26, 2025 in Houston, Texas. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images After a Week 3 victory during which it seemed like the 49ers’ injuries were reaching critical mass, San Francisco got several pieces of good news on Monday. Veteran wide receiver Mike Evans, left tackle Trent Williams and Dre Greenlaw all left the win over the Arizona Cardinals with injuries, adding to the concerns for a roster that has already suffered a lot of setbacks on that front at this still early stage of the season. But there is a chance that all three could feature against the Denver Broncos on Sunday. Speaking in his Monday conference call, Shanahan confirmed an earlier report from Ian Rapoport that Evans is day-to-day with a rib injury . Evans will be evaluated throughout the week, with Shanahan saying of his injury: “It shouldn’t be long-term. We’ve got to see how it goes throughout the week. Guys have been in this position before, so we’ll see how it goes.” Shanahan added that Williams should be “good to go” by Thursday after sustaining a stinger, while Greenlaw — who suffered a quad contusion — will also be managed throughout the week. Of the three, Evans seems the biggest doubt to be involved as the 49ers welcome the Broncos to Levi’s Stadium. Defensive end Nick Bosa (calf) and defensive tackle James Thompson Jr. (high-ankle sprain) will not be play, however. But the Niners are poised to get some help on their depleted defensive front, to which they added veteran Matthew Judon on Monday, signing him to the practice squad . Last year’s first-round pick Mykel Williams is set to have his practice window opened this week, Shanahan confirmed. Williams started the year on the PUP list after suffering a torn ACL last November. Though he is not eligible to play this week, his return to practice indicates Williams is on track to make his season debut in Week 5 against the Seattle Seahawks. He may need some time to knock the rust off, but Williams’ prospective return will be a particularly big boost to a 49er run defense that has again been inconsistent at best so far this season. San Francisco ranks 14th in EPA per play against the rush through three games, but is last in the NFL with a 49.4 success rate allowed on run plays. In addition, the 49ers are set to get rookie defensive end Romello Height back in practice this week. The third-round pick, who had played 52% of the defensive snaps through the first two weeks, missed the Cardinals game due a broken hand. The 49ers are still very thin on the defensive front, but the returns of Height and then Williams will improve the situation at least somewhat. And having dodged bullets with the three key veterans, San Francisco is in better shape than might have been expected heading into a formidable two-game stretch
author: Nicholas McGee

title: Mike Evans is considered ‘day-to-day’ with rib injury
summary: The 49ers will be breathing a sigh of relief after getting good news regarding the injury to wide receiver Mike Evans. Evans left the 49ers’ Week 3 win over the Arizona Cardinals with two minutes left in the half following a collision with Budda Baker. The future Hall of Famer was clearly in considerable pain […]
full_text: SANTA CLARA, CALIFORNIA - SEPTEMBER 27: Mike Evans #5 of the San Francisco 49ers leaves the field after sustaining an injury during the second quarter of the game against the Arizona Cardinals at Levi's Stadium on September 27, 2026 in Santa Clara, California. (Photo by Ezra Shaw/Getty Images) | Getty Images The 49ers will be breathing a sigh of relief after getting good news regarding the injury to wide receiver Mike Evans. Evans left the 49ers’ Week 3 win over the Arizona Cardinals with two minutes left in the half following a collision with Budda Baker. The future Hall of Famer was clearly in considerable pain and had to be carted to the locker room. NFL Network and ESPN’s Ian Rapoport reported on Sunday that Evans was dealing with a rib strain. He followed up on Monday with a very encouraging update, revealing that, following an evaluation, Evans is considered day-to-day. A rib strain refers to a strain of the intercostal muscles between the ribs. Though it is clearly a painful injury, it is a huge positive for the 49ers that Evans is dealing with a relatively minor issue. While there is still a chance Evans could miss Sunday’s game with the Denver Broncos, Evans being day-to-day rather than week-to-week is a significant win ahead of a testing period for the 49ers in which they will face the Seattle Seahawks’ vaunted defense on the road following the visit of Denver’s fearsome group. Evans has made an impressive start to his 49er career. Though he left the win over Arizona earlier, he still made a huge impact, successfully linking up with Deebo Samuel on a hook-and-ladder play that went for an 80-yard score and then showing tremendous late hands to haul in a pinpoint throw from Brock Purdy for a 23-yard touchdown reception. With two touchdown grabs in three games, Evans has already established an excellent rapport with Purdy. Despite the painful nature of his injury, Evans’ connection with his quarterback won’t be interrupted for very long.
author: Nicholas McGee

title: The 49ers are signing a four-time Pro Bowl pass rusher to their practice squad
summary: The 49ers are adding to a pass rush decimated by injuries, with four-time Pro Bowler Matthew Judon set to provide a veteran presence on the defensive front. Judon is signing with the 49ers’ practice squad, the team confirmed following a report from ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler. He will reunite with San Francisco’s defensive coordinator Raheem Morris, […]
full_text: EAST RUTHERFORD, NJ - DECEMBER 07: Matthew Judon #8 of the Miami Dolphins rushes during the game against the New York Jets on December 7, 2025 at MetLife Stadium in East Rutherford, New Jersey. (Photo by Rich Graessle/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The 49ers are adding to a pass rush decimated by injuries, with four-time Pro Bowler Matthew Judon set to provide a veteran presence on the defensive front. Judon is signing with the 49ers’ practice squad, the team confirmed following a report from ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler . He will reunite with San Francisco’s defensive coordinator Raheem Morris, whom Judon played under during Morris’ time as the Atlanta Falcons head coach. Judon had 5.5 sacks in his only season with the Falcons in 2024. He played 13 games with the Miami Dolphins last year before being waived last December. Judon then played one game for the Buffalo Bills after signing with their practice squad. The 34-year-old made four consecutive Pro Bowls between 2019 and 2022, recording double-digit sacks for the Patriots in 2021 (12.5) and 2022 (15.5) after signing with New England following five seasons with the Baltimore Ravens. Those peak years may be behind Judon, but he is confident he can make a difference for a 49ers team lacking depth on the defensive line amid their plethora of injuries. Judon said in an interview with All32’s Arabia Tillery prior to Fowler’s report that he was set to sign with the 49ers. “With all of the injuries piling up over there I think I can just come in and help until some of those guys get back,” Judon said. The 49ers are very light on depth on the edge, with Nick Bosa out with a calf injury and rookie Romello Height dealing with a broken hand that kept him out of Sunday’s Week 3 win over the Miami Dolphins. In their absences, Keion White, Khalid Kareem and Ogbonnia Okoronkwo were the primary members of the edge rotation, with Viliami Fehoko playing 13 snaps in the win. Judon could make his 49er debut when San Francisco hosts the Denver Broncos on Sunday.
author: Nicholas McGee

title: 49ers grades vs. Cardinals: The offensive line is officially a strength
summary: If the San Francisco 49ers make the playoffs, nobody will look back and say, “Well, they almost lost in Week 3!” You can’t say the same about the other two playoff contenders in the division. Winning is all that matters. Here’s how the 49ers got there. Let’s hand out some positional grades. Quarterback: A If […]
full_text: (Photo by Ezra Shaw/Getty Images) | Getty Images If the San Francisco 49ers make the playoffs, nobody will look back and say, “Well, they almost lost in Week 3!” You can’t say the same about the other two playoff contenders in the division . Winning is all that matters. Here’s how the 49ers got there. Let’s hand out some positional grades. Quarterback: A If you didn’t watch the game, you’d look at Brock Purdy’s 55.6% completion percentage and think he played poorly. After all, he only completed 15 of his 27 passes. But 14 of those went for first downs. Another four went for touchdowns. Winners and Losers mentioned it , but it’s always a great sign when Purdy throws the ball away. No quarterback had a higher throwaway percentage in Week 3 than Purdy. The Cardinals did everything they could to condense the middle of the field. Over 40% of Purdy’s attempts came outside of the numbers. That’s not where the 49ers generally operate. Winners and Losers also highlighted how Brock Purdy passes Lamar Jackson for the all-time record for the most games in a career with at least a 130 passer rating. In Week 3, Lamar’s EPA per pass was 0.51, an excellent number and second-best in the league that week. Purdy’s was 0.81. A number you’d be hard-pressed to accomplish in Madden. Nearly every time Purdy dropped back, he added a point to the scoreboard. Purdy gets an A because the Cardinals were down multiple members in their secondary, and it’s the Cardinals. Plus, he wasn’t perfect. There were at least two throws he’d want back. And if we’re going to judge him like the MVP candidate he is, then he should be graded on an MVP scale. Purdy’s been in complete control through three games. His EPA per pass was higher in Week 2 (the 11th-best mark for any quarterback since 2022). You love to see Purdy pick and choose when to scramble. Purdy became the second quarterback since 2022 to post an EPA per pass of 0.8 or higher in back-to-back weeks. He was great, and the 49ers need him to be. Running back: A Last week in this piece, we mentioned how Kaelon Black left some yards on the field. He’s a rookie. There will be games like that. So it’s no surprise to see Christian McCaffrey get the lion’s share of carries in a divisional game. Purdy being awesome will overshadow how well McCaffrey played. It shouldn’t. McCaffrey forced four missed tackles, averaged 2.6 yards after contact, and five yards per carry. When the 49ers ran the clock out toward the end of the game, McCaffrey chewed up much-needed yardage and time, keeping the defense off the field. McCaffrey picked up three first downs as a receiver. He gained 24 yards after the catch on 41 receptions. He’s still one of the most dangerous receivers out of the backfield, despite the declining speed. McCaffrey played 41 snaps compared to Black’s 8. Wide receiver: C+ The wide receiver group wasn’t bad, but most of the production came from the quarterback or the scheme. Was it cool to see Jordan Watkins catch passes? Of course. Making plays in your first regular-season game could be exactly what Watkins needs to build confidence moving forward. He was wide open on both receptions. On the play before the half, he was the only player in the picture. Deebo Samuel didn’t have a reception. He showed he can still run, but he had zero targets across 22 routes. Jacob Cowing was targeted twice across 14 routes. Losing Mike Evans changed everything. He ran only 12 routes but was targeted on six of them. KhaDarel Hodge played the second-most snaps behind Deebo, but that’s because of what he can do in the run game. It’s evident that Purdy really only trusts Evans. Maybe a better way to phrase it is that Purdy might be most comfortable throwing to Evans. If Evans is out for multiple weeks, which it seems like that’s where we’re headed, this group faces an uphill battle, going against two of the best secondaries in the NFL in the next two weeks. Tight end: B+ If Luke Farrell stays in-bounds on his one target and George Kittle doesn’t egregiously hold on Purdy’s touchdown run, then this is an A. Farrell is so much better as a run blocker than he was a year ago. His blocking prowess lets the team let Kittle run routes. A novel concept, isn’t it? Both players have Shanahan’s trust in pass protection: Always like seeing how teams are incorporating 'smoke breaks' for their tackles in pass pro. Few from SF here. pic.twitter.com/VQ1yH1UcEM — Brandon Thorn (@BrandonThornNFL) September 28, 2026 Purdy’s success rate targeting Kittle was 85.7%. Kittle caught his lone contested catch, forced a missed tackle, picked up 30 yards after the catch, caught a couple of touchdowns, and reached 17.06 miles per hour, which is crazy when you consider he’s basically been playing football for a month after a torn Achilles. Offensive line: A- Jake Brendel was the only player to keep a clean sheet in pass protection, but if you allow two pressures — which a few of the linemen did — on 28 pass-blocking snaps, in no way is that a bad game. In what field is being successful 92% of the time considered bad? None that I’m aware of. Through three weeks, the #49ers have two of the top 6 and three of the top 13 offensive linemen in the league in pressure rate allowed, per Next Gen Stats: No. 1 — C Jake Brendel – 0% T-No. 6 — RG Dominick Puni – 2.2% No. 13 — LT Trent Williams – 3.7% — Nick Wagoner (@nwagoner) September 28, 2026 For the season, the line has allowed 12 pressures in true pass sets. They are winning almost every rep. A neck stinger for Trent Williams meant Vederian Lowe would finish the final 19 snaps at left tackle. He held up well. Per Sumer Sports, each lineman recorded impact plays, with Dominick Puni leading the way with three. Brendel and Colton McKivitz each had two apiece. McCaffrey averaged 2.6 yards before contact on his attempts. That’s incredible. There were two to three series that felt like the Cardinals got the best of the line, but across 50 plays, the Niners won the battle and did so convincingly. There’s no need to sugarcoat it: the offensive line is a strength for the 49ers, and pretending otherwise is either being purposely obtuse or you’re living off plays from past years. The real test happens over the next two games. Defensive line: B- Since we are humans, we don’t have to trash a defensive line whose longest-tenured player is Keion White: The 49ers defensive line yesterday: Player they traded for last October Player they signed on August 6 Player they signed on August 24 Player they signed on September 4 Player they traded for on March 11 Player they drafted in the 4th round of '26 Practice squad player making… — Kyle Posey (@KP_Show) September 28, 2026 You cannot have high expectations when you enter a game with two defensive tackles who were on the roster entering training camp, and one of those gets hurt halfway through the game. Khalid Kareem played 51 snaps. He was a last-minute add ahead of Week 1. Raheem Morris did everything in his power to increase the variance. He blitzed Jacoby Brissett on 50% of his dropbacks. In a way, it worked. Ogbo Okoronkwo and Keion White had a sack. Okoronkwo managed a 15.2% pressure rate. Newcomer Viliami Fehoko won a couple of his pass rushes and turned them into pressures. White has been closer to good than average through three weeks. His pass rush win percentage was 15.9%. The problem is when you ask role players, in this case pass rush first players, to play the run, they wear down, and you get the second half against the Cardinals. Fehoko was the only edge rusher to make a run stop. Jeremiyah Love averaged 1.81 yards before contact on 21 attempts. Sebastian Valdez had two run stops, and Naquan Jones added a run stuff. Those two held up well against the run but offered little in the pass-rush department. Kevin Givens flashed. Osa Odighizuwa made an impact rushing the passer. Gracen Halton was headed for another strong performance before an injury. But after he left, Odighizuwa couldn’t leave the field,…

title: Buccaneers Week 3 Top Performers vs. Minnesota Vikings
summary: I’ve done Top Performers recaps for quite a while — since 2020 in fact. Good year to start! Since then, we’ve seen the longest stretch of sustained success this millennium for the Buccaneers, and as such a lot more good than bad to write about. We got a Super Bowl, multiple playoff wins, 5 straight […]
full_text: TAMPA, FLORIDA - SEPTEMBER 27: David Walker #51 of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers celebrates a sack against the Minnesota Vikings during the first half at Raymond James Stadium on September 27, 2026 in Tampa, Florida. (Photo by Mike Carlson/Getty Images) | Getty Images I’ve done Top Performers recaps for quite a while — since 2020 in fact. Good year to start! Since then, we’ve seen the longest stretch of sustained success this millennium for the Buccaneers, and as such a lot more good than bad to write about. We got a Super Bowl, multiple playoff wins, 5 straight playoff appearances, 4 NFC South titles. Plenty of debates can be had about the value of the latter accomplishment given the state of every team residing within the division, but wins are still wins, and we all would’ve happily taken such results through the dearth of the 2010s. It was a dark time, and when such a time must be alluded to in the year of our lord 2026, there’s plenty of reason for concern. On Sunday, the Buccaneers floundered to their first 0-3 start since 2014, as they saw themselves overwhelmed by a relentless Minnesota Vikings defense in a 23-16 defeat. The score remained within reach all game, but it never really felt obtainable — one of the more agonizing types of defeat. The offense remained completely inoperable, setting an all-time franchise worst in third-down offense by converting only twice on 17 attempts. It was a bottom-5 performance by any team thus far in offensive EPA, as Baker Mayfield and Co. could muster only 243 total yards while permitting 6 sacks. The defense actually played very well, arguably shutting down the Vikings even more thoroughly. However, it was all for naught as they could only do so much against short fields generated by the offense’s mistakes. Special teams allowed the deciding score in the form of an 86-yard punt return for a touchdown — Minnesota’s first in 10 years. Given how solid the unit has been on kickoff returns and coverage, it was a frustrating gaffe during a stretch of games where nothing is going Tampa’s way. Needless to say, we’re on the precipice of massive change. Most fans know that’s been brewing for awhile, but there’s only been three teams in the last 30 years to make the playoffs after starting 0-3. You don’t need a calculator to figure out the length of those odds. In his post-game presser, Todd Bowles remarked that the “funny thing” is that the team is only 1 game out of first place — y’know on account of the other 3 teams sucking butt at 1-2. I can’t really find the funniness in being the worst team in the worst division in football, but maybe Todd just has a different sense of humor than I. Maybe he knows his ill-fated time as head coach of this franchise is almost up, at long last. However, we’ve reached the point where I personally will need to see it to believe it. Nevertheless, let’s highlight some top performers quickly and move onto the next one. Green Bay awaits. Offensive Top Performer: No One Yup, the first “no one” of the season goes to the offense, and it feels quite earned. I’m not sure what’s broken in Baker Mayfield — other than his thumb now of course — but since November of last year, he has been one of the worst quarterbacks in football after being one of the best through all of 2024 and the beginning of 2025. This year, his current EPA is -33.62, which is bottom 3 in the NFL with Cooper Rush and Aaron Rodgers (who the Bucs get to play in 3 weeks…yay?). He’s not connecting on deep balls, he’s turning the ball over, and he is taking way too many sacks. He’s currently the most sacked quarterback in the league, and while the offensive line has underperformed, it has not been that bad. For reference, the Vikings actually generated their lowest pressure rate of the year on Sunday yet recorded a season high in sacks. Mayfield is now likely out for a month with his thumb injury and leaves the reins to undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels. It’s really tragic to say that Daniels can’t be much worse than Mayfield has been, but I guess we’ll see soon enough. It’s not all on Mayfield though, as new offensive coordinator Zac Robinson is quickly showing why Falcons fans cheered his departure. The offense completely lacks an identity, is undisciplined, can’t draw up easy answers for the quarterback, puts way too much focus on tight end Cade Otton when receivers are open, and refuses to rely on the run game despite it being the clear strength of the team. Robinson needs to overhaul this quick or he’ll be back to being Sean McVay’s coffee assistant for a long time. Shout out to rookie Ted Hurst for his first career touchdown. It was a completely busted coverage that any college player could’ve taken advantage of, but he’s still shown some good things and will hopefully continue that upward trend. Defensive Top Performer: EDGE David Walker It’s malpractice that David Walker played basically no snaps the first two games. With Rueben Bain Jr. out with a groin injury and Yaya Diaby banged up in game, it forced the team to play Walker a season-high 19 snaps. The result? A sack, a tackle for loss, and multiple pressures to jolt the pass rush to its best game of the year. If Bain continues to be out healing, there’s no reason Walker shouldn’t be playing more. David Walker with the sack on 3rd and 4 😤 @MINvsTB on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/s1MxQoKd11 — NFL (@NFL) September 27, 2026 The entire defensive line played well, specifically A’Shawn Robinson (who actually got an interception) and Vita Vea (4 total tackles, 2 passes defensed). Given the slow start in the first two contests, hopefully this is kickstart the front 7 needs. The secondary also played well outside of one long touchdown allowed by Jacob Parrish, who slipped trying to adjust to an underthrown ball. Antoine Winfield Jr. and rookie Keionte Scott both recorded top-5 Pro Football Focus grades for the team as they were part of an effort that allowed Kyler Murray to complete just 15 of 29 passes for a paltry 168 yards. If team has any hope of turning this season around, it begins with the defense carrying the load. A'SHAWN ROBINSON BIG MAN PICK! 🤯 📺: #MINvsTB on FOX pic.twitter.com/dZiVA7Q2Ul — Tampa Bay Buccaneers (@Buccaneers) September 27, 2026 Special Teams Top Performer: K Chase McLaughlin The special teams top performer in perpetuity, there’s not much to be said here. McLaughlin went out, did his job in stellar fashion (3 for 3 with a long of 54 yards), and watched as his offense did nothing else. McLaughlin remains the NFL’s all-time accuracy leader on kicks from 50+ yards, an impressive feat.
author: Mike Kiwak

full_text: Photo by Mike Carlson/Getty Images | Getty Images The Tampa Bay Buccaneers received potentially devastating news following Sunday’s 23-16 loss to the Minnesota Vikings. Quarterback Baker Mayfield suffered a dislocated right thumb on his throwing hand late in the fourth quarter, head coach Todd Bowles confirmed following the game. Mayfield was scheduled to undergo an MRI on Monday to determine the full extent of the injury, and he is expected to miss two to four weeks as he recovers. And the early outlook isn’t encouraging. NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport shares that Mayfield is likely to miss time because of the injury, though exactly how long he could be sidelined won’t be known until additional testing is completed. #Bucs QB Baker Mayfield dislocated his right thumb, per coach Todd Bowles. MRI tomorrow. But likely to miss time. pic.twitter.com/U5jZKK1oQ8 — Ian Rapoport (@RapSheet) September 27, 2026 Mayfield was injured late in the loss after taking a hit while attempting a pass on fourth down. He immediately grabbed at his throwing hand following the play. The injury is a massive blow for a Buccaneers team that has now fallen to 0-3 to begin the season. Tampa Bay returns home next week to face the Green Bay Packers, and Mayfield’s availability now becomes the biggest storyline surrounding the team heading into Week 4.

title: Titans QB Cam Ward is wasting this offensive line
summary: Remember when everyone was worried about the Tennessee Titans’ offensive line prior to the 2026 season starting? Fast forward past Week 3 and the tape has revealed an even more concerning revelation. Sophomore quarterback Cam Ward is actually wasting a pretty good offensive line. Pro Football Focus has the Titans’ pass-protection unit ranked as No. […]
full_text: NASHVILLE, TENNESSEE - SEPTEMBER 20: Cam Ward #1 of the Tennessee Titans looks on prior to the national anthem of the game against the Philadelphia Eagles at Nissan Stadium on September 20, 2026 in Nashville, Tennessee. (Photo by Johnnie Izquierdo/Getty Images) | Getty Images Remember when everyone was worried about the Tennessee Titans’ offensive line prior to the 2026 season starting? Fast forward past Week 3 and the tape has revealed an even more concerning revelation. Sophomore quarterback Cam Ward is actually wasting a pretty good offensive line. Pro Football Focus has the Titans’ pass-protection unit ranked as No. 3 in the entire NFL , with a grade of 71.9. Through three weeks, Titans left tackle Dan Moore Jr. is the team’s only offensive lineman who has been assigned primary blame for a sack. Ward has been sacked on just five occasions through three games. Collectively, the Titans’ starting five has allowed 16 pressures. Some of these numbers may be slightly too favorable, but the point gets across. The Titans have done an excellent job protecting Ward in the passing game. ESPN Analytics has the Titans as a middling unit in pass protection. Whichever metric you believe, the takeaway is similar. The Titans have fielded a pretty good offensive line in protection. Ward is wasting that effort away. Ward has bailed some clean pockets. Inaccurate misses have been a weekly occurrence. The situation reached a boiling point on Sunday when Ward left 14 points on the board through two glaring red-zone errors in Week 3. As a rookie, many of the offense’s shortcomings were blamed on Ward’s supporting cast. That’s no longer the case. The offensive line has been upgraded. The wide receiver corps looks way better with Wan’Dale Robinson and Carnell Tate. The unfortunate truth is that Ward is the biggest preventative factor from the offense showing improvement right now. He’s a young QB who is struggling mightily in a new system, but many of his struggles are issues that date back to his rookie season (bad footwork, inaccurate passes). Ward needs to start playing better before the Titans consider doing something rash in 2027.

title: Did Cam Ward make a bad decision or a bad throw yesterday?
summary: Watching the Tennessee Titans’ final offensive play in real time yesterday, it looked to me like Cam Ward made a terrible decision to throw the ball. On the broadcast, it looked like there was a lot of room to run in front of him when he decided to throw the pass that was ultimately intercepted […]
full_text: EAST RUTHERFORD, NEW JERSEY - SEPTEMBER 27: Cam Ward #1 of the Tennessee Titans attempts a pass against Tremaine Edmunds #49 of the New York Giants during the third quarter at MetLife Stadium on September 27, 2026 in East Rutherford, New Jersey. (Photo by Elsa/Getty Images) | Getty Images Watching the Tennessee Titans’ final offensive play in real time yesterday, it looked to me like Cam Ward made a terrible decision to throw the ball. On the broadcast, it looked like there was a lot of room to run in front of him when he decided to throw the pass that was ultimately intercepted to end the game. After rewatching the play about 100 times, not running there was the smart play. There were two defenders between him and the end zone that would have stopped him. The real issue was the throw. Here’s the final play: Cam is catching a ton of heat for this response, and maybe he could have worded it differently, but he is right. EZ angle supports this. If he floats the ball to the corner of the end zone, it’s potentially a TD. Decision wasn’t issue. Type of throw was the problem. https://t.co/0DMYU6elC1 pic.twitter.com/O20Ybhf02j — Superhorn (@Super_Horn) September 28, 2026 Elic Ayomanor is running to the back left corner of the end zone. As old friend SuperHorn mentions, if Ward throws it to that corner, Jevon Holland has no chance to pick it off, and Ayomanor would have had a chance to catch it for a touchdown. The real problem is the accuracy of the throw. Watch it again. There is no shot that ball Ward threw was getting completed, even if he is able to throw it over Holland. With that being said, I also don’t think Ward was being reckless with the ball here. As I mentioned above, a throw to the corner is either a touchdown or an incomplete pass. That means they win the game or live to play another down – which would have been 2nd and goal from the 7. Ward has done more wrong than right this year. The thing that is really starting to scare me is his overall inconsistency. There have still been flashes of a solid quarterback in there, but he can’t put that together consistently from play to play, much less from game to game. The only way he is going to be a franchise quarterback is to play consistently. Through 20 NFL games, he has not shown the ability to do that.

title: Sonny Styles, Marcus Mariota among best Commanders from Week 3
summary: Every victory deserves some serious love in this league, and the players who deliver standout performances deserve to be recognized. After two disheartening weeks, our squad bounced back with a massive, hard-fought 33-31 win over the Seattle Seahawks on Sunday at Northwest Stadium.   To celebrate, I wanted to create a space for us fans […]
full_text: Every victory deserves some serious love in this league, and the players who deliver standout performances deserve to be recognized. After two disheartening weeks, our squad bounced back with a massive, hard-fought 33-31 win over the Seattle Seahawks on Sunday at Northwest Stadium. To celebrate, I wanted to create a space for us fans to give credit where credit is due and honor the guys who truly stepped up when we needed it most. This introduces our new weekly tradition: The Boss Hog of the Week. Moving forward, I hope to keep these fan votes running throughout the entire season. The rules are simple: each week represents a standalone vote, and at the end of the year, I’ll tally up all the weekly winners to crown the official, definitive Boss Hog of the season. Without further ado, let’s look at the standout performers. Here are your nominees for this week’s award: QB Marcus Mariota Stat line: 19-for-31, 183 passing yards, 3 passing TDs, 0 INTs | 5 carries, 11 rushing yards Marcus Mariota stepped into a high-pressure situation and delivered exactly what this team needed. Following a deflating loss to Dallas, Mariota was named the starter for the week with Jayden Daniels sidelined with a left elbow dislocation. In a massive show of confidence, the team also named him an all-season captain — and he rewarded that trust. Mariota led a smart, calculated attack, exploiting a Seattle defense that was missing both starting safeties. While it wasn’t always pretty, it was efficient, largely mistake-free football. He finished the day throwing for three touchdowns and sealed the victory himself, picking up a critical first down on a gritty third-and-7 run to run out the clock. It was a remarkably strong, poised performance from the veteran, who will now look to carry this momentum across the pond as the team heads to London. WR Terry McLaurin Stat line: 5 receptions, 78 receiving Yards, 1 receiving TD Terry McLaurin stepped up when his team needed him most. After frustratingly missing out on the end zone three separate times last week, McLaurin bounced back with a rock-solid performance to finally find paydirt this week. While he didn’t quite match the explosive stat line put up by his opponent, Jaxon Smith-Njigba, his impact on the outcome of the game was undeniable. McLaurin’s clutch 30-yard touchdown reception gave the team the necessary cushion to maintain the lead, serving as a perfect example of a squad that simply refused to give up. It was exactly the kind of gritty, winning football you want to see from a true leader. LB Sonny Styles Stat line: 4 solo tackles, 1 assisted tackle, 1 interception , 2 passes defensed, 1 forced fumble , 1 QB Hit. Sonny Styles had a true breakout performance . Many fans, including myself, thought his transition to this important defensive role would be a steep hill to climb, but he is completely shattering those expectations. He has been progressing week-to-week, proving that, while there are still areas to refine, he is absolutely fearless when facing a challenge. He was an absolute menace and an instant playmaker on Sunday, single-handedly disrupting the offense by being a part of two massive turnovers. His most impressive sequence didn’t even show up on the turnover sheet. It was a jaw-dropping play where he went stride-for-stride down the field with explosive Seattle running back Jadarian Price, perfectly tracking the ball to force a clutch pass breakup. That rare combination of size, speed, and coverage ability is exactly what Washington’s defense was desperately missing all of last season. He isn’t just surviving the transition; he’s becoming a star in the process. CB Amik Robertson Stat line: 6 total tackles (4 Solo), 4 passes defensed, 1 forced fumble The box score won’t reveal Amik Robertson’s true impact. Not just on Sunday, but over the previous weeks. Amik has been head-and-shoulders above the rest as the best cornerback on this team. He has fought tooth-and-nail to make every play miserable and difficult for opposing wide receivers. He was targeted relentlessly on Sunday, ultimately allowing four receptions for 36 yards and a touchdown, all to Seattle’s elite wideout Smith-Njigba. What truly earned Amik a spot on this ballot is his sheer, unyielding effort. Whether it’s laying out for pass breakups, ripping the ball away for a forced fumble or great pursuit to ensure a play doesn’t extend an inch further, he refuses to give up. Amik has established himself as the heart and soul of this defensive backfield, a secondary that should get better when Trey Amos makes his return. LB Kain Medrano The Stat Line: 5 Total Tackles (3 Solo), 1 Interception, 1 Pass Defended, 1 QB Hit, 1 Touchdown (Pick-Six). Welcome to the show, Kain! I had some very strong reservations about Medrano. He still has some clear tackling issues that carried over from his college days, but stepping into the fire the moment Leo Chenal went down was the ultimate test. He didn’t just fill a gap; he made arguably the play of the game with that beautiful interception on Sam Darnold, taking it to the house for a spectacular touchdown. It was an absolutely incredible moment for a player who simply kept his head down, stayed ready, and answered the call the second his chance arrived. OC David Blough David Blough deserves tons of love for this win, too. Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald’s defense has been an absolute buzzsaw since last season. That background makes this masterpiece of a game even more impressive for our first-year play caller. Blough drew up an excellent game plan and executed it beautifully. Seattle hadn’t given up an explosive play all year until Blough dialed up that 21-yard screen play to receiver Jaylin Lane. Following that up with the 30-yard touchdown strike to Terry McLaurin made it two explosive cracks. Even with several key players missing from his own unit, Blough kept a top defense completely off-balance and confused at times. This was a statement game for Blough, and doing it against a defensive juggernaut is a huge bonus for our coaching staff moving forward. This is the type of game that will either be a once-in-a-blue-moon moment or the exact shift of energy the Commanders needed to bounce back for the rest of the season. But, for right now, let’s just enjoy this massive upset! Be sure to vote in the poll below, and if there’s anyone I missed, make sure to post them in the comments. I hope you all enjoy this new series!

title: You can vote for Marcus Mariota as FedEx Air & Ground Player of the Week
summary: When Jayden Daniels was ruled out ahead of Sunday’s matchup against the Seattle Seahawks, I was personally confident in Mariota and the Commanders offense despite the fact that, usually, facing an opportunistic defense with a backup quarterback under center can be a recipe for white-knuckle football in Washington. As it turned out, I was right […]
full_text: LANDOVER, MARYLAND - SEPTEMBER 27: Marcus Mariota #8 of the Washington Commanders passes the ball against the Seattle Seahawks during the third quarter at Northwest Stadium on September 27, 2026 in Landover, Maryland. (Photo by Scott Taetsch/Getty Images) | Getty Images When Jayden Daniels was ruled out ahead of Sunday’s matchup against the Seattle Seahawks, I was personally confident in Mariota and the Commanders offense despite the fact that, usually, facing an opportunistic defense with a backup quarterback under center can be a recipe for white-knuckle football in Washington. As it turned out, I was right about veteran Marcus Mariota. He stepped into the huddle and delivered the kind of poised, veteran leadership this coaching staff envisioned when they kept him aboard. The NFL recognized his efforts on Tuesday, officially naming him a nominee for the FedEx Air Player of the Week. The nominees for the @FedEx Air & Ground Players of the Week. Vote for your winners below! ⬇️ pic.twitter.com/AiDqutNbmq — NFL (@NFL) September 28, 2026 To my eye, Mariota’s command of offensive coordinator David Blough’s scheme was steady from the opening whistle. He finished Sunday’s 33–31 thriller completing 19 of 31 passes for 183 yards, three touchdowns, and crucially, zero turnovers—good for a sharp 110.0 passer rating. Along the way, he also surpassed 18,000 career passing yards, joining an exclusive club of active NFL signal-callers to reach that milestone. It marked Mariota’s first three-touchdown outing since Week 8 of the 2022 season. Whether it was threading an 11-yard strike to Treylon Burks, flipping a screen out to Rachaad White, or improvising off-schedule to find Terry McLaurin for an acrobatic 30-yard score down the sideline, Mariota consistently took what the defense surrendered and protected the football in high-leverage spots. Blough kept the game plan balanced and in rhythm, and Mariota executed it to perfection. We saw flashes of this caliber of play last season when Mariota stepped in against Carolina, completing 78% of his passes to preserve a blowout victory. On Sunday, however, Washington needed (almost) every single one of those 33 points to hold off Seattle. Voting for the FedEx Air & Ground awards is open to fans online through Wednesday afternoon. Regardless of whether Mariota takes home the trophy over his fellow nominees, having a backup who can step onto the field and pilot a 30-plus point victory is a luxury few franchises enjoy.

title: Washington Commanders Whiteboard: Notes and observations from Week 3
summary: Before the advent of media devices, football coaches at all levels used simple whiteboards to outline plays, map out player positions and explain schemes in real time. Nowadays digital playbooks and tablets have taken over, but coaches still use whiteboards on occasion to impart information quickly and effectively. The following are some quick notes and […]
full_text: Before the advent of media devices, football coaches at all levels used simple whiteboards to outline plays, map out player positions and explain schemes in real time. Nowadays digital playbooks and tablets have taken over, but coaches still use whiteboards on occasion to impart information quickly and effectively. The following are some quick notes and observations from the Washington Commanders’ 33-31 upset win over the Seattle Seahawks at home. David Blough is developing quickly as a play-caller The Week 1 edition of Whiteboard noted that David Blough improved in his play-calling towards the end of his debut in Philadelphia but posed the question of if Dan Quinn and the Washington Commanders could afford to wait for a rookie player-caller to develop. Blough’s performance was better in Week 2 versus the Cowboys, but it was fair to question if the improvement was due to Blough’s continued growth as an offensive coordinator or the product of a suspect Dallas defense. In Week 3 versus Mike Macdonald and the defending Super Bowl champion Seahawks, David definitively answered the question. He is developing rapidly. Headed into a tough matchup with a backup quarterback and depleted offensive line, David Blough called an outstanding game. After taking advantage of the Seahawks’ first turnover, Blough dialed up a fake swing pass in the second quarter that was in actuality a tunnel screen to Jaylin Lane, resulting in the first 20-plus yard play of the season allowed by the Seahawks defense. David Blough was in his bag today for the #Commanders and called a hell of a game against an elite Seahawks defense. Favorite play of the game was the fake out to Rachaad White then screen to Jaylin Lane. #RaiseHail pic.twitter.com/7UABnY21Wu — Carolina Commander (@SC_Commanderr) September 27, 2026 Blough continued to call the game with an eye for time of possession, staying committed to the run and short passing game, but also taking downfield shots on occasion. The offensive coordinator was quick to attack after turnovers, and following Sonny Styles’ interception, it took only three plays for Washington to score on a 30-yard touchdown pass to Terry McLaurin. Commanders OC David Blough called a great game but was really impressed by the checks he had prepared for Mariota at the line. Here, the motion shows Seattle is in single high, Mariota kills the original play call, and Terry McClaurin wins his 1-on-1 pic.twitter.com/uoDBQksScE — Steven Ruiz (@theStevenRuiz) September 28, 2026 Blough kept his finger on the pulse of the game, and after feeding Bill Croskey-Merritt on RPOs for the majority of the contest, he dialed up the read option for Mariota on third and long to seal the game for the Commanders. Blough’s arrow will be pointing up when the Commanders head across the Atlantic in Week 4. The defense failed, but still carried the day Going into the game, the plan for the defense should have been to contain or limit Jaxson Smith-Njigba and make Cooper Kupp and A.J. Barner beat them. They failed in this respect , as JSN ended with 10 receptions for 128 receiving yards and two touchdowns, while Barner finished with five receptions for 69 yards. Cooper Kupp also recorded 4 receptions for 46 yards and a touchdown. All told, Sam Darnold threw for 379 yards and four touchdowns, and Seattle scored more than 30 points. The defense still won the day by unlocking their ability to generate takeaways. Headed into the contest with no forced turnovers, Daronte Jones’ scheme finally produced. Amik Robertson got things started by creating a forced fumble, punching the ball out of the arms of Seattle’s first-round pick, Jadarian Price. Sonny Styles delivered early in the second half, with a leaping interception of a deflected pass. Robertson and Styles led the defense for the Washington Commanders, with Amik having one of the best games of his seven-year career and Styles the best of his rookie season thus far. Amik Robertson Week 3 vs. Seahawks: 6 TKL | 4 SOLO | 4 PD | 1 FF Right after the two-minute warning, Seattle had 2nd & goal at the 2, down 14–7. Robertson broke up the throw, the D stopped the next two, and Seattle walked away with nothing. First W of the season came by two… pic.twitter.com/xqGmtJDp4N — SleeperCommanders (@SleeperWSH) September 27, 2026 Sonny Styles put on one of the most dominant individual performances on Washington’s defense we’ve seen since Sean Taylor. • 5 total tackles • 1 FF • 1 INT • 2 PD’s • Made the pre-set check putting Kain in position for the pick-six Superstar ⭐️ #RaiseHail pic.twitter.com/Vj70DcxKz5 — Nick Kerns (@nicktkerns) September 28, 2026 Odafe Oweh did his part by providing pressure on Kain Medrano’s interception, and the defense ended the day with three total turnovers, including a pick-six. The defense also made the Seahawks’ offense one-dimensional, allowing only 44 total rushing yards and no touchdowns to Seattle’s rushing attack. The Washington Commanders’ run defense has been elite through 3 games, allowing 168 rushing yards on 51 attempts, for a 3.3 yards per carry average and 0 TDs allowed. The overall performance might not have been dominant, but the defense did what they needed to do in order to secure the team’s first win of the season. Upgraded talent doesn’t just benefit the starting quarterback Marcus Mariota struggled in relief of Jayden Daniels last season, starting eight games with a 2-6 win-loss record. The team had already been decimated by injuries by the time Mariota started the majority of his games, and his play slowly deteriorated over the course of the season. On Sunday, the quarterback benefited from an upgraded wide receiver room and the addition of receiving back Rachaad White. Mariota found White for his first passing touchdown of the day while Stefon Diggs offered Mariota a safety blanket against a relentless Seahawks’ defense. Marcus targeted the veteran receiver several times underneath while finding Treylon Burks and star wide receiver Terry McLaurin for touchdowns on his way to throwing for a 183 passing yards, 3 touchdowns, 0 interceptions, with 5 rushes for 11 yards. Rachaad White gets 6️⃣ on the board for the Commanders! @SEAvsWAS on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/S3wsMvhedS — NFL (@NFL) September 27, 2026 3. Beautiful setup from Blough. Using Diggs as the RB pins the underneath defender just long enough to open up the window for Treylon Burks to score his first TD of the season pic.twitter.com/e83RC4BS9p — Full Command (@FullCommandShow) September 28, 2026 Most importantly, Mariota capitalized on his opportunities, the Commanders converted 20 points from turnovers vs. Seattle. The last time Washington scored 20 or more points off turnovers was in Week 17 of the 2005 season. An impressive performance from a backup quarterback operating under a new offense. The win was truly a team effort At the conclusion of last week’s Whiteboard , it was speculated that Marcus Mariota could win games going forward, but the entire team needed to improve their play in order for him to do so. While there’s certainly still room for improvement, several members of the team played critical roles to cement the win. Drew Stevens gets a 57-yarder to go as the half expires! 📺: FOX/FOX One pic.twitter.com/RHWv1cp5En — FOX Sports: NFL (@NFLonFOX) September 27, 2026 6. Tim Settle installed two magnets, one in the football and one in his helmet, when nobody was looking. Sonny Styles uses his 6’5 frame to soar up and pluck the Commanders’ first INT of the season out of the air! pic.twitter.com/LiWPjelRb1 — Full Command (@FullCommandShow) September 28, 2026 yeah… absolute cinema pic.twitter.com/dryMXPxtA5 — Washington Commanders (@Commanders) September 28, 2026 Who knows what happens if Bates doesn’t go from blocking the corner to blocking the safety. Best blocking TE in the league! #RaiseHail pic.twitter.com/Gj55DEjrk0 — SJM 🪖 (@DMVCommanders) September 27, 2026 Credit to Dan Quinn for having his players ready to…

title: Commanders QB Jayden Daniels traveling to London, possibly playing Colts
summary: Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels will travel with the team to London in advance of a Week 4 clash with the Indianapolis Colts at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium.   While it’s uncertain, and seemingly unlikely that Daniels will play in that game, the door’s open just the slightest crack.   We know for sure that Daniels will […]
full_text: Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels will travel with the team to London in advance of a Week 4 clash with the Indianapolis Colts at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium. While it’s uncertain, and seemingly unlikely that Daniels will play in that game, the door’s open just the slightest crack. We know for sure that Daniels will start practicing with the team this week, not too long after suffering a dislocated left elbow during a Week 2 loss at Dallas . That starts Daniels’ return to play process, an important step in getting him back on the field in games. “He has been putting in the work,” head coach Dan Quinn told reporters in a Monday virtual press conference . “I am excited to get him back on the practice field.” Daniels is not the only injured Commanders player going to London to start practice. Linebacker Frankie Luvu (groin) and tight end Chig Okonkwo (hamstring) will do the same, though the jury’s still out on guard Sam Cosmi (concussion) and safety Nick Cross (internal/illness). The Commanders leave for England on Tuesday evening. Daniels’ situation is a positive one that should include a return to play faster than he did in 2025, when he missed three games after suffering the same injury. Quinn didn’t identify why there are different timelines, only that the team doing what it’s told by doctors. “We’re just following the guidelines for him going through the process of him getting opinions from New York and L.A. sets the plan in motion,” Quinn said. “We’ll stick to that.” The Commanders will see how Daniels responds in practice and adjust its plans accordingly. Wednesday’s session, after a long travel day, is more of a walk-through. Thursday will be more at full speed and provide a good indication of Daniels’ status. The same can be said for Luvu and Okonkwo. “Once we get there, that’ll give us a little more of an indication of where we’re at and how we can go into that space,” Quinn said. “Just the fact that we’re working back into that space gives me optimism heading into the week about where we’re at from a health perspective.”

title: Commanders Vs. Seahawks – Studs and Duds
summary: The Commanders entered their first game at Northwest Stadium this season as home underdogs against the defending Super Bowl champions. But, through a gritty performance that saw them secure three turnovers, they pulled off a STUNNING 33-31 victory. Now 1-2 on the young season, and with a little momentum going their way, they head overseas […]
full_text: The Commanders entered their first game at Northwest Stadium this season as home underdogs against the defending Super Bowl champions. But, through a gritty performance that saw them secure three turnovers, they pulled off a STUNNING 33-31 victory . Now 1-2 on the young season , and with a little momentum going their way, they head overseas to London to take on the 1-2 Colts before coming back home to face the Giants. These next two games will likely define their season, so all hands need to be on deck if Dan Quinn hopes to move this squad towards respectability. Below are my Studs and Duds of the game followed by some notes. Studs: QB Marcus Mariota: Mariota looked completely in control the entire game. He made appropriate checks at the line, delivered the ball with accuracy and came up big with the game on the line. He finished the contest 19-for-31 passing for 183 yards and three touchdowns and was sacked just twice, but no play was bigger than his read option run on third-and-9 late in the fourth quarter. A great game by the captain. 3rd and 9 – PLAY OF THE GAME by Mariota!!!!! pic.twitter.com/TUM5jvMpT0 — Tiller56 (Hogs Haven) (@Tiller56) September 27, 2026 4th and 1 – Mariota hits Terry for the 1st! pic.twitter.com/HDgPVQcWvo — Tiller56 (Hogs Haven) (@Tiller56) September 27, 2026 WR Terry McLaurin: Terry had his breakout game of the 2026 season, leading the team with six receptions for 77 yards and a leaping score. It was great to see F1 get on track! Terry goes up over Jones for the TD! 💥 pic.twitter.com/8TbV0awjiV — Tiller56 (Hogs Haven) (@Tiller56) September 27, 2026 Mariota finds Terry for 18yds before the half pic.twitter.com/IoJTHGE3Rf — Tiller56 (Hogs Haven) (@Tiller56) September 27, 2026 RT Josh Conerly: The second-year right tackle has come a long way from his difficult rookie season. He is starting to show a better anchor in pass protection, and his run blocking has been excellent. He didn’t allow a pressure against a very good Seattle defense. DL Javon Kinlaw: Kinlaw was a beast inside all afternoon. A lot of his play may have went unnoticed, but a lot of the defensive success stopping the run was because of him. He had two stuffs and two pressures on the afternoon. Kinlaw with another stuff. He’s having a big game pic.twitter.com/z6BNjZxxDt — Tiller56 (Hogs Haven) (@Tiller56) September 27, 2026 Kinlaw with another pressure pic.twitter.com/HC4ASDbWTp — Tiller56 (Hogs Haven) (@Tiller56) September 27, 2026 Kinlaw playing BIG inside. Gets the Stuff here pic.twitter.com/feA6L886Hs — Tiller56 (Hogs Haven) (@Tiller56) September 27, 2026 LB Sonny Styles: Sonny had a very good game, and I can’t wait for All-22 to come out to really study his work. He was solid against the run, showed very good coverage (two passes defended), recorded his first NFL interception off a tipped pass by Tim Settle and forced a fumble at the goal line that ended up getting recovered by the tight end who fumbled for a touchdown. title: 2026 NFL Power Rankings: How all 32 teams stack up for Week 4
summary: How do all 32 NFL teams stack up through three weeks? Plus, we picked out each team's biggest fantasy surprise -- good or bad.
full_text:
Week 3 of the 2026 NFL season  was filled with close matchups. There were 12 games decided by eight or fewer points Sunday, tying the record for the most such matchups in a single day, per ESPN Research.

 Along with those close contests came plenty of  intriguing fantasy performances . So in addition to our 1-32 rankings, we asked our NFL Nation reporters to look at every team's fantasy football surprise (good or bad) this season. They went off ESPN Fantasy 's draft rankings ,  average draft position (ADP) and  current scoring leaders in PPR leagues.

 To form the list, our power panel of more than a dozen NFL analysts evaluates how all 32 teams stack up against one another, ranking them from No. 1 to 32. And here are a few highlights from this week's rankings:

 
 The 3-0 Raiders are shooting up our list, climbing six spots after doing the same last week. They're the first team in the common draft era (since 1967) to start 3-0 after selecting a QB No. 1 ( Fernando Mendoza ) in the previous draft, per ESPN Research. And against the Saints, they broke a franchise-worst streak of 39 regular-season games in which they failed to score 30 points. 
 New England fell six more spots after quarterback  Drake Maye  registered a 15.5 Total QBR in a blowout loss to the Jaguars -- a career worst with at least 15 dropbacks. Through three games, the Patriots' offense is averaging the lowest EPA per play and points per drive by any team since the 2023 Jets, who had Zach Wilson at QB, per ESPN Research. 
 After starting 0-3, the Buccaneers are ahead of only the Titans and Dolphins. This is the team's worst record to begin a season since 2014, when it finished 2-14 in its first year under current general manager Jason Licht. And things might not get easier for the Bucs, who are expected  to play undrafted rookie free agent Jalon Daniels in place of the injured Baker Mayfield (thumb) for at least the next three weeks. 
 
 Let's get into the full list, starting with the same No. 1 team as last week.

 Previous rankings: Week 2 | Week 3 

 

 
 Jump to a team: 
 ARI | ATL | BAL | BUF | CAR | CHI | CIN 
 CLE | DAL | DEN | DET | GB | HOU | IND 
 JAX | KC | LAC | LAR | LV | MIA | MIN 
 NE | NO | NYG | NYJ | PHI | PIT | SF 
 SEA | TB | TEN | WSH 

 
 

 

 1. Buffalo Bills (3-0) 
 Week 3 result: Beat the Chargers 24-16 
 Week 3 ranking: 1 

 Fantasy surprise: TE Dalton Kincaid 

 

 Through three weeks, Kincaid leads all NFL tight ends in receiving yards and has caught 14 of the 17 passes thrown his way. He ranks among the top 10 tight ends in targets, posting the best catch percentage (82.4%) of any tight end or wide receiver with at least that many targets. Not bad for someone who was ranked as TE15 in ESPN's draft rankings. -- Nick Suss 

 
 

 

 2. San Francisco 49ers (3-0) 
 Week 3 result: Beat the Cardinals 36-30 
 Week 3 ranking: 3 

 Fantasy surprise: TE George Kittle 

 

 Under normal circumstances, it would not be a surprise to see Kittle as the TE4 in fantasy. But given that he  tore his right Achilles on Jan. 11 and missed all of training camp, that he returned in Week 1 close to his usual self is a testament to his passion for the game. And the Niners have needed every bit of his production to help weather the storm of injuries elsewhere. Kittle ranks fifth among all tight ends in receiving yards (174), 11th in receptions (12) and tied for first in touchdowns (three).  -- Nick Wagoner 

 
 

 3. Kansas City Chiefs (3-0) 
 Week 3 result: Beat the Dolphins 24-10 
 Week 3 ranking: 4 

 Fantasy surprise: RB Kenneth Walker III 

 

 Most fantasy owners knew Walker was a good choice, especially after his impressive postseason run to help the Seahawks win the Super Bowl. But not even the Chiefs could have expected this level of production from Walker, who has the second-most total fantasy points at RB this season. He has already produced 442 scrimmage yards and four total touchdowns. Walker is the first player in franchise history to have two games with a rushing and receiving touchdown within the first three weeks, per ESPN Research.  -- Nate Taylor 

 
 

 4. Seattle Seahawks (2-1) 
 Week 3 result: Lost to the Commanders 33-31 
 Week 3 ranking: 2 

 Fantasy surprise: RB Jadarian Price 

 

 Price was 25th among running backs in ADP, reflecting the fact that he was going to be part of a timeshare in Seattle's backfield. But even with those modest expectations, the rookie first-round pick is off to an underwhelming start. He ranks 47th in fantasy points among running backs after a dud of a performance in Week 3, when he totaled 22 scrimmage yards on six touches with a lost fumble. The fumble was Price's second in as many weeks, which was a big reason for his diminished workload. -- Brady Henderson 

 
 

 5. Baltimore Ravens (2-1) 
 Week 3 result: Beat the Cowboys 34-31 
 Week 3 ranking: 7 

 Fantasy surprise: TE Mark Andrews 

 

 Andrews had surrendered the title of Lamar Jackson 's No. 1 target to WR Zay Flowers , but there was hope that he would remain an option in the red zone. He has only one red zone target on eight routes run this season. Now, he is dealing with a hand injury that limited his playing time in Week 3. Andrews, who was ranked as the TE14 before the season, is currently 19th in scoring at his position.  -- Jamison Hensley 

 
 

 

 6. Denver Broncos (2-1) 
 Week 3 result: Beat the Rams 30-26 
 Week 3 ranking: 8 

 Fantasy surprise: WR Courtland Sutton 

 

 The Broncos' offensive struggles, especially in first halves, have dragged down everybody's numbers. They haven't found a rhythm much of the time, and save for Jaylen Waddle 's 138-yard effort against the Jaguars in Week 2 , the WRs have been caught up in the wash ( Pat Bryant  has the group's only TD catch). Sutton, who is second in targets to Waddle with 16, could be seen as the biggest disappointment. He has yet to eclipse more than 10 fantasy points in any game. -- Jeff Legwold 

 
 

 7. Los Angeles Rams (1-2) 
 Week 3 result: Lost to the Broncos 30-26 
 Week 3 ranking: 5 

 Fantasy surprise: WR Puka Nacua 

 

 Despite missing part of training camp with a psoas injury , Nacua had an ADP of 9.0. But he has played only in Week 1 because of a groin injury, putting up 12.4 points in PPR leagues. On Sunday, ESPN's Adam Schefter reported  that the injury "has impacted [Nacua's] explosiveness." Last week, coach Sean McVay said  that barring a setback, the expectation is that Nacua will be able to play in Week 4  against the Eagles. -- Sarah Barshop 

 
 

 8. Philadelphia Eagles (2-1) 
 Week 3 result: Lost to the Bears 27-7 
 Week 3 ranking: 6 

 Fantasy surprise: WR Dontayvion Wicks 

 

 Wicks has the second-most receptions (nine) and receiving yards (179) on the team behind DeVonta Smith . He is currently the WR30 in fantasy. There was some thought heading into the summer that rookie Makai Lemon could ascend to the No. 2 role, but injuries left him on the sideline for most of camp. In the meantime, Wicks and QB Jalen Hurts  have developed a comfort level with one another, particularly in high-leverage moments.  -- Tim McManus 

 
 

 9. Minnesota Vikings (3-0) 
 Week 3 result: Beat the Buccaneers 23-16 
 Week 3 ranking: 12 

 Fantasy surprise: WR Justin Jefferson 

 

 Jefferson had an ADP of 13.4, but he has had only one fantasy-productive game for a variety of reasons. That came in Week 1, when he caught two touchdown passes from backup quarterback Carson Wentz  and scored 31.2 fantasy points. The Vikings played their Week 2 game at rainy Soldier Field, and in Week 3, Jefferson played only one series before departing with an ankle injury . Jefferson could be back as soon as Sunday against the Dolphins, but with the Vikings' offense struggling, it's unclear whether Jefferson can get back on track. -- Kevin Seifert

 Week 3 ranking: 13

title: 2027 NFL draft order projections for Round 1, top pick, more
summary: ESPN's Football Power Index projects the 2027 NFL draft order for Round 1, complete with each team's chances to pick in the top five, in the top 10 and at No. 1.
full_text:
The 2027 NFL draft is still months away, but with the 2026 season underway, we're starting to track pick order in Round 1. Which teams are in position to add elite prospects in the top 10 next April? What about the top five ... or even at No. 1?

 What follows is not the current draft order based on records. It is a projection of what ESPN's Football Power Index thinks the order ultimately will be by the end of the season. Each week during the season, the FPI projects the draft order by simulating the remainder of the season 10,000 times. Game probabilities are based primarily on the model's team ratings and game locations. The draft order is determined by the records the model projects for each team after 17 games, as well as each team's average draft position across the simulations.

 So where do things stand? Here are the full sortable projections, complete with each team's chances to pick in the top five, in the top 10 and at No. 1.

title: NFL Week 3's best arrivals, led by Jalen Hurts
summary: NFL stars continue to turn game-day arrivals into their own weekly fashion showcase.
full_text:
The official start of fall means it's fit season, when players start dominating the gameday tunnels with eye-popping jackets, sweaters and pants.

 Last week, the Philadelphia Eagles played a blazing hot game in Nashville that had players' cleats melting with with temperatures of up to 157 degrees Fahrenheit on the turf . 

 Hopefully this week is the start of a heat decline with more cloudier 50-to-75 degree days ahead to allow players to comfortably show off their fits.

 To kick off Week 3, Green Bay Packers quarterbacks Jordan Love and Tyrod Taylor rocked my two favorite outfits of the Thursday primetime slate.

 Love came in shining -- literally -- with a Public School New York x KAY jewelry collaboration jacket: the definition of a statement piece.

 Meanwhile, Taylor's Dries Van Noten sweater is the perfect kickoff to fall -- warm but fashion-forward. There are so many fabric design details within this one piece, showing the value of layers.

 Here are Week 3 fits that caught our eye:

 

 Monday night fashion 
 
The Philadelphia Eagles and Chicago Bears brought plenty of style to Soldier Field ahead of their "Monday Night Football" matchup.

 Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts pulled off a beige double-breasted suit look that was equal parts fly city jazz singer and CEO of an upstart-turned-Fortune 500 company.

 This Week 3 fit is a perfect example of Hurts' signature soulful style that commands respect and translates seamlessly from the tunnel to the field to his postgame presser one-liners. 

 
 Sunday's best 
 For primetime show, it's a who wore it better. The Los Angeles Rams duo of Davante Adams and Byron Young went with all-denim jacket and pant combos. Both can't miss ahead of "Sunday Night Football."

 

 The Baltimore Ravens and Dallas Cowboys brought their contrasting styles to Maracanã Stadium for the NFL's first game in Rio de Janeiro. Lamar Jackson donned a graphic tee paying homage to the late rapper DMX, while George Pickens ' fit featured Brazil's national colors in a nod to the host country. 

 San Francisco 49ers safety Malik Mustapha styling with an eye-popping Kid Super jacket was my favorite of this window.

 

 From Stefon Diggs ' black jacket covered in NBA throwback logo patches, to Malik Nabers ' custom "H1M" pendant, players brought plenty of style and personality ahead of the early slate.

 Four standouts in this window included Los Angeles Chargers cornerback Donte Jackson 's Boardwalk Vintage fit, which completed a preppy rockstar vibe. Carolina Panthers quarterback  Bryce Young KITH x New York to the world jersey was a winner. Cleveland Browns running back Quinshon Judkins leaned into the Fall Cleveland vibes with this unique Celine sweater. I love retro call backs so must give Diggs love on his vintage NBA bomber jacket.

 

 

 
 Thursday night fashion 
The Green Bay Packers host the Atlanta Falcons to kick off Week 3's slate, and quarterback Jordan Love entered the home opener in style, pairing an oversize studded leather pullover with black trousers, a crisp white shirt and black tie. He completed the look with dark sunglasses and a checkered duffel bag.

title: How active NFL players continue to redefine all-time sack list
summary: Myles Garrett's torrid pace up the all-time sack list paces active players making their moves among the greats.
full_text:
Last season, defensive end Myles Garrett won his second Defensive Player of the Year award after setting the NFL's single-season record with 23 sacks with the Cleveland Browns . 
 
 This season, he'll continue his climb up the NFL's all-time sack list as a member of the Los Angeles Rams  after a blockbuster trade  in June -- making the Rams favorites to win the Super Bowl, according to DraftKings Sportsbook, heading into the season. 
 
 Garrett entered the season with 125.5 career sacks, which was tied for 20th in NFL history and third among the other six active players --  Von Miller  (No. 9), Cameron Jordan  (No. 17), Calais Campbell  (No. 25), T.J. Watt  (No. 26), Danielle Hunter  (tied for No. 27) and Khalil Mack  (T-29th) -- in the top 30.  
 
 Joining the top 30 soon could be  Aaron Donald ,  who unretired  to join Garrett on the Rams' defensive line. Donald's 111 sacks currently sits two behind 30th.  
 
 As for Garrett, he entered his 10th season in the NFL averaging approximately 14 sacks per season. If he were to replicate that production, he would tie Pro Football Hall of Famer Jason Taylor, who currently sits at No. 7. If Garrett were to have another historic season, he would surpass Michael Strahan (No. 6) and approach career top-five territory. 
 
 
 
 Miller, who signed with the  Dallas Cowboys  in August, can also pass Strahan in his 15th season -- as he sits only three sacks behind him.   
 
 But Garrett's 125.5 career sacks heading into the season was 10.5 more than any other player since his rookie season in 2017, according to ESPN Research. The pass rusher recorded at least 14 sacks in each of the past five seasons, the longest such streak by any player since 1982. 
 
 If Garrett has 18.5 or more sacks this season, he will hold the record for the most over a two-season span since 1982, according to ESPN Research, and his current ascension up the career list ranks as the second-fastest pace among the top five all time behind only Reggie White's.  
 
As we look at how the sack list is redefined this season, we'll highlight milestones across the NFL landscape 
 We will update this file as the active players move up, and we'll add nuggets and milestones throughout the season. 
 

 

 Week 3 update 

 There wasn't much movement on the list this week with only Mack (1) and Hunter (.5) recording sacks. Watt, Campbell, Hunter and Mack (in that order) now make up 25 to 28 on the all-time list. Along with Campbell, the three top active leaders -- Miller, Jordan and Garrett -- have yet to record a sack this season.  

 Week 2 update 

 The second week of the season saw little movement near the top of the career list, but Watt's hot start continues, with the defensive end recording 1.5 sacks to now put him at 3.5 through two weeks (No. 2 in the NFL this season) and break a tie with Campbell to move to 25th. 

 Hunter (27th) and Mack (29th) also recorded one sack apiece over the weekend to break ties and move up one spot on the list. 

 Donald (33rd) made his  season debut on "Monday Night Football" against the Giants after taking two years off. He finished with three tackles, one for a loss, but did not record a sack. 

 

 

 Week 1 update 

 Of all the active sack leaders, Watt was the only one to record a sack, finishing the game with two to move to a tie with Campbell for 25th. 

 And while Donald was held out of the Rams' Week 1 game, Garrett will be out for at least the next four after failing to record a tackle in Australia and landing on injured reserve after having to have arthroscopic surgery on his knee.

 After the Rams' opening loss, Garrett said this was " the worst version of myself that I've put out there."

title: Seven things Solak thinks entering NFL Week 4
summary: Bowers will go off under Klint Kubiak? The Rams need another pass catcher? Steelers-Browns will be fun? And Lamar Jackson for MVP? Get ready for Week 4 with some takes.
full_text:
Who's ready to put their thinking caps on? Week 3 of the 2026 NFL season will go down in the history books, as 12 -- count 'em, 12! -- Sunday games finished within one score, the new single-day record for the league. Toss in two fun primetime games on Thursday and Monday and that was about as good a week as NFL football gets.

 Every Tuesday of the NFL season , I'll turn the page from the previous week to the upcoming one with seven things I think. These aren't full-scale predictions; those come later. They aren't concrete takeaways from the past week of NFL action, either; those are fired off Sunday or Monday. Instead, these are the uncertain topics. They are things that might be true, but it'll probably take the next few games to find out. And at the bottom, you'll find a few extra half-thoughts ... just those little inklings I'm unable to shake.

 This week, I'll start with the one player I've been most excited to see in his new system, make another pick for MVP (I'm up to two in three weeks) and highlight an intradivisional game between surprising 2-1 teams you should probably watch for fun. Here are seven things I think ahead of Week 4.

 

 
 Jump to: 
 Bowers is the new JSN 
 Jackson for league MVP 
 Lawrence reminds us to be patient with QBs 
 Rams should make one more trade 
 Steelers-Browns is suddenly important 
 I will never trust the Bills 
 McCarthy won't save the Giants 
 Five extra inklings 

 

 
 

 I think ...  Brock Bowers is the new Jaxon Smith-Njigba 
 We had to wait a few extra weeks for it, but one of the most anticipated debuts of the 2026 season struck Sunday. Bowers, the third-year Raiders tight end fresh off a meniscus cleanup, took his first snaps in Klint Kubiak's offense against the Saints. The final card? Ten catches, 116 yards and a score. Bowers has four career games of 10-plus receptions, 100-plus yards and a touchdown. Since he entered the league in 2024, the rest of the NFL's tight ends combined  have only four such games.

 

 So, he picked up where he left off.

 Watching Bowers is such a delight. He has receiver-like instincts and catch technique. He has receiver-like movement skills. He can run receiver-esque routes -- routes other coaches wouldn't think to ask of their tight ends.

 Now, you've likely heard other tight ends erroneously called "quasi-wide receivers." Analysts were obsessed with flex tight ends in the prime of Travis Kelce and Mark Andrews , so we started throwing the label around willy-nilly. It's important, in our appreciation of what Bowers brings to the Raiders' offense, to be objective about the uniqueness of his impact.

 Think of a smaller pass-catching tight end who's having a productive year: Dalton Kincaid with the Bills has been a breakout star. Against the Lions in Week 2, Kincaid had seven targets from traditional wide receiver alignments -- either in the slot or wide -- which was one of the highest among all tight ends this season. Arizona's Trey McBride , the league's preeminent move tight end, had 10 such targets against the Seahawks in Week 2 and the Chargers in Week 1.

 Bowers had 13 on Sunday against the Saints. In fact, all 13 of his targets were from slot or wide alignments. It's the most such targets a tight end has seen in the past three seasons. Specifically out wide, Bowers was targeted eight times, which ties the most out-wide targets a tight end has had since the 2016 season -- as far back as I have alignment data. He caught six passes out wide ... which ties the most out-wide receptions a tight end has had since the 2016 season.

 That is wide receiver usage. The Raiders were in "multi-tight-end" sets on 81% of their snaps Sunday -- the highest rate for any team in a game this season -- because they're not actually multi-tight-end sets . It's really 11.5 personnel, because they have the skeleton key in Bowers.

 Let's see what this looks like in practice. On a key third down late in the third quarter of Sunday's win, the Raiders isolate Bowers on the backside by motioning to a four-strong formation. With all four receivers to the opposite side of the field, the Saints' hands are tied -- they have to play Bowers in man coverage with their best man corner, Kool-Aid McKinstry . Watch Bowers feint the slant, and when McKinstry doesn't bite, he bursts to McKinstry's upfield shoulder to threaten the go-ball and open up space for the back-shoulder throw. It's short, because  Kirk Cousins  underappreciated Bowers' speed, and Bowers makes a great adjustment for the first down.

 

 This is obviously super-duper sick. For most teams, a tight end in isolation on a cornerback is not a win -- for the Raiders, it is.

 What's particularly cool is that Kubiak wants to give these opportunities to Bowers over anyone else on the Raiders' roster. When Kubiak was the Seahawks' offensive coordinator last season, that player for him was star receiver Smith-Njigba. We see almost the exact same play here, in the Seahawks' 2025 Week 7 game against the Texans. Sam Darnold alerts to the man coverage on the backside and throws Smith-Njigba on the vertical route against press coverage, keeping the ball vertical instead of throwing it to the back shoulder given the positioning of the corner.

 

 This is far from the only example we can find of Bowers getting the JSN treatment from Kubiak. Again in isolation on the backside of the formation and again on third down, Bowers uses his reduced alignment to get into an out-breaking route at the sticks. Smith-Njigba was used on similar routes in similar alignments for Kubiak on money downs last season.

 

 Here, Bowers motions into a stack alignment to get a free release into an option route -- look at how easily he widens McKinstry before snapping back into space. He has special burst and body control for a tight end, much as Smith-Njigba has special burst and body control for a wide receiver. Smith-Njigba takes the option route the other direction, but the usage is the same.

 

 That Kubiak is giving Bowers the same plays he gave Smith-Njigba is important because Smith-Njigba was as high volume a receiver as we had seen in decades. Smith-Njigba had a preposterous 44.1% of the Seahawks' receiving yards and 35.9% of the Seahawks' targets through the 2025 season -- the highest share of a team's receiving production since Brandon Marshall with the 2012 Chicago Bears. In one game, Bowers had 46.8% of the team's receiving yards and 41.9% of the team's targets. That's Smith-Njigba usage and Smith-Njigba volume.

 Of course, because Bowers is a tight end, he won't get the same explosive opportunities that Smith-Njigba got down the field. JSN had a heavy dose of crossing patterns that Bowers largely didn't see in Week 3 -- those are big-play run-after-catch chances of play-action. Smith-Njigba could also outrun a corner for a 50-yard vertical, and Bowers isn't doing that.

 But what he is doing, we haven't seen at the tight end position since peak Kelce -- fitting, given the Raiders (3-0) face the Chiefs (3-0) in Week 4. Bowers now has two career games with at least six targets or at least five receptions from wide alignments -- games we could reasonably call "high volume" games on the outside. He is only 30 games into his NFL career. Kelce has played in 168 games since 2016. If Bowers' Week 3 usage keeps up, he'll join prime Kelce as the lone tight end of this era who lines up on the outside and wins , over and over again.

 

 

 It will be interesting to see how the Chiefs handle this. Through three weeks, they have played two teams without a strong tight end feature -- the Broncos (2-1) and the Dolphins (0-3), with the Colts (1-2) and Tyler Warren sandwiched there in the middle. Warren went for 21 yards on six catches (seven targets) against the Chiefs, as the Colts have devolved into targeting him shallow on designed touches to protect the recovering Daniel Jones from long dropbacks. Bowers will be the Chiefs' first real tight end test.

 Now,…
