title: Lions post 31 points for record-setting third time to start 2026
summary: There just aren't many positions in which you can the push the Lions' offense that it can't get out of.
full_text:
DETROIT -- Dan Campbell could finally let out a big sigh of relief on Sunday evening.

 For 60 minutes, the New York Jets -- led by his former defensive coordinator Aaron Glenn -- pushed his Detroit Lions to the limit as they narrowly escaped with a 31-24 victory at home.

 Campbell described the win as being "just what the doctor ordered," with star running back Jahmyr Gibbs scoring three touchdowns and the defense securing a pivotal takeaway.

 "I'm just proud of that defensive staff. I'm proud of those players over there and as a whole," Campbell said. "That was a good win."

 The offense scored exactly 31 points for the third consecutive game this season, marking the first time in franchise history the Lions have scored 30 or more points in each of their first three games, according to ESPN Research.

 Lions quarterback  Jared Goff called the point total "our lucky number," and Campbell said he has enjoyed the high-scoring affairs so far.

 "I'll tell you what, you're coming to our games? You're loving this now. I mean, these are exciting games. These are exciting," Campbell said. "Come down to the wire. Nobody's leaving early. And that was the point. We're not going to let anybody leave early this year."

 With Lions legend Barry Sanders in the building as part of the alumni homecoming festivities, Gibbs pulled out his best impression of the Hall of Famer on a 17-yard rushing touchdown to push Detroit ahead 17-7. On the play, Gibbs faked out the multiple Jets defenders after being tossed the ball, then cut along the left side to find the end zone at 10:56 in the third quarter for his fourth TD of the season.

 He also surpassed Billy Sims (42) for the second-most rushing touchdowns in Lions franchise history while trailing only Sanders (99) and his 11-yard touchdown reception from Goff with 2:25 remaining in the fourth gave Detroit its final lead.

 "Every time he's here, I gotta step up my game a little bit," Gibbs said of Sanders. "So, to be in the same conversation as him is humbling. I'm blessed to be in it. It's somebody I've looked up to for a long time."

 Goff ran the offense like a well-oiled machine, completing 25-of-32 passes for 269 yards, two touchdowns and zero interceptions. He has now thrown a touchdown in 26 consecutive games, which is the longest active streak in the NFL and extends his franchise record.

 He was nearly perfect against the Jets' blitz on Sunday, going 15-of-16 for 159 yards and two touchdowns. Through three games this season, Goff has four touchdowns and has completed 77% of his passes against the blitz, both his best marks through three games in his career, per ESPN Research.

 

 "I think I've done a good job of being disciplined and not getting frustrated, I guess, with the lack of deep throws," Goff said. "It's not that we're not calling them. It's just that they're playing with so much depth, and it's my job to not get frustrated and stay within myself and take the checkdowns, and I have, and it's been good."

 Although the offense was solid, it was the defense that saved the day with a critical takeaway on the Jets' final possession where defensive coordinator Kelvin Sheppard dialed up a safety blitz with under a minute left.

 Lions safety Chuck Clark forced a strip sack on Jets QB Geno Smith , and the fumble was picked up by linebacker Jack Campbell to seal the win.

 Detroit's defense received heavy criticism throughout the week for allowing 71 points through the first two weeks, but Campbell was proud of the unit for showing up when it mattered.

 Against the Jets, Detroit shook up its secondary with Rock Ya-Sin serving a reserve role. CB Roger McCreary started at outside cornerback alongside veteran D.J. Reed .

 Entering the Jets game, the Lions were outgained by 191 total yards this season, which was the fifth worst in NFL, but Sheppard refused to do any finger pointing following the Week 2 loss to the Bills.

 Instead, he held a meeting on Monday to dissect the defensive struggles, where honesty was shared between players and coaches and they were able to hash out some things, and the unit responded by allowing a season-low 24 points, although they still have areas to clean up.

 "That was an outstanding call by him. I'm proud of him," Campbell said of Sheppard. "It takes a lot of intestinal fortitude to hang in there and trust and believe in what you do, and your guys, what we're about and trust them to bring it to life and then they did it. That was awesome."

title: Tracking Jaguars CB/WR Travis Hunter through 2026 season
summary: Every week, we will look at how many snaps the two-way corner/receiver plays on offense and defense. Is there a trend in his usage?
full_text:
The Jacksonville Jaguars were emphatic in the offseason that cornerback/wide receiver  Travis Hunter was going to play on both sides of the ball in 2026. However, unlike his rookie season, the plan was for the 2025 No. 2 overall pick to be a starter on defense. Now, he is just being mixed in on offense with a specific package of plays. The situation is fluid, though, and head coach Liam Coen has maintained that Hunter's usage could change weekly.

 "You want to continue to do what we think is going to give us the best chance at winning throughout the course of the week," he said. "And so, if that's Travis getting more touches [on offense], then [he] absolutely will."

 Hunter played more on offense than defense in his 2025 rookie season, which ended after seven games because of a right knee injury. The 2024 Heisman Trophy winner had 28 catches for 298 yards and a touchdown and 15 tackles and three pass breakups. He played 67% of the team's offensive snaps and 36% of the defensive snaps before his injury, which occurred during practice on Oct. 30.

 How has Hunter's usage evolved this season? Each week we'll track his stats and evaluate the impact he had on the game.

 

 

 

 Week 3 vs. New England Patriots 
 In a 35-6 win against the Patriots, Hunter saw an increase in snaps with 42 on defense (70%) and a decrease on offense with four snaps (6.7% of all offensive snaps). He recorded four tackles and his first career interception, picking off New England quarterback Drake Maye in the back of the end zone late in the first half to preserve the Jaguars' 14-3 lead. Maye was trying to hit receiver Efton Chism III on third-and-goal from the 2-yard line, but Hunter out-jumped Chism for the ball. Hunter didn't touch the ball on offense for the second consecutive game, leaving him with only two touches so far this season.

 
 

 Week 2 at Denver Broncos 
 Hunter played 43 total snaps in the loss against the Broncos: 35 on defense (59.3% of all defensive snaps), seven on offense (12.7% of all offensive snaps) and one on special teams. He had one pass breakup and four tackles, and he was penalized for pass interference on a Bo Nix sideline pass to receiver Courtland Sutton . The 22-yard penalty -- plus Coen's unsportsmanlike conduct penalty for arguing the call -- gave the Broncos the ball at the Jaguars' 3-yard line. The Broncos scored what turned out to be the game-winning touchdown on the next play. Hunter was not targeted on offense.

 After Week 2, Coen explained that his cornerbacks are handling drives with a planned rotation -- which is why Hunter was in for only 59.3% of defensive plays.

 "We did it for the most part of the last season as well, before Travis got hurt," Coen said. "It's something that we got to continue to do. We have corners that we have confidence in. Those guys can all make plays for us. They can all communicate for us. They've been in the system now.

 "But yeah, it's a rotation. Pre-game, we have it all laid out. The players know it. They all know the rotation. It's been clearly laid out to them what the expectations and standards are."

 
 

 Week 1 vs. Cleveland Browns 
 Hunter started at cornerback and played 27 snaps on defense (55.1% of total defensive snaps) and four on offense (7.1% of total offensive snaps) against the Browns. On offense, he had one carry for 3 yards on a jet sweep and one catch for 8 yards on a screen pass. He has had at least one catch in every game in which he played (eight games) to this point. On defense, Hunter was targeted once on defense which resulted in a Deshaun Watson completed a 4-yard pass to KC Concepcion .

title: Matthew Stafford makes cameo in Taylor Swift's 'Patient Zero' music video
summary: Why, yes, that was Matthew Stafford. Here's why all signs pointed to the reigning NFL MVP's music video cameo.
full_text:
Never let it be said Matthew Stafford lacks range.

 If you find yourself watching Taylor Swift's recently debuted music video for "Patient Zero" and see someone who happens to bear a striking resemblance to the Los Angeles Rams quarterback, that's because it is said quarterback.

 In the video, which also stars actors Colin Farrell, Dakota Johnson and Cara Delevingne, the Super Bowl LVI champion and reigning NFL MVP makes a cameo at a black-tie affair alongside his wife, Kelly Stafford. Stafford's not the only athlete in the scene, as former Los Angeles Kings center and two-time Stanley Cup champion Jarret Stoll can be spotted next to him.

 For those struck by the randomness of that duo appearing in a Swift video, you clearly don't know the lore.

 

 So let's get into it.

 The Staffords are friends with the 14-time Grammy Award winner and her husband, Kansas City Chiefs tight end Travis Kelce , as are Stoll and his wife, Erin Andrews. The couples attended the Madison Square Garden wedding of Swift and Kelce this summer alongside Charissa Thompson and her significant other, Steven Cundari -- the latter of whom is also featured in the black-tie event scene of Swift's video posing next to Farrell.

 As for Andrews and Thompson, the duo have been vocal supporters of Swift and the Kansas City Chiefs star's relationship since before they started dating, even making a plea on their "Calm Down" podcast for the singer to give Kelce a chance. Meanwhile, the Staffords' four daughters are known Swift fans, with Kelly sharing in 2024 that she and Matthew surprised the girls with a trip to see "The Eras Tour" in New Orleans. Kelly and her daughters also attended the June premiere of "Toy Story 5" in Los Angeles where Swift made a surprise appearance to perform her song "I Knew It, I Knew You."

 Then there's the Emmy's Easter egg of it all. Swift sent her fans into overdrive when she appeared via prerecorded video skit at the 87th Emmy Awards alongside her cat, Olivia Benson, and the show's host, Mariska Hargitay, who plays Swift's cat's namesake on "Law & Order: Special Victims Unit." In the sketch, the pop superstar addressed the camera and said, "I think what we're gonna be looking for is hiding in plain sight: Saccharide Aries from the vineyard north or south."

 Upon the Stafford reveal, the "Aries" reference has been decoded as a nod to the symbol for the astrological sign for Aries being a ram. As for the rest of the cryptic message? "Saccharide" is a reference to Farrell's role in the show "Sugar," "from the vineyard" is the old French translation of Delevingne and "north or south" is a play on Dakota.

 And while you ruminate on all of that, we're going to ponder how we got a Stafford Easter egg before the Tayvis wedding photos. Any day now.

title: J.J. McCarthy traded to Giants: Will he succeed in New York?
summary: With Jaxson Dart out for the season, the Giants dealt a fifth-round pick to Minnesota for McCarthy. But does this move the needle for New York? Can it work?
full_text:
After Jaxson Dart went down with a season-ending knee injury  in Week 2, it was probably inevitable that the Giants would add another quarterback to their roster. Jameis Winston can be combustible at his best, and while the weather wasn't great at MetLife Stadium on Sunday, he has averaged 4.7 yards per attempt and completed 51% of his passes since inheriting the starting job. With Jake Haener as the only other QB on the roster, getting someone to back up Winston and potentially take over if he continues to struggle was a no-brainer for the Giants.

 And while Giants fans might have loved the idea of adding someone like Joe Flacco to continue the veteran's tour of Northeast football, teams weren't about to trade a useful backup who was one injury away from being their starter to the Giants out of pity. The market was QB3s, not QB2s, which left one very clear choice for New York:  J.J. McCarthy 

 Landing a fifth-round pick for McCarthy was an obvious call for the Vikings. Once their quarterback of the future after they traded up to take him in the first round of the 2024 draft, McCarthy had quickly and brutally fallen out of favor in Minnesota. After being the NFC Offensive Player of the Week in his NFL debut last season -- an opening-week win over the Bears -- McCarthy's inability to work all areas of the field, operate within the structure of the offense or avoid negative plays frustrated a Vikings organization that had let Sam Darnold leave in free agency to hand the job to him.

 
 Subscribe: 'The Bill Barnwell Show' 

 
 While it was no surprise when McCarthy lost something resembling a QB competition to new starter Kyler Murray in training camp this summer, the writing was really on the wall once it became clear that Kevin O'Connell preferred Carson Wentz as his second option. Trading McCarthy netted some small amount of draft capital for the Vikings while also saving them $4.6 million over the next two years in the process.

 So, the trade makes sense for both organizations. Will it work out for McCarthy, who is still only 23 years old and younger than Ty Simpson , whom the Rams took with their first-round pick in this year's draft? We're living in a bit of a golden era of second (or third) acts for quarterbacks around the NFL, with the likes of Darnold, Bryce Young , Malik Willis , Baker Mayfield  and others enjoying varying levels of success after their first organization gave up (and/or benched) them before the end of their rookie deals. Could McCarthy be the next to follow in their footsteps and turn his career around after a rough start?

 In the wake of the Giants' trade, I'll argue both sides of that question. I'm not sure where I'll land, but I can see a case for McCarthy thriving in New York, and I can see one where he disappoints Giants fans who are hoping for an answer. I'll lay out both potential outcomes and see if one resonates more than the other when I'm done. Naturally, let's start with the positive side of things. Why should Giants fans believe that McCarthy is the guy who can help keep their season afloat?

 

 
 Jump to: 
 Why this could work 
 Why this can't work 
 And ... will it work? 

 
 

 The case for McCarthy 
 With young quarterbacks, growth isn't linear, and what we see at the very beginning of a player's career might not fully represent what he can be by even the end of his rookie campaign. Two picks after the Vikings selected McCarthy in the 2024 draft, the Broncos went after their own QB of the future in Bo Nix , who struggled to open his career. Across his first four starts, Nix completed 60.1% of his passes, averaged 4.8 yards per attempt and threw one touchdown against four picks.

 From that point forward, Nix has been about a league-average NFL starter, completing more than 68% of his passes, averaging 7.3 yards per attempt and throwing 28 touchdowns against eight picks. He has had his ups and downs since, and, as we saw in the Rams-Broncos game Sunday night, those bumps in the road can come in the same game. Nix has been good enough to sustain the Denver offense, though, and if it weren't for a poorly timed fractured ankle , Nix might have been quarterbacking the Broncos in last season's Super Bowl.

 

 Nix was awful at the very beginning of his career, but we have a large enough sample of games since then to suggest that his true level of play is more in line with a solid quarterback. We're not there yet with McCarthy given the significant amount of time he has missed with injuries. McCarthy's first six games as a pro were generally a mess. He completed 54.1% of his passes, averaged 5.8 yards per attempt, took sacks on more than 11.1% of his dropbacks and threw 10 interceptions on 159 pass attempts. That is an unplayable quarterback.

 But over his final four starts in 2025, McCarthy was quietly ... pretty good? Returning from  a concussion , he oversaw four victories as the Vikings worked their way back to respectability over the end of the year. And over that stretch, McCarthy wasn't a problem for the Minnesota offense. He completed 64.3% of his passes, averaged a robust 8.4 yards per attempt and threw five touchdown passes against two picks, adding two more scores with his legs. McCarthy's sack rate dropped to 7.7%, which is still higher than you would like but much improved on what he had produced early in the season.

 Those aren't superstar numbers, but the McCarthy of the first six games was one of the worst QBs we've seen over the past decade, whereas the guy over the final four starts was completely playable. His 70.3 Total QBR over that stretch was the seventh-best mark in the league, just behind Matthew Stafford , who was finishing up an MVP season for the Rams. He was fourth in yards per dropback and eighth in passer rating.

 That's only a four-game stretch, of course, but it's also 40% of McCarthy's career as a starter and the four most recent games we've seen from him as a pro. If he is that quarterback moving forward, he's a completely viable starter. And given that he still has yet to turn 24, it's fair to project some semblance of growth from McCarthy if he could stay on the field long enough to get more reps.

 It's not great to see a respected offensive mind like O'Connell move on from McCarthy so quickly, but are the Vikings infallible as quarterback evaluators? They were originally the ones who targeted McCarthy and took him in the top 10. They moved on from Darnold after a disappointing stretch at the end of 2024, only for him to excel with the Seahawks.  They traded for Sam Howell and then gave up on the backup before he ever played a snap with the team, preferring to sign Wentz last summer. And while I can't fault them for targeting Murray, given his contract and skill set, the early returns have been very disappointing, even as the defense has led Minnesota to a 3-0 start. The Vikings might just be wrong in the same way that other organizations were wrong about Darnold, Mayfield and Willis.

 While McCarthy had plenty of big names around him on offense, they weren't as effective as the Vikings might have hoped. An expensively assembled offensive line didn't live up to expectations. The run game was inconsistent. And McCarthy's  receivers dropped a full 6% of his passes, the highest rate for any quarterback with at least 150 pass attempts last season. That could be on the QB, but Vikings receivers also dropped 4.6% of the throws from Wentz and Max Brosmer last season.

 And frankly, the Giants don't need McCarthy to shoulder the workload. This is going to be a run-heavy team, built through their offensive line, heavy personnel groupings and a Cam Skattebo -led backfield. McCarthy can make an impact with his legs, where he ran for 181 yards and four touchdowns in 2025. The Giants can retain some of the RPOs they installed for Dart, giving McCarthy easy answers for confidence-building completions. McCarthy was at his best booting out of the pocket and getting on the run, where…

title: What has gone wrong for the Patriots' offense, Drake Maye?
summary: New England is last in the NFL in offensive points per game at 9.7. Can Maye and his supporting cast settle things down and turn it around?
full_text:
FOXBOROUGH, Mass. -- Patriots quarterback Drake Maye had committed his third turnover, which was quickly turned into a touchdown, and was preparing to take the field again late in the third quarter of Sunday's 35-6 blowout loss  to the Jaguars.
 Before he did, there was a moment on the sideline with head coach Mike Vrabel, who looked directly into Maye's helmet as he wrapped both of his arms around the quarterback's shoulder pads, play sheet still in his left hand. Vrabel was doing his best to uplift Maye, whose start to the season has unexpectedly spiraled downward with six interceptions and a lost fumble. The defending AFC champions are now 1-2 heading into Sunday's road game against the 3-0 Bills ( Sunday, 1 p.m. ET, CBS ).

 What has happened to Maye?

 He had said his comfort level entering the second season in coordinator Josh McDaniels' offense was high, but he has looked mostly uncomfortable -- which has led to poor decision-making, defenses successfully pressing him and myriad miscues as he has navigated injuries to No. 1 receiver A.J. Brown and other core players around him. Maye called the offense "unacceptable" -- the unit ranks last in the NFL in points per game (9.7) -- and said he planned to "look in the mirror and take this as a turning point."

 

 Vrabel cited a golf analogy in identifying one place for him to start.

 "I think sometimes, we really want to make a good score, right? Sometimes we're so focused on it, we try to choke the life out of the golf club, and we're squeezing it so damn tight that the ball has no choice but to go sideways," Vrabel said on sports radio WEEI.

 "We need to stop trying to choke the life out of every single play. We need to relax. We need to settle in and go play football and not try to force things that aren't there."

 Maye's struggles have contributed to the Patriots scoring the third-fewest points through three games by a reigning conference champion in the Super Bowl era; their 36 trail only the 1999 Falcons (28) and 2007 Bears (33). Their 0.97 points per drive makes them the first team with less than one point per drive through three games since the 2021 Jets quarterbacked by Zach Wilson . And their minus-0.21 EPA per play is the worst by any team through three games since the 2023 Jets.

 Teammates and coaches have consistently mentioned that the team's early-season challenges aren't solely on Maye, though.

 "I think this is just an offensive unit deal, a team thing," receiver Romeo Doubs said. "The fundamentals are key ... fundamentals aren't strong enough. I keep emphasizing on it because that's part of this league, this game. You cannot win games doing your own thing. You have to have some sort technique and some professional initiative to get things rolling."

 Maye has no touchdowns and five interceptions when targeting wide receivers, a group adjusting to being without Brown since early in the third quarter of the season opener at Seattle due to a right high ankle sprain . In the past two games, Maye has targeted Mack Hollins a WR-high 11 times, followed by Doubs (8), DeMario Douglas (7), Kyle Williams (5) and Efton Chism III (3). Hollins has led the group with eight receptions (for 108 yards) while Doubs has the most receiving yards with 145 (on six catches). According to NFL Next Gen Stats, Patriots receivers rank 30th in average route speed at 12.85 mph when passes are completed to them.

 

 Brown, who was present in the locker room Monday and walking with a normal gait according to observers, is out for at least the next two games while on injured reserve. Sources familiar with his injury wouldn't be surprised if his absence extends beyond that, but players' recoveries often vary, and Brown was wearing cleats and a small ankle wrap Monday.

 The running game, meanwhile, has flashed at times but has been too inconsistent (tied for 19th in the NFL at 3.9 yards per carry). And blocking has also been an issue. Maye was pressured on 47% of his dropbacks against the Jaguars, according to ESPN Research, which is his highest total this season and the fourth highest of his career. Overall, Maye has been pressured on 41.4% of his dropbacks, up from 33.9% in 2025. His off-target percentage against pressure is a whopping 36%, up from 17% last season. That ranks 26th in the NFL.

 Losing starting right guard Mike Onwenu to a broken right ankle in the first half of a Week 2 win over the Steelers created a sizable void at the line of scrimmage. And then his replacement, veteran Greg Van Roten , was knocked out of Sunday's loss with a thigh injury in the second quarter.

 Another factor in Maye's early-season struggles? How defenses are scheming against him.

 ESPN Research noted that Maye faced zone on 51% of his dropbacks last season, but that has jumped to 65% this season. Specifically, defenses' usage of Cover 2 with two deep safeties to take away the long ball has increased from 19% last season to 32% this year. Maye dominated against man coverage in 2025, leading the league with an 89.2 QBR, 68% completion percentage and 9.0 yards per attempt. His 23 passing touchdowns against man looks ranked second in the NFL behind MVP Matthew Stafford (34). But now Maye is seeing way more zone coverage.

 "We have to get this thing right, by all of us," Vrabel reiterated, adding he has had no thoughts of giving Maye a break on the sidelines.

 Teammates continue to rally behind Maye, too: "That's my quarterback. When I got here, I was excited to work with him. And I look forward to growing with him," Doubs said.

 So, what now? Vrabel pointed to the practice field when asked how he might help Maye loosen his grip on the golf club.

 

 "Confidence comes from your preparation, and it comes from going out there. I can't manufacture confidence," he said. "You have to practice. You have to hit those plays in practice and you have to feel good about it.

 "We just have to be able to make sure that we're on the same page, that everybody knows what is expected of them, have a few details, and then go play football."

 The challenge ahead for Maye is amplified by the teams the Patriots face -- a trip to the undefeated Bills in the third-ever game in Buffalo's new stadium, then a home game against the resurgent 3-0 Raiders. Drop one of those games, and the Pats will have already matched their loss total from all of 2025. Lose both, and it would put them in a most vulnerable spot to defend their AFC championship.
